title: National Professional Officer (Health Financing)
body:
## OBJECTIVES OF THE PROGRAMME

WHO’s work in countries operationalizes the General Programme of Work (GPW14) and the European Programme of Work 2025-2029 (EPW2). GPW14 focuses on accelerating progress toward Health for All by strengthening systems for health, improving access to essential services, advancing preparedness and resilience, and reducing health inequalities. EPW2, endorsed at RC75 following extensive consultation with Member States, reaffirms WHO/Europe’s role in bringing unique value to countries through five core functions:  
1\.  **International knowledge hub for health** – providing authoritative evidence, norms, policies and best practices from across the Region and globally to inform national public health decision-making.  
2\. **Impartial coordinator for everyone’s health** – convening national stakeholders and partners to align strategies and support coherent, multisectoral responses to shared health challenges.  
3\. **Leader in tracking and managing cross-border health threats** – supporting surveillance, preparedness, and coordinated action on public health emergencies in line with the Preparedness 2.0 agenda.  
4\. **Driver of health system transformation** – advising national authorities on evidence-informed reforms and policies that strengthen health systems and improve performance.  
5\. **Voice for health equity** – helping countries identify who is being left behind and integrating equity considerations into health policies and strategies.

In this context, WHO Country Offices enable the translation of global and regional commitments into national action. They support Member States by providing strategic advice, convening dialogue across sectors and partners, connecting national authorities with WHO’s technical expertise, and facilitating the use of evidence and best practices to inform policy.

## DESCRIPTION OF DUTIES

With the overall aim of advancing progress towards Universal Health Coverage, promoting good practices in health financing and reducing financial hardship, the incumbent leads WHO's health financing work in Ukraine and provides technical advice to national counterparts on health financing policy and reform.

Key duties:   
1\. Coordinate and provide technical leadership for the design, implementation and monitoring of WHO's health financing workstream, as programmed in the Country Cooperation Strategy (CCS) Biennial Collaborative Agreement (BCA), including WHO's contribution to health sector coordination and national policy dialogue.   
2\. Provide technical advice to the Ministry of Health, the National Health Service of Ukraine (NHSU) and other national partners on the development, implementation and evaluation of health financing policies and reforms at national and subnational levels, including strategic purchasing, the design of the Programme of Medical Guarantees, public financial management, to improve health system performance, including financial protection and progress towards universal health coverage.  
3\. Identify and guide priority areas for collaboration, capacity development and technical assistance in health financing, and translate these priorities into deliverable and costed workplans under the CCS BCA and donor-financed projects.  
4\. Lead and oversee the generation and use of evidence to support health financing policy and reform. This includes overseeing the analysis of health financing data and the planning, commissioning and quality assurance of studies, policy briefs, situation analyses, reports and other technical products on health financing, health system performance, service coverage and aid effectiveness. Work closely with WHO technical programmes to ensure that evidence generated is used to inform policy advice and dialogue, as well as the monitoring and evaluation of health financing reforms.  
5\. Lead and oversee the effective and high-quality implementation of health financing activities under donor-financed initiatives and agreed partnerships at country level. Provide technical direction for technical assistance, policy dialogue and capacity development, ensuring that activities are aligned with agreed objectives, priorities and deliverables. Monitor implementation and results and ensure timely and appropriate reporting to relevant stakeholders and donors.  
6\. Represent WHO, as appropriate, in discussions with national authorities, development partners and other stakeholders on health financing. Lead and contribute to technical discussions, coordination mechanisms and policy dialogue, and strengthen collaboration among partners to support coherent implementation of health financing reforms.  
7\. Supervise and provide technical direction to the staff working on health financing. Assign and prioritize work, clarify responsibilities, review the quality and timeliness of technical outputs, provide feedback and guidance, and support their performance and professional development. Ensure effective coordination between their respective areas of work and coherence across the health financing portfolio.  
8\. Contribute to strengthening national capacity in health financing through technical guidance, knowledge sharing and capacity development activities, in collaboration with national institutions and relevant partners.  
9\. Organize and substantively support WHO missions, visits and high-level engagements on health financing, and follow up on agreed recommendations and actions to ensure appropriate implementation.

## REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

### Education

**Essential:** A university degree (Bachelor's level) in business administration, management, economics or health economics, health policy, public health, social and political sciences, with concentration in health financing.  
**Desirable:** Master's degree or postgraduate degree in any of the above fields.

### Experience

**Essential**: At least five years of professional experience in health systems strengthening, including substantial experience in health financing. Experience working with national health authorities, purchasing agencies, academic institutions, international organizations and/or non-governmental organizations. Demonstrated experience contributing to or providing technical input to national health financing policy processes and policy dialogue.  
**Desirable**: Experience in WHO/UN and international agencies; Experience providing policy advice on health systems strengthening, health financing and health sector reform, particularly in transition, reform or post-crisis settings.

### Functional Skills

- Demonstrated knowledge of health systems and health financing policy in the countries of the WHO European Region, including purchasing, benefit package design, public financial management and financial protection monitoring.
- Proven ability to translate technical analysis into policy advice for senior decision-makers and to formulate technical positions independently.
- Ability to interact appropriately and with credibility with high-level stakeholders, including senior officials and ministers.
- Ability to lead high performing teams. Ability to work within significant uncertainties in a rapidly changing environment and to set priorities with limited supervision.
- Data management and data analysis skills.
- Good computer skills (word processing, spreadsheet, PowerPoint presentations).
- Strong written and oral communication skills, including drafting for policy audiences.
- Emotional intelligence: ability to identify and manage one's own emotions, as well as helping others to do the same.

### WHO Competencies

1\. Teamwork  
2\. Respecting & promoting individual and cultural differences  
3\. Communication  
4\. Moving forward in a changing environment  
5\. Building and promoting partnerships across the Organization and beyond

### Use of Language Skills

**Essential**: Expert knowledge of English. Expert knowledge of Ukrainian.

**Desirable:** Intermediate knowledge of any other UN language.

## REMUNERATION

Remuneration comprises an annual base salary starting at USD 64,825 (subject to mandatory deductions for pension contributions and health insurance, as applicable) and 30 days of annual leave.

**Link to apply:** [**Job Description - National Professional Officer (Health Financing) (2604631)**](https://careers.who.int/careersection/ex/jobdetail.ftl?job=2604631&tz=GMT%2B03%3A00&tzname=Europe%2FKiev)

title: Documentary Film Production Consultant
body:
**Terms of Reference (ToR):** Documentary Film Production Consultant, STRIVE Program – Indonesia

**Location:** Indonesia

**Assignment Date:** Until May 2027

**Contract Type:** Consultant (6 months)

**A. BACKGROUND**

Nurani Perdamaian Indonesia (NPID), through the GCERF, is implementing the Strengthening Rehabilitation and Reintegration and Improve Social Cohesion against Violent Extremism (STRIVE) Program from January 2025 to December 2027.

Implemented in partnership with national and local civil society organizations and in close collaboration with relevant government institutions, the STRIVE Program seeks to strengthen Indonesia's efforts in preventing violent extremism by supporting the reintegration and rehabilitation of returnees, former violent extremist offenders, and individuals at risk, while fostering resilient and inclusive communities. The program is implemented across three primary intervention areas:

- Jakarta
- Bima, West Nusa Tenggara
- Poso, Central Sulawesi

Throughout its implementation, STRIVE has promoted multi-stakeholder collaboration involving government agencies, civil society organizations, community leaders, religious leaders, youth, women, and beneficiaries to strengthen social cohesion and sustainable reintegration.

As the program approaches its completion, NP Indonesia intends to produce a high-quality documentary film that captures its journey, achievements, lessons learned, and the human stories behind the intervention. The documentary is expected to serve as a legacy product, an advocacy tool, and a knowledge resource that highlights the importance of sustained investment in community resilience and reintegration beyond the program period.

**B. PURPOSE**

The purpose of this consultancy is to produce a compelling documentary film that captures the overall implementation and impact of the STRIVE Program while communicating the continued importance of community-based reintegration and resilience-building efforts.

The documentary should present authentic stories, demonstrate evidence of program achievements, and inspire continued collaboration among governments, communities, civil society, and development partners.

**C. OBJECTIVES**

The documentary shall aim to:

1. Document the implementation of the STRIVE Program across Jakarta, Bima, and Poso.
2. Capture stories of transformation among beneficiaries, families, communities, and institutional stakeholders.
3. Showcase collaborative efforts between government institutions, civil society organizations, and local communities.
4. Demonstrate the program's contribution to strengthening community resilience, social cohesion, and sustainable reintegration.
5. Produce a high-quality legacy documentary suitable for advocacy, public communication, knowledge sharing, and future resource mobilization.

**D. SCOPE OF WORK**

The selected consultant shall be responsible for the complete production process, including pre-production, production, and post-production.

**1. Pre-Production**

The consultant shall:

1. Participate in inception meetings with NP Indonesia.
2. Review program documents and communication materials.
3. Develop a creative concept and documentary treatment.
4. Prepare storyline, interview framework, and production schedule.
5. Identify key interviewees together with the program team.
6. Prepare filming plans and logistics.

**2. Production**

The consultant shall conduct field production in:

1. Jakarta
2. Bima, West Nusa Tenggara
3. Poso, Central Sulawesi

The filming should include, but not be limited to:

1. Program implementation activities
2. Beneficiary interviews
3. Family member interviews
4. Community leaders
5. Religious leaders
6. Government representatives
7. Consortium partners
8. Community interactions
9. Environmental and supporting footage
10. Drone footage (where permitted)

The consultant is expected to adopt a cinematic documentary approach that emphasizes authentic storytelling and high-quality visual production.

**3. Post-Production**

The consultant shall:

1. Develop the documentary narrative.
2. Edit all footage.
3. Produce motion graphics and animated statistics where appropriate.
4. Add background music and sound mixing.
5. Prepare English and Bahasa Indonesia subtitles.
6. Incorporate revisions based on feedback from NP Indonesia.
7. Deliver final mastered versions.

**E. DOCUMENTARY APPROACH**

Rather than producing a chronological record of program activities, the documentary should adopt a story-driven, human-centered approach.

The documentary should:

1. Highlight authentic experiences.
2. Balance emotional storytelling with evidence-based program achievements.
3. Showcase collaboration among communities, government institutions, and civil society.
4. Present transformation at individual, community, and institutional levels.
5. Maintain a professional cinematic quality suitable for international audiences.

The documentary should conclude with a forward-looking message that emphasizes the importance of sustaining the gains achieved through the STRIVE Program and continuing collective efforts toward resilient communities.

**F. DELIVERABLES AND TIMELINE**

The consultant shall deliver:

**Deliverables**

- One documentary film.
- One shortened version of the documentary film.
- One promotional trailer.
- Five short social media video clips.
- Subtitles in English and Bahasa Indonesia.
- High-resolution photographs from field production.
- All raw video footage.
- Editable project files, upon request.

**Timeline**

- **December:** Procurement process, inception meeting, desk review, development of the creative concept and storyline, preparation of the interview list, shooting plan, and logistics.
- **January to March:** Field production in Jakarta, Bima, and Poso.
- **April:** Editing, script writing, motion graphics development, subtitling, music scoring, and preparation of the first cut.
- **May:** Review and revision process, final cut, mastering, and submission of all final deliverables.

**G. CONSULTANT QUALIFICATION**

The consultant or production company should possess:

- Minimum five (5) years of professional experience in documentary film production.
- Demonstrated experience producing documentaries for international development programs, humanitarian organizations, or donor-funded projects.
- Strong storytelling and cinematic production capabilities.
- Proven experience conducting field production in diverse cultural contexts.
- Ability to produce bilingual documentary outputs.
- Availability to travel to all program locations.
- Experience working with government institutions and civil society organizations is considered an asset.

**H. PROPOSAL REQUIREMENTS**

Interested consultants shall submit:  
**1. Technical Proposal**

1. Understanding of the assignment.
2. Proposed documentary concept.
3. Creative treatment.
4. Storytelling approach.
5. Production methodology.
6. Workplan and timeline.
7. Team composition and roles.
8. Relevant portfolio.
9. Risk management approach.

**2. Financial Proposal**

1. Professional fees.
2. Travel costs.

**Job Title:** Safety & Security Officer (Ukrainian nationals)

**Department:** Safety & Security

**Division:** Operations

**Duty Station:** Mykolaiv, Ukraine

**Line Manager:** Safety & Security Manager

**Line Management Responsibility:** N/A

**Position Type:** Full-time

**Overview:**

Nonviolent Peaceforce (NP) is a dynamic, international non-governmental organisation. We work with people affected by violent conflicts to enhance their security and dignity through Unarmed Civilian Protection (UCP). We work to reduce violence, protect civilians in countries affected by violent conflict and its aftermath, and help transform the world’s response to conflict situations.

NP first established a presence in Ukraine in 2014/2015 working on peacebuilding and conflict mediation. NP has had a sustained presence in Ukraine since April 2022. NP occupies a unique space in the protection response in Ukraine; simultaneously providing direct protection to at-risk civilians and providing hands-on support to front-line volunteer collectives to directly contribute to the sustainability and safety of their actions.

**Job Summary:**

The Safety and Security Officer works directly with the Head of Operations and Security to contribute to the safety and security of NP staff in Ukraine. The position will support with analysis and security inputs and will engage directly with programmes teams for security monitoring and guidance. The position contributes to making sure effective safety and security arrangements are in place for NP staff.

The ideal candidate will bring security expertise developed through experience working in the security and/or humanitarian sector. They are focused and driven by a keen interest and personal commitment to civilian protection – the core of NP’s work.

**Key Responsibilities:**

**Safety & Security Management**

- Implement and uphold NP safety and security policies, procedures, SOPs, and contingency plans at field and office level.
- Conduct regular security and risk assessments to identify threats, vulnerabilities, and mitigation measures.
- Support the operationalisation of security plans including travel management, incident response, emergency communications, evacuation, relocation, and hibernation procedures.
- Ensure offices, guesthouses, and programme sites meet minimum physical security standards through regular infrastructure and security audits.
- Immediately report and document all security incidents, breaches, threats, or near-misses affecting staff, assets, or operations.

**Operational Support & Staff Movement**

- Provide real-time tracking, monitoring, and oversight of staff and vehicle movements in line with established procedures.
- Ensure vehicles, communications equipment, and personal protective equipment are available, functional, and compliant with minimum standards.
- Work closely with Logistics to identify, procure, and maintain safety and security equipment and resources.

**Information Management & Analysis**

- Collect, verify, analyze, and disseminate security-related information from formal and informal sources.
- Maintain up-to-date records of security incidents, trends, and contextual developments.
- Provide timely security briefings, updates, and advisories to staff and management in response to changes in context.
- Contribute to weekly and monthly security reports relevant to NP areas of operation.

**Training & Capacity Building**

- Deliver regular security briefings, inductions, and awareness sessions for staff.
- Identify security capacity-building needs and support the design and delivery of relevant trainings.
- Train, mentor, and support designated Security Focal Points across field offices.
- Supervise, train, and develop security staff at office or area level where applicable.

**Coordination, Liaison & Access**

- Maintain strong working relationships with NGOs, UN agencies, INSO, security providers, and relevant coordination platforms.
- Liaise with local authorities, community leaders, and other relevant stakeholders to support safe access and programme implementation, in line with humanitarian principles.
- Participate in security coordination forums and inter-agency meetings as required.
- Support access analysis and security input for programme planning and expansion into new areas of operation.

**Assessments & Compliance**

- Participate in security assessments for new locations and evolving operational areas.
- Ensure adherence to NP security risk management standards and country-specific SOPs.
- Support senior management in internal security reviews and audits.

**Safeguarding & Conduct**

- Comply with and uphold NP safeguarding policies, including child protection, prevention of sexual exploitation and abuse (PSEA), and policies on bullying and harassment.
- Act in accordance with NP Codes of Conduct at all times.

**Critical Interfaces**

- All NP staff and departments.
- Senior Management Team.
- Programme and Operations teams.
- Logistics and Administration.
- External coordination and security actors.

**Qualifications:**

- Post-secondary education in a related field with at least 2 years related work experience or equivalent in work experience.
- Relevant security experience in humanitarian settings / previous experience working with security providers, law enforcement entities, and/or intelligence resources and utilizing information to create and deploy actionable security plans and programs.
- Understanding of current security management good practice.
- Good grasp of various communications technologies commonly used, including VHF radio systems, satellite phones, cell phones, Power Bi, etc.
- Excellent interpersonal, representation and negotiation skills, with the ability to influence, build consensus and develop partnerships.
- Ability to work well under pressure in unstable and frequently changing security environments.
- Training and facilitator skills; ability to support training sessions is a plus.
- Commitment to and understanding of NP’s methodologies, core values and mission.
- Advanced proficiency in written and spoken English, Ukrainian and Russian.
- Computer literacy, particularly in Word, Excel, PowerPoint, databases.
- Valid Ukrainian driving license.
- Knowledge of and commitment to safeguarding, whistleblowing, PSEA and anti-corruption.

**Skills and Competencies:**

**Independent Judgment/Analytical:**

- Ability to set priorities, solve problems and analyse data.
- Ability to manage information with discretion.
- Identify safety and security issues and propose solutions.

**Interpersonal:**

- Ability to communicate effectively with individuals and motivate and provide leadership to team and to work and live in a multi-cultural environment.
- Ability to exert solutions-focused, creative behaviour.
- Proven ability to build relationships with the full range of actors including government, military, police and non-state actors.
- Flexibility and adaptability.

**Languages:**

- Ability to interact confidently in English with colleagues and external contacts, including in writing, and to present effectively relevant information.

**Information Technology:**

- High level skills in Microsoft Office applications (Outlook, Excel, SharePoint, PowerPoint, Word, Power BI).
- Knowledge of Digital Mapping and GPS tracking software.
- Knowledge of computer software for VHF radios.
- Emergency Response Systems.

**Working Conditions:**

- Ukraine is a complex security environment, and the evolution of the war is completely unpredictable – experience in insecure environments is essential to success in this position.
- A strong motivation to do what’s necessary in a complex environment.
- Willingness to work some weekends and evenings to contribute to security support and preparedness.

**OVERVIEW**

Since 2020, NP has worked alongside local communities in the U.S. to interrupt cycles of violence and build bridges across polarized communities. Responsive to community needs, NP builds relationships with community members, leaders, and organizations to identify risks to safety and ways to work together to keep communities safe through nonviolent strategies. These strategies include protective presence, training, safety planning, and rapid response. This work takes us to demonstrations, marches, courts, voting centers, health facilities, pantries, and other public spaces where people may face violence and intimidation. In partnership with local organizations we help build stronger protection networks, coordinate responses to emerging risks and advance the practice of nonviolent community-led approaches to protection in communities across the country.

title: Humanitarian Representative - Russia
body:
**Location:** Any MSF Office\*

**Contract:** 100%

**Duration:** 12 months

**Deadline to apply:** 11th of November 2026

**Starting date:** 01st December of 2026

**Compensation and Benefits:** MSF practice is to offer the compensation and benefits package in line with the MSF entity offering the contract.

\**By default, the successful candidate will be offered a contract in the MSF office, able to issue a contract, of their country of residence at the time of application.*

**MSF International**

Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) is an international, independent, medical humanitarian organisation that delivers emergency aid to people affected by armed conflict, epidemics, healthcare exclusion and natural disasters. MSF offers assistance to people based only on need and irrespective of race, religion, gender or political affiliation. MSF International is the legal entity that binds MSF’s 24 sections, 28 associations and other offices together. Registered in Switzerland, MSF International provides coordination, information and support to the MSF Movement, as well as implements international projects and initiatives as requested.

**Scope of the Position**

MSF seeks to strengthen its engagement, contextual understanding and institutional memory related to the Russian Federation and the Former Soviet Union (FSU). The position provides a focused capacity for engagement with Russian representatives outside the Russian Federation, contextual analysis, internal coordination and support to MSF operations in relevant contexts.

The role operates within a sensitive and evolving geopolitical and legal environment. It contributes to maintaining institutional links and information flows while supporting operational teams and ensuring relevant developments and strategic considerations are surfaced to appropriate MSF stakeholders.

**Position Background and Purpose**

The Humanitarian Representation Team (HRT) works to enhance MSF’s ability to understand, inform, and where possible, influence the actions and decisions of external stakeholders for the purposes of protecting MSF’s operational space, advocating for needs-based humanitarian action and, when requested, conveying MSF’s témoignage. The HRT supports MSF operations through linkages and actions to and from a wide array of external networks that include governments, multilateral institutions and agencies, humanitarian and civil society organisations, medical associations, think tanks, research centres, and other influential interlocutors. The HRT consists of a full-time secretariat covering multilateral bodies (UN, EU-NATO, AU), permanent UNSC members (US, UK, China, Russia), and other key regions (East Africa, West Africa, the Middle East & North Africa, and the Asia Pacific). The HRT Secretariat’s work is supported by a global network including more than 20 representatives linked to MSF entities and offices worldwide.

Working under the leadership of the IOHRC and alongside the Deputy IOHRC & RIOD Advisor, the position holder will be responsible for support, coordination and expansion of MSF’s engagement and network with Russian representatives outside the Russian Federation. As a member of the HRT secretariat, the holder of the position should be available for deployments in support to country programs, and on-the-ground engagement support as requested by operational teams or HRT network members, and in agreement with the IOHRC.

**Accountabilities**

**1. Analysis**

- Provide contextual analysis and updates on developments in the Russian Federation, the South Caucasus, and Central Asia that may impact MSF’s operations and humanitarian engagement.
- Support operations by providing ad hoc analyses and briefings on topics of interest.
- In coordination with operations, continue developing and reviewing scenarios regarding MSF’s presence in Russia, with particular attention to conditions and entry points for potential future operations.
- Monitor and assess opportunities for the potential reopening of institutional dialogue and an operational presence in the Russian Federation in close coordination with HRT Representative in Geneva.
- Continue monitoring and analyzing the risk of MSF being designated as an "undesirable organization" in Russia and the potential implications for the organization.

**2. Engagement and networking**

- Maintain the existing network of Russian interlocutors and identify or create engagement opportunities globally, including at conferences, events or through bilaterial engagements.
- Develop and expand the network with new and relevant Russian and Russian-affiliated contacts for the MSF movement and operations.
- Ensure continuity and accompany ongoing efforts to engage with Russian representatives globally on issues related to the contexts in which MSF operates.
    
    \- Support MSF operational teams in their engagement with Russian representatives in countries where MSF maintains operations. ting MSF research and academic work.

**3. Internal coordination**

- Coordinate the HRT BRICS working group and facilitate information sharing and strategic alignment among its members.
- Facilitate interdesk meetings when relevant and share outcomes with relevant colleagues in accordance with the Interdesk terms of reference set by the RIOD.

**4. Other responsibilities**

- Facilitate coordination, information sharing, and reporting among MSF colleagues engaging with Russian stakeholders.
- Build and maintain the Russia Online Archives to collect the data of the RBO and other data coming from OPS engagement with Russian representatives.

**Autonomy, Complexity**

The incumbent will operate with a high degree of autonomy in a politically sensitive and complex environment, requiring the ability to independently assess developments, identify strategic opportunities, and define engagement priorities. The role involves managing senior-level relationships with government authorities, diplomatic actors, and other stakeholders in an environment in which MSF has very limited space. The Representative is expected to exercise sound judgment in navigating high sensitivities and providing timely analysis and recommendations to open the space for MSF in support of operations. The position requires balancing operational, political, legal, and reputational considerations while representing the organization externally and ensuring coherence with broader institutional objectives.

**Safeguarding requirements for the role**

The incumbent commits to contribute to a safe, supportive, inclusive, equitable, diverse, respectful, and healthy workplace, free from abuse and other misconduct. They will not engage in any form of abuse including those detailed in MSF Typologies of Abuse and when an employee suspects or observes abuse, they will report it (without investigating it) to protect others.

**Requirements**

**Education**

- Master's degree (M. A.) or equivalent, or six to ten years related experience and/or training; (or equivalent combination of education and experience).

**Experience**

- Extensive (field) working knowledge/experience with MSF is mandatory.

**Knowledge**

- Demonstrated interest in and commitment to the humanitarian action and principles of MSF.
- Demonstrated knowledge of international humanitarian affairs and solid knowledge of diplomatic networks in Russia and countries and institutions within their orbit.
- Strategic vision and creativity in problem solving.
- Knowledge of basic provisions of International Humanitarian and Human Rights Law.
- Ability to synthesize complex and sensitive material and analyze and report on it cogently to colleagues.
- Ability to write high-level correspondence and interact with senior diplomatic officials.
- Excellent interpersonal skills, judgment and diplomatic skills.
- Excellent written and oral communications skills.
- Ability to travel on a frequent basis throughout the region and beyond.
- Ability to set priorities and organise his/her own work.

**Languages**

- Written and spoken English and Russian are required.

**Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.**

**At MSF, we are committed to an inclusive culture that encourages and supports the diverse voices of our employees. We welcome applications from individuals of all genders, ages, sexual orientations, nationalities, races, religions, beliefs, ability status, and all other diversity characteristics.**

**MSF is committed to preventing abuse, inappropriate behaviour, lack of integrity and financial misconduct in its work and care spaces. MSF expects all staff to share this commitment and promote an environment where abuse and misconduct is not tolerated.**

**We are committed to removing barriers for people with specific accessibility needs. If you need an adjustment to the recruitment process to be considered for the role, please let us know from the beginning of the selection process.**

**Note: All offers of employment will be subject to reference checks and to appropriate screening checks. By submitting an application, the job applicant confirms his/her/their understanding of these recruitment procedures.**

title: Consultant to Produce Explainer Video on the Civic Space in Nigeria
body:
**Scope:** Consultant to Produce Explainer Video on the Civic Space in Nigeria

**Location:** Abuja, Nigeria/Remote  
**Application Close**: October 28, 2026

Global Rights is an international human rights and governance capacity-building non-governmental organization. We work with local activists in Africa to promote and protect the rights of marginalized populations. For more than 30 years, we have worked to build the capacity of underserved communities in Nigeria and build platforms for participatory governance, working on a wide range of cross cutting issues including: women’s rights, access to justice, natural resource governance, climate change and human rights; civic space strengthening; and security and human rights.  
Global Rights works at the intersection of the protection, promotion and fulfilment of human rights through good governance. Mandatorily, women’s rights, access to remedies, and disabilities issues, are focal threads woven through the fabric of all our programs.

**Background**

Nigeria’s civic space is facing growing pressure from legal, regulatory and administrative measures that risk restricting the ability of civil society organizations (CSOs), human rights defenders, journalists and citizens to operate freely, organize collectively, and hold public institutions accountable. While regulation is necessary to promote transparency and accountability, the use or expansion of regulatory powers in ways that undermine freedom of association, expression and peaceful assembly raises serious concerns about the protection of fundamental rights and the sustainability of democratic participation.

These concerns are heightened by existing legal frameworks and proposed legislation that could expand government oversight of civil society, impose additional obligations on organizations, or create opportunities for arbitrary restrictions on their activities. The Companies and Allied Matters Act (CAMA) 2020, particularly provisions relating to the regulatory powers of the Corporate Affairs Commission (CAC) over incorporated trustees, has been the subject of legal contestation over the limits of regulatory authority and the autonomy of civil society organizations. More recently, proposed legislation, including the Foreign Aid Bill, has generated concerns about the potential implications of increased state oversight of foreign funding, organizational independence, and the ability of CSOs to carry out legitimate human rights and governance work.

Beyond the provisions of individual laws and bills, the cumulative effect of restrictive legal and regulatory measures can create an environment in which civil society organizations face uncertainty, increased compliance burdens, and potential interference in their operations. Such an environment may discourage civic participation, weaken independent advocacy, constrain access to resources, and limit the ability of marginalized communities to organize and seek redress. These risks have particular implications for organizations working on accountability, human rights, gender equality, natural resource governance, and the protection of vulnerable and underserved populations.

As part of Global Rights' broader efforts to strengthen civic space and promote informed public engagement, Global Rights is producing a new edition of its [**We No Go Gree**](https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLZXvVYMe6oOY) video series, using ongoing legal and policy developments as an entry point to examine the broader challenges facing civic space in Nigeria. The episode, **We No Go Gree 104**, will explore how existing laws and proposed legislation may affect the operating environment for civil society, the constitutional rights of citizens, and the ability of organizations to contribute to democratic governance and public accountability. The CAMA litigation, undertaken by Global Rights in partnership with the Network of University Legal Aid Institutions (NULAI) Nigeria, will serve as one illustrative example of the legal and constitutional questions arising from the regulation of civil society.

The video will translate complex legal and policy issues into accessible, engaging content for a wider public audience. It will be published on Global Rights’ YouTube channel and repurposed into shorter clips for dissemination across its social media platforms, with the aim of raising awareness, encouraging informed public discussion, and strengthening public understanding of the importance of protecting civic space in Nigeria.

**Goal**  
To increase public awareness and understanding of the CAMA litigation and its implications for civic space, civil society organizations, and the regulatory environment in Nigeria through accessible and engaging digital media content.

**Objectives**

- To explain the CAMA litigation and the specific legal and regulatory issues under consideration in accessible language.
- To increase public understanding of how the regulation of incorporated trustees and CSOs affects civic space and civil society operations.
- Promote informed public discussion on the constitutional limits of regulatory powers and the protection of civic space.

**Scope of Work**

- Develop a concept, narrative and script for the episode in consultation with Global Rights.
- Explain the CAMA regulatory framework and the broader questions it raises about the powers of regulatory authorities and the autonomy of civil society organizations.
- Explore wider civic-space issues, including the implications of proposed legislation such as the Foreign Aid Bill.
- Produce a video (We No Go Gree 104) using a presenter-led format supported by infographics, text overlays and other visual elements, as well as shorter clips for social media distribution.
- Identify and engage a suitable influencer or content creator with a relevant audience to present the video.

**Key Issues to Be Addressed**  
The video should address the following questions:

1. The regulatory framework established by CAMA 2020 for NGOs in Nigeria.
2. The powers of regulatory authorities under CAMA and the implications for the independence and autonomy of civil society organizations.
3. The implications of existing and proposed legislation, including the Foreign Aid Bill, for civil society.
4. The broader implications of restrictions on civic space for citizens’ participation, freedom of association and the ability to hold public institutions accountable.

**Expected Deliverables**

- An approved script for the video
- Identification and engagement of a suitable influencer or content creator to present the episode
- One completed We No Go Gree 104 video not exceeding 10 minutes
- Short clips adapted from the video for social media distribution

**Timeline**

3 weeks

**Reporting Line**

The consultant will report directly to the Executive Director or the designates.

**Intellectual Property Rights**

All intellectual property rights arising from the consultancy will be the property of Global Rights. The consultant will not disclose or use any confidential information obtained during the consultancy for any other purpose without the written consent of Global Rights.

**Confidentiality and Ethical Considerations**

The consultant will ensure that all data collected during the consultancy is treated with the utmost confidentiality and in accordance with ethical principles. In particular, the consultant will obtain informed consent from all participants before collecting any data and will ensure that data is stored securely and only accessible to authorized personnel. The consultant will also comply with any relevant legal and ethical standards and will report any ethical concerns or violations to Global Rights immediately.

**Expected Qualifications:**

- Proven experience in narrative video and documentary production.
- Proficiency in video production, camera operation, sound recording, and video editing
- A creative vision for translating reports into a visually engaging and emotionally resonant explainer video

**Proposal Submission:**

Interested qualified consultants are invited to submit a proposal that includes the following:

- An understanding of the requirements
- Methodology and work plan for performing the assignment
- Project delivery plans
- Relevant services undertaken in the past with detailed reference list indicating the scope of similar assignments
- Budget
- At least one sample of similar work

title: Regional Internal Auditor - Sahel & Francophone
body:
**About MSI**

MSI Reproductive Choices is one of the world’s leading providers of sexual and reproductive healthcare. We believe that everyone should have the right to choose. From contraception to safe abortion and life-saving post-abortion care, we are committed to delivering compassionate, affordable, high-quality services for all.

Today, our organisation has around 10,000 team members working in 36 countries across the world. Our success lies in the fact that MSI teams are locally led, entrepreneurial and results-driven, and are passionate about delivering high quality, client-centred care in their own communities. As a social business, we focus on sustainable delivery, efficiency, and funding models that are built to last, so that the women and girls we serve today will have a choice in the future too.

We know that access to reproductive choice is life changing. For some, it can mean the ability to complete an education or start a career. For others, it means being able to look after the family they already have. For everyone, it means the freedom to decide their own future, creating a fairer, more equal world.

**About the Role**

The role reports directly and functionally to the MSI Head of Operational & Financial Audit, with an administrative dotted-line relationship to the Hostl Country Director. This arrangement will facilitate local coordination and integration while ensuring that responsibility for audit planning, scope, conclusions, performance management and professional oversight remains with Global Internal Audit, thereby preserving the independence of the audit function.

The role provides independent assurance across Mali, Senegal, Burkina Faso and Niger, with support to other Francophone Africa programmes where required. The post holder will complement Group Internal Audit cyclical audits through risk-based audits, targeted and routine monitoring, follow-up of audit actions and fraud investigations. The role will cover key financial, operational, donor compliance and programme risks, and will require regular regional travel.

**About You**

For us, it’s vital that every MSI team member believes in and is committed to our organisational mission, vision and values.

**This means that we will only accept applications from candidates who are unequivocally pro-choice.**

Our values act as guiding principles, providing us with a clear direction. They set the tone for how we approach our work, interact with others and align ourselves as ‘One MSI’. It’s important that our team members truly resonate with our values and demonstrate them consistently, in all that they do.

We recruit talented, dynamic individuals with diverse backgrounds who share our mission and are focused on delivering measurable results. As an equal opportunity employer, we are committed to fostering an inclusive workplace where everyone can participate and contribute meaningfully. We value open-mindedness, curiosity, resilience, and a solutions-oriented mindset, alongside a commitment to promoting equality and safeguarding the welfare of both team members and clients.

We seek exceptional communicators who are self-motivated, solutions-driven, and aligned with MSI’s mission and entrepreneurial mindset. You should be dedicated to driving social change in an environment focused on sustainable impact, both locally and globally, and comfortable working with diverse teams in an ambiguous setting.

**To perform this role, you’ll need the following skills:**

- **Fluent in French and English;**
- Ability to plan and scope risk-based audits and translate key risks into proportionate audit procedures
- Ability to perform and document walkthroughs, control design assessments and tests of controls
- Strong data analysis skills, including use of CAATs to identify trends, anomalies and control exceptions
- Strong investigative skills, including root cause analysis, evidence evaluation and identification of fraud indicators
- Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to produce clear, concise audit and investigation reports
- Strong stakeholder management and influencing skills, including confidence engaging and constructively challenging senior management.

**To perform this role, you’ll need the following experience:**

- Strong internal audit experience (at least 5 years), obtained through practice (Big 4/Mid-tier) or industry, with a working knowledge of the IIA Standards (essential)
- Experience conducting or supporting fraud and misconduct investigations (essential)
- Experience working in Francophone West Africa, the Sahel, or comparable fragile and conflict-affected environments, with a strong understanding of local operating contexts (desirable)
- Experience of working in an international, donor-funded service delivery organisation (desirable)

**Formal education/qualification**

- Holds a recognised professional accountancy/audit qualification (e.g., CA/ACA, ACCA, CPA, CIA etc.)

Please email Joshua.Wright@msichoices.org for the full job description.

**Location:** Dakar, Senegal.

**Full-time hours.**

**Contract type: 2 year fixed term contract.**

**Salary**: Gross Monthly Salary of 1,600,000 FCFA - 2,000,000 FCFA, plus benefits - dependent on experience.

**Salary band: Niveau 8**

**Closing date: 5th November 2026 (midnight GMT**). Interviews may take place before this date for exceptional candidates.

***For internal employees applying from an MSI country programme, the role will be positioned within the existing salary structure of the country. Local terms and conditions of the country will apply.***

title: Assistant, Community Based Protection (Baidoa)
body:
**Duty station**: Baidoa

**Field travel:** Baidoa — Bay, Bakool and Lower Shabelle including high-risk frontline locations, subject to CIVIC security procedures.

**Expected start date**: 1 December 2026, to be confirmed and subject to project funding.

**Contract duration**: 12 months, to be confirmed and subject to project funding.

**Project and funding status**: Anticipated project. Funding has not yet been secured; recruitment and appointment are contingent on confirmed funding and approval to proceed.

1\. **Background**

Center for Civilians in Conflict (CIVIC) is an international non-governmental humanitarian protection organization that works to protect civilians affected by armed conflict. CIVIC works with communities, governments, security actors, civil society, and other partners to prevent, mitigate, and respond to civilian harm. In Somalia, CIVIC supports community-based protection, civilian harm mitigation, community-security and civil-military dialogue, engagement with security institutions, evidence and research, and policy and institutional efforts to strengthen civilian protection. A central part of CIVIC’s approach is supporting conflict-affected communities to identify and prioritize protection concerns, develop locally led responses, engage relevant authorities and security actors, and follow up on actions intended to improve civilian protection.

CIVIC supports Community Protection Groups (CPGs) and Community Protection Champions as locally rooted mechanisms for community engagement, protection analysis, advocacy and dialogue. CIVIC works with these structures to strengthen their capacity to identify and document protection concerns, conduct Protection of Civilians (PoC) awareness and engagement activities, engage authorities and security actors, participate in community-security dialogues, follow up on protection concerns and agreed actions, and monitor changes affecting civilian safety. To strengthen the capacity, leadership and sustainability of community-based protection structures, and to sustain CIVIC’s field presence and accompaniment alongside them, the Somalia Programme anticipates recruiting an Assistant Community-Based Protection based in Baidoa. These positions are planned for an anticipated project for which funding has not yet been secured. Recruitment and appointment are contingent on confirmation of project funding and approval to proceed.

2\. **Position Summary**

The Assistant, Community-Based Protection will support implementation and day-to-day follow-up of CIVIC’s community-based protection and civilian harm mitigation activities within an assigned geographic area. Through sustained support to Community Protection Groups (CPGs) and Community Protection Champions and direct engagement with local authorities, security and armed forces and conflict-affected communities, including in high-risk frontline areas, the Assistant will strengthen community leadership, facilitate safe, inclusive dialogue and follow up on commitments to reduce civilian harm. The Assistant will support community consultations and protection analysis, PoC workshops and community-led activities; prepare communities and security actors for structured dialogue; and follow up on protection concerns and agreed actions.

Central to the role is strengthening CPGs’ and Champions’ ability to independently convene discussions, conduct PoC awareness and workshops, engage authorities and security actors, raise protection concerns, facilitate or participate in dialogue, and follow up agreed actions. The Assistant will maintain regular community and stakeholder relationships, monitor community protection mechanisms and document changes resulting from community-led action and CIVIC-supported engagement.

The role requires sustained field presence and regular travel, including to high-risk frontline and conflict-affected areas under CIVIC security procedures. This position is based in Baidoa, covering Bay, Bakool and Lower Shabelle. All travel and activities depend on programme priorities, access assessments, security clearance and CIVIC duty-of-care requirements.

3\. **Key Responsibilities**

Across all responsibilities, strengthen the capacity, ownership and sustainability of CPGs and Community Protection Champions to increasingly lead protection activities independently of CIVIC.

**A. Community Engagement and Protection Analysis**

• Maintain continuous, inclusive community engagement beyond workshops and dialogues, involving women, youth, elders, persons with disabilities, displaced communities, minority groups and others facing heightened protection risks.

• Support consultations and joint analysis with communities and CPGs to identify and prioritize protection concerns, determine community-led responses, and distinguish issues requiring authorities, security, humanitarian or other actors.

• Identify emerging protection concerns and promptly communicate significant developments through CIVIC programme and management channels.

**B. CPG and Community Protection Champion Capacity Strengthening**

• Provide structured accompaniment, mentoring, training, refresher sessions, coaching and peer learning to build CPGs’ and Champions’ capacity, confidence and independence in PoC, civilian harm, community-based protection, conflict sensitivity, early warning and locally led approaches, including developing and updating protection action plans.

• Support CPGs and Champions to prioritize issues, prepare objectives and increasingly plan, organize and lead PoC workshops, consultations, awareness and protection engagements. Accompany activities, progressively transfer facilitation and leadership, coach engagement with decision-makers, and support documentation of issues, decisions and agreed actions.

• Follow up and document agreed actions and examples of independent activities, authority or security engagement, and resolution or escalation of protection concerns.Promote meaningful participation of women, youth and groups facing heightened risks, and exchange learning across programme locations where appropriate.

**C. Engagement with Security and Armed Forces and Frontline Dialogue**

• Prepare communities, CPGs, authorities and security and armed forces for structured civil-military and community-security dialogue, including in frontline areas. Conduct separate consultations to prioritize concerns, agree discussion points and assess participation, confidentiality and retaliation risks.

• With CIVIC staff and CPGs, organize and facilitate safe, inclusive dialogue with security and armed forces, including commanders and liaison officers, supporting community representatives to raise concerns and agree practical civilian harm prevention and mitigation measures.

• Record commitments, focal points and timelines in an action tracker; follow up implementation with communities, authorities and forces, and provide community feedback. Maintain district, state and field-level security relationships under CIVIC protocols; support recurring dialogue, safe communication and PoC awareness with colleagues, raise emerging harm concerns and encourage improvements. Engagement must exclude operational intelligence gathering or sharing.

**D. Protection Concerns, Referrals and Follow-Up**

• Support safe identification, confidential documentation and records of protection concerns under CIVIC policies and programme approaches, avoiding unnecessary risks to community members.

• Help CPGs and Champions identify safe pathways to raise concerns with authorities, security and armed forces or other stakeholders. Support specialized referrals through established protection service providers, with informed consent and confidentiality, within CIVIC’s mandate and procedures.

• Follow up concerns, document actor responses and monitor unresolved issues requiring programme, advocacy or management attention.Immediately escalate sensitive, serious or urgent concerns through appropriate CIVIC channels.

**E. Monitoring Community Protection Systems**

• Monitor CPG and Champion functionality, effectiveness and progress toward independent leadership, including regular meetings, identification of concerns, action plans, decision-maker engagement and follow-up. Assess participation and representation of women, youth and other relevant groups, and identify additional mentoring, training or support needs.

• Maintain updated membership, Champion activity, community-led initiative and follow-up records; contribute to periodic reviews of functionality, sustainability and readiness for greater ownership or transition.

**F. Monitoring Outcomes, Evidence and Learning**

• Document changes from community engagement, CPG advocacy, workshops, dialogue and other interventions; track whether commitments change security-force practices, authority responses, community behaviour or other protection outcomes.

• Conduct or support focus groups, key informant interviews, perception surveys and other monitoring and learning activities. Collect feedback on intervention relevance and perceived changes in safety, access and relationships with authorities and security actors.

• Identify successful community-led approaches, recurring barriers and lessons for adaptation. With programme and monitoring colleagues, ensure accurate, documented evidence for decision-making, programme and donor reports, learning products and advocacy.

**G. Stakeholder Engagement and Coordination**

• Maintain constructive relationships and updated stakeholder mapping with community leaders, district and state government institutions, relevant security structures, civil society, women’s and youth groups, humanitarian and protection actors and other stakeholders.

• Safely connect CPGs and communities with appropriate stakeholders to address protection concerns; attend local coordination meetings when requested, provide timely programme feedback and support CIVIC and partner field missions.

**H. Programme Implementation and Reporting**

• Support activity planning and implementation with CPGs, Champions, communities and stakeholders, including logistical and administrative arrangements.

• Prepare timely activity reports, field updates and meeting notes; maintain accurate participant records, required sex- and age-disaggregated data, and a tracker of CPG activities, concerns, dialogue commitments, community-led actions and outstanding follow-up.

• Update the Community Engagement Officer on progress, emerging issues, stakeholder dynamics, risks and opportunities; contribute field evidence, outcomes, challenges and lessons to monthly, quarterly and donor reporting.

**I. Frontline Travel, Conflict Sensitivity, Safeguarding and Duty of Care**

• Apply conflict-sensitive, inclusive and do-no-harm approaches; maintain strict confidentiality and avoid exposing participants, CPG members or Champions to retaliation or other risks through engagement, documentation or advocacy.

• Avoid expectations or commitments outside CIVIC’s mandate or authority.Immediately report safeguarding, security and serious protection concerns through established procedures and comply with CIVIC’s Code of Conduct, safeguarding requirements and organizational policies.

• Coordinate travel with programme and security focal points, obtain clearance, follow approved movement, communication and check-in arrangements, and promptly report access or security changes. Postpone, relocate or suspend travel or dialogue when CIVIC procedures require it or participant safety cannot be adequately addressed.

4\. **Geographic Responsibilities**

Duty station: Baidoa. Geographic coverage: CIVIC programme locations across Bay, Bakool and Lower Shabelle, including Baidoa and Hudur, as prioritized by the Somalia programme. The Assistant will travel regularly from Baidoa to support community-based protection, engagement with relevant security and armed forces, and dialogue in conflict-affected and high-risk frontline locations.

Provide sustained accompaniment to CPGs and Champions across assigned locations; strengthen their ability to identify protection concerns, implement community protection action plans, lead PoC awareness activities, engage authorities and armed forces, and follow up on dialogue commitments. In Hudur and other locations, tailor mentoring to the capacity and needs of each community protection structure and promote progressive community ownership. Field visits and frontline activities require CIVIC authorization, security and access assessments, movement planning and compliance with duty-of-care procedures.

5\. **Qualifications and Experience**

• Bachelor's degree in social sciences, human rights, international relations, development studies or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

• Minimum 6 years of relevant experience in community engagement, protection, humanitarian, human rights or peacebuilding programming, preferably in Somalia or a comparable context.

• Demonstrated experience working with community-based structures or similar participatory community protection mechanisms.

• Familiarity with Protection of Civilians (PoC), civilian harm prevention and mitigation, community-based protection, and civil-military and community-security dialogue approaches. Experience working in frontline or other high-risk conflict environments is an asset.

• Demonstrated skills in community-based protection, inclusive facilitation, conflict-sensitive communication and community liaison, including experience engaging security and armed forces and facilitating dialogue with conflict-affected communities.

• Fluency in Somali required; working proficiency in English is essential.

• Willingness and ability to undertake regular field travel from the assigned duty station, including to high-risk frontline and conflict-affected locations, subject to CIVIC access conditions including travelling on road where necessary.

• Strong written and spoken communication skills, including experience preparing activity reports, meeting notes and field updates.

• Commitment to CIVIC's mandate and values, and to conflict-sensitive, inclusive and do-no-harm approaches.

7\. **Safeguarding and Code of Conduct**

CIVIC is committed to safeguarding the people it works with and maintains a zero-tolerance approach to sexual exploitation, abuse and harassment, and to any other conduct that undermines its mission. All offers of employment are subject to satisfactory references and background checks. The successful candidate will be required to sign and adhere to CIVIC's Code of Conduct and Safeguarding Policy.

**Additional Details**

**Application Deadline: October 29, 2026**

Due to the high volume of applications, only candidates selected for an interview will be contacted. ***Shortlisted candidates will receive an email invitation from TestGorilla to submit their resume. Please complete this step promptly to ensure your candidacy is fully considered.***

CIVIC is an Equal Opportunities Employer committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive environment, and does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, or any other protected characteristic.

Note to Recruiters and Placement Agencies: CIVIC does not accept unsolicited agency resumes and does not pay placement fees for candidates submitted by agencies other than its approved partners.
