title: Senior Specialist, MEAL – TCIS
body:
**Opportunity Type:**

Regular

**Summary:**

The Senior Specialist, MEAL provides senior technical MEAL expertise and support to Terwilliger Center for Innovation in Shelter (TCIS) projects across Southeast Asia, including the Philippines, Indonesia and Cambodia and to assigned regional programmes, including Housing Finance Systems (HFS) and Small and Growing Business (SGB).

Working towards HFHI’s One MEARL Vision, the Senior Specialist helps ensure agreed organisational standards, indicators, systems and practices are consistently applied and that evidence informs programme improvement and wider organisational learning.

**Key Responsibilities:**

## Essential Duties

- Lead the technical development and application of theories of change, results frameworks, MEAL plans, indicators and measurement approaches for projects, programmes and relevant proposal development, across the region
- Provide senior technical MEAL support, coaching and guidance across assigned projects in Southeast Asia, advising programme and project teams and promoting consistency and alignment across countries and programmes.
- Collaborate with programme and project teams to integrate MEAL requirements into project management, reporting and organisational systems throughout the programme or project lifecycle, in line with agreed structures and standards.
- Develop and review monitoring, data-collection, reporting and data-quality approaches and provide technical quality assurance to strengthen the reliability and use of programme evidence.
- Design and lead internal evaluations, assessments and applied research, and lead technical inputs to external evaluations, including development of scopes of work, review of methodologies and deliverables, and coordination with evaluators as required.
- Analyse and synthesise evidence across projects and programmes to identify trends, risks, learning and evidence gaps, and translate findings into practical recommendations for programme adaptation and decision-making.
- Facilitate reflection, learning and knowledge-sharing processes and contribute to learning agendas, evidence products and cross-country learning.
- Contribute technical expertise, evidence and learning from assigned projects to relevant Collective Impact Initiative workstreams, including advancement of the One MEARL vision, and support the application of agreed approaches

## Minimum Requirements

- Bachelor’s degree in international development, social sciences, economics, statistics, monitoring and evaluation or related field; postgraduate qualification preferred.
- 5+ years of progressive MEAL experience, including demonstrated technical experience across multiple countries or regional/complex programmes.
- Demonstrated experience developing theories of change, results frameworks, indicators and MEAL plans and applying qualitative and quantitative monitoring, research and evaluation methods, including evaluations, data-quality assurance, reporting and evidence synthesis.
- Strong analytical, project management, facilitation and communication skills, with the ability to independently manage complex technical assignments and work effectively across countries, cultures and functions.
- Knowledge of current MEAL practice, including accountability, safeguarding, participatory approaches and relevant data collection/analysis tools.
- Proficiency with relevant data-collection, analysis and visualisation tools, including Excel and tools such as Power BI or Tableau.
- Knowledge of current MEAL practice, including accountability, safeguarding and participatory approaches.

## Preferred Requirements

- Experience in market systems development, housing, housing finance, financial inclusion, private-sector development or related programming.
- Familiarity with systemic MEAL approaches for market systems development.
- Experience working with enterprises, small and growing businesses (SGBs), or innovation programmes.
- Familiarity with impact investment metrics, enterprise performance measures and basic financial analysis.
- Experience with applied research, accountability and feedback mechanisms, and capacity strengthening.

**About Us:**

Habitat for Humanity, founded in 1976, is a global, Christian-based nonprofit organization that grew out of an intentionally multi-racial community in rural Georgia. Seeking to put God’s love into action, Habitat brings together people of all faiths and people of no faith to build homes, communities and hope. Working alongside each other, we help families and individuals build and improve places to call home and achieve the strength, stability and self-reliance they need to build better lives for themselves. Habitat seeks individuals who have a willingness to affirm these principles and values.

At Habitat for Humanity International, we are compelled by our Koinonia roots to put God’s love for all into action and pursue housing equity and opportunity by bringing all people together to build community and drive impact. We strive to build a culture rooted in learning, accountability and trust, attracting and retaining mission-driven talent reflective of the global communities we serve.

**Equal Opportunity Employer Statement:**

As an equal opportunity employer, we realize our success depends on courageously committing to being a workplace where all staff feel safe, welcome, visible, respected, supported and valued, and building a workforce that reflects a variety of lived experiences, backgrounds and perspectives, in which every person experiences dignity and respect.

title: Group Cash Transfer (Cash & Markets) Manager Sudan (Open for Sudanese only_Internals will be assessed before externals)
body:
**Background:**

We are seeking a skilled and experienced Group Cash Transfer (GCT) Manager to oversee and manage all aspects of our Group Cash Transfer programmes. Within the Cash & Market thematic team, the GCT Manager will be responsible for designing, implementing, and monitoring group cash transfer initiatives in collaboration with Core Competency Specialists and local stakeholders, including Emergency Response Rooms, CBOs, NGOs and community partners.

The ideal candidate will have strong leadership, project management and financial management skills, along with a deep understanding of humanitarian principles and best practices in cash transfer programming.

**What you will do:**

1. **Programme Design and Planning**

- Lead the design and development of group cash transfer programmes, ensuring alignment with organisational goals and objectives.
- In consultation with stakeholders and line management, conduct assessments and analysis to identify target communities and beneficiaries, as well as their specific needs and preferences.
- Collaborate with stakeholders to develop detailed implementation plans, timelines and budgets for programme activities.

**2. Partnership Management**

- Identify and establish partnerships with local Emergency Response Rooms (ERRs), NGOs, community-based organisations (CBOs), government agencies and other relevant stakeholders.
- Build and maintain strong relationships with Area Managers, Area Program Managers, Core Competency (CC) Specialists, partners, and stakeholders, ensuring effective communication, collaboration and coordination throughout programme implementation.
- Provide technical guidance and support to partners in the planning, implementation, and monitoring of group cash transfer activities.

**3. Programme Implementation**

- Oversee the implementation of group cash transfer programmes, ensuring adherence to programme design, standards, and protocols.
- Coordinate with internal and external stakeholders to facilitate programme activities, including fund transfers, beneficiary registration, cash distribution and monitoring.
- Monitor programme progress and performance, identify challenges and opportunities, and take corrective action as needed to achieve programme objectives.
- Coordinate with the M&E unit and CC Specialists on building and regularly updating the Capacity Building Programme targeting local responders.

**4. Financial Management**

- Develop and manage programme budgets, ensuring accurate forecasting, expenditure tracking, and compliance with the internal standards of the Risk and Compliance section, donor requirements and financial regulations.
- Monitor cash flow processes and financial transactions related to group cash transfer activities and ensure timely and efficient use of funds.

**5. Training, Capacity Building and Awareness Raising**

- Develop training materials and resources for programme staff, partners and community members on group cash transfer methodologies, financial management and programme implementation.
- Deliver training sessions and capacity-building activities, ensuring that participants have the skills and knowledge to implement and manage group cash transfer programmes effectively.
- Conduct awareness-raising campaigns and community engagement activities to promote understanding of group cash transfer programmes, encourage participation, and address potential misconceptions or concerns.

**6. Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning**

- Develop and implement monitoring and evaluation plans to assess programme effectiveness, efficiency, and impact.
- Collect and analyse data on programme outputs and outcomes, and use findings to inform programme adjustments and improvements.
- Facilitate learning and knowledge sharing among programme staff, partners and stakeholders to promote continuous improvement and innovation.

**7. Project Staff Management**

- Supervise, coach and mentor project staff, ensuring clear roles, workplans and performance objectives, and conduct regular performance reviews.
- Plan and allocate staff across projects and locations, including Country Office, Areas Offices in Darfurs, Kordofans.
- Support recruitment, onboarding and professional development of project staff, and identify capacity gaps and training needs.
- Foster a safe, respectful, and collaborative team environment, ensuring staff adherence to NRC policies, code of conduct and safety and security protocols.
- Hold regular team meetings and coordinate with Finance, Logistics, HR and M&E colleagues.

**What you will bring:**

- Bachelor's degree in international development, humanitarian assistance, social sciences or a related field (Master's degree preferred).
- Minimum 3 Years of experience in humanitarian or development work. Including Managing, Coordinating and implementing Projects with CVA (Cash and Voucher Programming) Component.
- Proven experience in project management, including programme design, planning, implementation and monitoring.
- Strong financial management skills, including budgeting, financial analysis and compliance.
- Excellent communication, negotiation and interpersonal skills, with the ability to work effectively with diverse stakeholders.
- Knowledge of humanitarian principles, standards and best practices in cash transfer programming.
- Fluency in Arabic and English (written and spoken) is required.
- Ability to work independently, under pressure and with minimal guidance, in a challenging and dynamic environment.
- Commitment to the organisation's mission, vision and values.

- **What we offer:**
- Duty station: Al-Geniena, Darfur
- Contract: 12 Months (renewable based on funding and performance)
- Salary/benefits: grade 8 on NRC’s **national** salary scale.
- NRC is an equal opportunities employer. We are committed to diversity without distinction to age, gender, religion, ethnicity, nationality, and physical ability.
- We think outside the box, encourage ideas, and give responsibility to all employees at all levels. You will have many opportunities to be heard and take the initiative.

[Find out more about the benefits of working for NRC](https://www.nrc.no/career/what-we-offer/)

Important information about the application process

- *For Internal candidates: To apply as an internal candidate, log in with your official email or click on Opportunity MarketPlace.*
- When creating your profile, include your full name as given on your passport. Complete all the system-required fields for experience, employment history and education.
- Applicants who do not fill in the required information will not be considered for the role.
- Submit your application and CV in English, taking care to attach your latest CV.
- Applications that do not meet the minimum standards in terms of experience or qualifications will generally not be considered. Unsolicited applications not related to this specific job advertisement will not be considered.
- Mandatory to submit the below when applying:
    - **Your most updated English CV and remove all previous outdated CVs.**
    - **Your most updated Cover Letter**
    - **Do not attach certificates or any other documents apart from the two mentioned above.**
    - **Incomplete applications will not be considered.**
- **This position is open for national candidates who have the legal right to work in Sudan. NRC will not sponsor visa nor residency.**
- **Internal national candidates will be assessed before externals.**
- We receive many applications for each vacant position. Therefore, only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.
- If you have any questions about this role, please email **esa.recruitment@nrc.no**with the job title as the subject line.

**Why NRC?**

The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) is an independent humanitarian organisation helping people forced to flee. Our 15,000 staff work in crises across 40 countries, providing life-saving and long-term assistance to millions of people every year.

[Watch this short video](https://vimeo.com/736782633) to see NRC in action.

We are looking for people who are passionate about helping refugees and people forced to flee. Are you one of those people? If you are, NRC offers you the opportunity to:

At NRC, we give responsibility to employees at all levels and foster professional growth and innovative teams. You can expect a supportive culture and an open dialogue with management. We are committed to diversity, equity and inclusion.

title: PRF33834 Request for Proposals to Conduct Baseline Evaluation Strengthening Gender and Disability-Inclusive Climate Action in Bungoma County(Phase II)
body:
[https://kenyaredcross-my.sharepoint.com/:b:/g/personal/tenders_redcross_or_ke/IQADcP_o5VapSLdp7-4uz8sKAeF9zakl_iM0GTydw1Ty7YM?e=BeQ06q](https://kenyaredcross-my.sharepoint.com/:b:/g/personal/tenders_redcross_or_ke/IQADcP_o5VapSLdp7-4uz8sKAeF9zakl_iM0GTydw1Ty7YM?e=BeQ06q)

**Request for Proposals to Conduct**

**Baseline Evaluation**

**Strengthening Gender and Disability-Inclusive Climate Action in Bungoma County (Phase II)**

**Document Release Date: 14/10/2026**

**Last Date for Receipt of Proposals: 28/10/2026**

**Time: 11:00 HRS**

**Tender Number: PRF33834**

**Submission Method: email to tenders@redcross.or.ke**

**Tender Opening Venue and Time: Virtually via Microsoft Teams at 1200hrs**

1. **Summary of the baseline survey**
    1. **Purpose**:

The baseline evaluation aims to establish the benchmark statistics for the project “Strengthening Gender and Disability-Inclusive Climate Action in Bungoma County” (Phase II), a new phase of the Kenya Red Cross Society (KRCS)/CBM Global “Promoting Inclusive Climate Change Resilience in Bungoma County” project (Phase I). It will document the current situation of target communities, including persons with disabilities, women, youth and other marginalized groups, against the Phase II results framework, validate the relevance and measurability of the log frame indicators and targets, and provide a robust reference point against which the project's future mid-term review and end-term evaluation will measure change.

**Partners**

CBM Global Disability Inclusion (CBM Global), Kenya Red Cross Society (KRCS), Disability Empowerment Network (DEN), National Government, Bungoma County Government and relevant departments (Directorate of Climate Change, Ministry of Water, Tourism, Environment and Natural Resources, Ministry of Youth, Gender and Social Development, Ministry of Health, Ministry of Labor and Social Protection, National Council for Persons with Disabilities (NCPWD), Association for Persons with Disability Kenya (APDK), Kenya Meteorological Department, Organizations of Persons with Disabilities (OPDs)).

**Duration**

35 days

**Estimated Dates**

5/11/2026 – 9/12/2026

**Geographical Location**

Bungoma County, Kenya - focusing on Tongaren, Bumula and Webuye East sub-counties

**Target Population**

Persons with disabilities (men, women, boys and girls), women- and youth-headed households, older persons, indigenous and other marginalized community members, Organizations of Persons with Disabilities (OPDs), Ward Climate Committees, Village Savings and Loan Association (VSLA)/self-help groups, County and Sub-County Government departments (climate change, disaster management, health, social protection), and Kenya Red Cross Society/DEN staff and volunteers.

**Deliverables**

Inception report and tools, cleaned datasets and codebook, draft and final baseline report, PowerPoint presentation, dissemination/validation workshop, and an easy-read version of the report.

**Methodology**

Mixed methods - quantitative and qualitative, disability- and gender-inclusive data collection approaches.

**Evaluation Management Team**

KRCS MEA&L team, KRCS Project representatives, and CBM Global representative(s).

1. **Background Information**

Climate Change is a threat to the development of the global economy and the greatest impediment to the achievement of sustainable development goals. Current global weather extremes affect millions of people, resulting in food and water insecurity in addition to affecting agricultural productivity. In Kenya, Climate Change has resulted in extreme weather events that have led to loss of lives, reduced agricultural productivity, displacement of populations, and destruction of infrastructure, among other adverse impacts. Bungoma County has also not been spared, with increased cases of flooding, landslides, and drought resulting in displacement of people, damage to infrastructure and low agricultural yields.

According to the 2019 Kenya census report, an estimated 40,186 persons with disabilities live in Bungoma County, representing 2.4% of the population. This population continues to face disproportionate risks due to structural barriers such as limited access to climate information, restricted mobility, limited access to services, and exclusion from planning and decision-making spaces at community and county levels. Barriers to their full participation in society prior to disasters and other emergencies tend to be exacerbated by climate-related hazards, and failure to consult persons with disabilities and their representative organizations in the development of plans to respond to emergencies increases their risks and vulnerabilities.

With support from and in partnership with CBM Global, Kenya Red Cross Society implemented a 3-year project dubbed “Promoting Inclusive Climate Change Resilience in Bungoma County” (Phase I, 2023-2025) in Cheptais, Kopsiro and Bungoma South (Kanduyi) sub-counties. Phase I demonstrated the feasibility and value of disability-inclusive climate action: it empowered more than 800 persons with disabilities to participate in climate resilience processes and reached over 20,000 community members through early warning dissemination, climate-smart livelihood activities, and community-led advocacy.

The Phase I end of project findings informed the design of Phase II, reflecting the learnings the results and the current needs. Building on the achievements, lessons and gaps identified under Phase I, KRCS and CBM Global have designed a new phase - “Strengthening Gender and Disability-Inclusive Climate Action in Bungoma County” (Phase II, 1st July 2026 - 31st December 2028) - implemented by KRCS as lead implementing partner in partnership with the Disability Empowerment Network (DEN) as the primary sub-partner. The project will be implemented in Tongaren, Bumula and Webuye east sub-counties. Phase II adopts a rights-based, gender-responsive, disability-inclusive, and community-led approach that tackles the root causes of vulnerability while enhancing adaptive capacities. It combines: strengthened Inclusive Early Warning and Early Action (EWEA) systems using multiple, accessible communication channels for different disability groups; climate-smart livelihood interventions targeting women, youth, and persons with disabilities, including underrepresented and indigenous communities; capacity building of county institutions and community structures to institutionalize inclusive climate governance; and integration of Mental Health and Psychosocial Support (MHPSS) to address the emotional and social impacts of climate-related stressors.

As the project design form notes that a baseline assessment is planned within the first quarter of project implementation, this baseline survey is required to establish reliable starting values for the Phase II log frame indicators, sharpen the theory of change, and inform the Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and Learning (MEA&L) plan to be finalized within three months of project commencement.

1. **Project Objectives**

Overall Project Goal: To reduce the impacts of climate-related risks for communities by strengthening their capacity for preparedness, early action, and inclusive disaster risk management, while ensuring full participation and protection of persons with disabilities and other at-risk groups.

- Specific Objective 1: To strengthen the ability of at-risk communities to apply inclusive, climate-adaptive approaches and engage in advocacy mechanisms that enhance their participation and resilience to climate-related shocks.
- Specific Objective 2: To improve adaptive livelihoods, access to services, and social protection for persons with disabilities and at-risk households.
- Specific Objective 3: To strengthen evidence generation, advocacy and learning for inclusive climate action.

1. **Key Project Stakeholders**

The project is implemented in close coordination with the National and Bungoma County Governments and their departments, including the Directorate of Climate Change, the Ministry of Water, Tourism, Environment and Natural Resources, the Ministry of Youth, Gender and Social Development, the Ministry of Health (rehabilitation and physiotherapy departments), the Ministry of Labor and Social Protection, the National Council for Persons with Disabilities (NCPWD), the Kenya Meteorological Department, and the Association for Persons with Disability Kenya (APDK).

Key implementing partners are Kenya Red Cross Society (KRCS), as lead implementing partner, and the Disability Empowerment Network (DEN), as primary sub-partner. The project also works with Organizations of Persons with Disabilities (OPDs), Ward Climate Committees, women-led organizations, grassroots community structures, VSLA/self-help groups, and National Government Administrative Officers. At the regional/global level, the project engages with the Early Warnings for All (EW4ALL) pillar leads (UNDRR, NDOC, WMO, ITU, CA, IFRC, KRCS).

1. **Baseline survey Purpose & Scope**
    1. **Purpose.**

The baseline survey aims to establish the current status of the target population and systems against each Phase II log frame indicator, ahead of project implementation. It will provide a credible evidence base against which project progress and impact will be measured at mid-term and end-term.

The baseline survey will establish the pre-intervention values for the Phase II log frame indicators in Tongaren, Webuye East and Bumula sub-counties. These values form the benchmark against which change will be measured at mid-term and end-term. The survey will also confirm that the indicators, targets and monitoring arrangements are realistic and measurable, so that the project can track and demonstrate its results from the start.

1. To establish baseline values for key project outcome and output indicators, including climate-related risks, community adaptive capacity and existing resilience practices across the three sub-counties.
2. To assess community perceptions and experiences of participation, disability inclusion, feedback, accountability and safeguarding mechanisms, and identify key gaps.
3. To identify priority project risks, assumptions and monitoring requirements that may affect implementation and achievement of results.
4. To provide practical recommendations to refine programme targeting, implementation, monitoring and learning.
5. **Key Questions**

The consultant will develop key questions to enable the baseline survey to generate the information needed on the project's starting context and indicators. The following are proposed key questions; the consultant may suggest changes/additional questions at the inception stage:

**Baseline values and indicators**

- What are the baseline values for each Phase II log frame indicator?
- Are the current indicators and targets realistic, measurable, and appropriately disaggregated (sex, age, disability, geography)?
- What data sources and collection methods are most appropriate for tracking each indicator going forward?

**Context and needs analysis**

- What is the current level of climate risk awareness, preparedness, and early warning access among target communities, disaggregated by gender and disability?
- What livelihood strategies do households, including persons with disabilities, currently use, and how climate-adaptive are they?
- What is the current status of VSLA/self-help groups, microenterprises, and access to rehabilitation and assistive devices in the target areas?
- What is the level of functioning of Ward Climate Committees, DRM coordination platforms, and OPD engagement in county governance processes?

**Capacity assessment**

- What is the current institutional and technical capacity of KRCS, DEN, OPDs, and county departments to deliver and monitor a disability-inclusive climate resilience project?
- Key MEA&L capacity gaps within DEN that require strengthening to enable DEN to meaningfully support MEA&L functions within the project.

**Community Engagement, Accountability and Safeguarding**

- What complaints and feedback mechanisms currently exist in the target communities, and how accessible are they to persons with disabilities?
- What safeguarding risks (including GBV, exploitation, and exclusion of persons with intellectual or psychosocial disabilities) are present in the target context, and what systems currently exist to mitigate them?
- To what extent are community members, including persons with disabilities and women, currently involved in decision-making processes relevant to climate resilience?

**Gender and Disability Inclusion**

- What specific barriers do women, men, persons with disabilities (by type), youth and older persons currently face in accessing climate information, livelihoods, and services?
- How are gender relations, decision-making power, and leadership currently distributed within target communities and OPDs?

**Risks and Assumptions**

- Are the key assumptions in the log frame (e.g. continued institutional commitment, market functionality, community adoption of livelihood diversification) currently valid in the project context?
- What additional risks (climate, security, political, or operational) should be considered in the project's risk register?

1. **Survey Methodology**

The consultant will be expected to propose the most appropriate study design, sampling methods, sample size, and data collection and analysis approaches for the baseline survey. These should be clearly outlined in the bidding document/proposal and will be further discussed with the assessment management team if the firm qualifies for the oral stage. The firm should identify and justify the target respondents or data sources that can effectively address the log frame indicators. The proposed methodology should incorporate triangulation of findings and ensure an adequate, representative sample of the target beneficiaries, with clearly defined sampling procedures, disaggregated by sex, age, and disability status (using, for example, the Washington Group Questions).

All log frame indicators should be given operational definitions in the bid submission. A detailed data analysis plan should also be included, indicating how each indicator will be analyzed, and how baseline values will be presented and structured to allow direct comparison at mid-term and end-term.

Additional documents that can be used during the baseline survey include the following, in additional to any other relevant documents/literature to inform the survey process:

- Phase I End-Term Evaluation report and Phase I project reports.
- Phase II project design form, theory of change, and log frame.
- Phase II project risk register and safeguarding risk assessment.
- Existing needs assessments and contextual analyses for Bungoma County.
- Documents, policies and frameworks by partners, county and national government (e.g. Bungoma County Integrated Development Plan (CIDP) 2023-2027, Kenya Climate Change Act 2016, National Climate Change Action Plan (NCCAP) 2023-2027, Disability Inclusion Policy).

The project's Overall Objective, Specific Objectives and Results-level indicators are shown in the table below:

**Hierarchy of Objectives**

**Objectively Verifiable Indicators (OVI)**

**Overall Objective (Impact):**

**Strengthened disability-inclusive, gender-responsive, and community-led climate resilience systems in Bungoma County.**

**Specific Objective 1 (Outcome):**

**Communities at risk of climate shocks in Bungoma County apply inclusive coping, early warning, and advocacy mechanisms that reduce vulnerability and strengthen resilience.**

% of supported communities implementing inclusive early warning and coping mechanisms. (Survey reports)

% of persons with disability, women, and marginalized persons accessing and responding to early warning information. (Surveys)

% of supported households reporting diversified and climate-adaptive livelihoods (Surveys)

**Result 1.1 (output):**

**Coping mechanisms of communities at risk of climate shocks are strengthened.**

Number of Ward Climate Committees applying disability- and gender-inclusive planning.

Number of at risk households supported with inclusive climate-adaptive livelihoods.

Number of strengthened VSLA groups which are functional.

**Result 1.2 (output):**

**Participatory, community-led Early Warning Early Action (EWEA) systems accessible to all (including persons with disabilities) are strengthened.**

% of persons with disabilities reporting access to timely and understandable early warning information.

Number of functional DRM coordination platforms at ward, sub-county and county levels. Baseline (Phase I):

Number of persons accessing rehabilitation, assistive devices and referral services.

**Result 1.3 (output):**

**Strengthened gender, age and disability-inclusive climate governance through OPD-led advocacy.**

Number of OPDs actively participating in county climate and DRM governance processes.

Number of OPD-led advocacy initiatives on inclusive climate action.

Number of county plans, policies or processes influenced by OPD advocacy.

**Result 1.4 (Output**

**Project accountability, safeguarding, monitoring and learning systems strengthened.**

Number of joint monitoring visits conducted.

% of beneficiaries reporting satisfaction with project services.

Number of learning and advocacy products developed.

**Specific Objective 2 (Outcome):**

**Improve adaptive livelihoods, access to services, and social protection for persons with disabilities and at-risk households.**

% of targeted households demonstrating improved income and livelihood diversification.

% of people (persons with disabilities/women) reporting increased access to social protection or adaptive livelihood schemes.

Number of persons with disabilities, women, and marginalized persons engaged in climate-smart livelihood initiatives.

**Result 2.1 (Output):**

**Persons with disabilities, women and other marginalized groups have improved access to adaptive, climate-smart livelihoods and initiatives.**

Number of livelihood interventions designed with inclusive adaptation measures.

Average household income of participants.

Number of persons with disabilities, women, and marginalized persons participating in climate-smart livelihood projects.

**Result 2.2 (Output):**

**Rehabilitation and assistive technology services are scaled up and linked to livelihood and resilience initiatives.**

Number of livelihood initiatives integrating access to rehabilitation or assistive services.

Number of beneficiaries accessing assistive devices to support participation in livelihood activities.

Number of partnerships established between service providers and livelihood programmes.

**Result 2.3 (Output):**

1. **Quality & Ethical Standards**

The consultant shall take all reasonable steps to ensure that the survey is designed and conducted to respect and protect the rights and welfare of the people and communities involved and to ensure that the assessment is technically accurate and reliable, is conducted in a transparent and impartial manner, and contributes to organizational learning and accountability. Therefore, the survey team shall be required to adhere to the assessment standards and applicable practices as recommended by the International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies.

- **Utility:** Assessments must be useful and used.
- **Feasibility:** Assessments must be realistic, diplomatic, and managed in a sensible, cost-effective manner.
- **Ethics & Legality:** Assessments must be conducted ethically and legally, with regard for the welfare of those involved in and affected by the assessment.
- **Impartiality & Independence:** Assessments should be impartial, providing a comprehensive and unbiased assessment that considers the views of all stakeholders.
- **Transparency:** Assessment activities should reflect an attitude of openness and transparency.
- **Accuracy:** Assessments should be technically accurate, providing sufficient information about the data collection, analysis, and interpretation methods so that its worth or merit can be determined.
- **Participation:** Stakeholders should be consulted and meaningfully involved in the assessment process when feasible and appropriate.
- **Collaboration:** Collaboration between key operating partners in the assessment process improves the legitimacy and utility of the assessment.
- **Inclusion:** The assessment must include clear steps to ensure meaningful engagement and participation of all sections of the community, including persons with disabilities and women.

It is also expected that the assessment will respect the seven Fundamental Principles of the Red Cross and Red Crescent: 1) humanity, 2) impartiality, 3) neutrality, 4) independence, 5) voluntary service, 6) unity and 7) universality.

1. **Qualifications and Experience for Consultants**

1. A minimum of a master’s degree in Public Health/climate change and adaptation/environmental science and Environmental studies/disaster risk management & disaster preparedness/sustainable development/development studies/project planning and management/Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) or Applied Researchor related field.
2. A minimum of 5 years’ extensive experience in carrying out comprehensive baselines or similar assignments.
3. Good understanding of climate change and climate-related risks, with demonstrated expertise in mainstreaming gender equality, disability inclusion, and age considerations among vulnerable populations in Kenya.
4. Proven experience in participatory and results-based M&E knowledge and practical experience in quantitative and qualitative research methods.
5. Must have led at least five participatory assessments. Experience of conducting evaluations, monitoring and assessment work in the target or similar communities (preferred).
6. High level of professionalism and an ability to work independently and in high-pressure situations under tight deadlines.
7. Strong interpersonal, facilitation, and communication skills
8. The team must have a statistician able to analyze quantitative and qualitative data, as well as key technical team members to handle specific components of the project baseline.
9. The team must have experience in participatory data collection methods and using mobile phone technology for data collection, monitoring and reporting.
10. The lead consultant must have strong analytical skills and the ability to clearly synthesize and present findings, draw practical conclusions, make recommendations, and to prepare well-written reports in a timely manner.
11. Availability for the period indicated and ready to carry out the assignment and deliver results within the specified period/time.
12. Proven track record of integrating gender-responsive and disability-inclusive approaches in baseline surveys, including demonstrated ability to capture the perspectives of women, men, youth, and persons with disabilities through appropriate participatory methods.

Availability of experts in each of the subject areas, with experience and relevant qualifications for the assignment, will be highly preferred.

title: Financial Planning & Analysis Advisor
body:
**Selection Criteria:** The Financial Planning and Analysis Advisor position is open to candidates residing in countries where Medical Teams International can legally employ staff, either directly or through an approved third-party Employer of Record (EOR). To support collaboration with global teams, candidates must be located within the UTC-8 to UTC+3 time zone range.

The Financial Planning and Analysis Advisor contributes to the calling of Medical Teams International by providing financial and business analytics support to drive financial planning and help make informed business decisions. This senior level role serves as a strategic business partner to executive and departmental leadership by providing forward-looking financial insights, enterprise performance analytics, and decision-support tools that optimize organizational resources and advance strategic priorities. The Financial Planning and Analysis Advisor leads organization-wide forecasting, scenario planning, performance measurement, and financial modeling activities to support sustainable growth, operational effectiveness, and mission impact.

**Medical Teams International Calling:**

Daring to love like Jesus, we boldly break barriers to health and restore wholeness in a hurting world.

Medical Teams International holds strict child and vulnerable adult safeguarding principles and a zero tolerance policy for misconduct related to sexual harassment, exploitation and abuse in the workplace and other places where the organization’s activities are rendered. Parallel to technical competence, recruitment & selection, hiring decisions will give due emphasis to assessing candidates’ eligibility, thorough background checks, police clearance, and professional reference check processes.

**ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES**

**Reporting and Analysis**

- Manage the financial planning and analysis (FP&A) process. This includes financial reporting, creating various financial metrics and dashboards, and scenario and predictive modeling.
- Lead indirect cost rate calculations and create cost recovery models across all business units.
- Prepare reports for Negotiated Indirect Cost Rate Agreement (NICRA).
- Develop and report monthly, quarterly, and annual metrics pertaining to departmental efficiencies, cost recovery, labor optimization, revenue, etc.
- Review, analyze, and distribute financial reports to budget holders and support interpretation of financial results.
- Create presentations for senior and executive management that provide insightful analysis, identify required action items, and effectively frame decisions to be made.
- Identify and research discrepancies and variances to forecast, budget, and prior-year and proactively identify opportunities for improvement across the enterprise
- Develop and maintain multi-year financial forecasts and strategic planning models to support organizational sustainability and growth initiatives.
- Establish and monitor enterprise key performance indicators (KPIs) and operational scorecards aligned with strategic objectives.
- Lead financial scenario analyses and sensitivity modeling to support executive decision-making, risk assessment, and resource prioritization.
- Partner with Development, Global Programs, and Executive Leadership to analyze funding trends, grant pipelines, donor concentration risks, and revenue sustainability.
- Prepare financial and operational analyses for executive leadership, Board committees, and senior management meetings.

**Budget**

- Oversee and coordinate data collection and input feeding into the annual global budget process.
- Create guidance documentation, and templates for budget holders, budget models for decision making, prior year analysis, current year projections plus providing budget system support and training.
- Identify foreign exchange exposure to include monitoring, reporting, and hedging as appropriate during annual budget and reforecasting cycle.
- Reconcile budget revisions and manage budgets in the ERP system. Input the finance department budget into the ERP system while offering educational assistance to other departments as needed.
- Lead quarterly reforecasting and rolling forecast processes across the organization.
- Evaluate investment proposals, staffing requests, and strategic initiatives through financial analysis and business case development.
- Partner with departmental leaders to identify opportunities for operational efficiency, cost optimization, and resource alignment.

**ERP and Financial Systems Support**

- Serve as a Finance ERP champion and the primary focal point for coaching, support and troubleshooting.
- Identify opportunities for financial process improvements by leveraging the ERP platform and other modules alongside the IS department.
- Develop training material and facilitate knowledge sharing and training on the use of digital tools for budget and reporting evaluations.
- Lead finance data governance initiatives to ensure consistency, integrity, and reliability of enterprise financial data.
- Collaborate with Information Systems to expand business intelligence capabilities through dashboards, automated reporting, and advanced analytics tools.
- Identify and implement automation opportunities to reduce manual effort and improve financial reporting efficiency.

**Other Duties**

- Support safeguarding of program participants and employees through promoting an environment of awareness and upholding the code of conduct provisions of Medical Teams Protection from Sexual Exploitation, Abuse & Harassment, Child & Vulnerable Adult protection, and harassment-free workplace policies. Incumbents will remain alert and responsive to any child and adult safeguarding risks, acquire relevant knowledge and skills which will enable you to promote strong safeguarding practices, understand the child and adult safeguarding policy and procedures, and conduct yourself in a manner consistent with the Safeguarding code of conduct and behavior expectations.
- Support the Finance department as needed, while having a line of sight into the financial metrics and performance of Philanthropy, Marketing & Mobilization, Global Programs, and Executive Management.
- Facilitate cross-functional financial reviews and business performance discussions with organizational leaders.
- Support enterprise risk assessment activities by identifying financial, operational, and funding risks and recommending mitigation strategies.
- Participate in organizational transformation initiatives and support change management efforts related to finance systems, processes, and reporting.
- Participate in and support strategic projects as requested.
- Utilize volunteers when appropriate.
- Additional duties as assigned.

## **Qualifications**

**EDUCATION, LICENSE & CERTIFICATIONS**

**Required:**

- Bachelor’s degree in finance, accounting, business, economics, or closely related fields
- Valid passport

**Preferred:**

- Master’s degree and/or finance/accounting related certification
- Certified Corporate FP&A Professional (FPAC), CPA, CMA, CGMA, CFA, or equivalent professional designation
- Training or certification in business intelligence, data analytics, or financial systems administration

**EXPERIENCE**

**Required:**

- Minimum 6 years’ relevant experience in an NGO context
- 4 years’ financial planning, analysis, and non-profit budgeting experience
- 4 years’ indirect cost rate / NICRA modeling and reporting
- Prior experience in public accounting, audit, data analytics, business operations or relevant field
- Experience with Power BI, Tableau, Adaptive Planning, Workday Adaptive, or equivalent platforms
- Experience leading process improvement, automation, or finance transformation initiatives

**KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS & ABILITIES**

**Knowledge:**

- US-GAAP
- Non-profit financial statements and corporate finance reports
- Financial planning, forecasting, budgeting, and variance analysis principles
- Nonprofit accounting, restricted funding, grant budgeting, and donor compliance
- Indirect cost allocation, cost recovery, and NICRA principles
- ERP-based financial reporting and data structures
- Internal controls, financial policies, and audit-ready documentation practice
- Strategic planning and enterprise performance management frameworks
- Business intelligence, data governance, and analytics best practices
- Financial risk assessment and scenario planning techniques

**Skills:**

- Spreadsheet proficiency
- Data manipulation
- Data visualization
- Building business, operational, or financial reports
- Financial modeling from multiple data sources
- Strategic financial analysis and decision support
- Long-range financial planning and enterprise forecasting
- ERP/NetSuite, expense management systems, and Microsoft Office
- Facilitation and stakeholder management
- Data visualization and storytelling
- Exceptional communication skills, especially with executive and non-financial audiences

**Abilities:**

- Commitment to Medical Teams International Calling statement and Values
- Ability to manage multiple and shifting priorities while meeting deadlines
- Strong ability to analyze details, identify issues, and communicate with courage
- Strong Ability to learn new technologies quickly
- Ability to navigate complex business environments
- Ability to work proactively and collaboratively
- Ability to communicate difficult or detailed issues with courage
- Ability to translate complex financial information into actionable insights for executive and non-financial audiences
- Ability to think strategically while maintaining operational excellence
- Ability to influence organizational decision-making through data-driven recommendations
- Ability to lead change initiatives and drive adoption of new processes and technologies
- Ability to anticipate emerging financial and operational challenges and proactively recommend solutions

**Compensation:**

The anticipated hiring range for this position is **$86,000-$92,000 USD annually**. Final compensation will be determined based on the selected candidate's qualifications, relevant experience, internal equity considerations, and geographic location.

While the salary range listed applies to candidates residing in the United States, compensation for candidates located outside the U.S. will be determined using Medical Teams International's international compensation framework and may vary based on local market conditions and organizational compensation practices.

title: Monitoring and Evaluation Advisor
body:
## About the Role

All Hands and Hearts is seeking an experienced Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) Advisor to build and lead the monitoring, evaluation, accountability and learning systems for its humanitarian response in Gaza. Operating in a fast-changing environment with constrained access, AHAH needs reliable, timely evidence on what is reaching communities, what is working, and where programs must adapt. The successful candidate will focus primarily on nutrition Monitoring and Evaluation, ensure quality data collection and reporting to leadership and donors, and put in place mechanisms that let affected communities give feedback and hold the organization accountable.

## Key Responsibilities

- **M&E Systems and Frameworks:** Design and roll out AHAH's M&E framework for Gaza nutrition program, including results frameworks, data collection and analysis, indicator reference sheets and performance monitoring plans aligned with donor requirements and cluster standards.
- **Distribution and Commodity Monitoring:** Establish post-distribution monitoring, commodity tracking and verification processes to confirm that AHAH assistance reaches intended civilian beneficiaries, and flag diversion or access risks to leadership.
- **Data Collection and Management:** Develop data collection tools and lead the use of mobile data platforms; ensure data quality, security, beneficiary data protection and safe storage.
- **Assessments and Evaluations:** Lead or support needs assessments, baseline and endline surveys, and periodic program reviews; manage external evaluations where required.
- **Reporting and Learning:** Produce timely, accurate reports and dashboards for AHAH leadership and donors; document lessons learned and use findings to guide program adaptation.
- **Coordination:** Represent AHAH in inter-agency information management and assessment working groups; contribute data to cluster reporting, as appropriate.
- **Capacity Building:** Train and mentor field staff, on M&E methods, data collection and ethical data practices.
- **Resource Mobilization:** Contribute M&E plans, indicators and budgets to proposals for institutional and private donors.

## Qualifications & Experience

- Master's degree in Monitoring and Evaluation, Statistics, Public Health, Development Studies, Social Sciences, or a related field.
- Minimum 8–10 years of M&E experience, including at least 5 years in humanitarian or emergency settings.
- Demonstrated expertise in designing M&E systems, quantitative and qualitative methods, and donor reporting.
- Proficiency with mobile data collection platforms and data analysis tools
- Excellent analytical, communication and report-writing skills.
- Language requirements: Fluency in Arabic and English (written and spoken).
- Candidates must be willing to undergo a thorough background and security check prior to a final offer. Must demonstrate commitment to neutrality and community service.

## Salary

This is an 18-month, fixed-term contract/consultancy with compensation that will be competitive based on experience and location.

title: Senior Nutrition Advisor
body:
All Hands and Hearts is seeking an experienced Senior Nutrition Advisor to lead the design, delivery and quality of its emergency nutrition programming in Gaza. Acute malnutrition among children under five and pregnant and lactating women has risen sharply amid prolonged conflict, displacement and severe restrictions on food access. The successful candidate will provide technical leadership on nutrition across All Hands and Hearts' humanitarian response, ensure programs meet international standards, and represent the organization with the Nutrition Cluster, UN agencies, donors and partner NGOs. The Advisor will also help integrate nutrition into AHAH's wider food distribution, community health, shelter and education programs, and build the capacity of local staff and community health workers.

## Key Responsibilities

- **Technical Leadership:** Serve as AHAH's lead technical expert on nutrition in emergencies, setting program strategy and ensuring all nutrition activities align with Sphere standards, Nutrition Cluster guidance and Ministry of Health protocols.
- **Program Design and Delivery:** Design, launch and oversee nutrition interventions, which may include community-based management of acute malnutrition (CMAM), MUAC screening and referral, supplementary feeding, micronutrient supplementation, and infant and young child feeding in emergencies (IYCF-E).
- **Integration with Food Assistance:** Advise AHAH leadership and logistics teams on the nutritional adequacy of food baskets and distributions, targeting of vulnerable groups, and safe handling of specialized nutrition commodities (RUTF, RUSF, LNS).
- **Assessment and Surveillance:** Lead or support nutrition assessments, screening campaigns and surveillance (including SMART-style surveys where feasible) to identify needs, track trends and guide program decisions.
- **Coordination and Representation:** Represent AHAH in the Nutrition Cluster and relevant working groups; build partnerships with UNICEF, WFP, WHO, health facilities and local NGOs to strengthen referral pathways and avoid duplication.
- **Capacity Building:** Train and mentor AHAH staff, partner organizations and community health workers on nutrition screening, counseling, IYCF-E and the Code on breastmilk substitutes.
- **Monitoring, Reporting and Accountability:** Develop indicators and monitoring tools, ensure quality data collection, and report program results to AHAH leadership and donors. Ensure feedback and accountability mechanisms are in place for affected communities.
- **Resource Mobilization:** Contribute technical content to proposals, budgets and donor reports for institutional and private donors (e.g., USAID/BHA successor mechanisms, ECHO, UN pooled funds, foundations and Gulf donors).

## Qualifications & Experience

- MD or Master's degree in Public Health, Nursing, Nutrition, or a related field.
- Minimum 8–10 years of experience in health or nutrition programming, including at least 5 years in humanitarian or emergency settings.
- Demonstrated technical expertise in nutrition programming.
- Proven experience managing teams, training staff and working through local partners.
- Excellent analytical, communication and representation skills.
- Language requirements: Fluency in Arabic and English (written and spoken).
- Candidates must be willing to undergo a thorough background and security check prior to a final offer. Must demonstrate commitment to neutrality and community service.

## Salary

This is a 18-month, fixed-term contract/consultancy with compensation that will be competitive based on experience and location.

title: National MEAL Coordinator
body:
## Background

The CORE Group Partners Project (CGPP) is a multi-country, multi-partner initiative that provides on-the-ground technical assistance and guidance to support host country efforts to strengthen immunization systems, disease surveillance, and essential community-based health services. Globally, CGPP works across five technical areas (polio, maternal and child health, nutrition, malaria, and global health security) through existing networks of international and local NGOs operating in hard-to-reach areas with low immunization coverage. At the country level, a Secretariat coordinates the work of CGPP partner organizations in a manner that complements the efforts of all implementing partners. In Indonesia, CGPP supports national health strategies by strengthening routine immunization and polio eradication efforts while promoting maternal and child health through integrated community-based interventions.

CGPP works with the Government of Indonesia to improve maternal and child health (MCH) outcomes and strengthen routine immunization and polio eradication in selected districts of Papua and East Java and other CGPP-supported areas.

The CGPP Indonesia Secretariat, led by the Secretariat Director based in Jakarta, coordinates with the Ministry of Health (MOH) and other ministries, US Department of State (US DOS) Foreign Assistance team, UNICEF, STRIDES (FHI 360), other Global Polio Eradication Initiative (GPEI) partners, and Wahana Visi / World Vision Indonesia. The Director regularly briefs these stakeholders on project performance. Those briefings depend on project data that is complete, validated, and consistent with national MOH indicators and US DOS reporting requirements.

## Purpose of the Consultancy

CGPP Indonesia will engage a National MEAL Coordinator as a full-time consultant to make every number, report, and presentation that the Secretariat Director takes to the MOH and the US DOS accurate, consistent, and on time.

The National MEAL Coordinator will provide oversight support to CGPP Indonesia to ensure quality data and reporting. Working under the guidance of the CGPP Indonesia Secretariat Director, the consultant will:

1. Ensure CGPP project data is complete, accurate, timely and consistent with national MOH guidelines and indicator definitions and with US DOS Foreign Assistance reporting guidelines.
2. Ensure the quality of all CGPP Indonesia reports, data summaries, and briefings before submission.
3. Prepare and quality-check the presentations and briefing materials the Secretariat Director uses with MOH, US DOS, GPEI partners, and other forums.
4. Strengthen MEAL systems and capacity across the Secretariat and partner teams so that data is used for decisions and learning.

## Scope of Work and Key Responsibilities

### 1. Data quality and alignment with MOH and US DOS guidelines

- Review the CGPP Indonesia MEAL framework, indicator reference sheets, and data collection tools; align to CGPP Global MEAL Framework, indicator definitions, disaggregation, and reporting periods with MOH national standards (immunization, MCH, and surveillance systems) and with US DOS Foreign Assistance reporting requirements.
- Map source of the CGPP data (community, health facility, district, and partner sources) and document data flows, responsibilities, and reporting timelines.
- Establish and run a routine data quality assurance system: monthly validation checks, periodic data quality assessments (DQAs), and spot checks during field visits.
- Reconcile CGPP-reported results with MOH district and provincial data; flag and resolve discrepancies with field teams and partners before results are reported.
- Maintain a single, version-controlled master dataset and indicator tracking table as the official source for all CGPP Indonesia figures.

### 2. Quality of reports

- Review all CGPP Indonesia reports before submission (monthly updates, quarterly and semi-annual reports, annual reports, and ad hoc donor requests) for data accuracy, internal consistency, correct use of indicators, and clear analysis.
- Validate monthly data updates, performance indicators, and partner-reported results, as required by the Secretariat Director.
- Develop standard reporting templates and a reporting calendar with internal deadlines that allow time for review.
- Write the results and data analysis sections of reports, including progress against targets and explanations of variance.

### 3. Presentations and briefings for the Secretariat Director

- Prepare data-driven presentations, briefing notes, fact sheets, and talking points for the Director's meetings with MOH, US DOS, GPEI partners, UNICEF, STRIDES, and other coordination forums.
- Ensure every figure in these materials matches the master dataset and the latest submitted report.
- Produce clear charts, maps, and dashboards that show progress, gaps, and priority actions.
- Attend key meetings with the Director when requested, capture data-related questions and action points, and follow up.
- As per guidance of the CGPP Indonesia Director, represent CGPP Indonesia in national-level platforms.

### 4. Monitoring, evaluation, and learning

- Support the design and management of planned CGPP assessments, surveys, and evaluations, including terms of reference, tools, data analysis, and reports.
- Lead regular data review and reflection meetings with the Secretariat and provincial teams to turn findings into program adjustments.
- Document lessons learned, success stories, and good practices for internal learning and external sharing.

### 5. MEAL systems and capacity strengthening

- Work with the CGPP National Program Manager and MEAL team to harmonize workflows and maintain common MEAL standards across all partners.
- Train and mentor national and provincial staff on indicators, data collection, data quality, and data use.
- Recommend practical improvements to digital data tools and dashboards, in line with MOH systems.

### 6. Accountability

- Support community feedback and accountability mechanisms so community concerns are recorded, analyzed, and reported to decision-makers.
- Ensure data protection, confidentiality, and ethical standards in all data collection and storage.

## Reporting and Working Relationships

- **Reports to:** CGPP Indonesia Secretariat Director, who sets priorities, approves deliverables, and certifies payment.
- **Technical guidance:** CGPP Global Secretariat MEAL team and Senior Technical Advisor, for global indicator and reporting standards and program quality.
- **Internal:** CGPP National Program Manager, CGPP Indonesia MEAL team, Provincial Team Leaders, Wahana Visi / World Vision Indonesia program and MEAL staff, and finance and grants teams.
- **External:** MOH (national, provincial, and district health offices), US DOS Foreign Assistance team, UNICEF, STRIDES (FHI 360), and other GPEI partners, for data-related coordination as delegated by the Director.
- **Supervisory responsibility:** None. As a consultant, the MEAL Coordinator provides technical guidance and mentoring but does not supervise staff.

## Qualifications and Experience

### Required

- Master's degree in public health, epidemiology, biostatistics, demography, or a related field.
- At least 8 years of experience in monitoring and evaluation of public health programs, including at least 3 years leading MEAL for donor-funded projects.
- Hands-on knowledge of Indonesian MOH health information systems and indicators, especially immunization, MCH, and surveillance.
- Proven experience in data quality assessment, data validation, and reconciliation with government data.
- Experience preparing donor reports and presentations for senior government and donor audiences; US Government reporting experience strongly preferred.
- Strong skills in Excel and at least one statistical or visualization tool (e.g. Stata, SPSS, R, Power BI, or Tableau); experience with DHIS2, KoboToolbox, or ODK is an advantage.

### Preferred

- Experience with polio eradication, routine immunization, and MCH or GPEI partner programs.
- Work experience in Indonesia.
- Experience designing and managing surveys and evaluations.

### Skills and Abilities

- Close attention to detail and a commitment to accuracy.
- Ability to turn complex data into clear messages, charts and briefings.
- Ability to work to tight deadlines and manage several reports at once.
- Strong interpersonal skills to work with government, donors and partners.

### Languages

- **English**: Professional proficiency required, with ability to communicate effectively in writing and speech and with excellent report-writing in English.
- **Bahasa Indonesia**: Professional proficiency required in speaking, reading, and writing.

### Travel

- Must be willing to travel approximately 25-35% of the time.

## Terms

- **Contract:** Full-time consultancy with CORE Group, Inc., November 1, 2026 – August 31, 2027, with possible extension based on performance and funding.
- **Payment:** Monthly fee, paid on submission and approval of the monthly activity report, timesheet, and deliverables due that month. Travel costs are covered per CORE Group, Inc. policy.
- **Data ownership:** All data, reports, and materials produced belong to CGPP and may not be shared without the Secretariat Director's written approval.
- **Safeguarding:** The consultant must comply with CORE Group codes of conduct, including safeguarding and prevention of sexual exploitation and abuse.

## Disclaimer

- This scope of work is not an exhaustive list of the skills, effort, duties, and responsibilities associated with the position.

title: Communications Intern/Volunteer
body:
**Location:** The Hague, the Netherlands  
**Period:** 6 months, 15 November 2026 – 15 May 2027, Monday to Thursday

## **About us**

The Dr. Denis Mukwege Foundation (MF) is an international rights-based, survivor-centred organisation, dedicated to ending sexual violence as a weapon of war globally. The Mukwege Foundation supports survivors’ demands for a world where sexual violence as a weapon of war is no longer tolerated, and bears consequences for individual perpetrators and states. We work for a future where survivors receive the holistic care and compensation they need to rebuild their lives. We create opportunities for survivors to speak out and be heard, and where they can organise to create change, influence policies, and demand justice and accountability.

## **Background**

At the Mukwege Foundation, everything we do is guided by a five-year strategy (2024–2028) and a mission that matters: supporting survivors of conflict-related sexual violence and changing the global response to the use of sexual violence as a weapon of war. Communications are how that mission reaches people, helping them to understand and engage with the change we are working to achieve.

As our Communications Intern/Volunteer, you’ll help organise our communications assets, from powerful photos and videos to the archives and systems behind them. Your work will make our stories easier to share and use for years to come, so the voices of survivors keep reaching the people who need to hear them.

## **What you’ll do**

You will work side-by-side with our Communications Specialist on two fronts. First, you’ll help bring our social media campaigns to life. Second, you’ll play a central role in building our new media library: organising, cataloguing, indexing and migrating our communications assets so that everything is properly classified, easy to retrieve and accessible to colleagues across the organisation.

## **What you’ll gain**

This is your chance to get real, hands-on experience in a dynamic international non-profit organisation. You’ll learn what survivor-centred, ethical communications look like in practice across social media, newsletters and our website, and you’ll leave knowing that your work has lasting impact on how our mission is shared with the world

## **Tasks**

The Communications Intern/Volunteer will:

- Assist with the development of flagship communications materials, including the Annual Activity Report, social media posts, video scripts, news items and press releases.
- Support the maintenance, organisation and clean-up of the Mukwege Foundation media libraries, including the migration of photo and videos between SharePoint environments.
- Contribute to campaign content creation, including social media copywriting, design, and video editing, as well as scheduling, planning, and campaign coordination.

## **Profile of the candidate**

**Mandatory**

- The candidate must either be enrolled in or have recently graduated from a degree in Communications, Media, Journalism, Graphic Design, Marketing or a related field.
- Strong interest in the topic of armed conflict, gender-based violence, human rights, and/or conflict-related sexual violence.
- Proficient in Microsoft 365 tools, particularly SharePoint, Excel, Word.
- Attentive to detail, highly organised and autonomous.
- Ability to prioritise and work under pressure.
- Hands-on attitude and proactive mindset.
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English.
- Ability to manage large volumes of information accurately and systematically.

**Desirable**

- Experience managing databases, datasets, media libraries or digital repositories
- Experience with content migration
- Familiarity with WordPress (or similar CMS platforms)
- Experience using social media scheduling tools (e.g. Hootsuite)
- Experience in social media content creation
- Strong design skills

## **Reporting and Management**

The Communications Intern/Volunteer will report to the Communications Specialist.

## **Conditions of the internship/volunteer opportunity**

The internship/volunteering will be conducted under the following terms and conditions:

- The candidate undertakes this role on a volunteer basis or as an intern
- A small monthly allowance can be offered, based on Dutch law
- The candidate must be based in the Netherlands with occasional commute to the Foundation’s office in The Hague
- The candidate shall adhere to the Code of Conduct of the Mukwege Foundation
- Duration: 6 months, ideally starting on 15 November

title: Cash and Markets Project Manager Sudan Khartoum (Open for Sudanese only)
body:
**Background:**

The Cash Project Manager sits in the Country Office Cash & Markets team, reports to the Cash & Markets Programme Manager, and works at middle-management level. The role leads the day-to-day management of a portfolio of CVA grants across several Area Offices. It supervises the Cash & Markets Project Coordinator(s) and is the technical reference point for Area Office cash and market staff. It is the main link between the Country Office, Area Office teams, partners and support functions, turning strategy and donor commitments into on-time, compliant, quality delivery.

**What you will do:**

The Cash Project Manager leads the oversea of NRC's cash and markets projects from start to close-out. The role owns project cycle management across multiple grants and Area Offices: planning, budget follow-up, quality assurance, reconciliation of reach figures, and timely donor reporting. It ensures cash reaches people most in need safely and in line with NRC standards, and that market functionality and risk inform every modality decision.

The position sits in the Country Office Cash & Markets team and is a key link between the Programme Manager, Area Office teams, partners, the Sudan Collective technical unit and support functions.

General Responsibilities:

1. Line management responsibilities for directly reporting staff. This includes the
    - Performance management process; setting clear goals aligned to country strategy and priorities, and to follow up and support staff’s achievement.
    - Responsible for key processes as workforce planning, recruitment, staff induction and development and ensure Duty of Care for own staff
    - Manage cash projects (activities, budgets, procurement, partners, documentation) in line with proposals, strategy and donor requirements.
2. Report on progress regularly and on an ad-hoc basis, meeting all internal and donor deadlines.
3. Coordinate across NRC departments and Area Offices involved in delivery

**Specific responsibilities**

1. Project cycle management
    - Engage with AO teams to develop and maintain work plans, spending plans, MEAL plans and procurement plans for each CVA grant.
    - Lead grant opening, project review and grant closing meetings with Grants, Finance and Area Offices.
2. Cash and voucher delivery – Field based.
    - Oversee MPCA, sectoral cash, voucher delivery, both direct and partner led.
    - Ensure Area Office teams apply NRC Sudan SOPs: targeting, registration, verification, payment and complaints handling.
3. Markets and feasibility
    - Lead or support cash feasibility, market and risk assessments ahead of each response.
    - Identify opportunities for market-support interventions and integration with other Core Competencies.
4. Grants, budgets and reporting
    - Oversee CVA project budgets with AO teams and Finance: forecasting, BvA follow-up, and timely reallocation requests.
    - Reconcile reach and distribution figures across Area Offices, NRC systems, in close collaboration with the Information Management Coordinator.
5. MEAL, quality and learning
    - Work with MEAL on baseline, post-distribution monitoring and market monitoring, and act on findings.
    - Ensure complaints and feedback are tracked, referred and closed on time.
6. Partnership and coordination
    - Support partner capacity assessments and capacity building for local partners on CVA.
    - Represent NRC in the Cash Working Group and CCS technical meetings as delegated.
7. People management
    - Line-manage the Cash & Markets Project Coordinator(s) and provide functional guidance to Area Office cash staff.
    - Identify capacity gaps and deliver or arrange CVA training for NRC staff.

**Please refer to the** [**Job Description**](https://norwegianrefugeecouncil.sharepoint.com/:w:/s/JDsforNRCPeople/IQC6dQo7nbPSR5_U1Cn2kmuxAZK1nDO9GHQDXompx5lhLDk?e=DxdFER) **for detailed information as the above responsibilities are just a snapshot.**

**What you will bring:**

1. **Generic professional competencies:**

- Bachelor's degree in economics, business administration, social sciences, development studies or a related field. A Master's degree is an asset.
- At least 4 years of humanitarian experience, including a minimum of 3 years of experience managing Cash and Voucher Assistance (CVA) projects or similar interventions.
- Proven project cycle management: planning, budget management, risk management and reporting on multiple grants at once.
- Experience working in complex, insecure and fast-changing contexts.
- Line management experience, including recruitment and performance management.
- Documented results related to the position's responsibilities.
- Fluency in Arabic and English, written and spoken. Able to draft donor-quality reports in English.
- Advanced Excel skills. Experience with KoBo/ODK, Power BI or beneficiary data systems (e.g. LMMS, RedRose) is an asset.

**2. Context related skills, knowledge and experience:**

- Strong knowledge of the Sudan context, including displacement dynamics, the economic situation and access constraints.
- Knowledge of Sudanese markets, financial service providers and digital payment options (e.g. mobile money, bank apps).
- Experience with cash consortia or the Sudan Cash Working Group.
- Experience with institutional donor requirements, especially ECHO, BHA, SHF/CBPF and GFFO.
- Experience with partner-led delivery, including local NGOs and ERRs. Experience with group cash transfers is an asset.
- Familiarity with CALP, Sphere and MSMS market assessment tools\*.\*
- **What we offer:**
- Duty station: Al-Geniena, Darfur/**Update to the advert on 19th October: the duty station is changed from Al-Geniena, Darfur to Khartoum.**
- Contract: 12 Months (renewable based on funding and performance)
- Travel: 40% to Area Offices and field locations
- Salary/benefits: grade 8 on NRC’s **national** salary scale.
- NRC is an equal opportunities employer. We are committed to diversity without distinction to age, gender, religion, ethnicity, nationality, and physical ability.
- We think outside the box, encourage ideas, and give responsibility to all employees at all levels. You will have many opportunities to be heard and take the initiative.

[Find out more about the benefits of working for NRC](https://www.nrc.no/career/what-we-offer/)

Important information about the application process

- *For Internal candidates: To apply as an internal candidate, log in with your official email or click on Opportunity MarketPlace.*
- When creating your profile, include your full name as given on your passport. Complete all the system-required fields for experience, employment history and education.
- Applicants who do not fill in the required information will not be considered for the role.
- Submit your application and CV in English, taking care to attach your latest CV.
- Applications that do not meet the minimum standards in terms of experience or qualifications will generally not be considered. Unsolicited applications not related to this specific job advertisement will not be considered.
- Mandatory to submit the below when applying:
    - **Your most updated English CV and remove all previous outdated CVs.**
    - **Your most updated Cover Letter**
    - **Do not attach certificates or any other documents apart from the two mentioned above.**
    - **Incomplete applications will not be considered.**
- **This position is open for national candidates who have the legal right to work in Sudan. NRC will not sponsor visa nor residency.**
- We receive many applications for each vacant position. Therefore, only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.
- If you have any questions about this role, please email **esa.recruitment@nrc.no**with the job title as the subject line.

**Why NRC?**

The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) is an independent humanitarian organisation helping people forced to flee. Our 15,000 staff work in crises across 40 countries, providing life-saving and long-term assistance to millions of people every year.

[Watch this short video](https://vimeo.com/736782633) to see NRC in action.

We are looking for people who are passionate about helping refugees and people forced to flee. Are you one of those people? If you are, NRC offers you the opportunity to:

- do demanding and professional work, often in challenging contexts.
- join a work culture that empowers every employee to share ideas and take responsibility.
- be part of a welcoming and supportive community committed to human dignity.
- [Learn more about NRC](https://www.nrc.no/)
- [Learn more about Sudan](https://www.nrc.no/countries/africa/sudan/)

## About Us

The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) is a global humanitarian organisation helping people forced to flee.

Join us in assisting millions of people in areas where others cannot, tackling some of the world's most dangerous and difficult crises. Bring your skills and dedication to an organisation recognised for providing high quality aid and for defending the rights of refugees and internally displaced people.

At NRC, we give responsibility to employees at all levels and foster professional growth and innovative teams. You can expect a supportive culture and an open dialogue with management. We are committed to diversity, equity and inclusion.

Together, we save lives and rebuild futures.

Safeguarding is central to NRC’s work. We expect all employees to:

• treat everyone with respect and dignity

• contribute to building a safe environment for all

• never engage in any form of exploitation, harassment and specifically sexual exploitation, abuse and sexual harassment (SEAH)

• always report. NRC has a zero-tolerance approach to inaction against exploitation, abuse and SEAH
