title: MICRO-INFLUENCER CAMPAIGN TO PROMOTE THE CHOREOGRAPHY OF THE DISASTER RISK AWARENESS SONG
NVPPA Supervisor (Service Staff Supervisor)
body:
**IRC background**

The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**Job overview**

*“This position has an end date of Month, Day, Year:”*

The National Virtual Program for Professional Advancement (NVPPA) is a nationwide, fully virtual program through which IRC will serve newly arrived refugees under a cooperative agreement with the Office of Refugee Resettlement (ORR). Participants receive career navigation, training, job placement support, and direct financial assistance to advance an individualized career goal.

The NVPPA Supervisor manages the day-to-day work of the program's direct service team across a fully virtual, national caseload. This role is responsible for caseload management, case file review, escalation and resolution of participant issues, and consistent quality across Professional Advancement Plans (PAPs) and uses of direct financial assistance.

**Major responsibilities**

**Supervision and caseload management**

- Manage day-to-day caseloads for direct service staff, including assigning and balancing participants across Career Navigators and routing participants on credentialing and recertification pathways to specialized navigators.
- Conduct regular case file review to confirm that participant records, including eligibility documentation, PAPs, and case notes, are complete, accurate, and timely.
- Resolve escalated participant issues in partnership with the Customer Service Representative, and determine when an issue requires the Deputy Director's involvement.
- Support onboarding and ongoing training of direct service staff.
- Translate program requirements into standard operating procedures and desk guides for the direct service team.

**Program quality and compliance**

- Review PAPs for soundness and confirm that career goals and proposed uses of funds meet ORR eligibility requirements before assistance is requested.
- Ensure required safeguards are applied to higher-risk uses of financial assistance, such as vehicle purchases.
- Work with the data team to ensure required data is recorded in Efforts to Outcomes (ETO) and electronic case files are complete for ORR reporting.
- Monitor progress against program targets, identify barriers in the service model such as digital access, language access, or credential evaluation delays, and work with the Deputy Director on practical adjustments.

**Coordination**

- Coordinate handoffs among navigation, training, financial assistance, and job placement so that participants move smoothly through the program.
- Work with administrative and finance staff to ensure financial assistance requests are complete, documented, and aligned with each participant's PAP.
- Coordinate with other resettlement and employment programs, IRC offices, sister agencies, and local partners serving the same participants to support appropriate co-enrollment and avoid duplication of services.

**Job requirements**

- Undergraduate degree required, ideally in Social Work, Human Services, or a related field; comparable work and/or lived experience may be substituted.
- Minimum of 2 years of management or supervision experience required, including onboarding, coaching, and managing staff performance; experience with remote or distributed teams strongly preferred.
- Minimum of 2 years of relevant experience in human services, preferably in resettlement, workforce development, or employment services.
- Demonstrated experience overseeing high-volume caseloads in a compliance-heavy environment, including case file review and quality assurance.
- Demonstrated skills tracking and reporting information in a database; experience with ETO preferred.
- Familiarity with federally funded program compliance and eligibility documentation; experience with ORR-funded programming preferred.
- Experience developing standard operating procedures or workflow documentation, and familiarity with credential evaluation, professional licensing, or recertification pathways, preferred.
- Demonstrated commitment to client confidentiality and data protection, including oversight of how a remote team handles sensitive personal and immigration documents, required.
- Strong problem-solving, prioritization, and time management skills, and demonstrated success working in a multicultural environment.
- Commitment to anti-racism, ongoing learning, and equitable service to all eligible clients regardless of national origin, language, location, or resettlement agency, required.
- Lived experience as a refugee or immigrant preferred.
- Proficiency in Microsoft Office and remote collaboration tools required.
- Fluency in spoken and written English required; fluency in an additional language relevant to current refugee populations desired.

**Working environment**

- Fully remote, U.S.-based position requiring reliable high-speed internet and a private work space suitable for confidential client conversations.
- Scheduling flexibility is required to serve participants across U.S. time zones; occasional travel may be required.

**Compensation:** ($58,000 - $70,000 / Annually). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**US Benefits:** We offer a comprehensive and highly competitive set of benefits. In the US, these include: 10 sick days, 10 US holidays, 20-25 paid time off days depending on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163 per month, dental starting at $6.50 per month, and vision starting at $5 per month, FSA for healthcare and commuter costs, a 403(b) retirement savings plan with immediately vested matching, disability & life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program which is available to our staff and their families to support counseling and care in times of crisis and mental health struggles.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

title: Deputy Director, NVPPA
body:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**SCOPE:**

*“This position has an end date of Month, Day, Year.”*

The Deputy Director, NVPPA provides leadership to the National Virtual Program for Professional Advancement, an Office of Refugee Resettlement (ORR) funded program implemented in FY27. The Deputy Director leads the NVPPA team and ensures sound program implementation, compliance with ORR regulations, client success, and strong staff supervision and support.

NVPPA is a cooperative agreement carried out over a single 12-month period of performance, September 30, 2026 through September 29, 2027. The Deputy Director is accountable for delivering the program on time, within budget, and in compliance with the terms of the award.

**Major Responsibilities:**

***Program Implementation and Deliverables***

- Lead program start-up so that intake, staffing, data tools, and referral protocols are in place as clients arrive, with interpretation and device support where access is a barrier.
- Set and enforce service standards across a high-volume, light-touch model, including a completed Professional Advancement Plan (PAP) and documented career navigation for every enrolled participant.
- Oversee delivery of training, job development, and placement support, and ensure related records are maintained.

***Grant Compliance and Award Management***

- Ensure the program is implemented in accordance with ORR policy, the terms of the cooperative agreement, applicable federal award regulations and cost principles, and IRC policies on data protection, client confidentiality, and safeguarding.
- In partnership with the Senior Director, serve as the program's primary point of contact with the ORR program officer and coordinate with ORR staff, partners, and technical assistance providers.
- Protect the integrity of program eligibility, ensuring eligibility rules are applied consistently and documentation is collected and retained for every enrolled participant.
- Own the internal control environment for direct financial assistance, including documentation before disbursement, alignment with the participant's approved PAP, vendor and training provider verification, and application of IRC Global Supply Chain protocols.
- Maintain audit-ready documentation and ensure required program and financial reports are accurate and submitted on schedule.
- Identify, escalate, and resolve compliance risks, including suspected fraud, working with IRC finance, compliance, and award management colleagues on corrective action.

***Budget and Financial Oversight***

- With the Finance Manager, manage the program budget, monitor spending, and ensure full and timely spend-down and closeout of the award.
- Where a shortfall is projected, provide revised projections and propose reallocation to additional eligible services or a budget revision, at ORR's direction.

***Data, Performance, and Quality Assurance***

- Ensure Efforts to Outcomes (ETO) is configured to program requirements and serves as the system of record, working with the data team on data quality, reporting, and staff training.
- Monitor performance against outcome targets and use data to identify barriers and adjust the service model.
- Establish and oversee a routine quality assurance cycle covering case files, PAPs, and assistance documentation, with findings tracked to resolution.

***Supervision and Staffing***

- Lead recruitment, hiring, and onboarding of a newly formed, fully remote team, and ensure all staff are trained on eligibility rules, eligible uses of funds, documentation standards, and the database.
- Directly supervise the NVPPA Supervisor and the Customer Service Representative, and manage performance, workload distribution, and professional development, and structure staffing so that direct service capacity can be adjusted as enrollment volume becomes known.

***Coordination and Representation***

- In close collaboration with the Program for Initial Resettlement (PIR), oversee guidance on appropriate co-enrollment with PIR and other ORR programs, such as Matching Grant, so that participants can meet initial self-sufficiency requirements while pursuing career goals.
- Establish referral and coordination protocols with sister resettlement agencies, IRC offices, and other service providers so that eligible clients can access the program regardless of which agency resettled them, and represent the program to IRC office leadership and external partners.

**KEY WORKING RELATIONSHIPS**

**Position reports to:** Senior Director, Economic Empowerment

**Directly supervises:** NVPPA Supervisor; Customer Service Representative

**Indirect supervision:** Direct service team, through the NVPPA Supervisor

**Key relationships:** Internally, the NVPPA team, Economic Empowerment Technical Unit, IRC office leadership, and headquarters finance, compliance, and award management colleagues. Externally, ORR, PIR providers, sister resettlement agencies, training providers, and employers.

**Requirements:**

- University degree in Business, Public Administration, Social Work, Economics, Community Development, or a related field required; comparable work and/or lived experience may be substituted.
- Minimum of 10 years of experience with progressive responsibility in the design, development, and implementation of workforce, employment, or broader economic empowerment programming, including program monitoring and evaluation.
- Minimum of 5 years' experience managing staff, including remote or geographically distributed teams, with demonstrated ability to coach staff and manage performance directly and through supervisors.
- Demonstrated experience managing federally funded awards and their compliance and reporting requirements; ORR or other HHS award experience strongly preferred.
- Demonstrated experience overseeing client-level direct financial assistance or comparable payment processes, with a strong grasp of internal controls, required; experience with audits or funder monitoring preferred.
- Demonstrated ability to launch a program quickly and manage a budget of comparable scale through spend-down.
- Demonstrated understanding of refugee resettlement and employment services in the U.S. context; familiarity with credential evaluation and professional licensing pathways preferred.
- Excellent communication and organizational skills, including a track record of reporting difficult information to funders accurately and on time.
- Microsoft Office Suite required; ETO or comparable client database experience preferred.
- Commitment to anti-racism and ongoing learning, and English fluency, required.

**Working Environment**

Fully remote, U.S.-based position requiring reliable high-speed internet, a private work space suitable for confidential discussions, and scheduling flexibility across U.S. time zones; occasional travel may be required.

**Compensation:** ($94,000 - $105,000 \[GEO 1\]). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**US Benefits:** We offer a comprehensive and highly competitive set of benefits. In the US, these include: 10 sick days, 10 US holidays, 20-25 paid time off days depending on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163 per month, dental starting at $6.50 per month, and vision starting at $5 per month, FSA for healthcare and commuter costs, a 403(b) retirement savings plan with immediately vested matching, disability & life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program which is available to our staff and their families to support counseling and care in times of crisis and mental health struggles.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

title: Liaison and Partnership officer
body:
Danish Refugee Council, one of the world’s leading humanitarian NGOs, is currently looking for a highly qualified **Liaison and Partnership officer**.

## **About the job**

The Liaison and Partnership Officer supports DRC's access, operations, and partnerships across East (and South Libya when needed), under the line management of the Country Director and the technical supervision of the Partnerships Coordinator. This includes helping to build and maintain relationships with local authorities, civil society actors, humanitarian partners, and community leaders to support current and future programming.

The role requires a strong communicator who can navigate administrative systems and foster collaboration to support humanitarian goals, and who supports partner mapping, contract/sub-grant agreement (SGA) tracking, documentation and field follow-up in close coordination with the Partnerships Coordinator.

Your main duties and responsibilities will be:

**1. Liaison and Representation**

- Serve as a focal point with local authorities including ministries and municipalities, and relevant entities in East and South Libya.
- Facilitate approvals, permits, and coordination required for operations, staff movement, and program implementation.
- Represent DRC in relevant coordination meetings and stakeholder forums to promote organizational interests and ensure alignment with local frameworks.
- Monitor and interpret local administrative and context developments that may impact operations.
- Jointly with DRC's partnership unit, liaise with sub-grant partners to ensure the process is clear and all documents are received and updated on the system.
- Demonstrate competencies in drafting official letters in both languages (Arabic and English).

**2. Operational and Program Support**

- Support field teams in obtaining timely approvals for program activities, site access, and logistical facilitation.
- Assist in resolving access challenges, bureaucratic bottlenecks, and operational impediments.
- Coordinate with logistics, security, and program teams to ensure smooth field operations and staff deployments.

**3. Engagement and Entry Point Analysis**

- Identify and assess opportunities for expanding or initiating programming in under-served or priority areas.
- Provide contextual analysis, local dynamics, and potential partners or entry points.
- Support needs assessments, field visits, and donor missions by organizing meetings and access arrangements with local actors.

**4. Partner Mapping, Contract and SGA Tracking**

- Support the mapping and regular updating of information on current and potential partner organizations (national/local NGOs and CSOs) operating in the area of coverage.
- Maintain and update the partnership database/tracker, ensuring partner profiles, capacity information and contact details are accurate and up to date.
- Ensure proper filing and archiving of partnership-related documents (MoUs, agreements, amendments, assessments, correspondence) in line with DRC's document management procedures.
- Maintain an up-to-date tracker of partner agreements/SGAs, including start and end dates, budget lines, deliverables and reporting deadlines.
- Follow up with partners and relevant internal teams on the status of agreement modifications, amendments, no-cost extensions and renewals, flagging any delays to the Partnerships Coordinator.
- Support the collection and compilation of documentation required for partner selection, due diligence and capacity assessment processes.

**5. Field Monitoring and Partner Follow-up**

- Support field visits to partner-implemented activities to follow up on progress against agreed targets and identify implementation challenges.
- Follow up on partners' compliance with agreement commitments and action points arising from monitoring visits, review meetings and audits.
- Document field visit findings and share reports/updates with the Country Director, relevant teams and the Partnerships Coordinator.

**6. Reporting and Documentation**

- Maintain records of key meetings, communications, and agreements with stakeholders.
- Support drafting of MoUs with partners, routing them for review and validation, and following up until finalization.
- Provide regular updates and analysis on access, coordination, and liaison matters to senior management.
- Contribute to reporting requirements for donors, clusters, and internal management as needed.
- Support the collection and follow-up of partner and community feedback related to partnership activities.
- Contribute inputs to internal partnership reports, trackers and dashboards for the Country Director and the Partnerships Coordinator.
- Flag any irregularities, compliance concerns or incidents identified during field visits or partner engagement to the line and technical manager.

**Note:** this job description must remain flexible, to respond to additional tasks or changes as identified by the line and/or technical manager.

## **About you**

To be successful in this role we expect you to have At least 2-3 years of relevant experience in humanitarian or development sectors, with exposure to liaison, coordination, external relations or partnership/grants support functions.

Moreover, we also expect the following:

**Required**

- Strong understanding of the context and humanitarian landscape in East and South Libya.
- Experience engaging with local authorities, community leaders, and civil society actors.
- Experience maintaining trackers/databases and working with Excel or similar tools for data and document tracking.
- Excellent communication, negotiation, cultural sensitivity, and interpersonal skills.
- Willingness to travel frequently and work in dynamic field environments.

**Desirable:**

- Experience working with both government and INGOs and/or UN agencies in a liaison role.
- Prior experience in access negotiation, humanitarian coordination, or partnership/grant support.
- Knowledge of humanitarian principles and operational standards; knowledge of donor compliance basics is an asset.

In this position, you are expected to demonstrate DRC’ five core competencies:

- **Striving for excellence:** You focus on reaching results while ensuring an efficient process.
- **Collaborating:** You involve relevant parties and encourage feedback.
- **Taking the lead:** You take ownership and initiative while aiming for innovation.
- **Communicating:** You listen and speak effectively and honestly.
- **Demonstrating integrity:** You uphold and promote the highest standards of ethical and professional conduct in relation to our values and Code of Conduct, including safeguarding against sexual exploitation, abuse and harassment.

## **We offer**

- Contract length: Open Ended Contract
- Band: NMH2
- Designation of Duty Station: Benghazi Based (with regular travel to South and West of Libya plus Tunis when needed)
- Suggested Start date: 01 Nov 2026

Salary and conditions will be in accordance with Danish Refugee Council’s Terms of Employment for national employees; please refer to [our website](https://drc.ngo/about-drc/vacancies). For questions regarding the vacancy please contact Us.

## **Application process**

All applicants must upload a cover letter and an updated CV (no longer than four pages) in English. Applications sent by email will not be considered.

**Closing date for applications: 27 October 2026**

For further information about the Danish Refugee Council, please consult our website [drc.ngo](https://drc.ngo/).

title: Fundraising Specialist Adviser – Donor Journey
body:
**What we’re looking for:**

NRC Norway is looking for an experienced **Fundraising Specialist Adviser – Donor Journey** to help grow sustainable, unearmarked funding by inspiring individuals worldwide to support NRC’s life-saving humanitarian work.

You will shape personalised donor journeys that transform awareness into meaningful engagement and long-term giving. From one-off and regular donations to legacies, purchases and peer-to-peer fundraising, you will help create compelling experiences that motivate people to give and stay connected to NRC’s mission.

The ideal candidate must have proven experience in fundraising, marketing or developing and delivering income-generating initiatives. Proficiency in Marketing Cloud, practical knowledge of direct marketing tools for fundraising, as well as strong data analysis skills, with the ability to translate insights into effective fundraising strategies and informed decisions is also mandatory.

**Please note:** This is a temporary, one-year cover position.

If you are passionate about connecting people with a humanitarian cause and turning those connections into lasting impact, this is an opportunity to help mobilise the resources that enable NRC to support people forced to flee.

Please download a more detailed[**JOB DESCRIPTION**](https://norwegianrefugeecouncil.sharepoint.com/:w:/s/JDsforNRCPeople/IQD1tVyTWcXMTK3k9LwJQsc4AWwynZHsOQRqIGqJj5xF0LM?e=TILEGs) for more specific and generic duties and responsibilities.

**What you will bring:**

- At least 3 years of experience in fundraising or marketing, preferably within an organisation.
- A bachelor’s degree or higher in Marketing, Communications, or a related field.
- Proficiency in Marketing Cloud, preferably Salesforce Marketing Cloud.
- Proven experience in developing and implementing income-generating initiatives and fundraising activities.
- Practical experience with direct marketing tools, including email and SMS fundraising campaigns.
- Experience using marketing automation tools to deliver targeted and personalised donor communications.
- Strong data analysis skills, with the ability to use insights to inform decision-making and optimise fundraising performance.
- Knowledge of CRM systems and their application in donor management, reporting and analytics.
- Excellent communication and marketing skills, with a strong understanding of donor-centric engagement.
- Fluency in both Norwegian and English, written and spoken.
- Strong analytical and organisational skills, with a structured and results-oriented approach.
- Excellent collaboration skills and the ability to work effectively with diverse stakeholders.
- Ability to manage multiple priorities, meet tight deadlines and deliver high-quality work in a fast-paced environment.

**What we offer:**

- Duty station: NRC’s Head Office in Oslo, Norway.
- Contract: 12 months.
- Travel: Up to 10%.
- Salary/benefits: grade 9 on NRC’s Resident salary scale, with accompanying terms and conditions.
- NRC is an equal opportunities employer. We are committed to diversity without distinction to age, gender, religion, ethnicity, nationality, and physical ability.
- We think outside the box, encourage ideas, and give responsibility to all employees at all levels. You will have many opportunities to be heard and take the initiative.

[Find out more about the benefits of working for NRC](https://www.nrc.no/career/what-we-offer/)

Important information about the application process

- For Internal candidates: To apply as an internal candidate, log in with your official email or click on Opportunity Market Place.
- When creating your profile, include your full name as given on your passport. Complete all the system-required fields for experience, employment history and education.
- Submit your application and CV in English, taking care to attach your latest CV.
- Applications that do not meet the minimum standards in terms of experience or qualifications will generally not be considered. Unsolicited applications not related to this specific job advertisement will not be considered.
- We receive many applications for each vacant position and so only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

If you have any questions about this role, please email **ho.recruitment@nrc.no**with the job title as the subject line.

**Why NRC?**

The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) is an independent humanitarian organisation helping people forced to flee. Our 15,000 staff work in crises across 40 countries, providing life-saving and long-term assistance to millions of people every year.

[Watch this short video](https://vimeo.com/736782633) to see NRC in action.

We are looking for people who are passionate about helping refugees and people forced to flee. Are you one of those people? If you are, NRC offers you the opportunity to:

- do demanding and professional work, often in challenging contexts.
- join a work culture that empowers every employee to share ideas and take responsibility.
- be part of a welcoming and supportive community committed to human dignity.

## About Us

The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) is a global humanitarian organisation helping people forced to flee.

Join us in assisting millions of people in areas where others cannot, tackling some of the world's most dangerous and difficult crises. Bring your skills and dedication to an organisation recognised for providing high quality aid and for defending the rights of refugees and internally displaced people.

At NRC, we give responsibility to employees at all levels and foster professional growth and innovative teams. You can expect a supportive culture and an open dialogue with management. We are committed to diversity, equity and inclusion.

Together, we save lives and rebuild futures.

Safeguarding is central to NRC’s work. We expect all employees to:

• treat everyone with respect and dignity

• contribute to building a safe environment for all

• never engage in any form of exploitation, harassment and specifically sexual exploitation, abuse and sexual harassment (SEAH)

• always report. NRC has a zero-tolerance approach to inaction against exploitation, abuse and SEAH

title: Global Social and Behaviour Change (SBC) Manager
country: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
body:
**About MSI**

MSI Reproductive Choices is one of the world’s leading providers of sexual and reproductive healthcare. We believe that everyone should have the right to choose. From contraception to safe abortion and life-saving post-abortion care, we are committed to delivering compassionate, affordable, high-quality services for all.

Today, our organisation has around 10,000 team members working in 36 countries across the world. Our success lies in the fact that MSI teams are locally led, entrepreneurial and results-driven, and are passionate about delivering high quality, client-centred care in their own communities. As a social business, we focus on sustainable delivery, efficiency, and funding models that are built to last, so that the women and girls we serve today will have a choice in the future too.

We know that access to reproductive choice is life changing. For some, it can mean the ability to complete an education or start a career. For others, it means being able to look after the family they already have. For everyone, it means the freedom to decide their own future, creating a fairer, more equal world.

**About the Role**

MSI seeks an exceptional Global SBC Manager to support the strategy and implementation of SBC best practice through the provision of technical assistance (remote and in-person) on both design and implementation as well as the coordination and documentation of internal best practice and adaptation of external best practice examples and resources.

In particular, the role will initially support the Gates-funded bilateral projects in Ethiopia and Nigeria as well as other donor-funded SBC programmes across Anglophone Africa and Asia.

The role reports to the Senior Global SBC Manager and will work closely with the others in the global marketing team, regional team and donor management teams.

**About You**

For us, it’s vital that every MSI team member believes in and is committed to our organisational mission, vision and values.

**This means that we will only accept applications from candidates who are unequivocally pro-choice.**

Our values act as guiding principles, providing us with a clear direction. They set the tone for how we approach our work, interact with others and align ourselves as ‘One MSI’. It’s important that our team members truly resonate with our values and demonstrate them consistently, in all that they do.

We recruit talented, dynamic individuals with diverse backgrounds who share our mission and are focused on delivering measurable results. As an equal opportunity employer, we are committed to fostering an inclusive workplace where everyone can participate and contribute meaningfully. We value open-mindedness, curiosity, resilience, and a solutions-oriented mindset, alongside a commitment to promoting equality and safeguarding the welfare of both team members and clients.

We seek exceptional communicators who are self-motivated, solutions-driven, and aligned with MSI’s mission and entrepreneurial mindset. You should be dedicated to driving social change in an environment focused on sustainable impact, both locally and globally, and comfortable working with diverse teams in an ambiguous setting.

**To perform this role, you’ll need the following skills:**

- Fluent English skills required, French language skills desirable.
- Excellent communication skills – written and verbal.
- Ability to translate data and research into actionable insights for SBC strategic decision making.
- Strong knowledge of behaviour change theories and SBC evidence-based best practices
- Highly developed planning and organisational skills with the ability to juggle multiple projects to deliver with quality and on time.
- Ability to lead and facilitate programme design- and skill-building sessions/workshops related to SBC.
- Ability to build relationships across teams (including with external partners) with evidence of highly sensitive cross-cultural skills and good influencing and negotiation skills.
- Action- and results orientated with ability to stay on track and thrive when working under tight deadlines.
- Ability to train, mentor and develop skills within others.
- Ability to translate complex information into a format and language that can be understood by a wide range of people and present in a compelling and engaging way.
- Ability to work independently and pro-actively with minimal supervision.

**To perform this role, you’ll need the following experience:**

- Minimum four years’ experience in designing and implementing SBC programming on sexual and reproductive health, in at least two different country contexts.
- Minimum two programme examples of having implemented HCD approaches
- Experience in translating qualitative and quantitative data into actionable insights to inform and evaluate SBC programming.
- Proven experience in building buy-in of teams and stakeholders outside of your direct control
- Experience facilitating training and other capacity strengthening approaches

**Formal education/qualification**

- No formal educational requirement, qualification through experience is sufficient.

Please see job framework [here](https://www.msichoices.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/International-Job-Framework-Global-SBC-Manager-2027.pdf).

**Location:** London, UK (minimum of 2 days per week in the office) or Ethiopia, Ghana, Kenya, Malawi, Nigeria, Sierra Leone, South Africa, Tanzania, Uganda, Zambia or Zimbabwe.

**Full-time:** 35 hours a week, Monday to Friday.

**Contract type: Permanent.**

**Salary**: £48,900 - £56,300 per annum for London applicants. For country programme applicants, the salary will be strictly banded within the local national context.

**Salary band: BG 9**

**Closing date: 28th October 2026 (midnight GMT**). Interviews may take place before this date for exceptional candidates.

***For internal employees applying from an MSI country programme, the role will be positioned within the existing salary structure of the country. Local terms and conditions of the country will apply.***

title: Project Financial Audit: English & Ukrainian Speaking
body:
## 1.Introduction

CBM seeks to engage an **independent external financial auditor or an audit firm providing a suitably qualified audit team** to conduct a final financial audit upon completion of the above-mentioned project. The audit shall cover the **entire 12-month project implementation period**. The audit is commissioned and funded by CBM to fulfil **CBM’s internal audit requirements**. It is *neither* commissioned by DG ECHO *nor* a contractual requirement under the project’s DG ECHO grant agreement.

CBM Christoffel-Blindenmission Christian Blind Mission e.V. (herein referred to as “CBM”), together with the National Assembly of People with Disabilities of Ukraine (herein referred to as “NAPD“) and Momentum Wheels for Humanity (herein referred to as “Momentum”), is currently implementing humanitarian action in **Chernihiv, Sumy, Kharkiv and Poltava** **oblasts** from May 2026 to April 2027 funded by The European Commission’s Directorate-General for European Civil Protection and Humanitarian Aid Operations. The action focuses on health, rehabilitation and protection, with particular attention to persons with disabilities and other groups facing heightened barriers to humanitarian assistance. For more information, please see: [Ukraine: Restoring Access to Health](https://www.cbm.org/news/news-articles/2026/ukraine-restoring-access-to-health.html)

## 2. Scope of services/work

The assignment consists of **one final external financial audit covering the entire 12-month project implementation period,** **May 2026 to April 2027**, including the portions falling within the 2026 and 2027 financial years. The audit shall be conducted following project completion.

For the purposes of this engagement, the project shall be examined as one continuous audit period. Separate annual project audits or separate audit opinions for 2026 and 2027 are not required under these Terms of Reference. The auditor shall nevertheless verify the reconciliation between the project records for both financial years, including year-end balances, amounts carried forward and the correct allocation of transactions to the relevant reporting periods. This arrangement does not alter routine financial reporting obligations or any separate organisational or statutory audit requirements.

The audit is commissioned and financed by CBM to fulfil its internal financial accountability and assurance requirements. It is neither commissioned by DG ECHO nor undertaken as a contractual DG ECHO audit requirement for this project. Any audit separately initiated by DG ECHO falls outside this engagement and remains unaffected by it.

The scope encompasses project funds managed and expenditure incurred by **CBM and both implementing partners, the National Assembly of People with Disabilities of Ukraine (NAPD) and Momentum Wheels of Humanity (Momentum)**. It includes DG ECHO funding, CBM co-financing and relevant project transactions recorded at headquarters level. The assignment is limited to the project’s financial information and related controls; it does not constitute an audit of the organisations’ complete financial statements.

### 2.1Applicable Requirements

The auditor shall assess project financial management and expenditure against the signed grant agreement and its annexes, approved budgets and amendments, partnership agreements, and applicable organisational and national requirements.

For CBM, this includes the relevant provisions of the Finance Handbook and related financial management, procurement and internal control policies. For NAPD and Momentum, the auditor shall assess compliance with their contractual obligations towards CBM and the policies and procedures applicable to their implementation of the project. CBM-specific procedures shall apply to the partners only to the extent required under their agreements.

**Provision and clarification of reference documents**

Before the audit begins, CBM shall provide the auditor with the relevant contractual documents, applicable versions of its Finance Handbook and related policies, and any additional internal audit requirements applicable to this assignment.

Any conflicting or unclear requirements, including questions concerning their applicability or precedence, shall be clarified with CBM during audit planning and documented in the audit work plan.

**Auditing standards and audit opinion**

The audit shall be conducted in accordance with the **International Standards on Auditing (ISA)**, as applicable to the engagement and the financial reporting framework adopted for the consolidated project financial statement.

The auditor shall express an **independent audit opinion** on whether the consolidated project financial statement has been prepared, in all material respects, in accordance with the applicable financial reporting framework described in the notes to the statement.

The auditor shall also report significant findings concerning compliance with the applicable project requirements and relevant internal controls in the **management letter**.

### 2.2 Areas of examination

**Financial reporting and reconciliation:** Reconcile the consolidated final project financial statement *in EUR* with the project ledgers, transaction listings and financial reports of CBM, NAPD and Momentum. Verify funding received, CBM co-financing, transfers to implementing partners, reported expenditure, outstanding advances, project-related liabilities, refunds and closing balances. Verify that transfers between the organisations are not counted again as expenditure in the consolidated project financial statement.

The financial statement shall include notes disclosing the basis of preparation, the accounting and currency conversion principles applied, and the treatment of advances, liabilities, exchange-rate differences, closing adjustments, project-related transactions settled after the implementation period and, where applicable, non-cash entries. The auditor shall assess whether the disclosed reporting framework has been consistently and appropriately applied.

**Financial-year reconciliation and closing adjustments:** The auditor shall verify that project-related balances and transactions recorded in the 2026 and 2027 financial years are properly reconciled to the consolidated project financial statement. Examine the continuity of records between the two financial years and ensure that the financial-year split has not resulted in omissions or duplication.

This shall include reviewing relevant year-end adjustments, subsequent corrections to project-related accounting records, and the treatment of project-related payments, refunds and liabilities settled after the end of the implementation period, in accordance with the applicable reporting framework and eligibility rules. Any material discrepancies between the annual accounting records and the consolidated project financial statement shall be reported.

**Expenditure and use of funds:** Examine whether expenditure was incurred for the approved project purposes, complies with the applicable funding conditions, is properly authorised and supported by adequate documentation, and is accurately recorded and classified. Review budget amendments, exchange-rate calculations, shared-cost allocations, tax and VAT treatment, and potential duplicate charging or financing. Where indirect costs are reported on a flat-rate basis, verify the applicable contractual rate and calculation base.

**Procurement and contracted services:** Review the application of relevant procurement procedures, including procurement planning, competition, supplier selection, bid evaluation, contract award, documented exceptions, delivery and payment. Examine relevant safeguards against conflicts of interest and compliance with applicable restrictive measures. For medical equipment, assistive devices and other project supplies, review the quality-assurance documentation required under the applicable project rules and evidence of receipt or handover to the intended facilities or recipients.

**Personnel and operating costs:** Examine project-related employment and consultancy contracts, payroll calculations, timesheets or other accepted evidence of staff-cost allocation, payment records, and relevant tax and social contribution documentation. Verify that personnel, travel and office operating costs charged to the project are supported and allocated in accordance with the applicable requirements, including costs paid or recorded at headquarters level.

**Cash, banking and advances:** Review project-related bank and cash records, reconciliations, payment authorisations, fund transfers and the settlement of advances. Trace selected transactions through the accounting records, supporting documentation and proof of payment. Examine outstanding balances and their treatment at the financial-year boundary and at project closure.

**Cash assistance:** Review the financial procedures and supporting records for cash assistance, including Cash for Health where applicable. Examine documented beneficiary eligibility and approval decisions, payment instructions, evidence of transfer or receipt, reconciliations, and the treatment of failed, returned or unclaimed payments. Access to personal and health information shall be limited to what is necessary for the audit and handled confidentially. Where feasible, anonymised or pseudonymised documentation shall be used.

**Assets and stocks:** Examine project-related asset and stock records, supporting procurement documentation, evidence of existence and project use, and relevant handover, transfer or disposal documentation. Review the financial treatment of assets and stocks remaining at project closure, including any documented losses or damage.

**Internal controls, partner oversight and financial monitoring:** Assess the design and operation of controls relevant to project financial management throughout the implementation period, including segregation of duties, delegated authority, payment approvals, record-keeping, reconciliations and management review.

Particular attention shall be given to whether the enhanced staffing, supervision and financial monitoring arrangements envisaged for the project were implemented and operated during the relevant periods. The auditor shall consider changes in these arrangements over time and examine evidence of ongoing financial oversight, early risk identification and corrective action, rather than assuming their effectiveness solely from the existence of policies or staff appointments.

Review CBM’s monitoring of partner expenditure, the review and reconciliation of partner financial reports, documented financial checks and the follow-up of relevant previous findings. Significant weaknesses and recommendations shall be included in the management letter, with findings clearly attributed to CBM, NAPD or Momentum, as appropriate. This review does not constitute a separate audit opinion on the effectiveness of the organisations’ entire internal control systems.

### 2.3 Audit approach and locations

arrangements. The meeting shall take place either in person in Kyiv, subject to security conditions, or online via Zoom. The auditor shall provide a work plan, a document request list and a proposed timetable.

The auditor shall apply a **risk-based audit approach**, independently selecting samples that provide sufficient coverage of all three organisations and the **entire 12-month project implementation period**, including the portions falling within 2026 and 2027. Particular attention shall be given to significant expenditure categories and **high-value or high-risk transactions**. The auditor shall document the materiality applied, the sampling methodology and the coverage achieved by transaction number and value, and shall expand testing where findings warrant it. No fixed sampling percentage or automatic review of 100% of supporting documents is prescribed under these Terms of Reference.

Fieldwork shall include on-site visits to the **offices of CBM, NAPD and Momentum in Kyiv**, subject to security conditions. Relevant project records held at headquarters level shall be reviewed remotely. Any additional visits to health facilities, warehouses or other project locations shall be agreed with CBM in advance, with any additional costs separately identified and agreed.

Where security conditions prevent planned visits, the auditor shall discuss and agree alternative arrangements with CBM. The auditor shall document the alternative procedures performed and report any unresolved limitations affecting the audit.

**Confidentiality and data protection**

*The auditor shall maintain the confidentiality of all financial, contractual and personal information obtained during the assignment.*

*The auditor shall implement appropriate safeguards for the secure transfer, storage, retention and disposal of audit-related information, in accordance with applicable data protection requirements and the engagement agreement.*

## 3. Expected Deliverables

**Before fieldwork**

The auditor shall submit:

- **Work plan:** The proposed audit approach, team responsibilities and arrangements for on-site visits and remote review.
- **Document request list:** The records and supporting documentation to be prepared by CBM and the implementing partners (English & Ukrainian)
- **Proposed timetable:** Dates for fieldwork, draft reports, management responses and final submission, to be agreed with CBM (English & Ukrainian)

These documents shall be provided in English. The document request list and timetable should also be available in Ukrainian where possible.

**Following fieldwork**

The auditor shall provide:

- **Draft audit report and exit meeting:** Present preliminary findings to CBM and the relevant partners and submit a draft audit report and management letter for factual review and written management responses. This review shall not interfere with the auditor’s independent opinion. (English & Ukrainian)
- **Final audit report:** A signed report expressing an independent opinion on the consolidated project financial statement in accordance with its disclosed reporting framework. The report shall include the audited financial statement in EUR, explanatory notes and financial breakdowns by organisation and financial year. It shall state the auditing standards applied, summarise sampling coverage and explain any limitations or modifications to the opinion.
- **Management letter and findings schedule:** Identify weaknesses in financial records, procedures, controls and compliance, with practical recommendations. A supporting schedule shall list questioned or potentially ineligible expenditure by organisation, transaction reference, amount, currency and reason, distinguishing corrected and unresolved items.

All reports shall be submitted to CBM in English. Presentation of findings in English & Ukrainian. The final audit report and audited financial statement shall be provided as a signed PDF, with the management letter also in Word and supporting schedules in Excel. Suspected fraud, corruption or serious irregularities shall be reported promptly through CBM’s designated confidential channels, without waiting for the final report.

title: Fraud and compliance investigations support Global
body:
**Background and context**

Tiko (formerly Triggerise) uses its digital platform to encourage young women and adolescent girls (primarily ages 15–24) to make positive health choices. Through nudges—including reminders, discounts, in-person and digital follow-ups, and reward points—Tiko enables users to access healthy products, services, and entrepreneurial opportunities. Reward points cover or subsidize sexual and reproductive health (SRH) products and services, eliminating cost barriers for users.

Tiko operates in Kenya, Uganda, Ethiopia, South Africa, Nigeria, and Burkina Faso. To ensure integrity across operations, Tiko is seeking qualified investigative firms to conduct desktop reviews and field investigations regarding staff and third-party misconduct, including fraud, compliance breaches, bribery, and corruption. Bidders may apply for one or multiple target markets based on demonstrated delivery capacity.

**Geographic Scope**

- **Kenya:** Nairobi, Mombasa, Kisumu, Machakos, Nakuru, Migori, Kilifi, Homa Bay, Bungoma, Nyamira, Kisii, Busia, Kakamega
- **Uganda:** Kampala, Wakiso
- **Ethiopia:** Addis Ababa, Hawassa
- **South Africa:** City of Johannesburg, Ekurhuleni, Tshwane
- **Nigeria:** Abuja FCT, Nasarawa State
- **Burkina Faso:** Ouagadougou, Bobo-Dioulasso

**Firms may apply for one or more markets where they can demonstrate ability to deliver the assignments.**

**Scope of Work**

The firm shall be required to adequately understand our operations and the roles of the different actors on the platform. The firm will therefore collect evidence of misconduct or fraud and other ad-hoc checks to support fraud and compliance risk management activities. Investigations must adhere to strict SLAs: 72 hours for desktop reviews and 1 week for field investigations.

**Key Investigative Tasks:**

**Desktop Reviews**: Analyze automated risk flags assigned to the firm, assess flag validity, and provide actionable recommendations.

**Targeted Investigations**: Execute discreet or scheduled misconduct and fraud investigations across platform actors.

**Evidence Collection**: Conduct surveillance, interviews, electronic evidence reviews, document examinations, and third-party checks.

**Data Verification**: Perform on-site facility data verification procedures during investigations as required.

**Reporting**: Formulate Factual Findings Reports incorporating field observations, operational insights, and actionable risk management recommendations.

**TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS**

Bidders must demonstrate the following qualifications:

- **Sector Expertise**: Proven experience in fraud risk management and investigations within relevant sectors (such as non-profit/NGO, financial, health, or insurance), leveraging technology for operational efficiency.
- **Team Capacity and Readiness**: Qualified investigation team capable of managing multiple concurrent matters effectively.
- **Key Personnel CVs**: Resumes of proposed staff and core management, highlighting direct experience in fraud risk matters.
- **References**: Details of at least three (3) clients serviced for similar assignments, including contact person, designation, contact number, service scope, and engagement length.
- **Legal & Regulatory Compliance**: Proof of firm registration in the application country and full compliance with local tax, privacy, data protection, legal, and ethical standards.

**EVALUATION CRITERIA**

Proposals will be evaluated in two parts. The experience, technical proposal and financial quotation shall bear 70% of the total marks while the references and financial capacity shall bear 30% of the total marks.

- Proposals should be clear about the relevant skills, experience and capacity of the participant, in respect of this particular SoW.
- Proposals must contain the details of the proposed approach to be adopted in order to deliver the service in accordance with the SoW.
- Proposals should clearly indicate whether or not bid participants have the capacity to meet the requirements of the SoW.
- Proposal should clearly indicate compliance with the appropriate data protection, privacy, legal, social, tax and ethical issues applicable to the country applid for
- Must be a registered firm in the country where they seek to provide the services.
- A firm can bid for one or more markets depending on capacity.

**Functionality evaluation criteria**

**Description**

- Experience, Skills and Ability of Service Provider
- Past experience in similar work of this nature.
- Team member experience (accompanied by brief CV's).
- Ability of the bidder to fulfill Tiko’s requirements.

title: Request for Proposal: Provision of Ground Transport Services October 2026 Kenya
body:
**Request for Proposal: Provision of Ground Transport Services**

**October 2026**

**Kenya**

## **Procurement Summary**

**Item Details**

RFP Title Provision of Ground Transport Services

RFP Issue Date 3th October 2026

Proposal Deadline 30th October 2026

Contract Type Framework Agreement

Contract Period Up to three years, renewable annually subject to satisfactory performance

Submission Email suppliers@girleffect.org

RFP Reference Ground Transport Services 2026

## **Who We Are**

Girl Effect is an international non-profit that builds media that girls want, trust and need. From chatbots to chat shows and TV dramas to tech, our content helps adolescent girls in Africa and Asia make choices and changes in their lives. We create safe spaces for girls, sharing facts and answering questions about health, nutrition, education, and relationships, empowering girls with the skills to negotiate and redefine what they are told is possible “for a girl”.

Our reach is 50 million and counting. And we’re using technology to reach girls at scale so every girl can choose to be in control of her body, health, learning and livelihood.

Because when a girl unlocks her power to make different choices that change her life, it inspires others to do so too. She starts a ripple effect that impacts her family, community, and country.

That’s the Girl Effect.

## **Objective**

The purpose of this request for proposal is to identify and engage a specialized Taxi and Car Hire service provider for Girl Effect Kenya who will be contracted under a Framework agreement for a maximum of three years, renewable annually. Through the taxi and car hire service provided, Girl Effect Kenya will obtain the most competitive, qualified, responsive and high-quality service, representing the best value for money, for all taxi and car hire requirements. The service provider should have a performing fleet with experienced personnel and management to provide GE with taxi and car hire service that represents cutting-edge technology, processes and systems for the benefit of its users.

## **Scope Summary**

The Terms of Reference and Scope of Services shall include, but not be limited to, the details specified herein:

- Provision of Taxi and Car Hire services to GE staff in any or the majority of the project activity locations. This will include: Nairobi, Machakos, Kiambu, Mombasa, Kilifi, Kwale, Nakuru, Uasin Gishu, Elgeyo Marakwet, Narok, Migori and Garissa Counties.
- The car rental services are defined within four (4) separate categories as follows:

○ Category 1: 4 X 4 Vehicles

○ Category 2: Salon Vehicles

○ Category 3: 7-8 Seater Minivans

○ Category 4: 30-seater bus

**Lot Service Typical use Vehicle categories**

**Lot 1** Taxi and on-demand transfers Point-to-point trips within towns and cities,

including airport transfers.

Charged per km and waiting time. Cat 2, Cat 3

**Lot 2** Car hire with driver Full-day or multi-day hire with a driver within

a county. Charged per day.

Cat 1 to Cat 4

**Lot 3** Regional and long-distance travel Trips between counties, for example

from Nairobi to Narok, including multi-day trips

and group travel. Charged per day.

Cat 1 to Cat 4

- Assign clean and comfortable vehicles with valid licenses and comprehensive insurance cover.
- Assign clean, road-worthy, sober and well-behaved drivers with valid driving licenses and Certificate of Good Conduct.
- The driver shall always be smartly dressed while on duty.
- Provide security tools, including but not limited to, vehicle tracking, SOS alert response and security backup services.
- Must have fully operational approved seat belts and speed governors as applicable in transport regulations in force.
- Ability of the firm to maintain and demonstrate COVID-19 protocols & Health and safety for GE
- Ability to provide off-site vehicle recovery for all classes of vehicles
- Provide an online interactive booking & customer management tool for both car hire & taxi services (If available)
- For a non-online platform (voucher-based), the following will be required:

Before starting the journey, the Taxi user must record the following in an official Taxi Services Order (Taxi Voucher):

■ Date of taxi hire

■ The registration number of the taxi

■ Speedometer reading at pick-up point

■ Speedometer reading at the dropping point

■ Time logs for pick-up and drop-off

■ Waiting time

■ The name and ID of the Taxi driver

■ The location of departure

■ The destination of the journey.

○ Invoices shall be submitted with copy/copies of the Taxi Service Orders (vouchers), duly endorsed by the user for settlement. The invoice amount shall be based on actual mileage & time and the applicable rate for the category of vehicle used and emailed to the address that will be provided at the time of engagement.

- For the online platform, the users shall electronically confirm the journey, and the parameters outlined shall be computed by the vehicle’s GPS-based tracking system. Invoices shall be submitted with copy/copies of the Transactional statements/parameters and applicable costs to the email address that will be provided
- Thirty (30) days credit terms will apply

**Mandatory Requirements**

- Copy of Registration Certificate /Certificate of Incorporation
- Valid tax compliance certificate/Pin Certificate
- Valid Comprehensive insurance, logbooks & PSV Licenses for the fleet of vehicles owned by the firm or lease agreements for leased cars (attach document).
- Audited accounts for the last 2 years
- Evidence for operational offices, including base stations, vehicle recovery & support, including a 24-hr. dedicated support service
- Online tools for both booking & security management (If available) Share link/Screenshot/s
- List of similar assignments carried out, including at least three (3)Corporate clients, date and budget.

**Reporting**

The consultant will work closely with the Operations team to facilitate all travel requirements.

## **Period of Performance**

- The framework agreement will run for a maximum of three years, renewable annually, based on performance, unless terminated earlier by either of the parties as per agreed-upon contract terms.

**Tentative Timelines:**

- Terms of reference published:13th October 2026
- Deadline for responses: 30th October 2026

**Who You Are:**

- We welcome bids from established ground transport operators of any size that meet the requirements below. Suppliers need at least two (2) years of experience operating taxi, car hire or passenger transport services.

**Proposal Submission**

**Lots & Geography:** Bidders may submit proposals for any single Lot or combination of Lots.

**Coverage Flexibility:** Bids may cover all project locations or be limited to specific counties/regions where the bidder operates or maintains fleet capability.

Your proposal, should you be interested, shall cover the following:

## **Technical Proposal**

- **Profile**: Please showcase any previous work that you consider relevant to what we are trying to achieve, and how we approach our work and the audience we cater to. Describe the qualifications, experience and capabilities of the firm or consultant in providing the requested services.
- **Reference:** Provide at least 3 references for similar contracts with a description of the service provided and the contract periods of performance.
- **Lots and Geographical Coverage:** Bidders may propose services under one or more lots, and may limit their bids to specific geographies where they have proven capacity.

## **Financial Proposal**

The quotation should be for a schedule of rates per vehicle category per day within the routes indicated. This rate should be VAT inclusive in KES and inclusive of fuel, drivers, maintenance/spare parts, insurance, etc. Requests resulting in higher prices based on the rise in fuel rates must be supported by documentation. Any destination or vehicle that may not be easily classified, after due diligence, into any of the pre-determined categories, shall require a separate quote to be submitted for approval by Girl Effect prior to travel/provision of service and shall be reasonably based on existing rates within the agreed price schedule.

## **Pricing Schedule**

To facilitate price comparison, bidders are requested to complete the Price Schedule Sheet[ here](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1v7LlHQsx1evuAHX5uC5l59A50_J727rSVT5Yi6inoQA/edit#gid=0).

Bidders are expected to indicate the rates of service charges in the price schedule. Bidders shall also indicate prices charged for any other extra service that can be rendered.

## **Financial Proposal;**

- Must be submitted using the format provided above
- Price must be quoted in (KES)
- All applicable taxes (VAT and withholding taxes) shall be included
- If the financial proposal is silent on taxes, GE shall assume that these are inclusive.
- The financial proposal shall be valid for a period of 90 days from the date of bid closure
- The financial proposal shall be sent as a separate attachment

In the proposal, the bidder must demonstrate an understanding of the requirements described in the RFP and demonstrate how the bidder will meet the requirements of the evaluation criteria.

GE is not liable for any cost incurred during the award/contract preparation, submission, or negotiation of the award/contract. All submitted documentation and/or materials shall become and remain the property of GE.

VALIDITY of the proposal shall be for 90 days from the date of bid closure.

**Evaluation Criteria**

The criteria against which proposals will be evaluated are listed below.

## **Technical Evaluation**

- Credential/Profile - 25%
- Geographical experience in the areas of operations - 15%
- Evidence of a minimum of 3 contactable references signed - 15%
- Firms must demonstrate the Capacity of fleet size (Owned or leased) (Share list of fleet size)-15%

**Financial Evaluation**

- Value for money/proposed budget breakdown - 30%

## **General and Commercial Terms**

- Contracting: The successful bidder will enter into GE's standard Framework Agreement. Appointment does not guarantee any minimum volume or expenditure.
- Taxes: Bidders are responsible for understanding and clearly stating applicable taxes. GE will deduct or account for taxes where required by law.
- Confidentiality & Data Protection: The successful bidder must protect GE and traveller information and comply with applicable confidentiality and data protection requirements.
- Safeguarding: The successful bidder will be expected to comply with GE's safeguarding requirements and may be subject to appropriate due diligence checks.
- Conflicts of Interest: Bidders must disclose any actual or potential conflicts of interest that could influence the delivery of services or recommendations to GE.
- Equal Opportunities: GE is committed to equal opportunity and encourages proposals from diverse organisations and professionals.
- Right to Award: GE reserves the right to seek clarifications, negotiate, amend or cancel the procurement process, reject any or all proposals, and is not liable for costs incurred in preparing a proposal. Due to the volume of applications expected, only shortlisted bidders will be contacted for further evaluation
- Proposal Validity: Proposals must remain valid for 90 days from the submission deadline.

title: Senior AI Technical Specialist
body:
## About Development Gateway and the Early Grade Education Activity (EGEA)

[Development Gateway: An IREX Venture (DG)](https://developmentgateway.org/) is an international non-profit organization with approximately 80 team members based in more than 10 countries worldwide. By leveraging the combination of programmatic and IT developer capacity and skills within DG, over the last 20 years we have *researched* data ecosystems, *built* digital tools to support those data ecosystems, and *advised* on data strategy and digital transformation to strengthen decision-making, transparency, and service delivery.

DG is one of several consortium partners, led by [IREX](https://www.irex.org/), implementing the Early Grade Education Activity (EGEA, also known as ‘ASAS’) program in Jordan between 2023-2028, funded by the U.S. Department of State. As a large-scale development program, ASAS is a complex, high-paced and outcome-oriented initiative. The consortium itself comprises well over 50 individuals working on the program at any given time (based both in Jordan and abroad). From DG’s side alone, there are likely to be approximately 8-10 personnel supporting implementation at any given time, with at least 4 staff based in Amman, including the Senior AI Technical Specialist.

The overarching objective of ASAS is to improve the quality of early grades (K-G3) education outcomes for children in Jordan. The program aims to achieve this objective by supporting the education of student teachers while they are still at university (pre-service teachers), and also by supporting early grades students and teachers (in-service teachers).

DG’s role within the consortium includes supporting the safe, effective, and responsible integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into Jordan’s education sector, in alignment with the national AI policy. In partnership with the Ministry of Education and Human Resources DevelopmentDG is embarking on an ambitious set of activities that will test AI capabilities in real-world settings.

## Job description

This is an exciting opportunity for an AI specialist who can situate cutting-edge developments in AI within Jordan’s policy context and understand how new technologies can strengthen education systems. Based in Amman, you will turn fast-moving AI advances into practical opportunities for the Ministry of Education, schools, and universities, and explain their value clearly and simply to non-technical audiences.

Rather than executing backend software development or heavy algorithmic coding, your focus is on driving active stakeholder participation, co-designing AI sandbox environments in schools and universities, and explaining complex technical concepts in accessible Arabic and English. You will directly complement IREX’s overarching coordination work by grounding high-level planning into practical, school- and university-level deliverables–ensuring MoEHRD counterparts, school staff, faculty, and administrators remain energized, engaged, and aligned with core project requirements.

Embedded within the ASAS project office in Amman, you will report directly to DG’s Director of Software Development (US) for technical strategy, with a dotted reporting line to DG’s local Project Lead/Advisor for daily operational alignment. Working alongside 30+ Jordan-based consortium colleagues, you will join a creative, globally distributed team that values hard work, practical problem-solving, and collaboration. If you excel at turning institutional friction into clear technical momentum, this role offers the platform to drive meaningful digital adoption across Jordan's education ecosystem.

At DG, we are a creative and dynamic group of people based around the globe. We value and reward hard work, innovative thinking, a commitment to teamwork, and a good sense of humor. With this role, we are looking for a new colleague to join our team and be our Senior AI Technical Specialist on the ASAS program in Amman.

The work you get to do

*In-Service AI: School-Level AI Centers & Sandbox Pilots*

- Provide technical support to establish six AI Centers in MoEHRD-selected schools, including assessing facility readiness, defining equipment and technical specifications, and verifying that installed centers are ready for use.
- Work with the MoEHRD and relevant stakeholders to co-design the scope, governance, school selection, institutional roles and implementation approach for AI sandbox pilots in three schools across the country including facilitating technical consultations and participatory workshops. Support the preparation of a technical brief outlining the objectives, scope, expected outcomes, and implementation approach for the school AI sandbox pilots, aligned with the Year 3 AI Readiness Assessment and policy brief.
- Lead the technical set-up of school sandboxes, support the design and delivery of sensitization workshops and hands-on training, , and help pilot schools shortlist 2–3 priority AI use cases.
- Support monitoring and evaluation of AI sandbox pilots, including assessment of technical performance, usability, pedagogical relevance, user adoption, and documentation of results, challenges, and lessons learned.
- Support the organization and technical facilitation of workshops to present and validate pilot results with MoEHRD, participating schools, and relevant stakeholders.
- Provide ongoing virtual sandboxing support, including a helpdesk that responds to technical questions and pedagogical questions on applying AI to agreed use cases.
- Translate pilot results into evidence and recommendations for MoEHRD leadership, the National AI for Education Forum, and a national approach to scaling successful use cases.
- Support MoEHRD and Field Directorates in assessing technical, institutional, and operational requirements for sustaining school AI Centers and scaling successful AI applications.

*Pre-Service AI: University Engagement & Institutional Integration*

- Serve as the lead technical interlocutor for partner universities, directly tackling engagement friction and driving active academic participation in project activities.
- Uncover operational bottlenecks and university requirements, translating qualitative institutional feedback into structured digital use cases.
- Lead the co-design, testing, and university-level rollout of sandbox AI environments, establishing clear feedback loops with faculty and administrators.

*Requirements Scoping & Technical Translation*

- Scope functional requirements for applied AI initiatives (e.g., automated reporting, documentation synthesis, data collection tools) without needing to write heavy software code.
- Translate complex technical concepts into accessible, bilingual (Arabic/English) specs and guidance notes for non-technical stakeholders, MoEHRD and university leadership, and vendors.
- Establish User Acceptance Testing (UAT) protocols, rollout sequencing, and data stewardship standards for school, university and ministry systems.

*Alignment with IREX Coordination & Programmatic Support*

- Complement IREX's programmatic coordination and oversight by serving as the Jordan-based technical liaison between DG's development team, IREX, MoEHRD, schools, and partner universities, translating agreed plans into actionable technical activities and supporting the timely resolution of implementation challenges.
- Serve as the primary Jordan-based technical liaison between DG's development team, IREX technical teams, MoEHRDHRD counterparts, schools, and partner universities, ensuring timely validation of requirements, coordination of technical implementation, resolution of operational challenges, and alignment with agreed work plans and institutional priorities
- Co-develop SOPs, workflows, and training materials that enable school and university staff to practically adopt AI tools in their daily routines.
- Provide regular, proactive updates on school and university technical readiness, operational risks, and adoption milestones to project leadership.

*Data Governance & Responsible AI*

- Establish practical ethical standards, governance rules, and privacy protections across all school and university AI sandbox pilots.
- Define data de-identification practices, accuracy checks, and hosting protocols to protect sensitive institutional and student data.

## Qualifications and experience requirements

- **Experience:** 5+ years of experience in data systems, digital transformation, or technology adoption, with proven success driving stakeholder engagement within Jordanian universities or national institutions. Experience with AI applications, data science tools, or emerging technologies in education.
- **Technical Alignment:** Demonstrated capacity to map user requirements to applied AI/data tools and structure low-risk use cases (no direct programming required).
- **Language Skills:** Professional fluency in written and spoken Arabic and English, with demonstrated ability to draft technical specifications in both languages.
- **Education:** Bachelor’s degree in STEM, Information Management, Education, or a related field.

## Preferred (desirable) qualifications

- Degree and/or certification in artificial intelligence, machine learning, or computer science is a plus.
- Familiarity with donor-funded programming (e.g., U.S. State Department) and their reporting standards.

Position Details

This is a **full-time staff position**, embedded in the ASAS office in Amman. The role is expected to run for approx. 2 years, pending annual performance reviews. The expected annual salary range is USD 50,000-65,000, depending on relevant experience.

title: Grants and Reporting Officer
body:
**Job Title:** Grants and Reporting Officer

**Function:** Programme Support

**Job Group:** Programmes

**Duty Station:** Odesa, Ukraine (with potential travel to field locations)

**Line Manager:** Programme Development Manager

**Line Management Responsibility:** N/a

**ABOUT US:**

Nonviolent Peaceforce (NP) reimagines security and civilian protection in areas most impacted by conflict by working alongside communities to interrupt and prevent violence. NP is a global civil society organization that works with people affected by violent conflicts to enhance their security and dignity through Unarmed Civilian Protection (UCP) and by helping to transform the world’s response to conflict. Programming is founded on unarmed civilian protection and is thematically focused on protection in displacement, child protection, gender-based violence protection and inter-communal violence reduction, social cohesion, and civic engagement.
