NP first established a presence in Ukraine in 2014-15 working on peacebuilding and conflict mediation. NP has had a sustained presence in Ukraine since April 2022 and is operational in Kharkiv, Donetska, Dnipropetrovsk, Kherson, Mykolaiv and Odesa oblasts. NP occupies an established space in the protection response in Ukraine; simultaneously providing direct protection to at-risk civilians and providing hands-on support to front-line volunteer collectives to contribute to the sustainability and safety of their actions.

**JOB PURPOSE:**

The Grants and Reporting Officer (GRO) will collaboratively work with the Programmes, Finance and Operational Teams in NP’s Ukraine Country Office to ensure compliance with donor regulations and monitor grant implementation in-line with agreed workplans and objectives. This includes project activity oversight, donor reporting and supporting proposal development (where applicable).

**KEY OBJECTIVES/RESPONSIBILITIES:**

**Grants Management and Reporting**

- Lead in drafting narrative donor reports and relevant annexes (i.e. logical frameworks, impact assessments, case studies), ensuring excellent quality, accuracy and adherence to donor guidelines.
- Support programmes, finance and field teams to understand donor contractual requirements, ensuring grant compliance from the outset of grant roll-out (i.e. through inception workshops).
- Maintain information management and involve all internal stakeholders in communications on fundraising issues for grants.
- Lead on updating relevant online platforms (e.g. UN’s Grants Management System (GMS)) with project data and reports, as well as responding to notifications and/or additional information requests from key donors.
- Compile and analyse data to write field activity reports submitted by staff and partners, aligning with grant deliverables.
- Act as team focal point for Salesforce (NP’s global online project management system), including creating new opportunities / projects, updating project activities, monitoring project outputs, tracking progress and extracting relevant information for reporting.
- Coordinate with the finance department to ensure that financial reports are submitted on time, comply with financial reporting requirements and align with narrative reported activity progress.
- Review donor reports, project proposals and communication materials as required.

**Partnership Support**

- Maintain regular communication and coordination with NP’s Partnership department to collect and synthesise data for activity and donor reports.
- Support NP’s Partnership department to draft sub-grant contracts in-line with donor compliance and agreed logframes, objectives and activities.
- Follow up with partners’ implemented activities and report progress through Salesforce.
- Support ad-hoc capacity development requests from partners and provide trainings, guidance and mentoring as needed.

**Other**

- Support with rolling out NPUA’s country strategy across all project sites.
- Travel to project sites to enhance understanding of the context and programming to develop proposals and report to/liaise with donors.
- Undertake other relevant tasks as requested.

**QUALIFICATIONS AND COMPETENCIES:**

**Education, Knowledge, and Experience**

- Excellent and precise command of English, with exemplary oral and written communication skills, and an ability to develop high quality and engaging communications. There is a significant amount of writing required in this position.
- Significant experience developing narrative donor reports (for multilateral and institutional donors including the UN, FCDO, GAC, ECHO, SDC) under minimal supervision.
- Previous grants management, monitoring and evaluation (M&E) or reporting experience within a non-governmental organisation (NGO).
- Experience in institutional donor compliance and familiarity with basic rules and regulations. An understanding of basic statutory requirements would also be an asset.
- Experience in implementing, analysing and utilising M&E tools.
- Experience implementing programmes, ideally in humanitarian emergencies and/or in Ukraine.
- Knowledge or demonstrable interest in civilian protection, human security, violence reduction, protection and/or peacebuilding.
- Relevant university degree in social sciences, international development or related area of studies is preferred but not required. Corresponding work experience will also be considered.

**Skills**

- Diplomacy, professionalism and adept at relationship building.
- Ability to manage sensitive information with discretion.
- Demonstrable conflict analysis skills, identify entry points and design prevention and protection strategies.
- Ability to communicate effectively with individuals and work and live in a multicultural environment.
- Solutions-focused, creative problem solver.
- Genuine commitment to, and interest in, living and working at the community level.
- Flexibility and adaptability.

title: Head of HR, Africa Region
body:
**BRAC International (BI) is Hiring! Join BRAC International to create opportunities for people to realise their potential.**

**Position: Head of HR, Africa Region**

**Job Location:** **Nairobi, Kenya**

**Application deadline: October 31, 2026**

**About the Role:**

BRAC International is seeking a Head of HR, Africa Region- to provide greater support to Country Offices’ HR Functions across several HR-critical areas. The region currently covers Ghana, Liberia, Kenya, Rwanda, Sierra Leone, Tanzania, and Uganda and a workforce of over 4,000 staff.

This position will report to the Regional Director, Africa. Collaborating closely with the Dhaka Central Office HR and the Regional Director, this role encompasses both country-specific and Nairobi Central Office responsibilities.

Key to the role will be providing support to both the Country Offices and the Nairobi Central Office, ensuring HR policies are contextualised and adhered to, and that any breaches are thoroughly investigated, with appropriate action taken and lessons learned.

**Key Responsibilities:**

- Lead thedevelopment and delivery of the BI HR Strategy in the Africa region.
- Lead Country Offices in the contextualisation of HR policy in line with national law, roll-out, and adherence, with sign-off from BI Central Office.
- Work with Country Office Senior Leadership to contextualise office structure and organograms, ensuring fit-for-purpose staffing across all units to achieve results.
- Guide recruitment processes in-country for staff below Head of/Deputy, ensuring HR recruitment policy is followed, and the right staff are in place to deliver across signed-off structures.
- Play a liaison role with the Dhaka Central Office in the recruitment of Country Directors and Deputy Country Directors/ Heads of Programme, as well as supporting the induction and onboarding of those staff.
- Play a lead role in the grievance and disciplinary processes for staff below Head/ Deputy, ensuring processes are followed as per policy.
- Drive the rollout of a new salary scale for Country Offices and any subsequent reviews.
- Ensure Performance Management processes are being implemented in Country Offices, including for CD and DCD/ Head of Programme.
- Assist in the development of security guidance and policy, including management of live safety and security issues.
- Work with the Dhaka Central Office HR Team to roll out the talent management process and succession planning for country management teams in the Africa region.
- Work with Country Teams to drive a OneBRAC culture across all teams
- Support the transition to a digital HR system, working in collaboration with the Central Offices staff.
- Training and support to Country Offices in all HR-related issues.
- Lead HR set-up for expansion into new countries, including workforce planning, recruitment of initial staff, employment contracts, payroll and benefits, in line with national law.
- Ensure HR practices meet donor requirements for grant-funded staffing, including staff costing in proposals, time allocation, fixed-term contracts aligned to grant cycles, and fair, well-planned transitions when grants end.

Regional Office Responsibilities

- Ensure the running of HR processes in the Nairobi Central Office in line with the policy.
- Ensure the Nairobi Central Office is fully staffed in line with the signed-off structure.
- Key point of contact for the Central Offices on all Nairobi Central Office HR matters, including running performance management processes, setting objectives, and reviewing staff in the Nairobi Central Office Team.
- Work with the Regional Director as well as HR staff across other units based in the Nairobi Central Office to ensure a one BRAC culture and team.

Safeguarding Responsibilities

- Establish a safeguarding culture by implementing safeguarding policies, hiring staff following safe recruitment and vetting, making any decisions guided by the do-no-harm principle, mitigating safeguarding risks, and maintaining a safe working environment where staff feel encouraged to voice concerns without fear of retaliation.
- Ensure 100% of team members, partners and service providers have access to and receive mandatory training on the safeguarding policies and reporting channels.
- Introduce a mandatory safeguarding agenda in monthly meetings to support continuous dialogue & reminders as part of building a safeguarding culture.

**Academic Qualifications:**

- Minimum of a Bachelor’s degree in any relevant discipline and a recognised professional HR qualification (e.g., CIPD or a national equivalent) is an advantage.

**Experience Requirements:**

- A minimum of 10 years of experience in the HR function, including at least 5 years in the multinational/international development sector.
- Experience in the areas of leadership and people management, and in strategy development and delivery.
- Experience/ working knowledge of multiple human resource disciplines, including talent management, performance management, talent acquisition, compensation practices, organisational diagnosis, employee relations, diversity, and employment laws, is highly preferred.
- Experience driving expansion and country footprint in complex markets.

**Required Skills, Competencies & Knowledge:**

- Strong analytical skills and a data-driven approach to continual improvement.
- Excellent judgment, sensitivity, and integrity.
- Frequent travel across the region and working with geographically dispersed teams.
- Demonstrated expertise in interpreting, navigating, and strategically applying complex employment laws, regulatory frameworks, and organisation policies.
- Competent in managing multicultural staff, working effectively with senior management teams.
- Strong interpersonal skills/ communication skills in English and collaborative mindset.
- Effective stakeholder management and negotiation skills.
- Proficiency in MS Office applications.
- Possess high ethical and moral standards.
- Hold a professional HR certification (e.g., CIPD or a national equivalent).

**Type of Employment:** Contractual

**About BRAC International:**

BRAC International (BI), a leading non-profit organisation, is on a mission to empower people and communities facing poverty, illiteracy, disease, and social injustice. Our vision is to create a world free from exploitation and discrimination, where everyone has the opportunity to realise their potential. We design proven, scalable solutions that equip people with the support and confidence they need to achieve their potential.

BRAC was founded in Bangladesh in 1972 and over the last five decades has grown to become one of the world’s largest non-governmental organisations (NGOs), reaching over 100 million people. We started our first international operation by venturing into Afghanistan in 2002, building on lessons from our work in Bangladesh to support a nation devastated by war. Currently operating in 14 countries across Asia and Africa. Born, proven and led in the Global South, BRAC International brings a unique Southern perspective and commitment to continuous learning, providing a depth of insight, experience and evidence to meet the needs of diverse communities with humility and courage across Asia and Africa. To learn more about BRAC International, please visit [www.bracinternational.org](http://www.bracinternational.org)

**Our Core Values:**

**Integrity:** We approach our work with honesty and integrity.

**Innovation:** We innovate and iterate to improve our impact.

**Inclusiveness:** We foster inclusion to reach those who need it most

**Effectiveness:** We strive for effectiveness to better serve people in poverty

title: Grants Manager
body:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**Job Overview:**

The Grants Team at IRC in Sacramento works to leverage public and private funding opportunities through prospecting, proposal development, grants, and subaward contract management. The Grants Manager is primarily responsible for overseeing the full range of pre- and post-award activities required to prepare concept notes, proposals, and budgets, comply with internal approval processes, and align with compliance requirements of public agencies and private foundations. Work is performed under the supervision of a Development Director and in collaboration with IRC Sacramento’s leadership, finance, programs, as well as headquarters’ technical team, and awards and business development units.

**Major Responsibilities:**

***Development and Grants Management***

Prospecting

- Represent Sacramento office in all regional opportunities, particularly for restricted funding, in close coordination with Site Directors, Development Director, Technical Advisors, relevant program leads, and grant coordinators.
- Collaborate with the Development Director in prospecting efforts, utilizing an internal standard operating procedure to support both restricted and unrestricted fundraising needs.
- In collaboration with IRC Sacramento Development Director, work with the Site Director to develop a funding strategy and timeline and perform prospective research on potential public and private funders.

Proposal Development (Pre-Award)

- Develop and manage the Sacramento region’s proposal calendar.
- Lead concepts note, proposal, and budget development, including ensuring log frames, program design, and narrative meet high quality standards in coordination with Programs/Site director, Finance Director, and headquarters’ Resource Acquisition and Management (RAM), and ensure all supporting documentation in the applications are up to date.
- Provide pre-award support and coverage when needed to the local offices.
- Lead negotiation and agreements stage with donors and ensure contract terms are communicated with Finance and Programs through grant kick off meetings and recorded in Asana project tracking.
- Coordinate grant opening and closing meetings for every funded opportunity across the Sacramento office portfolio.

Grants Management (Post-Award)

- Modify final budgets as requested by donor and Site Director/program lead and communicate with Finance and RAM to ensure incoming restricted funds will be tracked.
- Lead negotiation and agreements stage with donors and ensure contract terms are communicated with Finance and Programs through grant kick off meetings and recorded in Asana project tracking.
- Provide support with reports, including copy-editing, coordinating report timelines with headquarters, and submission.
- Serve as a main point of contact for donors across Sacramento office to ensure communication adheres to IRC policy and best practices.
- Develop and ensure the effective maintenance of contract and grant files for each funded program with consistent documentation standards.
- Be a local subject expert for IRC’s Business Development Standards.
- Be a local subject expert for IRC’s internal grants systems (PEERS and OTIS).

Partnerships

- Be a local subject expert in IRC’s internal partnership process, PEERS, to provide technical support to the Partnership Grants Coordinator to ensure subawardees’ contracts are drafted with detailed information on scope of work, deliverables, fund disbursement, and monitoring plans in coordination with the partners and program staff, and in compliance with Finance and RAM.

***Supervision & training:***

- Provide leadership and management of the Grant Coordinator in Turlock, to ensure all tasks are covered and team workload is managed in a way that respects and promotes work life balance and professional growth.
- Provide training and support to new hires ensuring staff meet the expectations of their role and meet responsibilities in a timely manner.
- Be a local subject expert in OTIS and IRC’ RAM’s Business Development processes, and the local Sacramento/Turlock Business Development workflow.

***Systems & Accountability:***

- Maintain proposal calendar, pipelines, grants tracking, and regularly update senior management with up-to-date data
- Ensure the go/no-go review process of opportunities are consistently applied and strengthened by working with senior management to ensure proposals are of high quality and grants staff are at capacity
- Ensure continuous improvement on the utilization of Asana to track opportunity pipelines, award management, and reporting in coordination with senior management, Finance, and program staff
- Establish and continuously update a Standard of Practice (SOP) for Grants staff in coordination with the Finance team and headquarters’ Resource Acquisition and Management (RAM
- Leverage regular communications with Finance, RAM, and the Sacramento office to improve SOP and workflow

**Secondary duties:**

- Work closely with site leads and program staff to prepare interim and final reports to grantors.

**Key Working Relationships:**

- **Position Reports to:** Development Director
- **Position Supervises:** Grants Coordinator (in Turlock office)
- **Indirect Reporting:** Site Director  
    **Other Internal and/or External Contacts:**
- ***Internal:*** Director of Finance, Sacramento/Turlock Executive Director, Sacramento Program Managers & Coordinators, Technical Advisors, HQ Resource Acquisition and Management department
- ***External***: Foundations and public funders at city, county, state, and federal levels

**Job Requirements:**

***Education:***

- Bachelor’s Degree required in nonprofit management, community development, social sciences, social work, or related fields, or demonstrated work experience of similar knowledge. Master’s degree a plus.
- Certification or continuing education in project management, proposal development and/or fundraising a strong plus.

***Work Experience:***

- Five+ years of nonprofit or public sector experience in development and grants.
- Five+ years of experience in a supervisory role.

***Demonstrated Skills and Competencies:***

- Excellent writing, research, and organizational skills.
- Familiarity with grants process of government funding agency(ies) (federal, state, or county/city level)
- Familiarity with the Sacramento non-profit/philanthropy environment a plus
- Familiarity and comfort working with budgets and finance departments
- Ability to work autonomously in their scheduling and prioritizing within tight deadlines and focused on the work product.
- Self-directed but with strong interpersonal skills and the ability to work well within a team
- Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications: Word, Excel, Outlook, and project management tools, e.g. Asana
- Experience in IRC systems of PEERS and OTIS a plus (for IRC internal candidates)
- Valid driver’s license and access to a personal, insured vehicle.

***Language Skills:***

- Excellence in written and spoken English

**Working Environment*****:***

- Standard hybrid office environment (this is not a fully remote position)
- Occasional travel to Turlock office site as needed

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Compensation:** ($84,872-$91,137 - Annually). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**Benefits:** IRC offers a comprehensive and competitive benefits package. Highlights include 10 paid sick leave, 10 U.S. holidays, 20-25 generous paid time off based on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163/month, dental starting at $6.50/month, and vision starting at $5/month, flexible spending accounts (healthcare, dependent care, and commuter), a 403(b) retirement savings plan with employer match (immediate vesting) along with a non-elective employer contribution based on age and years of service (3-year vesting), disability and life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program (EAP) offering confidential counseling and support services for employees and their families.

title: HR and Administration Coordinator
body:
Danish Refugee Council, one of the world’s leading humanitarian NGOs, is currently looking for a highly qualified HR and Administration Coordinator.

**About the job**

To provide advice, coordination, capacity building and technical support to HR focal person at field location and overall coordination of HR tasks at country level.

The Human Resources Coordinator ensures compliance to DRC's human resource procedures and guidelines within the country operations. The role contributes to the development of country strategies, which are translated into action plans and day-to-day tasks.

The job is based in Tunis with potential 20% travel to field offices.

Your main duties and responsibilities will be:

**Human Resources Support**

- Provide technical support and advice to the Human Resources team
- Advise and assist managers in Human Resources related issues and concerns

**Recruitment**

- HR focal person for recruitments of national and expat staff (excluding bands C, D & E with HQ)
- Define and ensure proper onboarding process for new staff
- Coordinate and organize inductions on country level on a regular basis, including coordination with facilitators and participants
- Ensure oversight and consistency in position titles and grades, across all field locations.
- Advise hiring managers in development of Job description, inclusive job advertisements and team structures.

**HR Function and compliance**

- Developing/updating HR policies, Employee/HR Handbook, procedures and tools and close monitoring to ensure compliance.
- Collaborate with Senior Management Team in the analysis of the organizational structure across the three countries to ensure consistency, coherency, and efficiency
- Focal point for DRC coordination office legal matters, liaison with legal Advisor and monitoring of ongoing/ new legal cases against DRC.
- Supporting country director in keeping the registration status updated to incorporate changes in legal representative etc. by seeking timely support from legal advisors on the process.
- Advise and train HR and admin focal person in digitalization of HR and Admin tools and platforms.
- Coordination with finance unit to ensure payroll, taxes are captured accurately in the three countries.

**Learning and Development, Performance, and Well-being**

- Support managers & staff with performance management and review processes, including providing specialized trainings like People management skills.
- Act as an impartial mediator in disciplinary procedures and ensure that they follow DRC policies and meet all legal and labor regulations and requirements
- Implementation of Global, regional, and country level HR initiatives example (DRC Voices, minimum standards, staff wellbeing, diversity, and inclusion etc)
- Coordinate with senior managers to develop country wide training calendar.

**Compensation and Benefits**

- Take lead in salary review process in partnership with service provider, Finance team, Senior Management team at country and HQ and coordinate compensation review process and compensation adjustments.
- Analysis of benchmarking reports and the design of new salary grids; Support implementation of DRC’s new Compensation policy, including salary progression
- Prepare monthly payroll for Tunisia and review Algeria and Libya payroll to ensure compliance.
- Register employees in social security for all LE hosted by TUN legal entity.

**DRC Dynamics and Digitalization and reporting**

- Follow up the correct implementation of DRC Dynamics (HR Module) and the quality of the data entered in the system.
- Train HR focal person in TUN, Libya and Algeria and where required others in WANALA region.
- Monitoring accuracy and timely update of master data in dynamics for TUN, Libya and Algeria for the HR module
- Producing monthly HR reports for TUN, Libya and Algeria
- Ensure org chart for TUN, Libya and Algeria are up to date and produce when required by managers
- Develop/update HR templates digital/manual (recruitment tracker, onboarding and offboarding checklist and forms, recruitment request forms, exit clearance forms, contract request etc)
- Manage digital spaces like Share point (HR), MACH forms etc
- Provide training in Dynamics (HR Module) for HR focal person and relevant module like Employee self-service to new joiners
- Developing and maintaining full record of legal status/file of DRC’s registration in Tunisia.

**Partnerships:**

- Participate actively to the assessment of local partners capacities in terms of HR from the compliance and transparency perspective.
- Provide technical training to local partners in the fields covered by the scope of work of the HR coordinator Position.

**Code of Conduct**

- Will support country director in ensuring that required CoC structure is in place at country office.
- Coordinates with HQ and regional CoC focal person to seek technical inputs on the subject.
- Support country director in managing CoC structure in the country/operation.

**About you**

To be successful in this role we expect you to have at least 3 years’ working experience (officer and above) in Human Resources functions, preferably within an NGO.

Moreover, we also expect the following:

*Required*

- Demonstrated understanding and working knowledge/experience of Human Resources Management principles, concepts & processes
- Ability to interpret and transform local labor laws in DRC internal policies.
- Experience in developing Human Resources strategies and policies, and driving implementation
- Experience using an online system for recruitments and ERP system
- Payroll management and experience in salary benchmarking exercise
- Experience and understanding of local labour laws and managing legal services
- BA in Human Resources, Management, Administration or related subject is mandatory
- Fluency in French and Tunisian language is must
- Working knowledge of English is mandatory

*Desired*

- MA in a related subject is desired

In this position, you are expected to demonstrate DRC’ five core competencies:

**Striving for excellence:** You focus on reaching results while ensuring an efficient process.

**Collaborating:** You involve relevant parties and encourage feedback.

**Taking the lead:** You take ownership and initiative while aiming for innovation.

**Communicating:** You listen and speak effectively and honestly.

**Demonstrating integrity:** You uphold and promote the highest standards of ethical and professional conduct in relation to our values and Code of Conduct, including safeguarding against sexual exploitation, abuse and harassment.

**We offer**

Contract length: Open ended with 6 months probation period

Band: Non management G level 1

Designation of Duty Station: Tunis, Tunisia

Suggested Start date: 01 December 2026

Salary and conditions will be in accordance with Danish Refugee Council’s Terms of Employment for national employees; please refer to [our website](https://reliefweb.int/void(0)). For questions regarding the vacancy please contact [Us](https://reliefweb.int/void(0)).

**Application process**

All applicants must upload a cover letter and an updated CV (no longer than four pages) in English. **Applications sent by email will not be considered.**

Closing date for applications: 01 November 2026

For further information about the Danish Refugee Council, please consult our website [drc.ngo](https://reliefweb.int/void(0)).

title: Supply Chain Coordinator
body:
Danish Refugee Council, one of the world’s leading humanitarian NGOs, is currently looking for a highly qualified **Supply Chain Coordinator.**

## **About the job**

The Supply Chain Coordinator is responsible for all procurement of goods and services, warehousing, transportation of good and people, vehicle fleet management and general logistics support to the Programme. He also localizes and adapts DRC policies within support area to local circumstances  
and contributes to the development of country strategies.

The job is based in Tunis with potential 20% travel to field offices

**Geographic scope:**  
This role has a country focus and ensures compliance to DRC procedures and guidelines within the three countries of operations of the ALT Mission. The role contributes to the development of country strategies, which are translated into action plans and day-to-day tasks. The role provides support and/or technical guidance to country operations while overseeing country activities.

Your main duties and responsibilities will be:

### **Coordination**

- Contributes to the daily operation with comprehensive knowledge in logistics and procurement
- Lead the coordination with the programme staff to ensure logistics & procurement involvement in the whole programme cycle
- Ensure that all logistics & procurement specific DRC/donors’ rules and policies are understood and respected
- Follow the SC KPIs in each geographical areas an propose concrete solutions to improve the overall efficiency of the SC functions across the ALT mission.
- Provide Technical support to the supply chain teams across the ALT mission.

### **Procurement**

- Ensure that procurement policies and procedures are rigorously followed
- Procurement of all goods and services (Ensure the quality of procurement documentation before advertising and serves as compliance focal point to SC related matters).
- Establish and follow up annual procurement plans
- Track all orders, purchases and deliveries
- Oversight of all purchase and service contract to ensure DRC's interests are protected
- Optimize all logistics operations to increase cost effectiveness including setting up longer term supply contracts
- Ensure DRC supplier due diligence is effective

**Logistics**

- Fleet: management of rental and owned vehicles, generators, speed boats & motorbikes (in line with DRC guidelines)
- Transport: management of all transportation of goods and people (via road, river, air) to-from areas of operations and-or other DRC offices
- Asset: registration, maintenance, repairs-maintenance & disposal of DRC assets accordingly to donors’ rule and policies (in line with DRC guidelines)
- Warehouse: manage the DRC warehouse and stores (in line with DRC guidelines)
- Premises: health and safety, contract management and repairs/maintenance at DRC premises

**As Coordinator the post-holder is responsible for the following:**

- Responsible for coordinating strategy and operations within the three ALT legal entities
- Has technical line responsibilities within a given discipline, for both strategy and operations
- Provides expert advice and support to set strategy and assure operational quality and compliance

### **Partnerships:**

- Participate actively to the assessment of local partners capacities in terms of HR from the compliance and transparency perspective.
- Provide technical training to local partners in the fields covered by the scope of work of the HR coordinator Position.

### **DRC Dynamics and Digitalization and reporting**

- Follow up the correct implementation of DRC Dynamics (SC Module) and the quality of the data entered in the system.
- Train SC focal persons in TUN, Libya and Algeria.
- Monitoring accuracy and timely update of master data in dynamics for TUN, Libya and Algeria for the SC module
- Producing monthly SC reports for TUN, Libya and Algeria
- Develop/update SC templates digital/manual (Procurement tracker, warehouse reports, fleets reports)
- Manage digital spaces like Share point.
- Provide training in Dynamics (SC Module) for new joiners

## **About you**

To be successful in this role we expect you to have At least 3-5 years of practical experience in similar role with International NGOs, donors or UN agencies.

Moreover, we also expect the following:

- Field experience
- Working experience from an international humanitarian organisation
- A good understanding of the procurement rules and regulations of major international donors
- Experience working in an (I)NGO
- Excellent skills in MS Word, Excel, and PowerPoint
- Full professional proficiency in English
- Master's degree in e.g. Logistics and/or Supply Chain Management
- Certification in Humanitarian Logistics Supply Chain (desired if no academic degree) or significant SC field experience in humanitarian contexts.
- Fluency in French and Arabic is must
- Working knowledge of English is mandatory

In this position, you are expected to demonstrate DRC’ five core competencies:

- **Striving for excellence:** You focus on reaching results while ensuring an efficient process.
- **Collaborating:** You involve relevant parties and encourage feedback.
- **Taking the lead:** You take ownership and initiative while aiming for innovation.
- **Communicating:** You listen and speak effectively and honestly.
- **Demonstrating integrity:** You uphold and promote the highest standards of ethical and professional conduct in relation to our values and Code of Conduct, including safeguarding against sexual exploitation, abuse and harassment.

## **We offer**

- Contract length: Open Ended
- Band: NMG1
- Designation of Duty Station: Tunis
- Suggested Start date: 15 Dec 2026

Salary and conditions will be in accordance with Danish Refugee Council’s Terms of Employment for national employees; please refer to [our website](https://reliefweb.int/void(0)). For questions regarding the vacancy please contact [Us](https://reliefweb.int/void(0)).

## **Application process**

All applicants must upload a cover letter and an updated CV (no longer than four pages) in English. Applications sent by email will not be considered.

**Closing date for applications: 01 November 2026**

For further information about the Danish Refugee Council, please consult our website [drc.ngo](https://reliefweb.int/void(0)).

title: Grants and Collaborations Team Leader – Performance Enhancement
body:
## ***Description***

The **Pacific Community (SPC)** is the principal scientific and technical organisation in the Pacific region, supporting development since 1947. We are an international development organisation owned and governed by our 27 country and territory members. In pursuit of sustainable development to benefit Pacific people, our organisation works across more than 25 sectors. We are known for our knowledge and innovation in such areas as fisheries science, public health, geoscience, and conservation of plant genetic resources for food and agriculture.

The **Operations and Integration (O&I) collective** delivers essential enabling services that support the organisation’s scientific and technical portfolio. Our key functions include corporate services, programme support, partnerships, resource mobilisation, and strategic engagement. These services are coordinated through our regional and satellite offices across the Pacific and Europe. Additionally, the O&I collective leads a dedicated workstream focused on organisational change and transformation to drive continuous improvement and adaptability.

The role – **Grants and Collaborations Team Leader – Performance Enhancement** will lead a small team within the Grants and Collaborations Team to ensure the effective and timely delivery of high-quality grant management services across SPC. The incumbent will provide expert advice and support on complex grant-related activities, strengthen grants management processes, and drive continuous improvements in grant systems and practices. The Team Leader will also play a key role in fostering strong relationships with internal and external stakeholders, ensuring grant activities meet SPC’s standards, comply with funder requirements and contribute to the achievement of SPC’s strategic objectives.

The key responsibilities of the role include:

**Systems and processes: Grants Performance, Quality and Continuous Improvement**

- Lead the development and implementation of initiatives to improve the efficiency, effectiveness, quality and consistency of SPC's grants and collaborations function.
- Develop practical improvement plans and oversee their implementation, monitoring progress and reporting results to the Grants and Collaborations Manager.
- Identify and implement improvements to Grants and Collaboration Tools and Systems: Enhance the tools and systems used for managing grants and collaborations, ensuring they support better understanding, compliance, and efficiency across SPC.
- Monitor the performance of grants management processes and identify trends, bottlenecks, control weaknesses, recurring issues and opportunities for improvement.
- Establish and maintain appropriate performance indicators, service standards and quality measures for the Grants and Collaborations function.

**Systems, Data, Digitalisation and Process Improvement**

- Lead the review and improvement of grants and collaborations systems, tools and workflows including supporting the evaluation, selection and implementation of a Grants Management System (GMS) including definition of business requirements and integration with Business Central (PR-to-Pay); and contribute to the transition to a Centre-Led operating model for grants management.
- Identify opportunities for automation, digitalisation and improved use of technology across the grants lifecycle.
- Work with ICT and relevant business units to define business requirements for grants management systems and digital solutions.
- Promote the use of reliable grants data to support operational management, performance monitoring, reporting and decision-making.
- Develop and maintain appropriate management information, dashboards and performance reports.

**Advice and Guidance**

- Provide expert advice on SPC grants and collaborations processes: Provide expert advice to the Grants and Collaborations Manager and senior management on grants management performance, risk, systems and process improvement.
- Provide advice to decision-makers on complex grant and collaboration Issues: Provide evidence-based advice to relevant committees and decision-makers on systemic grants management issues and proposed improvements.
- Brief decision-makers on trends, performance issues, risks and opportunities for improvement.
- Prepare high-quality reports, briefing notes, dashboards and management information for internal stakeholders.
- Support the Grants and Collaborations Manager in preparing reports for senior management, the Executive, governing bodies and the Audit and Risk Committee.

**Management of staff**

- Team leadership and supervision: Lead the staff, ensuring clear direction, support, and motivation is provided to staff.
- Recruitment and staffing: Lead the recruitment and selection process ensuring that staffing level and capabilities are appropriate to meet operational needs.
- Performance management, training and development:
- manage the performance management process for staff ensuring that team performance goals are aligned with SPC objectives.
- manage the training and development needs for staff ensuring continuous learning and skill development within the team.

**Outreach, education and training**

- Develop mechanisms to capture, share and institutionalise lessons learned across the Grants and Collaborations Team.
- Lead communication and change-management activities associated with new or revised grants processes, systems and requirements.
- Provide capacity building: Lead the development and delivery of training programs to internal and external stakeholders to enhance understanding and management of grants and collaborations, including pre-award and post-award processes, and as part of SPC’s performance enhancement work.
- Build collaborative relationships: Lead on fostering strong, collaborative relationships with all SPC stakeholders, ensuring alignment and support for grants and collaborative activities.
- Ensure effective communication: Lead on maintaining open and effective lines of communication with key stakeholders, building strong relationships to support the effective implementation of grants and collaborative initiatives.

For a more detailed account of the key responsibilities, please **refer to the online job description**.

## ***Key selection criteria***

**Qualifications**

- A postgraduate qualification in a relevant field such as law, finance, grants management, business administration or international development or equivalent body of knowledge and experience.

**Technical expertise**

- At least 7–8 years of relevant experience in grants management, programme/project management, business administration, finance, risk management, compliance, process improvement, international development, law or a related field.
- Demonstrated experience leading or coordinating teams and/or complex cross-functional initiatives.
- Demonstrated experience reviewing and improving organisational processes, systems or operating procedures.
- Experience in performance monitoring, data analysis and management reporting.
- Experience developing guidance, procedures, tools and training materials.
- Demonstrated ability to translate complex information into practical recommendations.

**Language skills**

- Excellent English communication skills (oral and written) with a working knowledge of French being an advantage.

**Interpersonal skills and cultural awareness**

- Ability to work in a multicultural, inclusive and equitable environment.

## ***Salary, terms and conditions***

**Contract Duration** – **3 years** – subject to renewal depending on funding and performance.

**Remuneration** – The **Grants and Collaborations Team Leader – Performance Enhancement** is a band 11 position in SPC’s 2026 salary scale, with a starting salary range of 3,245‒4,057 SDR (special drawing rights) per month, which currently converts to approximately FJD 10,028–12,535 (USD 4,349–5,436; EUR 3,924–4,905). An offer of appointment for an initial contract will normally be made in the lower half of this range, with due consideration given to experience and qualifications.Progression within the salary scale will be based on annual performance reviews. Remuneration of expatriate SPC staff members is not subject to income tax in Fiji; Fiji nationals employed by SPC in Fiji will be subject to income tax.

**Benefits for Staff in a position advertised internationally (EPAI) whose duty station is Suva –** SPC provides a housing allowance of FJD 1,500–5,200 per month. Establishment and repatriation grant, removal expenses, airfares, home leave travel, health and life and disability insurances and education allowances are available for eligible employees and their eligible dependents. Employees are entitled to 25 working days of annual leave per annum and other types of leave, and access to SPC’s Provident Fund (contributing 8% of salary, to which SPC adds a 10% contribution).

**Languages** – SPC’s working languages are English and French.

**Recruitment principles** – SPC’s recruitment is based on merit and fairness, and candidates are competing in a selection process that is fair, transparent and non-discriminatory. SPC is an **equal-opportunity employer**, and is committed to cultural and gender diversity, including bilingualism, and will seek to attract and appoint candidates who respect these values. Due attention is given to gender equity and the maintenance of strong representation from Pacific Island professionals. If two interviewed candidates are ranked equal by the selection panel, preference will be given to the **Pacific Islander**. Applicants will be assured of complete confidentiality in line with SPC’s Privacy Policy.

title: Advocacy Specialist: Treaty Bodies
body:
ILGA World is seeking an Advocacy Specialist on Treaty Bodies, who will work as part of our advocacy programme and coordinate the organisation’s day-to-day engagement with [the United Nations human rights treaty body system](https://www.ohchr.org/en/treaty-bodies).

**Deadline for applications:** Tuesday, 10 November 2026 – 23:59 (Central European Time, CET)  
**Start of the position:** January/February 2027, subject to successful work authorisation and any applicable notice period

## Who can apply?

Anyone

- with dedication to – and experience in regard to – the human rights of persons with diverse sexual orientations, [**gender**](https://ilga.org/glossary/gender/) identities, gender expressions and [**sex characteristics**](https://ilga.org/glossary/sex-characteristics/)
- who meets the requirements set out below

is welcome to apply.

## Overview

The Advocacy Specialist: Treaty Bodies is part of ILGA World’s advocacy prgramme and coordinates the organisation’s day-to-day engagement with the [**United Nations**](https://ilga.org/glossary/united-nations/) human rights treaty body system.

The role advances the rights of people and communities of diverse SOGIESC by connecting grassroots, national and regional advocacy with international human rights mechanisms. It provides technical assistance to ILGA World members, regions and human rights defenders; supports strategic engagement with treaty bodies; and helps ensure that movement priorities, evidence and lived realities inform [**country reviews**](https://ilga.org/glossary/country-reviews/), normative developments, jurisprudence and follow-up at national level.

Working under the strategic direction of the Advocacy Senior Manager and closely with colleagues across the advocacy programme, ILGA regions, member organisations and partner organisations, the Specialist monitors treaty body processes and opportunities, coordinates submissions and briefings, supports strategic litigation and national follow-up, analyses recommendations and jurisprudence, develops capacity-strengthening resources, and maintains relationships with treaty body members and OHCHR staff. The role also works across ILGA World programmes to connect advocacy with knowledge production and movement strengthening.

## Responsibilities

The Advocacy Specialist: Treaty Bodies reports to the Advocacy Senior Manager and is responsible for the day-to-day coordination and delivery of ILGA World’s Treaty Bodies portfolio within the Advocacy Programme.

### Specific to this position, this includes:

- Implement ILGA World’s Treaty Bodies advocacy workplan and coordinate the organisation’s day-to-day engagement with the UN human rights Treaty Body system, serving as the organisational focal point for Treaty Bodies-related advocacy.
- Monitor Treaty Body sessions, reporting cycles, country reviews, lists of Issues Prior to Reporting (LOIPRs) under the Simplified Reporting Procedure, follow-up procedures, general comments, individual communications and other developments, identifying timely and strategic opportunities for SOGIESC advocacy.
- Develop and implement advocacy strategies to advance the human rights of people and communities of diverse SOGIESC through country reviews, normative development, individual communications and other relevant Treaty Body procedures.
- Provide technical assistance to ILGA World members, regions, LGBTI organisations and human rights defenders engaging with Treaty Bodies, including advocacy planning, reporting, preparation of written and oral submissions, briefings and follow up strategies.
- Coordinate and contribute to ILGA World and joint submissions, shadow report inputs, briefing materials, statements, position papers and other advocacy products in consultation with affected communities, members, regions, partners, and external legal experts
- Facilitate the meaningful participation of human rights defenders in Treaty Body processes, including organising briefings and engagement with Treaty Body members and OHCHR staff.
- Coordinate ILGA World’s strategic litigation engagement before Treaty Bodies, including identifying appropriate opportunities, supporting individual communications and third-party interventions, and contributing to follow-up on decisions in collaboration with members, partners and relevant legal experts.
- Monitor, systematise and analyse SOGIESC-related [**concluding observations**](https://ilga.org/glossary/concluding-observations/), recommendations, general comments, jurisprudence, decisions and other Treaty Body outputs, and contribute to compilations, briefings and analytical resources.
- Support ILGA World members and human rights defenders to use Treaty Body recommendations, decisions and jurisprudence in national advocacy, including follow up and implementation, and document relevant results, challenges and good practices.
- Develop and deliver training, webinars, guidance and other capacity strengthening resources to strengthen civil society engagement with the Treaty Body system.
- Build and maintain effective working relationships with Treaty Body members, OHCHR staff, civil society organisations, legal experts, academics and other relevant stakeholders, and represent ILGA World in relevant meetings, consultations and external spaces.
- Monitor and contribute to discussions concerning Treaty Body strengthening, accessibility, effectiveness and other institutional developments affecting the system.
- Work across ILGA World programmes and advocacy portfolios to strengthen coherence between Treaty Bodies, the Human Rights Council, Universal Periodic Review, Special Procedures and thematic advocacy, and ensure that relevant ILGA World research and monitoring data inform Treaty Body engagement.
- Contribute to planning, budgeting, monitoring, evaluation and learning, donor reporting and funding proposals relating to the Treaty Bodies portfolio, and work with the Communications team to make relevant opportunities, developments and outcomes accessible to members, partners and wider audiences.

### **General**

- Actively contribute to promoting and achieving the organisation’s objectives.
- Engage and collaborate with colleagues across the Advocacy Programme and other ILGA World teams to strengthen a shared organisational culture and ensure coordinated, movement-informed work.
- Ensure that all activities are carried out with full regard to ILGA World policies.
- Work as a part of the ILGA World staff team.
- Perform other duties as required.

### **Relationships with colleagues**

ILGA values creative and inclusive approaches to work and management that have been achieved through cross-service area working and the participation of staff at all levels in the organisation. Staff have line management arrangements and specific key relationships, which are detailed in their job descriptions, but they will also need to work collaboratively with their colleagues in order to achieve their agreed targets and outcomes to the required standards.

## Performance of duties, remuneration, and benefits

- This position requires relocation to Geneva, Switzerland.
- This position is subject to the successful granting of the necessary Swiss work authorisation.
    - Where required, ILGA World will submit and support the work permit application for the selected candidate. However, the relevant Swiss authorities make decisions on work authorisation, and ILGA World cannot guarantee that an application will be successful. Any offer of employment and appointment to the position is therefore conditional upon the required work permit being granted. If the necessary authorisation cannot be secured, ILGA World will not be able to confirm or proceed with the appointment.
- The position is advertised at 100% of a full-time position.
- ILGA World remunerates under a three-tiered salary matrix structure. The annual salary offered for the 100% position is 81,060 CHF.
- In addition, ILGA World offers 32 days, inclusive of legal holidays (“bank holidays”) and annual leave and contributions to health care costs.
- ILGA World operates under a flexible working system that – among others – includes flexible working hours.
- The weekly working time is 40 hours on a 100% position.

## Requirements

### **Education and qualifications**

- A master’s university degree or equivalent in [**international human rights law**](https://ilga.org/glossary/international-human-rights-law/), law, political science, international relations or a related field, combined with 6 years of relevant work experience

or

- A first-level university degree in combination with 8 years of relevant and qualifying experience

or

- 10 years of relevant and qualifying experience instead of a master’s or first-level degree

### **Experience**

- A minimum of 4 years of relevant experience in human rights advocacy, policy or legal work, preferably within an international, regional or national civil society organisation, multilateral institution or similar setting.
- At least 2 years of direct engagement with United Nations human rights mechanisms, including substantive experience working with one or more UN Treaty Bodies.
- Experience developing and implementing advocacy strategies relating to Treaty Body country reviews, normative development or other treaty body procedures.
- Experience drafting shadow reports, written submissions, briefing materials, statements, position papers or other advocacy documentation for international human rights mechanisms.
- Experience providing technical assistance, guidance or capacity strengthening to civil society organisations and human rights defenders engaging with international human rights mechanisms.
- Experience analysing international human rights standards, concluding observations, recommendations and/or jurisprudence and translating complex legal developments into accessible advocacy guidance.
- Experience with or strong familiarity with strategic litigation, individual communications or other forms of legal advocacy before international or regional human rights mechanisms.
- Demonstrated experience working collaboratively with grassroots organisations, LGBTI human rights defenders and diverse stakeholders across different national, cultural and political contexts.
- Experience in project coordination, including planning, monitoring, evaluation, learning and narrative reporting, including in donor-funded work.
- Experience building and maintaining working relationships with UN officials and experts, civil society organisations, legal practitioners, academic partners and other relevant stakeholders.

### **Technical requirements**

- Advanced skills in legal and policy analysis, with strong knowledge of international human rights law and its application to [**sexual orientation**](https://ilga.org/glossary/sexual-orientation/), gender identity, gender expression and sex characteristics.
- Demonstrated in-depth knowledge of the UN human rights Treaty Body system, including country review processes, normative outputs, follow-up procedures and individual communications.
- Ability to monitor, systematise and analyse Treaty Body recommendations, general comments, jurisprudence and other outputs and identify strategic advocacy opportunities.
- Strong research and drafting skills, including the ability to present complex legal and policy developments clearly and accessibly to different audiences.
- Demonstrated ability to build and sustain partnerships with member organisations, human rights defenders, UN officials, civil society organisations and other stakeholders.
- Strong understanding of SOGIESC human rights issues and commitment to feminist, decolonial, intersectional and anti-oppressive approaches to advocacy.

### **Other requirements**

- Strong communication, facilitation and diplomatic skills, with the ability to communicate clearly and effectively with diverse audiences
- Excellent organisational skills, sound judgement and the ability to prioritise work, meet deadlines and adapt to changing advocacy opportunities
- Proven existing professional relationships with the [**Office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights**](https://ilga.org/glossary/office-of-the-high-commissioner-for-human-rights/) (OHCHR) Secretariat staff and/or independent Treaty Body experts.
- Ability to work proficiently in English (mandatory). Knowledge of Spanish, French or another UN official language is an asset
- Adherence to and alignment with the ILGA World Code of Conduct, including a strong capacity for confidentiality, tact, discretion and respectful collaboration

title: Regional Business Development Manager- SWANA
body:
**About The Role**

**Team Purpose**  
Institutional funding is key for operationalizing Oxfam’s mandate globally and in the region. Institutional sources (including multilateral and bilateral agencies and donors) typically have decentralised operations, budgets and decision-making structures throughout the world. To engage effectively with these organisations Oxfam has an established global architecture that mirrors its key institutional relationships, builds stronger partnerships and delivers greater impact and influence at country, regional and global levels. This operational architecture also enables Oxfam to more readily purse multi-country / regional opportunities that are offered by institutional donors to address transnational issues such as migration, climate change, natural disasters and conflicts. Humanitarian crises which often cross-national borders also require standing capacity at regional levels to most effectively mobilise resources.

**Job Purpose**  
The Regional Business Development Manager will lead on new business development in support of all countries in their region; creating, identifying and accessing new funding opportunities; maintaining a consistent standard of donor relationship and high-quality proposal development across variable country contexts; and will actively seek to grow income for the confederation through multi-country funding opportunities and consortium partnerships.

The Regional Business Development Manager will also support the Regional Director in providing strategic leadership on resource mobilisation across all countries in the region. They will be responsible for developing and implementing the regions resource mobilisation strategies; supporting the Regional Director in building partnerships with regional donors and civil society stakeholders; identifying new funding opportunities; addressing key financial and reputational risks; and ensuring that there are strategies in place to maintain adequate skills and capacity, staffing and income within the portfolio of countries in the region.

The post holder will be expected to work across the confederation of Oxfam affiliates and the Oxfam International Secretariat in achieving the regional funding strategy and be the primary link for accessing technical fundraising assistance and support from the confederations fundraising architecture.

title: Procurement expert - HLGSC - Montreuil
body:
**Beginning of contract :** ASAP

**Type of contract** : Fix-term contract until 31/08/2027

**Localisation** : Montreuil (93) / France (possible home-working from metropolitan France)

The European Cooperative Society of Collective Interest "Humanitarian Logistics Cooperative", also known as "hulo", is the first humanitarian cooperative founded in June 2021. Led by humanitarian organizations and integrating new members regularly, hulo aims to improve the impact of humanitarian aid by strengthening collaboration and the implementation of joint projects in its countries of intervention. At hulo we are convinced that the sharing and pooling of resources and expertise between organizations contributes to increasing the performance of humanitarian logistics and the supply chain

Our action is based on a collaborative and participatory approach, collective intelligence and the animation of a community of practice. All our activities are structured around a common objective, involving several autonomous and interdependent stakeholders, who cooperate horizontally. Steering is distributed, based on consultation, co-responsibility and voluntary commitment.

In our 7 countries of intervention spread over 3 regions, we set up shared initiatives in the fields of purchasing, human resources and the environment. In support of humanitarian organizations, we coordinate shared international humanitarian transport initiatives for the most serious humanitarian crises. Finally, we are constantly developing digital solutions for the humanitarian community.

To find out more, you can consult the 2026 annual report by clicking on the link [https://hulo.coop/january-2026-annual-impact-report/](https://hulo.coop/january-2026-annual-impact-report/)

**JOB DESCRIPTION**

The Procurement Expert contributes NGO-side procurement expertise to the Global Humanitarian Procurement Collaboration and Performance Initiative, the 12-month HLGSC action co-led by WFP, hulo and NRC.

Working closely alongside the Project Manager, the WFP-hosted Procurement Expert (UN) and the wider Procurement Thematic Working Group (TWG), the position provides operational NGO experience to the design, testing and refinement of procurement cooperation guidance and procurement-integration tools, and supports the organisations participating in structured testing, pilots and validation.

A core dimension of the role is co-construction with the UN-side Procurement Expert: the two work jointly to identify which UN and NGO procurement practices are common ground and can be combined, and which need to remain distinct and why, and to translate this into tangible, evidence-based recommendations for the evolution of donor policies and regulations submitted to the HLGSC Donor Group.

He/she will have the main responsibilities of:

- Contribute to targeted procurement cooperation and collaboration guidance
- Strengthen procurement integration into organisational and project-level decision-making
- Support technical validation, consultation and cross-workstream coordination
- Contribute to monitoring, reporting and knowledge management

**MAIN MISSIONS**

**\#1 : Contribute to targeted procurement cooperation and collaboration guidance**

- Co-construct, jointly with the UN-side Procurement Expert, a shared methodological framework for procurement cooperation: identify which UN and NGO ways of working are common and can be combined, and which need to remain distinct, and why.
- Prepare, jointly with the UN-side Procurement Expert, the evolutions to be submitted to the HLGSC Donor Group, factoring in changes in donor policies and regulations, and build tangible, evidence-based arguments and expected gains to support these recommendations.
- Coordinate closely with the Data Specialist and the Academic Expert to ground this methodological and donor-facing work in the evidence base.
- Support the consolidation of tested NGO approaches to procurement cooperation, including piggybacking, use of existing framework agreements, mutual recognition and shared market intelligence.
- Contribute NGO operational experience to the development of procurement cooperation principles, guidance and decision-support tools
- Contribute to refining the guidance package and defining the uptake pathway based on testing and review findings.

**\#2 : Strengthen procurement integration into organisational and project-level decision-making**

- Support the consolidation of existing NGO practice on integrating procurement earlier into proposal development, demand planning, budgeting, market assessment and implementation planning.
- Contribute to the development of the practical procurement-integration tool package
- Support five pilot organisations in testing selected tools, and facilitate structured peer exchange on implementation experience.
- Contribute to documenting pilot learning and refining the final tool package.

**\#3: Support technical validation, consultation and cross-workstream coordination**

- Contribute to Procurement TWG technical consultations, comments matrices and decision records
- Support coordination with relevant cross-TWG touchpoints and with the HLGSC Donor Group on issues relevant to procurement cooperation and integration.
- Liaise with participating organisations and their focal points to support engagement, testing readiness and documentation of implementation learning.

**\#4: Contribute to monitoring, reporting and knowledge management**

- Provide inputs to the action's monitoring records, pilot documentation, risk register and implementation roadmap
- Contribute to knowledge products, learning notes and materials for wider dissemination

**YOUR PROFILE**

**Experiences / Educational background**

- BAC+5 in Supply chain management, procurement, international development, business administration or a related field.
- Minimum of 5 years on positions with responsibilities in procurement in NGO sector
- Experience in the humanitarian sector

**Technical and transversal skills**

- Expertise on procurement, in humanitarian context :
    - Proven experience with humanitarian procurement cooperation mechanisms (e.g. framework agreements, piggybacking, shared market intelligence)
    - Knowledge of donors' rules on procurement
    - Proven experience in analyzing procurement data and developing strategic recommendations.
- Collaboration and communication skills :
    - Experience working in multi-stakeholder or cross-organisational settings (e.g. UN-NGO coordination, working groups, consortia)
    - Excellent stakeholder management and facilitation skills, including the ability to co-construct outputs with counterparts from different organisational cultures (UN/NGO)
    - Excellent communication skills, comfortable adapting communication style and tone to audience and diverse contexts
    - Attentive and active listening skills, able to make others be heard and build consensus
    - Problem-solving oriented
- Strong analytical and drafting skills, with the ability to translate operational practice into guidance, tools and donor-facing arguments
- Experience in writing reports and other donor deliverables
- Familiarity with ECHO or other major institutional donor policies and reporting requirements is an asset
- Organised, autonomous, and comfortable operating within a compressed delivery timeline
- Strong interpersonal skills and experience in multi-language and multi-cultural environments
- Fluent command of English and French (very good level read, written and spoken).

**HULO WILL OFFER YOU THE FOLLOWING CONDITIONS**

A full time position

- Based in Montreuil with the possibility of working remotely in metropolitain France.
- Employment contract under French law for a fixed term.
- Executive status on an hourly basis (based on 1607 hours worked / year).
- Salary conditions:
    - Gross annual salary: €43,075 over 13 months
    - RTT: 22 days / year
    - AXA mutual insurance and provident insurance (100% covered by hulo)
- Meal vouchers: face value of €8, 60% covered by hulo
- Specific conditions and skills: prolonged sitting, oral expression, screen work, telephone contacts.
