*We are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, marital status, disability, gender, gender identity or expression. We are proud to be an equal opportunity workplace.*

title: Site and Research Manager - Mondika
body:
**Location:** Mondika (Nouabalé-Ndoki National Park), Republic of Congo.

**Reports to:** Nouabalé-Ndoki Director of Research and Principal Investigators of Mondika.

**Type of contract:** 1-year full-time contract, renewable.

**Position Summary:**

We are looking for a dynamic Site and Research Manager to manage Mondika research and monitoring activities, and liaise with the Tourist Manager to coordinate tourism activities. The successful candidate will have a strong scientific background, a strong interest in conservation, and in working in remote places in tropical forests. This is a full-time position. In 2023, the Mondika Gorilla Project research station was included in the NNNP along with the entire region known as the Djéké Triangle. The research station and activities are collaboratively conducted in partnership with the Goualougo Triangle Ape Project (GTAP) and its Co-Directors.

**Main tasks:**

**Management of Field Research at MDK**

- Supervise the effective implementation of the research protocols at the MDK field site.
- Coordinate fieldwork of all MDK’s Research Teams.
- Participate in daily follows/habituation of gorillas at MDK.
- Supervise the collection of data (e.g., behavioral observations, health symptoms using Animal Observer App, meteorology, SMART, Cybertracker) at the MDK site.
- Implement tests of reliability measures to ensure that research team members are collecting data accurately and in a standardized manner.
- Oversee the implementation of the direct observational health program for gorillas at MDK.
- Train Congolese Research staff in reduced impact protocols for daily ape follows, behavioral monitoring techniques, use of portable data collection devices, data management, and reporting.
- Contribute to the professional development of the Congolese Research staff at MDK, including individualized research projects to present in Bomassa and/or Brazzaville.
- Supervise data entry and backups for the MDK site and collaborate with the Goualougo Triangle Site and Research Manager to ensure standardization of data collection is maintained.
- Ensure the quality of collection, storage, inventory, and transport of biological samples (i.e., fecal, insect samples) obtained at MDK, as well as coordinated shipment to Bomassa.

**Communication and Personnel Management**

- Organize staff schedules and movement logistics.
- Compile monthly site reports summarizing data collection, field efforts, staff participation, and research highlights, which are submitted to the NNNP Director of Research and Ecological Monitoring and the Congo-Apes Project Co-Directors, Site Manager, and Tourism team.
- Work with the Congo-Apes Project Co-Directors, Principal Investigators of MDK, and the NNNP Director of Research and Ecological Monitoring to provide transparent, timely supervision of the gorillas, site, and personnel.
- Represent the research team during tourist visits and actively engage with visiting tourists to enhance their overall experience.
- Communicate and collaborate as necessary with the NNNP/WCS Tourism manager and team on all aspects of tourist activities taking place at MDK.

**Management of MDK Camp, Food Stocks, and Facilities**

- Oversee the submission, preparation, and arrival of food orders for the MDK site.
- Ensure MDK camp facilities are properly maintained.
- Ensure MDK Research staff maintain proper use and care of field equipment.
- Work with WCS/GTAP/Tourism and Logistics Departments to minimize the impact of the tourist site construction and footprint on MDK, including wildlife, staff, camp, and operations.

**Qualifications:**

- A master’s degree in Biological Sciences or extensive relevant conservation field research experience.
- Fluency in French and English, both oral and written.
- Good knowledge of animal behavior and ecology is crucial for a successful application, as well as experience in managing a remote field site.
- Previous experience in project management (staff supervision, work-planning and reporting, etc.).
- Knowledge of Excel/Word is mandatory, with working knowledge of GIS, SMART and R also preferable.
- Field tracking and navigation skills (with GPS and compass) are essential, with previous training in wilderness first aid also preferred.
- Previous experience using camera traps for research is also preferred.
- Excellent social and communication skills with local staff and all cooperation partners; s/he should be able to work in a multicultural and multinational environment while living in isolated field camps (solar power, limited satellite internet and no running water).
- S/he needs to be physically fit, enough for forest work in tropical climate.
- Additional skills could be a plus: mechanical aptitude, construction skills, electrical skills and problem-solving mindset.

title: Site and Research Manager - Goualougo
body:
**Location:** Goualougo (Nouabalé-Ndoki National Park), Republic of Congo.

**Reports to**: Nouabalé-Ndoki Director of Research and Biomonitoring.

**Type of contract**: Full-time contract.

**Position Summary:**

We are looking for a dynamic Site and Research Manager to implement and supervise research activities at the Goualougo research site (GLG), oversee camp management, ensure communication and reporting on all site activities, and provide scientific training, supervision, and general capacity building to Research Assistants and students. The successful candidate will have a strong scientific background, a strong interest in conservation and capacity building, and will be enthusiastic about working in remote places in tropical forest. This is a full-time position, and the ideal candidate can commit for a minimum of two years.

**Main tasks:**

**Management of Field Research**

- Supervise the effective implementation of the research protocols at the GTAP field site.
- Coordinate fieldwork of all GTAP’s Research Teams.
- Participate in daily follows/habituation of chimpanzees and gorillas at GTAP.
- Supervise the collection of data (e.g., behavioral observations, health symptoms using Animal Observer App, meteorology, SMART, Cybertracker) at the GTAP site.
- Implement tests of reliability measures to ensure that research team members are collecting data accurately and in a standardized manner.
- Oversee the implementation of the direct observational health program for gorillas and chimpanzees at GTAP.
- Train Congolese Research staff in reduced impact protocols for daily ape follows, behavioral monitoring techniques, use of portable data collection devices, data management, and reporting.
- Contribute to the professional development of the Congolese Research staff at GTAP, including individualized research projects to present in Bomassa and/or Brazzaville.
- Supervise data entry and backups for the GTAP site and collaborate with the Mondika Site and Research Manager to maintain standardized data collection.
- Ensure the quality of collection, storage, inventory, and transport of biological samples (i.e., fecal, insect samples) obtained at GTAP, as well as coordinated shipment to Bomassa.

**Communication and Reporting**

- Organize staff schedules and movement logistics.
- Compile monthly site reports summarizing data collection, field efforts, staff participation, and research highlights which are submitted to the NNNP Director of Research and Ecological Monitoring and the Congo-Apes Project Co-Directors and Site Manager.
- Work with the Congo-Apes Project Co-Directors, Principal Investigators of MDK, and the NNNP Director of Research and Ecological Monitoring to provide transparent, timely supervision of the chimpanzees and gorillas, site, and personnel.
- Represent the research team during tourist visits and actively engage with visiting tourists to enhance their overall experience.
- Communicate and collaborate as necessary with the NNNP/WCS Tourism manager and team on all aspects of tourist activities taking place at GTAP.

**Capacity building**

- Contribute to the professional development of the Research staff at the site, including one-on-one support of research projects to be presented to different audiences nationally and internationally.
- Schedule trainings held at GLG field station and or in Bomassa.

**Human resources**

- Conduct annual staff evaluations of site Research Assistants.
- Contribute to the selection of new hires within the project.

**Site management**

Work in close collaboration with the Congo-Apes Project Manager based in Bomassa, NNNP teams, and the site’s camp staff to ensure the following:

- Efficient planning of staff rotations and presence at the site.
- Effective site logistics and maintenance.
- Excellent stock management (camp and research materials).
- Effective communication and organization of all operations at the sites, including visits of researchers, communication teams, and donors.
- Ensure optimal implementation of ape/staff health protocols, research, site logistics, and overall functioning of the project, including care of field equipment.
- Assist in overseeing and maintaining site infrastructure and construction activities.

**Qualifications:**

- A master’s degree in Biological Sciences or extensive relevant conservation field research experience.
- A minimum of working proficiency in French and English, both oral and written.
- Good knowledge of animal behavior and ecology is crucial for a successful application, as well as experience in managing a remote field site.
- Previous experience in project management (staff supervision, work-planning and reporting, etc.).
- Knowledge of Excel/Word is mandatory, with working knowledge of GIS, SMART and R also preferable.
- Field tracking and navigation skills (with GPS and compass) are essential, with previous training in wilderness first aid also preferred.
- Previous experience using camera traps for research is also preferred.
- Excellent social and communication skills with local staff and all cooperation partners; s/he should be able to work in a multicultural and multinational environment while living in isolated field camps (solar power, limited satellite internet, and no running water).
- They need to be physically fit enough for forest work in a tropical climate.
- Additional skills could be a plus: mechanical aptitude, construction skills, electrical skills, and problem-solving mindset.

title: Project Manager / Assessment Researcher
body:
## **Job Description: Project Manager / Assessment Researcher**

**Program:** Iraq Higher Education AI Workforce Readiness Program

**Location:** Baghdad, Iraq (full-time, in-person)  
**Duration:** 12 months

### About Development Gateway

[Development Gateway: An IREX Venture (DG)](https://developmentgateway.org/) is an international non-profit organization with approximately 80 team members based in more than 15 countries worldwide. By leveraging the combination of programmatic and IT developer capacity and skills within DG, over the last 20 years we have *researched* data ecosystems, *built* digital tools to support those data ecosystems, and *advised* on data strategy and digital transformation to strengthen decision-making, transparency, and service delivery.

### **Position Summary**

The Project Manager / Assessment Researcher will serve as the senior in-country lead for Development Gateway (DG) on the Iraq Higher Education AI Workforce Readiness Program, a 12-month program implemented with IREX in coordination with institutional partners in Iraq. Based in Baghdad, the Project Manager will manage delivery of Development Gateway's workstreams while leading the research that establishes a baseline of AI readiness across Iraqi higher education institutions (HEIs).

This is a role for a professional who is comfortable working on strategic questions and on technical detail. The Project Manager will manage the program workplan, budget, and reporting; lead the AI ecosystem mapping, the virtual university survey, and stakeholder interviews; and turn the findings into a visual baseline report and individual university factsheets. The role will also guide the design of the in-person AI workforce convening and the AI readiness roadmaps, and will advise program leadership on political, institutional, and technical risks as they emerge.

The Project Manager will build and maintain relationships with Iraq government institutions, university leaders, U.S. technology firms, and the funder, and will guide and mentor the AI Technical Specialist and other technical colleagues so that their work stays complementary and linked to program goals. The role reports to DG's program leadership and works daily with the IREX Iraq team and a distributed DG team.

### **Key Responsibilities**

#### **Project Management and Delivery**

- Lead day-to-day management of DG's activities under the program in Iraq, ensuring timelines, deliverables, and budgets are met.
- Develop, maintain, and update work plans, MEL plan, activity trackers, and budgets in coordination with IREX and DG colleagues, and adjust direction as new priorities or contextual realities emerge.
- Ensure accurate and timely programmatic reporting to IREX, DG, and the funder, coordinating inputs across the team and partners, in English and Arabic as required.

#### **AI Readiness Assessment and Research**

- Lead the AI ecosystem mapping and rapid diagnostic of priority government institutions, private sector partners, and universities, in close partnership with the AI Technical Specialist and IREX counterparts and with support from the Deputy Director of Programs, adapting the AI readiness methodology developed by IREX and DG to the Iraqi context.
- Manage the virtual AI readiness assessment, including survey adaptation, the virtual orientation workshop, and participant support, with a target of at least 40 institutions across federal Iraq and the Kurdistan Region.
- Conduct 20 to 30 interviews with Ministry officials, university leaders, U.S. technology firm representatives, and other stakeholders, and review relevant policies, strategies, and grey literature.
- Analyze the data, including regional comparisons for the Southern and Western provinces and the Kurdistan Region, and produce a highly visual baseline report and 2-page factsheets for each participating university.

#### **Strategic Advisory**

- Maintain a view across all program workstreams, identify emerging political, institutional, and technical risks early, and propose practical solutions and adjustments to program leadership.
- Provide analytical input to and quality review of external-facing knowledge products, including the baseline report, factsheets, briefs, and roadmaps.
- Promote and support strategic and business development opportunities for DG in Iraq as required.

#### **Stakeholder Convening and Partnership Building**

- Lead engagement with government partners and university leadership to align the program with national AI and higher education priorities, working in close coordination with IREX and the funder.
- Guide the planning of the in-person Private Sector and Iraqi AI Workforce Convening, facilitate working sessions, and steer discussions toward concrete use cases, skill needs, and partnership commitments with U.S. and Iraqi employers.
- Guide the development and virtual validation of AI readiness roadmaps for selected universities, and represent DG at external events and in meetings with partners.
- Mentor and guide the AI Technical Specialist and other technical colleagues, and contribute to a collaborative working culture across DG and IREX teams in Baghdad.

### **Qualifications**

#### **Required Qualifications**

- **Education:** Bachelor's degree in public policy, education, information systems, a STEM field, or a related discipline.
- 7+ years of experience working in complex, multi-stakeholder environments, with a track record of managing project delivery and high-level institutional relationships, preferably on donor-funded programs.
- Demonstrable experience building strategic relationships with government stakeholders in Iraq, ideally in higher education, alongside subject-matter experience in higher education, digital policy, or workforce development.
- Experience designing and conducting applied research and assessments, including surveys, key informant interviews, and document review, and analyzing mixed-methods data.
- Experience guiding, mentoring, or coordinating technical staff and consultants across teams and organizations.
- **Language:** Professional fluency in written and spoken Arabic and English, with strong communication and diplomacy skills.
- **Work authorization:** Must have existing work authorization in Iraq.

#### **Preferred Qualifications**

- Master's degree in education, public policy, or a technology-related discipline.
- Demonstrable experience in AI policy or AI in education, including familiarity with national AI strategy developments in Iraq.
- Experience with U.S. Government-funded awards and with consortium-based programs involving several implementing partners.
- Experience organizing workshops, conferences, or convenings that include private sector participants.

Position Details

This is a full-time embedded in the IREX office in Iraq. The expected annual compensation range is **USD $42,000-$45,000**, depending on relevant experience. The position is for the duration of the project, which is 12 months.

DG will review applications on a rolling basis until the position is filled. Interviews are expected to begin in early November.

title: Erasmus Internship - Community Intern
body:
**Contract length:** 4–6 months, with a possible paid 6-month extension based on performance and budget availability

**Hours:** flexible,  
20-40 hours per week, during CET core working hours (Monday to Friday)

**Location:** Amsterdam or Lyon (to be confirmed) Hybrid arrangement: office-based with some remote flexibility

**Travel:** none, except relocating to Amsterdam or Lyon

**Reporting to:** Language Access and Engagement Specialist

Erasmus+ supports traineeships (work placements, internships) abroad at any workplace for students currently enrolled in higher education institutions in Program Countries at short-cycle Bachelor and Master level as well as for doctoral candidates. These opportunities are also open to recent graduates.

Erasmus+ traineeships are open to any student enrolled in a higher education institution holding an Erasmus+ Charter for Higher Education.

The traineeship must be relevant for the degree-related learning and personal development needs and, wherever possible, be integrated in the study program.

A traineeship can take place at any organization located anywhere in the world (with the exception of EU institutions, bodies and agencies).

CLEAR Global (previously known as Translators Without Borders) is an equal-opportunity employer, committed to having a diverse team where individuals of all backgrounds collaborate and learn from one another. We believe we can be most effective with diverse experience and expertise in our team. We recruit on merit, actively seek diverse applicant pools and encourage candidates of all backgrounds to apply. We do not discriminate on the basis of disability, age, gender identity and expression, national origin, race and ethnicity, religious beliefs, marital or parental status, or sexual orientation, and welcome all types of diversity.

Within CLEAR Global, the Influence & Language Justice (I&LJ) team sits at the intersection of language access and movement building. The team currently leads the integration of Tarjimly into CLEAR Global, bringing together two large and active communities of language volunteers and professionals around a shared language justice mission. Our work spans community engagement, advocacy, and operational support for language access initiatives across humanitarian contexts. As an intern on this team, you will be embedded in day-to-day activities that are both community-facing and behind the scenes, contributing to work that has a real impact on how people access information in their own language.

**The role**

Assist the Community team in engaging a volunteer community of over 200,000 language professionals, coordinate collaboration among volunteers, ensure healthy growth of the volunteer community, as well as timely and effective communication.

**Responsibilities**

- Maintain effective communication with community members, ensuring they remain engaged and have a clear understanding of expectations
- Assist with outreach to new community members, both strategically and in response to crisis
- Support in the planning, logistics and management of community engagement events and activities
- Support in the recruitment of community members for in-CLEAR Global roles and their training and preparation for these
- Support in the monitoring and development of community member dialogue within digital platforms
- Support CLEAR Global teams in identifying opportunities for community member involvement within workflows and activities
- Support the development of role descriptions, coordination structures and processes for community member engagement initiatives
- Support community members in their experience with CLEAR Global, and ensuring that various community programs and processes run efficiently
- Carry out administrative tasks, data entry and data collection
- Handle other community management tasks as assigned
- Other duties as required

Please note that these roles and responsibilities are approximate and may change over time.

**Qualifications**

- Eligible for the Erasmus+ traineeship
- Fluent in spoken and written English; knowledge of other languages an advantage
- Strong communication skills, with particular awareness of intercultural contexts
- Previous experience in translation and/or interpreting (internships and volunteering are considered valid experiences) an advantage
- Previous experience working with non-profit organizations an advantage
- Familiarity with technology (with a special focus on translation and/or data entry tools) a plus

**Requirements**

This internship position is very dynamic. The right person is an energetic team player and an individual who agrees with CLEAR Global´s basic beliefs and values and who can work productively in a remote setting, while interacting regularly with the international team.

- Self-starter and able to work independently
- Strong organizational skills
- Analytical thinker able to transform ideas into tangible actions
- Understands that communication in the right language is key to improved humanitarian response
- Team player, collaborative, adaptable and self-motivated
- Interested in acquiring translation and community management experience
- Able to adapt to new technologies and learn new skills quickly
- Has enthusiasm for humanitarian work
- Reliable and flexible and has the ability to uphold the Core Values of the organization
- Able to work during CET core hours

**About CLEAR Global**

CLEAR Global exists to help people get vital information, and be heard, whatever language they speak. We believe that everyone has the right to give and receive information in a language and format they understand. We work with nonprofit partners and a global community of language professionals to build local language translation capacity, and raise awareness of language barriers. Our network of over 200,000 community members translate millions of words of life-saving and life-changing information a year.

**Core values**

CLEAR Global employees and volunteers are people who believe passionately about the value of this work and take personal responsibility for achieving the mission. CLEAR Global’s mission and organizational spirit embody the core values established in its strategic framework:

- Excellence: As the leading voice for communicating humanitarian information in the right language, CLEAR Global is a leader in the translation industry and in the non-profit sector.
- Integrity: CLEAR Global believes that every person, whether it’s the people who we serve, our volunteers or our staff, has value, deserves respect and has inherent dignity.
- Empowerment: CLEAR Global believes in using language to empower people around the world to control their own development and destiny.
- Innovation: CLEAR Global recognizes and celebrates the power of innovation to address humanitarian and crisis issues around the world.
- Sustainability: CLEAR Global recognizes that meeting our mission necessitates establishment and maintenance of a solid financial and organizational infrastructure.
- Tolerance: Our staff and volunteers are highly knowledgeable and skilled; value each other, our partner and our recipients; create a supportive work environment; and, conduct themselves professionally at all times.

*CLEAR Global may re-advertise the vacancy, cancel the recruitment, offer an appointment with a modified job description or for a different duration at its discretion.*

title: Area Coordinator (national)
source: Agency for Technical Cooperation and Development
body:
**About Acted**

For the past 30 years, Acted has been working at the forefront of humanitarian action to save lives. Acted supports more than 27 million people in 43 countries, meeting their needs in hard-to-reach areas, while pursuing a triple mandate as a humanitarian, environmental, and development actor.

**Job Purpose**

The ***Area Coordinator*** provides high-level strategic guidance, quality assurance, and humanitarian coordination for Acted activities within their designated geographic area. This role focuses on translating external field realities into actionable project strategies, driving critical thinking, and mentoring staff.

The Area Coordinator is responsible for representing Acted's interests with area local authorities, donors, beneficiary communities and other key stakeholders. This includes all external engagement on behalf of capital COO or PCs as well as management of MOUs, exploratory meetings with LA’s and other government officials, and donors.

The Area Coordinator is a member of the senior management team and works to ensure program quality and operational implementation, as well as growth where appropriate and feasible, and strong representation. The Area Coordinator collaborates with Project Coordinators ensuring that projects and programs address beneficiary needs and are implemented according to Acted's global strategy, donor guidelines, approved work plans and budgets. The Area Coordinator also oversees day-to-day operations and security in the respective areas.

**Duties and Responsibilities**

***DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES***

**I. Strategic Input & Critical Thinking**

- Act as the primary strategic representative for responsibility area at regional UN Cluster meetings, Humanitarian Hubs, and (I)NGO forums.
- Initiate and lead regular meetings and information exchanges with other international and local NGOs, external engagement with NGO platform, UN/OCHA, partner INGOs, partner NNGO/CSOs, operating in relevant geographic areas.
- Establish regular dialogue channels with local Ukrainian universities, think tanks, and local research institutes. Leverage academic and institutional data and research to refine organizational program design.

**1.1. Networking, positioning and general representation:**

- Participate in donor meetings at area level and communicate relevant information to the Country Director and other relevant staff;
- Establish, maintain and improve active and regular working relationships with other NGOs, UN agencies, clusters, working groups, consortia, etc. at area level ensuring maximum visibility of Acted
- Establish, maintain, and improve active and regular working relationships with local authorities and where necessary non-state actors and obtain required authorizations and buy-in for Acted's activities at area level
- Development and application of the Acted country strategy at area level and tie ins to Country strategy.
- Ensuring Acted representation and positive relationship building in the responsibility area including MOUs with hromadas/oblasts, + gaining traction in municipal space discussions.

**II. Strategic Debriefing & Local Authority Analyses**

2.1 Context analysis: Ensure Acted has an up-to-date understanding of the area's socio-economic situation, trends, needs and gaps, and who does what and where (eg using 4W, other sourced data).

2.2 Strategy Implementation: Take a lead role in implementing Acted's country program strategy in the area identifying strategic opportunities for expanding Acted's work in the area, and in particular:

1. Identify new opportunities and new sectors of intervention;
2. Consolidate and stabilize programming;
3. Review the geographic and thematic footprint;
4. Ensure activities are relevant and meeting area/beneficiary needs;
5. Identify Acted added value;
6. Ensure humanitarian principals are adhered to;
7. Contribute to identifying new donors, private sector partners, national and international NGOs, think tanks, academia, etc. to work with in the area based on complementarity and added value

**III. Program Quality, Internal Coordination, and Advocacy**

**3.1 Program Quality, Development, and growth:**

- Matrix Guidance: Provide operational and strategic guidance to Project Coordinators (and Managers as useful), ensuring project implementation aligns with overall country strategies and donor commitments.
- Operational Troubleshooting: Identify implementation bottlenecks across departments and facilitate collaborative, cross-functional problem-solving sessions to unblock field activities.
- Proposal Input: provide inputs for CNs, proposals, N/CEs with high-quality, evidence-based field analysis derived from local operations, *hromada* interactions, and external networks.

3.1.1. Proposal development:

1. Lead assessment(s) at area level to ensure proposals are relevant; create and contribute to concept notes using local knowledge
2. Support the Country Director and Project Development Department in proposal conceptualisation (problem statement, logframe) within the framework of the country, regional and global strategy
3. Contribute to budget design and ensure budget needs at area level have been taken into consideration

3.1.2 Project Implementation Tracking:

1. Supervise Project Managers/Officers in the area as needed, and provide support to project implementation through trouble shooting and eliminating blocking points
2. Monitor output achievement and cash burn rates to assist timely completion of projects through review of BFUs and project reports
3. Anticipate and mitigate risks ensuring operations in the area are compliant with Acted finance, logistics, administration/HR, transparency and security (FLATS) procedures
4. Ensure that relevant project information is up-to-date and available for reporting purposes
5. Ensure coordination and complementarity amongst projects within the area of intervention

3.1.3. Project Quality Control:

1. Ensure the application of a practical field-based MEAL system/plan for each project
2. Conduct frequent field visits to project sites to assess activities and ensure efficient use of resources
3. Advise Project Managers to adapt projects according to monitoring and evaluation findings
4. Ensure beneficiary feedback mechanisms are in place
5. Ensure capitalisation of best practices and lessons learnt for projects in the area of operations, and explore options to learn from other areas and teams.

3.1.4. Partner Management:

1. Identify potential local partners in the area based on an assessment of complementarity and added value
2. Provide support to partners in project implementation and ensure timely and qualitative implementation of projects by partners in line with Acted and donor requirements

**3.2. Internal Coordination & collaboration**

ACs will work collaboratively with internal department heads, project coordinators, and capital coordination to achieve mission results. They are an integral part of FLATS and SMT meetings and coordination.

3.2.1. Internal Coordination and Staff Management

1. Facilitate interdepartmental communication and information sharing for a positive working environment
2. Ensure implementation of Acted coordination mechanism at area level
3. Ensure that all staff in the area understand and are able to perform their roles and responsibilities related to area operations and link with the capital Head of Departments to discuss improvement initiatives
4. Promote team building, productivity and staff welfare
5. Mentor and support the team to build capacities, and improve efficiency and performance, and follow career management
6. Manage interpersonal conflicts among staff at area level

3.2.2. Finance Management:

1. Although budgets are generally held at Capital level, the AC should be able to advise on project budgets at area level to help PCs avoid under/over spending.
2. Collaborate with Finance teams and PCs to ensure accurate budget forecasting and efficient cash flow management; lead Area BFU preparation and maintenance.
3. Assist with timely and accurate area finance TITANIC reporting, as requested

3.2.3. Logistics & IT Management:

1. Ensure timely procurement and adherence to rules of origin and nationality at area level
2. Ensure quality supply management at area level
3. Ensure proper asset management at area level and enforce asset investment policy
4. Ensure proper stock management at area level
5. Ensure proper IT systems, data back-up and protection from malware at area level
6. Ensure sufficient and reliable means of communication at area level
7. Ensure fitting office and guesthouse space depending on size of team and availability of budget
8. Assist with timely and accurate area logistics TITANIC reporting

3.2.4. Administration and HR Management:

1. Ensure transparent and timely recruitment of national staff and contribute to international staff recruitment upon capital request
2. Proactively advise Head of Department managers and Country Coordination around adaptive staffing structures, tailored to area needs and funding parameters
3. Ensure regular performance appraisal and career management for staff at area level
4. Assist with timely and accurate area HR TITANIC reporting, as requested
5. Ensure timely and complete exit forms

3.2.5. Transparency/Compliance Management:

1. Minimize risk of fraud and corruption by ensuring adherence to Acted FLATS procedures
2. Ensure that staff is aware of Acted's transparency and whistle blowing policy
3. Ensure appropriate action from departments and teams for department and project documentation, and uploading onto Archive 2.0

3.2.6. Security Management:

1. Analyse the security context at area level and in close collaboration with the Country Security Manager contribute to defining, analysing and evaluating risks
2. Engage with relevant key stakeholders at area level to ensure access and support of interventions
3. Address security and safety risks by implementing standard operating procedures defined for the area
4. Ensure the offices and houses conform to recommended security, health and safety standards
5. Ensure all staff in the area adhere to security procedures
6. Ensure security incidents at area level are promptly reported to the capital

**3.3. Advocacy**

The AC should act as both a collector of information for processing and use in Acted country proposals/strategy, as well as being an area advocate in groups and collective NGO meetings to discuss and formalize issues, and to raise relevancies for Country Coordination to follow through with state bodies as needed.

3.3.1. Advocacy: Contribute to drafting issues papers, advocacy notes, press releases on relevant humanitarian and development issues in the area of operation.

3.3.2. Promotion of Acted network: Keep abreast with and contribute to Acted's global initiatives and global trends, in particular Impact (REACH), HQ initiatives (3Zero), and the Acted Humanitarian Network.

**IV. Key Performance Indicators**

- Number of (elected) positions in area-based clusters, working groups, coordination mechanisms
- Knowledge of strategic partners and key stakeholders in area including analysis, networking, stakeholder mapping, and administrative (governmental) relationships
- Number of localised partnerships in the area and improvements catalogued by AC and /or partnerships team
- Number of projects in the area and % change as compared to previous year
- Retention rate among international and national staff
- Regular and timely holding of internal coordination meetings and submission of reports to D/CD
- Proactive contributions to donor reports and concept notes for capital level
- % ineligible expenses incurred at area level and % change as compared to previous year
- % of projects in area with contractual targets/indicators met
- Number of complaints received from beneficiaries and % change as compared to previous year
- FLAT folders are complete and sent to capital office in a timely manner

title: Malawi Case Investigation Senior Coordinator
body:
## About One Acre Fund

Founded in 2006, One Acre Fund equips 5.5 million smallholder farmers to make their farms more productive. Across nine countries that together are home to two-thirds of Africa's farmers, we provide high-quality farm supplies, tree seedlings, accessible credit, modern agronomic training, and a wide range of other agricultural services. On average, this model enables any farmer to increase their income and assets on supported land by more than 35 percent, while permanently improving their resilience. This is all made possible by our team of 9,000+ full-time staff, drawn from diverse backgrounds and professions. To learn more, please see our [Why Work Here](https://oneacrefund.org/careers/why-work-here) blog post.

Our Malawi program, founded in 2016, provides more than 670,000 farmers with quality farm supplies and training. Our office in Malawi is located in Zomba, in the country’s south. One Acre Fund works in Malawi’s southern region, which has the highest concentration of smallholder farmers in the country.

## About the Role

Lead our case investigation team. We are seeking an expert to manage audit execution, drive fraud prevention, and improve internal controls. You'll own a critical role in safeguarding program integrity and supporting our mission for farmers.

## Responsibilities

- Lead and Develop the Team: Manage a team of 4–5 audit officers, conducting regular check-ins, performance reviews, and targeted professional development to keep morale and performance high.
- Oversee Audit Operations: Build the yearly risk-based audit plan, manage weekly team bandwidth, and prioritize urgent ad-hoc fraud or harassment investigation requests.
- Ensure High Quality: Conduct weekly quality checks on reports, shadow field investigations, and provide on-the-ground coaching to close delivery gaps.
- Drive Investigations & Controls: Safeguard the program by investigating staff and farmer fraud, client harassment, and "ghost farmers," while constantly tightening internal control frameworks.
- Collaborate & Troubleshoot: Partner with HR on cash recovery, support Global Legal teams on high-level investigations, and collaborate with Field Operations on anti-fraud campaigns.
- Manage Data & Reporting: Consolidate monthly audit reports for stakeholders, maintain country and global trackers, and populate the Global Client Protection Heatmap.
- Shape the Future Framework: Work hand-in-hand with the Business Operations Lead to transition the team from traditional repayment audits into a pure case investigation unit.

## Career Growth and Development

We have a strong culture of constant learning and we invest in developing our people. You’ll have weekly check-ins with your manager, access to mentorship and training programs, and regular feedback on your performance. We hold career reviews every six months, and set aside time to discuss your aspirations and career goals. You’ll have the opportunity to shape a growing organization and build a rewarding long-term career.

## Qualifications

Across all roles, these are the [general qualifications we look for](https://oneacrefund.org/work-with-us/application-process/qualifications/). For this role specifically, you will have:

- Degree: Bachelor’s degree in Business Administration, Auditing, Accounting, or a related field.
- Experience: 2+ Proven track record in internal/external auditing, risk-based audit planning, and compliance monitoring.
- Technical Knowledge: Deep understanding of internal control frameworks and fraud investigation techniques.
- Data Skills: Basic to intermediate SQL skills and proficiency in at least one BI/visualization tool (e.g., Power BI, Superset).
- Soft Skills: Strong analytical thinking, rigorous attention to detail, and excellent team leadership abilities.

## Preferred Start Date

As soon as possible

## Job Location

Zomba, Malawi

## Benefits

Health insurance, paid time off

## Eligibility

This role is only open to citizens or permanent residents of Malawi.

## Application Deadline

01 November 2026. Please note that we hire on a rolling basis which means that applications are reviewed and processed on a continuous basis until a hire is made.

*One Acre Fund never asks candidates to pay any money or pay for tests at any stage of the interview process. Official One Acre Fund emails will always arrive from an @*[*oneacrefund.org*](http://oneacrefund.org/) *address. Please report any suspicious communication here (globalhotline@oneacrefund.org), **but do not send applications or application materials to this email address.***

*Diversity, Equity, Inclusion (DEI), and anti-racism are deeply connected to our organization’s mission and purpose. One Acre Fund aspires to build a culture where all staff feel consistently valued, represented, and connected – so that our team can thrive as professionals, and achieve exceptional impact for the farmers we serve.*

*We are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, marital status, disability, gender, gender identity or expression. We are proud to be an equal opportunity workplace.*

title: Senior Economic Empowerment Manager
body:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**Job Overview:** The Sr. Economic Empowerment Manager coordinates the development, implementation, and completion of all grants, contracts and activities related to the Economic Empowerment department, including workforce development, small business development, financial capabilities, and career pathways programming. The Sr. Manager provides direct oversight of the Refugee Cash Assistance (RCA) program and the One-Stop Operator program, supervising the RCA Program Manager and the One-Stop Operator Project Manager to ensure both programs are administered in compliance with donor, state, and federal requirements. The Sr. Manager also leads the ongoing development and long-term sustainability of workforce development and career pathways programming. Responsibilities include supervision of department staff to ensure program compliance across all Economic Empowerment programming.

**Responsibilities:** Include, but are not limited to:

**Oversight of Programs:**

- Effectively lead the development, implementation, compliance, and completion of Economic Empowerment grants and contracts.
- Responsible for the development of grant proposals and reports related to all areas of contracts and grants within the department.
- Supervise the provision of services through regular and systematic case file reviews, and quality assurance protocols including data QA to ensure compliance with donor requirements and provision of quality services.
- Lead all aspects of department program budget and manage expenses to ensure costs are maintained within allocated budgets.
- Provide oversight and strategic direction for the Refugee Cash Assistance (RCA) program, supervising the RCA Program Manager to ensure timely, compliant delivery of cash assistance benefits to eligible refugee and new American clients in accordance with Arizona Department of Economic Security (ADES) and federal guidelines.
- Provide oversight and strategic direction for the One-Stop Operator program, supervising the One-Stop Operator Project Manager to ensure integration of workforce development services across system partners and compliance with federal and local workforce standards.
- Lead the development and long-term sustainability of workforce development and career pathways programming, including building new pathways, employer and community partnerships, and funding streams to support program growth.

**Staff Supervision and Other Responsibilities:**

- Directly supervise the RCA Program Manager and the One-Stop Operator Project Manager, in addition to other Economic Empowerment department staff, ensuring each program area is well-led, compliant, and resourced.
- Participate as an active member of the office leadership team and relevant internal and external groups.
- Lead the team members; formally evaluate team and individual performance to ensure objectives have been met.
- Recruit and train staff in all aspects of economic empowerment programs responsibilities.
- Represent IRC in public, professional and governmental forums. Build community partnerships and Lead local outreach to small businesses.
- Facilitate interdepartmental communication and information sharing for monthly newsletters, program reports, etc.
- Other duties as assigned.

**Job Requirements:**

- University degree (four year, B.A.) required; advanced degree in related field preferred.
- 5+ years of related program management experience including staff management, program development, and monitoring and evaluation.
- Previous fundraising and grant writing experience.
- Experience overseeing multiple concurrent programs and program managers preferred; familiarity with Refugee Cash Assistance (RCA)/ADES requirements and workforce system operations (e.g., WIOA, One-Stop/American Job Center models) is a strong plus.
- Demonstrated ability to promote an organizational culture that reflects IRC’s core values of service, accountability, integrity, and equality. Ability to lead through the true collaboration of individuals from many cultures with a great variety of skills and perspectives.
- Strong analytical and training skills; excellent written and oral communication skills.
- Highly organized self-starter with proven success managing multiple priorities, making critical decisions, and delivering results in a fast-paced environment with tight deadlines.
- Solid diplomacy, relationship building, and networking skills; ability to effectively manage internal and external relationships, including community stakeholders and donors.
- Fluent in English, both spoken and written. Proficiency in a second language is desirable.
- Demonstrated proficiency in working with MS Office applications, with a strong command of Excel.
- Valid driver’s license and access to a personal, insured vehicle.
- Must possess or be eligible to receive an Arizona fingerprint clearance card.

**Working Environment:**

- A combination of standard office environment, remote work, and ‘field’ time within the service delivery area to perform the outlined responsibilities.
- May require occasional weekend and/or evening work.

**Compensation:** ($69,939.00 - $92,500.00/annually). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**Benefits:** IRC offers a comprehensive and competitive benefits package. Highlights include 10 paid sick leave, 10 U.S. holidays, 20-25 generous paid time off based on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163/month, dental starting at $6.50/month, and vision starting at $5/month, flexible spending accounts (healthcare, dependent care, and commuter), a 403(b) retirement savings plan with employer match (immediate vesting) along with a non-elective employer contribution based on age and years of service (3-year vesting), disability and life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program (EAP) offering confidential counseling and support services for employees and their families.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

title: Finance Manager
body:
**Kirkens Nødhjelp/ Norwegian Church Aid**

*Norwegian Church Aid ('NCA') is one of the largest aid organisations in the Nordic region. Together with our international network and partner organisations in the ACT Alliance we are able to reach millions of people each year and help make a positive difference around the world. Our mandate is to save lives, build resilience and seek justice and we therefore work with advocacy, long-term development in local communities and providing emergency assistance.*

Are you motivated by ensuring high standards of integrity and compliance, strengthening local capacity and systems, and making a meaningful difference through your work? Then you may be the candidate we are looking for.

**About NCA in Syria:**

*Norwegian Church Aid (NCA) is a non-governmental organisation registered in Norway, founded in 1947 and headquartered in Oslo. As one of the largest aid organisations in the Nordic region, NCA works in more than 30 countries through emergency response and long-term development programmes to support people in need. Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH), alongside the prevention of and response to Gender-Based Violence (GBV), are among NCA’s core areas of work globally. NCA is committed to assisting people regardless of their religious beliefs, ethnic background or political affiliation.*

*NCA has been providing humanitarian assistance in the Middle East for more than a decade. In Syria, NCA established its Damascus office in 2021 and its Aleppo office in 2023.*

**Purpose of the position:**

The Finance Manager is responsible for the overall financial management of NCA Syria. You will oversee accounting, grant management, internal controls and audits, and work closely with senior management, staff, partners, donors and Head Office to ensure transparency, accountability and high quality financial reporting.

**Key responsibilities**

- Ensure compliance with applicable Syrian financial and statutory requirements, including taxation, payroll-related obligations, social security contributions and financial reporting. Review and quality-assure budgets and financial reports, ensure compliance with grant conditions, and follow up on budget variances in a timely manner.
- Verify that financial transactions booked in NCA’s global accounting software adhere to NCA’s accounting principles and procedures.
- Oversee month-end-closings including reconciliations and follow-up of project and all types of balance accounts.
- Maintain and strengthen the internal control systems for both operational and partner‑based activities.
- Manage office budgets, cash flow and treasury operations, including banking arrangements, currency conversions and exchange-rate risks, and ensure that all payments and costs are correctly processed and documented in accordance with NCA procedures and donor requirements.
- Oversee partner financial management throughout the project cycle, including capacity strengthening and corrective actions.
- Lead processes for annual and project financial statements and external audits and follow up audit findings.
- Manage and build staff competence and interdepartmental cooperation.
- Represent NCA on financial matters with authorities, donors and Head Office, as agreed.

**Qualifications and experience**

- A Master’s degree in Business Administration, Accounting or Financial Management
- Certified Public Accountant with accounting experience.
- At least 7 years of experience in financial management, preferably in an International Non-Governmental Organization, including personnel management and technical supervision/quality control.
- Documented and diversified experience in financial and grant management for various governmental and institutional donors such as the UN and EU.
- Experience in ensuring compliance with national financial and statutory requirements. Familiarity with the Syrian regulatory context is an advantage.
- Solid knowledge about internal control measures and how to apply them in practice.
- Strong experience with accounting systems (Maconomy or similar) and advanced Excel skills.
- Highly numerate and able to analyze and interpret financial data to produce timely financial reports that can be understood by non-financial colleagues and that will support program colleagues in project follow up and management.
- Experience from working with national partners in various humanitarian contexts will be considered an advantage.
- Fluency in English is required. Arabic language skills are an advantage.
- Experience from working in high-risk environments is an advantage.

**Personal qualities**

- Structured and systematic, with strong attention to detail.
- Analytical and solutions-oriented.
- Comfortable working independently while collaborating closely with others.
- Strong interpersonal skills and cultural sensitivity.
- A clear and trustworthy communicator, able to build confidence across teams and partners.
- Patient and able to handle large workloads with short deadlines in a calm manner.

**What we offer**

- A meaningful leadership role in a long-standing, reputable organization.
- The opportunity to contribute to humanitarian and development work in a complex and demanding operational context.
- A professional, international work environment with committed and supportive colleagues across country offices and Head Office.
- Competitive salary and benefits.

**Important notes:**

- For international appointments, this is a non-family duty station, requiring the ability to live and work independently in a high-risk context.
- Contract length: 12 months.
- Applicants will be screened, shortlisted and interviewed on a rolling basis.
- Start-up date: as soon as possible.
- This position is open to both national and international (expatriate) candidates.
- Terms of employment: The selected candidate will be offered a contract under either NCA national staff terms or NCA international/expatriate terms, depending on their employment status. Selection will be based solely on the qualifications and competencies outlined in the vacancy notice.
- International (expatriate) candidates must have completed HEAT (Hostile Environment Awareness Training) within the last four years. Those who have not will be required to complete the training within the first three months of employment.
- Duty station: Damascus, Syria, with travel to programme locations as required.

We encourage all qualified persons to apply for a job with us, regardless of gender, age, disability or cultural background. Through our recruitment portal, you can register and submit your CV, write an application / cover letter and attach relevant certificates. Only applicants using this electronic portal will be considered for the position.

**Before you apply:**

We kindly ask you to carefully read the [ACT Code of Conduct for the prevention of misconduct, including corruption, fraud, exploitation an…](https://actalliance.org/wp-content/uploads/2017/01/ACT-Code-of-Conduct-revised-2024.pdf) and NCA’s Policy on [Protection from Sexual Harassment, Exploitation and Abuse and Child Safeguarding policy](https://www.kirkensnodhjelp.no/contentassets/ab6e6f761aa14774b55bd6c08944ad50/nca-pshea-and-cs-policy_word_en.pdf) before you submit your application. These documents outline our commitment to preventing misconduct, including corruption, fraud, exploitation, abuse, and safeguarding children. If you are the selected candidate for this position, you will be asked to complete and sign our **Code of Conduct and Protection from Sexual Harassment, Exploitation and Abuse, and Child Safeguarding Policy.**

In accordance with core humanitarian principles, NCA implements a range of safeguards to prevent or reduce the possibility of humanitarian aid falling into the wrong hands. This includes those individuals and groups who are subject to sanctions by the United Nations Security Council. As part of this process, **NCA will screen the details of the successful candidates for this post against the sanctions lists maintained by the UN and by some of NCA’s governmental donors**.

title: Safeguarding and Ethical Leadership Coordinator for MSF Boards and Associations
body:
**Location:** Any MSF office\*

**Contract:** 100% - Permanent

**Starting date**: 04th of January 2027

**Deadline to apply:** 30th of October 2026

**Compensation and Benefits:** MSF practice is to offer the compensation and benefits package in line with the MSF entity offering the contract.

\*By default, the successful candidate will be offered a contract in the MSF office, able to issue a contract, of their country of residence at the time of application. If no MSF office exists in their country of residence, the successful candidate will be expected to relocate to a country where an MSF office can issue a contract, provided the local legislation allows for that.

**MSF INTERNATIONAL**

Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) is an international, independent, medical humanitarian organisation that delivers emergency aid to people affected by armed conflict, epidemics, healthcare exclusion and natural disasters. MSF offers assistance to people based only on need and irrespective of race, religion, gender or political affiliation. MSF International is the legal entity that binds MSF’s 24 sections, 28 associations and 19 branch offices together. Registered in Switzerland, MSF International provides coordination, information and support to the MSF Movement, as well as implements international projects and initiatives as requested.

**SAFEGUARDING REQUIREMENTS FOR THE ROLE**

The incumbent commits to contribute to a safe, supportive, inclusive, equitable, diverse, respectful, and healthy workplace, and associative spaces free from abuse and other misconduct. They will not engage in any form of abuse including those detailed in MSF Typologies of Abuse and when an employee suspects or observes abuse, they will report it (without investigating it) to protect others.

**I. CONTEXT**

MSF is committed to creating a safe, respectful, and dignified environment for its patients, their caretakers, and the communities in which it works, and for all its volunteers and staff, board and associative members. To this end, all sections of MSF have adopted Behavioural Commitments designed to ensure all staff are aware of their obligations to create workspaces free from abuse and inappropriate behaviour. MSF is committed to safeguarding and ensuring zero tolerance of inaction on abuse.

MSF is continuously strengthening its safeguarding work, and safeguarding remains a top organizational priority. In line with this organization commitment, MSF has created a Board Strengthening Programme, as well as Ethical Leadership Minimum Standards (ELMS) applicable to all board members. As safeguarding expands, MSF’s associative structure is working to adopt the highest standards of safeguarding for and amongst its members.

**II. PURPOSE OF THE JOB**

The Safeguarding and Ethical Leadership Coordinator for Boards and Associations supports the implementation, operationalisation, monitoring, and continuous improvement of MSF’s safeguarding work with boards and associations across the MSF movement. This reflects the International Board’s commitment to minimum standards for safeguarding in associative networks.

The role:

- leads coordination and implementation efforts that translate safeguarding principles, commitments, policies, and standards into practical, measurable, consistent, coherent, and sustainable safeguarding practices across MSF’s boards and associative structures.
- advances safeguarding culture change by supporting MSF boards in understanding their role in safeguarding leadership and oversight; and by supporting the development of robust safeguarding understanding and putting in place safeguarding measures within associative structures and associations.
- contributes to strengthening prevention, detection, reporting, response to safeguarding cases.
- promotes accountability and institutional learning on safeguarding across the MSF movement.

**III. ACCOUNTABILITIES**

**A. Coordination, design, and implementation:**

- Lead the coordination, implementation, and training on the ELMS, as well as on safeguarding, and other ethics principles within MSF boards.
- Translate safeguarding and ELMS concepts into actionable documents, processes, and initiatives for MSF boards associations/networks in line with existing MSF initiatives on safeguarding.
- Develop implementation guidance, tools, frameworks, templates, and operational resources.

**Key Accountabilities:**

- Safeguarding ambitions are translated into practical implementation plans and deliverables.
- Implementation progress is systematically tracked, monitored, and reported.
- Approaches, tools, trainings, and guidance are developed and used by relevant stakeholders.

**B. Drive safeguarding culture change:**

- Drive integration of safeguarding as a core organizational practice across MSF boards and associations.
- Strengthen safeguarding accountability and leadership engagement, and ownership.
- Other tasks assigned by the ISC or the International President or their delegate.

**C. Lead monitoring, accountability, learning, and continuous improvement on Safeguarding and Ethical Governance:**

- Monitor implementation progress, identify risks and gaps, and drive corrective and improvement actions where needed.
- Analyze ELMS and safeguarding implementation, challenges, and lessons learned to inform strategic decision-making.
- Produce implementation reports, dashboards, briefing papers, presentations, and governance updates.
- Lead learning and knowledge-sharing initiatives related to safeguarding and ELMS implementation and best practices.

**Key Accountabilities:**

- Safeguarding is embedded into MSF associations and boards’ ways of working.
- Safeguarding considerations are integrated into associative and boards’ processes.
- Organisational awareness and ownership of safeguarding responsibilities is increased across the MSF associations and boards.

**D. Coordinate the framework and response to ELMS and safeguarding complaints involving senior leadership:**

- Ensure relevant frameworks and processes relating to triage, case management, investigation, and decision-making are implemented for ELMS and safeguarding complaints involving senior leadership (the incumbent will not engage, case management, investigations or decision-making directly, but rather ensure it is in place).
- Reception, and coordination, initial review and assessment of safeguarding and ELMs allegations involving senior leadership (i.e. General Directors and board members). Ensure a decision-making panel is formed for ELMS-related complaints, and ensure their decision is reported to the International Board.

**Key Accountabilities:**

- Ensure that ELMs related complaints are properly assigned to relevant experts for case management/investigation.
- Ensure a decision-making panel is formed for safeguarding or ELMs-related complaints, and ensure their decision is reported to the International Board.

**AUTONOMY, COMPLEXITY**

The role is responsible under the technical supervision of the ISC and the hierarchical supervision of the International President (or the IP’s delegate). The role will coordinate closely with:

- the Board Strengthening Programme concerning board training and direct board support activities with respect to safeguarding and ELMS implementation.
- the International Associative Team to ensure appropriate association support and training activities with respect to safeguarding.
- the ILD to ensure legal risks and statutory requirements are duly considered.

The role uses subject matter expertise, analysis, independent judgement and translates safeguarding, and ethical governance initiatives (such as the Ethical Leadership and Minimum Standards), and other safeguarding initiatives and concepts into relatable, understood, actionable documents, trainings, and actionable initiatives that support to ensure all parts of MSF have a robust understanding of, and structures that support safeguarding.

The role needs a strong understanding of, safeguarding policies, codes of conducts-including ethical governance principles, and how to draft them for associations (non-staff), alongside an understanding of the role of trustees and Boards as oversight for safeguarding.

The incumbent will also need to understand case management and administrative investigations to be able to explain these concepts and how they relate to oversight and associations.

The incumbent will also need to have good understanding of confidentiality, and act with the utmost discretion, when following up, and arranging that safeguarding and ELMs complaints involving senior leadership are properly and promptly addressed.

**V. REQUIREMENTS**

**Education**

A master's degree in relevant field such as law, human rights, administration etc. Or a bachelor's degree combined with significant relevant experience in safeguarding, governance of non-profits.

**Experience**

- A minimum of 5 years implementing safeguarding initiatives, especially with boards.
- Strong understanding of case management and administrative investigations in a workplace setting and principles guiding case management and ability to explain these concepts.
- Experience working with or as a board member for a non-profit organization.
- Experience drafting key safeguarding documents.
- Experience in designing and delivering safeguarding training.
- MSF experience is an asset.

**Knowledge / Skills**

- Strong understanding of safeguarding, conflicts of interest and the role of a trustee/governance of non-profit organisations.
- Ability to draft appropriate and relevant safeguarding standards/documents and to translate complex concepts into clear actions.
- Ability to coordinate and work with a range of stakeholders in a consultative, diplomatic fashion.
- Strong writing skills and ability to communicate safeguarding concepts simply to a range of audiences.
- A strong understanding of monitoring and evaluation.
- Demonstrated experience in coordinating or overseeing highly sensitive cases involving senior leadership; receiving and appropriately triaging sensitive allegations; governance and due-process principles; management of conflicts of interest and recusal; commissioning and oversight of independent investigations; confidentiality, secure information management and data protection; whistleblowing and retaliation considerations; and the ability to navigate complex situations involving boards, senior executives, safeguarding and legal functions.
- Demonstrated ability to lead complex implementation and coordination initiatives across diverse stakeholders.
- Ability to influence organisational change in multicultural environments.
- Strong strategic coordination and implementation management skills.
- Perseverance and ability to build consensus.
- Independence of judgement and the ability to challenge senior stakeholders, when necessary, alongside diplomacy and consensus-building.
- Demonstrated ability to drive accountability and follow-through across multiple workstreams.
- Ability to navigate sensitive safeguarding issues with discretion, diplomacy, and sound judgement.
- Cross cultural awareness and strong commitment to and understanding of diversity, equity, and inclusion principles.

**Languages**

English, other languages are an asset, especially French and Spanish.

**Other**

Motivation to work in a humanitarian organisation and a fast paced, dynamic environment.

**Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.**

**At MSF, we are committed to an inclusive culture that encourages and supports the diverse voices of our employees. We welcome applications from individuals of all genders, ages, sexual orientations, nationalities, races, religions, beliefs, ability status, and all other diversity characteristics.**

**MSF is committed to preventing abuse, inappropriate behaviour, lack of integrity and financial misconduct in its work and care spaces. MSF expects all staff to share this commitment and promote an environment where abuse and misconduct is not tolerated.**

**We are committed to removing barriers for people with specific accessibility needs. If you need an adjustment to the recruitment process to be considered for the role, please let us know from the beginning of the selection process.**

**Note: All offers of employment will be subject to reference checks and to appropriate screening checks. By submitting an application, the job applicant confirms his/her/their understanding of these recruitment procedures.**

title: Multi Country Representative for MENA, based in Amman
body:
## **BACKGROUND ON IMPACT INITIATIVES**

[IMPACT Initiatives](http://www.impact-initiatives.org/) is a humanitarian NGO based in Geneva, Switzerland. The organization supports evidence-based decision-making for humanitarian and development programming through data collection, analysis, and dissemination.

IMPACT is the implementing partner of REACH, a multi-agency initiative created in 2010 that supports humanitarian actors to improve planning and decision-making through in-depth, reliable information and analysis. All of IMPACT’s programs are implemented in support of humanitarian coordination structures.

IMPACT’s team comprises specialists in data collection, management, and analysis, as well as experts in humanitarian response, GIS, and remote sensing.

**We are currently looking for a Multi-Country Representative (MCR)** to oversee integrated missions and lead regional engagement in the Middle East and North Africa (MENA).

**Position**: Multi-Country Representative (MCR)

**Contract duration**: 24 months (100%)

**Location**: Amman, Jordan

**Starting Date**: ASAP.

## **REGIONAL PROFILE**

In 2025, IMPACT opened a Regional Hub in Amman, Jordan. This office hosts integrated missions across MENA, including country-based or remote programmes that are not sustainable as fully independent missions. The office also hosts regional and support teams.

As of June 2026, IMPACT has two *independent* missions in MENA (OPT and Syria) and three *integrated* missions (Yemen, Lebanon, and Libya).

## **FUNCTIONS**

Under the supervision of the IMPACT Regional Coordinator for MENA and Asia, the MCR leads and manages the Multi-Country Office and the regional Hub in Amman. Key functions include:

- **Mission management**: Oversee and lead program teams assigned to or shared across *integrated* missions in MENA (currently Yemen, Lebanon, and Libya).
- **Regional representation and fundraising**: Represent IMPACT with regional stakeholders, lead regional fundraising efforts, and build partnerships outside of *independent* missions.
- **Office and Hub set-up, and operations**: Lead the setup and structure of the Amman Multi-County Office and Hub to host and facilitate regional administrative, operational and programmatic support tailored to regional needs.

## **RESPONSIBILITIES**

***Team management***

- **Direct oversight**: Provide leadership and management to *integrated* mission teams as well as pooled and/or dedicated regional programme staff.[\[1\]](https://reliefweb.int/job/4228657/multi-country-representative-mena-based-amman#_ftn1) Establish team structures that can deliver outside *independent* missions, in line with IMPACT guidance.
- **Regional hosting**: Host regional admin/operations teams and (if needed) de-localized global staff, who remain functionally managed by HQ. Host mission-aligned staff, who cannot be based in their *independent* mission, due to operational / access constraints.
- **Collaborative support**: Work in close collaboration with *independent* missions in the region, while regalian functions and line management responsibilities for *independent* missions remain centralized at HQ.

***Office development and operational oversight***

- **Multi-country office set-up:** Design and implement an efficient administrative and logistical system for the office, aligning it with IMPACT’s global standards.
- **Risk management:** Ensure effective risk management, including security, financial, and operational risks, implementing mitigation strategies in collaboration with HQ.
- **Legal and compliance**: Where relevant, lead IMPACT’s registration process and ensure the office’s compliance with local laws, managing admin or legal challenges.

***Representation and external engagement***

- **Regional representation:** Act as IMPACT’s representative with regional and *integrated* mission stakeholders, including donors, UN agencies, and local partners covering MENA. Remain informed on *independent* mission priorities to support regional donor engagement when relevant.
- **Partnership development:** Build partnerships across the region (i.e., MENA), with a focus on forming robust, sustainable alliances with organizations that can facilitate IMPACT’s research and programmes, beyond established country missions.
- **Context awareness**: Maintain a strategic understanding of regional trends, needs, and opportunities, and coordinate with HQ and *independent* missions in MENA as well to leverage this knowledge for advocacy and to influence relevant decision-making.
- **Strategy and program development**
- **Strategy development**: In coordination with IMPACT HQ, develop a comprehensive regional strategic framework for MENA, defining the vision and priorities for IMPACT’s activities and coverage across the region, beyond existing country missions, as well as for *integrated* country missions, as appropriate.
- **Programme strategy implementation:** Lead team(s) on the development of regional and *integrated* mission programmes, aligned with IMPACT’s regional strategy and continuous contextual analysis.
- **Quality and standards:** Ensure IMPACT’s standards are upheld in all regional and *integrated* mission activities, including global research quality and ethical benchmarks.

***Fundraising and financial sustainability***

- **Donor engagement:** Lead fundraising efforts, engaging with donors and cultivating relationships to secure funding for *integrated* missions and regional programmes.
- **Funding submissions**: In coordination with the Regional Projects and Partnerships Manager (PPM), oversee and contribute to the development and submission of relevant project proposals, concept notes, and donor reports.
- **Financial accountability:** Collaborate with Regional Finance Control Manager (FCM), to oversee budget management, financial forecasting, and reporting to ensure sustainable financial practices of the multi-country office and *integrated* missions.

## **REQUIREMENTS**

- Work experience: Minimum 6 years of relevant experience in humanitarian settings, including experience leading and managing teams.
- Academic qualifications: Master’s degree or equivalent in a relevant discipline (e.g., humanitarian affairs, development studies, social sciences, political science, etc.).
- Demonstrated ability to lead multi-disciplinary teams and manage complex workflows.
- Capacity to work in a cross-cultural, fast-paced environment with tight deadlines.
- Detailed understanding of the humanitarian coordination system, and donor and governmental requirements.
- Experience in external engagement and advocacy with donors, UN, and other humanitarian and development stakeholders.
- Excellent writing and communication skills, including experience producing briefs and presenting to high level stakeholders.
- Fluency in English required; additional languages (e.g., French, Arabic) an asset.

## **COMPENSATION & BENEFITS**

- For this position, salary between 4’860 CHF and 4’920 CHF monthly (before income tax), etc as well as a monthly living allowance of 500 USD
- *NB - IMPACT salaries are strictly determined by our salary grid depending on the grade of the position and the level of education of staff. A location-dependent security and/or isolation adjustment is then applied as a recognition that some staff are required to work in difficult places where living and working conditions are much more difficult than elsewhere.*
- Accommodation and food provided in a guesthouse.
- Enrolment in Swiss private pension fund (Swisslife – approx. 9.975% of staff gross salary), health insurance, life insurance and repatriation assistance
- Flight tickets every 6 months & visa fees covered (in-country travel costs and professional expenses are fully covered)
- Contribution to the luggage transportation: between 20 and 100 kgs, depending on the length of the contract (+ luggage and personal property insurance)
- Annual leave of 36 days per year. Public holidays of the country of assignment. Family/compassionate leave when applicable.
- Predeparture induction - 3 days at IMPACT Initiatives’s HQ in Geneva + one week pre-departure training in ACTED HQ in Paris, including a 4-days in situ security training;
