title: COORDINATOR - UNITED NATIONS UNIVERSITY (UNU) HUB [FIXED-TERM PROJECT POSITION]
source: International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development
body:
## Position overview

ICIMOD is seeking a Hub Coordinator for its newly established United Nations University (UNU) Hub at ICIMOD.

The UNU Hub at ICIMOD is a newly established collaborative platform that advances research, education, and partnerships to strengthen the resilience of mountain communities in the HKH region facing climate and socio-economic change. Building on the long-standing collaboration between ICIMOD; United Nations University Institute for Environment and Human Security (UNU-EHS); Eurac Research, Italy; and the Himalayan University Consortium (HUC), the Hub supports the sustainable management of mountain social–ecological systems, particularly in the HKH. It aims to generate knowledge, foster innovation, and develop a new generation of mountain researchers, practitioners, and leaders. Through research, capacity building, outreach, and advocacy, the Hub promotes evidence-based solutions and regional cooperation for sustainable and climate-resilient mountain development. The focus topics of the first years will be designed as:

- mountain climate risk and adaptation,
- sustainable management of natural resources in mountains, and
- mountain habitability, local knowledge systems and intangible heritage.

The Hub Coordinator will be responsible for the strategic, programmatic, research, and financial coordination of the UNU Hub at ICIMOD. The role includes developing and implementing the Hub’s strategy, leading fundraising efforts and project proposal development, and ensuring sustainable funding. The coordinator will supervise the Hub team; coordinate the Hub steering board, advisory board, and management board meetings; manage technical and financial reporting to partner institutions; and serve as the primary liaison among ICIMOD, UNU-EHS, Eurac Research, and HUC to ensure effective collaboration and the delivery of the Hub’s objectives.

## Person specification/competencies

\[Experience, knowledge, and skills\]

### **ESSENTIAL**

- A Master's degree, preferably a PhD, in a relevant field.
- At least 5 years of project/programme/hub management experience.
- At least 3 years of experience in leading and coordinating large and complex research programmes, including managing partnerships, leading multisectoral coordination, project development, donor liaison, managing interdisciplinary teams, monitoring and reporting, and complex budget management.
- Excellent interpersonal, teamworking and communication skills, both written and spoken, comfortable working with and to all levels, internal and external.
- Excellent communication and report writing skills (in English) and analytical skills with an ability to understand and contextualise research.
- Respect for ICIMOD’s and UN core values

### **PREFERRED**

- Prior work experience with the UN or any international organisation.
- Familiarity with HKH, its social, economic, and ecological context
- Ability to travel within and outside the HKH region.

## Duration

Three-year fixed-term project contract, with a six-month probation period. There is a possibility of an extension, subject to performance, need for the position, and the Hub’s future funding levels.

## Remuneration

This is a Specialist/Senior Officer position at ICIMOD with a competitive salary and benefits. Salary comprises basic salary, provident fund, and family/post adjustment allowance. We offer a comprehensive benefits package which includes insurances (medical, life and accidental), children allowance and children’s education grant for a maximum of 2 children below 18 years of age, severance pay, paid leave (30 holidays and 10 public holidays per year) and day care facility.

For expatriates, there is a tax exemption in Nepal; they are responsible for paying their home country’s taxes. Expatriate staff are entitled to housing allowance, annual home leave ticket, shipment of personal effects, and an installation and repatriation allowance.

## ICIMOD’s core values

Our core values are integrity, neutrality, relevance, inclusiveness, openness, and ambition. These values express our culture and are central to the guiding beliefs and principles of our work and behaviour. Our core values will lie at the heart of ICIMOD operations and delivery. They will underpin everything we do and frame how we work with our partners. They reflect our founding intentions and the balances we seek to hold, while equipping ourselves for the future.

## UN Core Values and Behaviours

**Values:**

- **Inclusion** - Take action to create an environment of dignity and respect for all, regardless of age, culture, disability, ethnicity, gender, gender identity, gender expression, geography, grade, language, nationality, racial identity, religion, sex, sex characteristics, sexual orientation, social origin or any other aspect of identity.
- **Integrity** - Act ethically, demonstrating the standards of conduct of the United Nations and taking prompt action in case of witnessing unprofessional or unethical behaviour, or any other breach of UN standards.
- **Humility** - Demonstrate self-awareness and willingness to learn from others.
- **Humanity** - Act according to the purposes of the United Nations: peace, dignity and equality on a healthy planet.

**Behaviours:**

- **Connect and Collaborate** - Build positive relationships with others to advance the work of the United Nations and work coherently as One UN
- **Analyse and Plan** - Seek out and use data from a wide range of sources to understand problems, inform decision-making, propose evidence-based solutions and plan action
- **Deliver Results with Positive Impact** - Hold oneself and others accountable for delivering results and making a positive difference to the people and causes that the United Nations serves
- **Learn and Develop** - Pursue own learning and development and contribute to the learning and development of others
- **Adapt and Innovate** - Demonstrate flexibility, agility and the ability to think and act in novel ways

## Diversity, equity, inclusion, and safeguarding

ICIMOD’s human resource selection process is based on the qualifications and competence of the applicants. As an employer, ICIMOD is committed to promoting diversity, equity, and inclusion, and offers equal opportunities to applicants from all backgrounds and walks of life, including but not limited to gender, age, national origin, religion, race, caste, ethnicity, sexual orientation, disability, or social status. ICIMOD strongly encourages applications from all eligible applicants, especially women, from all parts of the HKH region.

ICIMOD is dedicated to establishing and upholding a safe and nurturing work environment, where all its employees can participate fully and meaningfully without fear of violence, harassment, exploitation, or intimidation. Any type of abuse or harassment, including sexual misconduct \[including child abuse\], by our staff, representatives, or stakeholders is not condoned or tolerated.

title: Casework Supervisor
body:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

***This position has an end date of September 30, 2027.***

**Job Overview:**   
The Casework Supervisor manages staff providing direct client services across the Program for Initial Resettlement (PIR) and Refugee Social Service (RSS) case management program. The Casework Supervisor plans programming, coordinates service delivery, supervises a team, ensures program goals are met, and satisfies budgetary, compliance, and reporting responsibilities for the assigned portfolio. This position is based in Louisville, Kentucky, with regular on-site presence within the office.

**Major Responsibilities:**

**Staff Supervision responsibilities**

- Lead and develop direct service staff through facilitation of team meetings and individual supervision, including coaching and goal setting.
- Liaise regularly with HQ colleagues for guidance, case consultations, direct financial assistance, and other support as needed, and share relevant information with the casework team.
- Cultivate a respectful and supportive environment for team members and clients.
- Recruit, train, and manage the team in accordance with IRC’s People Manager Standards.
- Carry out timely, professional interventions to ensure responsive, appropriate, and client-centered service delivery.
- Train direct reports on using IRC systems such as Integra, ETO, and IRIS.
- Representing IRC in public, professional, and governmental fora as needed.
- Other duties as assigned.

**Service Delivery**

- Guide PIR program implementation and ensure all required services are completed in a timely manner.
- Assign cases to caseworkers and manage timely provision of services including airport pickups, provision of safe, sanitary, and affordable housing, home visits, school enrollment, domestic health assessments, and connection to community resources as applicable.
- Supervise the RSS Case Management Program, including staff referrals, connection of clients to services, and tracking client participation and progress
- Ensure follow-up on all necessary services, including application to public benefits as applicable, referrals to immigration services, applications for Supplemental Security Income (SSI), and medical and mental health needs.
- Provide oversight so each client receives at least one meaningful interaction every 30 days during their service period.
- Ensure case closeout procedures are followed once a client has reached the goals of their program.

**Partnership Building**

- Manage relationships with property owners and managers to expand access to sources of affordable housing.
- Collaborate with colleagues to encourage timely internal referrals for additional services, such as employment, immigration services, and intensive case management.
- Identify and maintain relationships with local government and community-based organizations to connect clients with necessary benefits and services.
- Develop relationships with community resources such as shelters for temporary housing, domestic violence shelters, mental health providers, and medical specialists.
- Develop and maintain vendor relationships that create budgetary savings and improve efficiency.

**Documentation, Reporting and Contract Compliance**

- Ensure that case file documentation is maintained in compliance with contract requirements.
- Guide the timely implementation of program updates as needed.
- Liaise with the HQ colleagues to ensure thorough understanding of program guidelines and disseminate guidelines to the direct service team.
- Review data to meet donor reporting requirements.
- Assist with the preparation for all monitoring visits, including IRC, the Kentucky Office for Refugees (KOR), and the Office of Refugee Resettlement (ORR).
- Monitor program execution to ensure compliance with all funding requirements; communicate program needs to the management team.

**Job Requirements:**

**Education:**

- Bachelor’s degree is strongly preferred, preferably in social work or related field

**Work Experience:**

- Minimum two to three years of experience implementing domestic refugee resettlement or similar programs
- Experience supervising, supporting, and training staff strongly preferred
- Experience in program management and responsibility for budget management preferred

**Demonstrated Skills and Competencies:**

- Familiarity with Integra, IRIS, SMART, and Efforts to Outcomes (ETO) strongly preferred.
- Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications
- Ability to prioritize and manage time effectively
- Demonstrated ability to work effectively as a team member in a multicultural environment
- Excellent written and oral communication skills in English; proficiency in a language spoken by client populations is a plus
- Valid driver’s license, reliable access to a vehicle with current insurance, and the ability to travel regularly throughout the service delivery area

**Working Environment:**

- A combination of a standard office environment and ‘field’ time in and around the service delivery area to perform the above-outlined responsibilities.
- May require occasional weekend and/or evening work.

**Compensation:** ($$59,962.5 - annually). Compensation is based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements”.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**Benefits:** IRC offers a comprehensive and competitive benefits package. Highlights include 10 paid sick leave, 10 U.S. holidays, 20-25 generous paid time off based on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163/month, dental starting at $6.50/month, and vision starting at $5/month, flexible spending accounts (healthcare, dependent care, and commuter), a 403(b) retirement savings plan with employer match (immediate vesting) along with a non-elective employer contribution based on age and years of service (3-year vesting), disability and life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program (EAP) offering confidential counseling and support services for employees and their families.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

title: Consultancy for the Development of a Facilitation Guide and Facilitation of Trainings for Beach Management Unit (BMU) Members in Kwale County
body:
## **The full Request for Proposals (RFP) document is available at the following link:** [**https://drive.google.com/drive/u/1/folders/17XdKj9sJdsiyUeuwm7_8UrN15OJ6Zo97**](https://drive.google.com/drive/u/1/folders/17XdKj9sJdsiyUeuwm7_8UrN15OJ6Zo97)

## **About CEFA**

**CEFA** - European Committee for Training and Agriculture (Comitato Europeo per la Formazione e l’Agricoltura) is an Italian Non-Governmental Organisation established in 1972 and active in countries across Africa, Latin America and Eastern Europe. CEFA’s medium- and long-term interventions in the agricultural, environmental and human rights sectors focus on the sustainable development of communities, achieved by involving local counterparts and promoting the active participation of beneficiaries.

## Project Summary

The project **AGROBLUE - Promoting Sustainable Agriculture and Blue Economy in Kenya** is a 36-month initiative implemented in four sub-counties (Galole, Tana Delta, Msambweni and Lunga Lunga) within Tana River and Kwale Counties, Kenya. The project is implemented by a consortium of partners with extensive experience in resilient agricultural models and the blue economy, led by Action Against Hunger (ACF) in collaboration with CEFA, MWARP and Politecnico di Milano. The initiative works closely with the Ministry of Agriculture and the Ministry of Health to ensure institutional sustainability and long-term impact.

The project aims to increase food security, income and resilience to food crises through an integrated, climate-smart and gender-sensitive approach. It addresses barriers such as low productivity, high post-harvest losses and the limited economic participation of women by providing farmers and fishermen with the tools, technologies and knowledge needed to diversify their livelihoods and increase their incomes, while protecting natural ecosystems. The project works across three result areas:

- Increasing access for small-scale farmers and artisanal fishermen to products and services for climate-resilient production and fishing systems, and to community practices that prevent ecosystem degradation;
- Increasing access of farming and fishing families in rural and coastal areas to technical and financial services, infrastructure and knowledge to sustainably manage supply chains that add value to their food production, in order to increase and diversify their income;
- Sensitising communities on nutritional needs, with a focus on vulnerable groups such as women and children, to improve access to and consumption of diverse, nutritious food.

Within the project, CEFA works in the fisheries and beekeeping components, targeting farmers’ groups and Beach Management Units (BMUs) through training and the provision of equipment. The intervention adopts a value chain strengthening approach covering production, post-harvest handling and marketing.

## Objectives of the Consultancy

The objectives of the consultancy are:

- The development of a **facilitation guide** covering practical offshore fishing techniques and best practices; basic navigation, including the use of navigation equipment and the interpretation of weather and sea conditions; maritime safety, emergency preparedness and response procedures; sustainable management of marine resources, including marine ecosystem conservation, pollution prevention, overfishing and the impacts of climate change; and fisheries data collection and analysis, including data on fishing fleets, fishers, fishing gear, fishing effort and landings. The guide will provide practical guidance and standardised messages to support the delivery of the planned training sessions.
- The delivery of **four training topics, through five trainings and 18 sessions in total**, to BMU members, including fishermen, boat owners, members of BMU executive committees and fish traders, through refresher and cascading trainings, to strengthen technical skills, maritime safety practices, environmental awareness and the capacity to collect and use fisheries data.

## Timeline and Duration of the Consultancy

The consultancy covers a total of **37 days**:

- 10 days for the design and preparation of the training sessions and the drafting and finalisation of the facilitation guide;
- 24 days for the facilitation of the trainings, divided among the training sessions as set out under Methodology below;
- 3 days for the drafting and submission of the final consultancy report.

The consultancy shall commence in **November 2026** and will extend over a period of four months, concluding in **February 2027**. The allocation and scheduling of the training days will be agreed with the CEFA team according to the availability of participants, the project implementation timeline and the logistical requirements of each session, within the overall number of consultancy days established in the contract.

## Methodology

**Participants**

The trainings will be delivered to members of Beach Management Units, notably:

- Fishermen;
- Members of BMU executive committees (e.g. chairperson, secretary, treasurer);
- Boat owners and individuals involved in eco-tourism activities;
- Fish traders and dealers.

The total number of participants across all trainings will be **501**, drawn from **three** BMUs already selected in Msambweni and Lunga Lunga Sub-Counties.

**Content and Design of the Trainings**

BMU members will participate in five trainings covering, progressively, offshore fishing, marine resource management, maritime safety, and fisheries data collection and analysis:

- **Refresher Training on Offshore Fishing:** 20 members from each of the three BMUs will participate in a two-day training per BMU. The training will focus on practical offshore fishing techniques, navigation, interpretation of weather and sea conditions, and basic safety practices during fishing operations. One practical **at-sea session** is planned as part of the two-day training for each BMU. CEFA will provide the boat and all necessary safety equipment.
- **Refresher Training on Offshore Fishing (Restitution Session):** A one-day feedback and cascading session on offshore fishing will follow, reaching 210 BMU members (70 per BMU) through three sessions, so that the trained participants can pass on the knowledge acquired to a wider group of BMU members. The trained BMU members will deliver the cascading sessions under the supervision of the Consultant.
- **Environmental Impacts and Conflict Reduction in the Use of Marine Resources:** 20 members from each of the three BMUs will participate in a one-day training per BMU. The training will address marine ecosystems and their conservation, pollution and its impact on marine resources, overfishing and sustainable fisheries management, climate change and its effects on marine ecosystems, and approaches to reducing conflicts over the use of marine resources. It will also include a module on co-management areas and co-management plans for sustainable use.
- **Maritime Safety Training for Offshore Fishing:** 50 members from each of the three BMUs will participate in a one-day training, delivered through six sessions in total (two per BMU), each targeting 25 fishermen. The training will focus on the risks of illegal fishing, safety procedures, safe use of protective gear, safe operations at sea, risk prevention, emergency preparedness and response, and appropriate action in case of accidents or other emergencies during offshore fishing.
- **Fisheries Data Collection and Analysis:** 7 members from each BMU will participate in a two-day training delivered through three sessions, for a total of 21 participants. The training will cover data collection methodologies, data sources and basic data analysis, with a focus on fisheries information such as fleet characteristics, number of fishers, fishing gear, fishing effort and fish landings.

## Safeguarding and Do No Harm

The Consultant shall comply with CEFA’s safeguarding, PSEAH (Protection from Sexual Exploitation, Abuse and Harassment), Code of Conduct and data protection requirements. Personal data collected from participants, including attendance lists and pre- and post-training assessments, shall be handled in line with the Data Protection Act, 2019 and used only for the purposes of this assignment.

## Management and Implementation Responsibilities

The Consultant will report directly to the CEFA Project Manager and the CEFA Project Officer in charge of AGROBLUE implementation.

The Consultant will be responsible for their own insurance during the contract period, and CEFA will not be responsible for any injury or damage incurred during the assignment. The Consultant will also meet their own communication and incidental costs. The Financial Proposal must include all anticipated expenses, including travel to and from the assignment sites, local transport in Kwale County, meals and accommodation.

## Qualifications of the Consultant

**Essential**

- A minimum of a bachelor’s degree in Fisheries, Marine Resources, Aquaculture or a related field from a reputable institution;
- Relevant professional experience in fisheries development, sustainable fisheries management, offshore fishing, marine ecosystem conservation and/or capacity building of fishing communities and BMUs, preferably at least 7 years;
- Demonstrated experience in training fishermen and/or BMU members in the thematic areas of this assignment;
- Strong participatory training and facilitation skills, and good report-writing skills;
- Ability to deliver training in Kiswahili and English.

**Desirable**

- Previous experience working with fishing communities on the Kenyan coast, particularly in Kwale County.

title: Digital Development and Connectivity Program Specialist
body:
***Candidates must be authorized and able to work daily in Bogotá.***

**Position Summary**

The Digital Development and Connectivity Program Specialist serves as the Foreign Assistance Unit's (FAU’s) technical adviser for digital-infrastructure and connectivity programming across South America. The position provides technical analysis and recommendations to support Government officials in identifying, assessing, and structuring U.S. Government-funded digital development programs that advance U.S. foreign-policy and national-security objectives and respond to partner-country priorities. The portfolio may include information and communication technologies (ICT) deployment (fiber, wireless, satellite, and last-mile connectivity), digital inclusion strategies, cybersecurity considerations for critical digital infrastructure, and broadband/connectivity expansion planning.

The incumbent reports to the FAU’s Programs Team Lead and translate digital connectivity needs into technically credible and implementable program designs. Responsibilities include preparing technical scopes of work; contributing to program-design and acquisition or assistance documents; reviewing proposals, market studies, network designs, specifications, cost estimates, schedules, and other technical products; and providing input to the FAU on technical alternatives, implementation risks, project readiness, sustainability, and operations and maintenance considerations. The Specialist collaborates with other FAU technical and program personnel to ensure that digital infrastructure investments are appropriately incorporated into sector-specific programs.

Drawing from practices used across the U.S. Department of State and other U.S. Government agencies, the incumbent provides technical analysis and recommendations to support programming aligned with the America First foreign policy framework, including economic security, strategic competition, trusted and secure digital infrastructure, supply chain resilience, and partnerships that reinforce U.S. interests. The salary will be commensurate with an FSN 11 position within Colombia.

**Major Duties and Responsibilities**

**1. Strategic Digital Infrastructure Program Development (35%)**

Supports the identification, assessment, and design of USG-funded digital-connectivity programs that advance U.S. foreign-policy and national-security objectives. Responsibilities include:

- Identifies potential digital-development programming opportunities based on USG priorities, partner-country needs, connectivity gaps, existing investments, and regional market developments.
- Supports programs involving ICT infrastructure deployment, broadband and last-mile connectivity expansion, digital inclusion initiatives, secure network architecture, and cybersecurity-conscious infrastructure design.
- Translates connectivity needs and policy objectives into technically credible, feasible, and sustainable program concepts.
- Supports the development of technical scopes and statements of work, program descriptions, acquisition and assistance planning documents, budgets, implementation approaches, and other program-design products.
- Develop recommendations regarding the technical scope and requirements for market assessments, network design studies, cybersecurity risk assessments, digital-inclusion needs analyses, and other project-preparation activities.
- Provides technical recommendations regarding requirements, performance standards, implementation assumptions, schedules, cost parameters, and risk-mitigation approaches in collaboration with relevant FAU personnel.
- Assesses project readiness, technical feasibility, implementation risks, operational requirements, and the capacity needed to operate and maintain proposed digital infrastructure.
- Incorporates sustainability, commercial viability, and operations and maintenance considerations throughout program design.
- Coordinates technical, programmatic, procurement, financial, monitoring, and stakeholder inputs into coherent digital-development programs.
- Supports the adaptation, expansion, or modernization of existing connectivity programs when performance findings, policy changes, or market conditions warrant revised approaches.
- Identifies technical capability gaps and provides input on potential needs for short-term telecommunications, network engineering, or cybersecurity expertise.

**2. Technical Review and Quality Assurance (30%)**

Provides technical review and quality-assurance support for proposed and ongoing digital-development activities. Responsibilities include:

- Reviews proposals, market studies, network designs, technical specifications, pricing structures, cost estimates, schedules, work plans, and other technical submissions.
- Conducts market research and performs technical and commercial analysis of proposals for pricing, competitiveness, and commercial viability relative to comparable connectivity solutions.
- Conducts technical assessments of proposedapproaches to evaluate if they are credible, implementable, appropriately scaled, priced, and responsive to program requirements.
- Evaluates design assumptions, technology choices, deployment methodologies, energy and energy storage requirements, equipment specifications, sequencing, and operations and maintenance requirements.
- Reviews technical products for consistency with applicable host-country, U.S., and international standards, including relevant cybersecurity and data-protection standards.
- Compares technical and commercial alternatives and provides recommendations to the FAU on their relative feasibility, risks, lifecycle implications, and expected performance.
- Identifies technical gaps and potential implementation risks—including cybersecurity vulnerabilities—and recommends corrective actions or additional analysis.
- Reviews quality-assurance and quality-control approaches, testing requirements, commissioning arrangements, maintenance plans, and other measures necessary to support reliable digital-infrastructure performance.
- Provides technical input during proposal reviews and other procurement or assistance processes, as requested and consistent with applicable procedures and conflict-of-interest safeguards.
- **Conducts technical reviews for** GORs (Grant Officer’s Representatives), CORs (Contract Officer’s Representatives), and FAU leadership on whether technical products appear responsive to applicable requirements while preserving formal acceptance authority for designated USG officials.
- Confirms that designs, certifications, and other regulated technical products are prepared or approved by appropriately qualified professionals when required.

**3. Digital Infrastructure Portfolio Planning and Strategic Analysis (25%)**

Under Programs Team Lead guidance, provides analysis and planning support to guide the FAU's digital-development and connectivity portfolio. Responsibilities include:

- Maintains visibility over proposed, active, and emerging digital-connectivity initiatives supported by the FAU.
- Develops and maintains a digital-development opportunity pipeline that captures project status, technical-preparation needs, strategic relevance, principal risks, and required next steps.
- Provides analysis and recommendations to inform prioritization of large strategic connectivity investments and community-level digital-inclusion activities based on policy relevance, feasibility, readiness, and potential results.
- Conducts technical assessments of how individual digital-infrastructure activities contribute to broader economic-security, digital-inclusion, or strategic-competition objectives, including trusted-vendor and secure-supply-chain considerations.
- Identifies opportunities to connect digital-connectivity investments with complementary programming managed by other FAU specialists, including training, sustainability, and wraparound services needed to achieve public policy goals alongside commercial viability.
- Identifies recurring technical and management risks across the digital-infrastructure portfolio and recommends improvements to future program design.
- Captures and shares lessons from completed and ongoing activities to strengthen technical quality, implementation, and sustainability.
- Prepares technical briefing materials, analytical memoranda, talking points, and recommendations for FAU and Embassy leadership.

**4. Program Quality, Monitoring, and Reporting (15%)**

Supports GORs and CORs in monitoring assigned programs and awards, and assessing their continued strategic relevance and performance. Responsibilities include:

- Reviews program reports, work plans, technical deliverables, deployment updates, schedules, cost information, and performance data as requested by the responsible GOR or COR .
- Collaborates with the Monitoring, Evaluation, and Learning Specialist to gather, validate, analyze, and synthesize information from assigned programs.
- Participates alongside the responsible GOR or COR in site visits, monitoring activities, portfolio reviews, and meetings with implementers, contractors, government counterparts, private-sector partners, beneficiaries, and other stakeholders.
- Analyzes implementation progress and identifies technical, quality, cost, schedule, management, sustainability, cybersecurity, and operations and maintenance concerns.
- Reviews information on network quality, testing, contractor quality-control processes, security posture, commissioning, and readiness for intended use, as applicable.
- Provides recommendations to GORs and CORs when independent technical review, testing, cybersecurity assessment, or other specialized support may be required.
- Prepares monitoring observations, technical analyses, and evidence-based recommendations for consideration by the GOR, COR, and FAU leadership.
- Supports performance-management processes and internal reporting on program results, implementation risks, lessons, and strategic alignment.
- Supports assessments of whether programs require technical adjustment, additional analysis, specialized assistance, or revised implementation approaches.

All monitoring and award-support functions shall be performed under the direction of the responsible GOR or COR. The Specialist shall not direct recipients or contractors, approve or reject deliverables, certify technical products, modify award requirements, commit USG funds, or exercise responsibilities reserved for authorized USG officials.

**Supervisory Controls**

The Digital Development and Connectivity Program Specialist exercises independent technical judgment in assessing digital-infrastructure concepts, reviewing network and connectivity designs, evaluating cybersecurity considerations, developing technical requirements, and recommending approaches to address implementation challenges. The Specialist consults with the Programs Team Lead, responsible GORs or CORs, and other technical personnel when assignments involve significant policy, procurement, financial, security, or specialized technical considerations.

Work is reviewed for technical soundness, responsiveness to program requirements, compliance with applicable procedures, alignment with USG priorities, and contribution to effective program performance.

**Minimum Qualifications**

**Minimum Education:** One of the following combinations of education and professional experience is required:

- Master's degree in telecommunications engineering, information and communications technology, computer science, cybersecurity, digital development, or another closely related discipline, plus at least six years of relevant professional experience; or
- Bachelor's degree in one of these disciplines, plus at least 10 years of relevant professional experience.

Telecommunications, ICT, computer science, and digital-development degrees are equally acceptable. A professional certification (e.g., PMP, CISSP, or equivalent) is not required but is beneficial.

**Professional Experience:**

- Progressively responsible experience designing, reviewing, deploying, managing, or monitoring ICT and connectivity infrastructure projects.
- At least two years of direct experience with digital-connectivity projects of different sizes, technologies, and sectoral focus.
- Experience in aligning digital communications projects to social and economic development goals.
- Experience conducting market research and evaluating proposals for pricing, competitiveness, and commercial viability.
- Experience assessing cybersecurity considerations relevant to digital infrastructure and connectivity deployments.
- Experience preparing technical scopes of work and assessing project feasibility, implementation risks, quality, sustainability, and operations and maintenance requirements.
- Experience structuring subcontracted training, sustainability, and wraparound services to support public policy goals alongside commercial viability.
- Experience supporting project implementation, site monitoring, and multidisciplinary teams through clear technical analysis and recommendations.

**Preferred Professional Experience:**

- Experience supporting digital-development or connectivity programs funded by the U.S. Government, multilateral organizations, bilateral donors, or international development institutions.
- Experience working with the Department of State, USAID, MCC, USTDA, DFC, another U.S. Government agency, or a multilateral development institution.
- Experience with digital-inclusion strategies targeting underserved or rural populations.

**Language:** Level IV (Fluent) English and Level V (Fluent) Spanish required.

**Skills and Abilities:**

- Design complex international digital-development programs
- Lead proposal development efforts
- Build relationships with private-sector telecommunications and technology companies
- Translate policy into operational programming
- Integrate technical input into coherent program designs
- Develop strategic partnerships
- Communicate effectively with executive audiences
- Manage competing priorities under tight deadlines
- Produce high-quality analytical and written products
- Evaluate commercial pricing and competitiveness of technical proposals

**Comprehensive knowledge of:**

- ICT infrastructure deployment and connectivity-expansion planning
- Digital inclusion strategies and approaches
- Cybersecurity considerations for critical digital infrastructure
- Program design methodologies and proposal development
- Results-based management
- Digital-infrastructure program design and project-management methodologies
- Market research and competitiveness analysis
- Technical risk identification and mitigation

**Working knowledge of:**

- U.S. foreign policy objectives
- Environmental and social considerations applicable to digital-infrastructure activities
- Government digital-infrastructure planning and public-investment processes
- Procurement and implementation models
- Subcontracting structures for training, sustainability, and wraparound services

**Other Requirements**

- **Candidates must be authorized and able to work daily in Bogotá.**

title: Pediatrician
body:
**PAEDIATRICIAN – EBOLA EMERGENCY RESPONSE**

**PURPOSE**

Providing outpatient and/or inpatient paediatric care to patients/beneficiaries according to adapted and updated medical knowledge, MSFprotocols, values and universal hygiene standards to improve the new-born and child/beneficiaries health conditions

**WHO WE ARE LOOKING FOR A PAEDIATRICIAN IN THE DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF THE CONGO – EBOLA EMERGENCY RESPONSE**

- Available for deployment within the next 3 months for your first rotation of 12-16 weeks, followed by a mandatory 21-day post-deployment monitoring period.
- French proficiency (at least B2)
- Experienced in Ebola response, VHF, outbreak, or emergency response (strong asset)
- Flexible and adaptable in fast-changing environments
- Resilient under high-pressure humanitarian conditions
- Committed to teamwork and MSF principles
- Ready for remote and resource-limited field settings
- Medical Doctor diploma in a recognized university
- Paediatrics qualification preferred
- 2 years’ experience minimum as a Medical Doctor in paediatric hospital

**Accountabilities**

- Applying medical knowledge and skills to prevention, diagnosis and treatment of children, ensuring integrated new-born and paediatric care through Emergency, OPD, and IPD services in New-borns and cases of malnutrition. Prescribing the necessary treatment, respecting MSF protocols.
- Collaborating closely with the different department of the hospital (e.g. Maternity), Knowing and ensuring all updated MSF medical protocols and universal precautions are followed and implemented, reducing bio-hazard risks and improving infection control.
- As an expert in paediatrics, proposing strategy (modification on current new-born and paediatric care management) and implementing them after validation of Operation and Paediatric Advisor.
- Ensuring on-going new-born and paediatric training (formal and bedside) of the medical/paramedical multidisciplinary team in order to optimize the new-born and paediatric quality of care. Reviewing and discussing selected complicated cases or mistakes and giving technical input.
- Keeping patients and their families informed of the illness and the treatment to follow, checking that they have been understood. Ensuring professional autonomy and confidentiality are respected and a good attitude and proper bedside manner towards the patient and their care takers and the rest of the medical team.
- Following up the evolution of the hospitalized/IDP patients through daily visits, consultations and examinations, prescribing the necessary treatment following MSF protocols, deciding whether they can be discharged or transferred to other departments – in collaboration with other doctors- and informing their family about the patient’s evolution.
- Monitoring the proper functioning of the department, equipment or material and addresses the list of the missing item for new-born and paediatric activities. Providing inputs about general organization of the different paediatric wards, including the admission, transfer and discharge criteria + referral procedure from Maternity and post-delivery wards
- Checking and controlling the rational distribution of medicines and equipment under his/her responsibility and taking care the quality, disinfection and sterilization of the medical material. Assuring general compliance with standing hygiene standards.
- Participating in the introduction / improvement of the collection and analysis of epidemiological new-born and paediatric data, checking its validity and informing the line manager or project coordinator about any problems or complications of the patient’s illness and medical errors. Collecting Clinical cases for further trainings and list a series of comments to improve the current MSF protocols
- Managing the team under his/her direct responsibility according to MSF HR policies and procedures, supervising their performance, organizing and scheduling shifts and rotations, directly participating in emergencies and on calls if necessary.
- Designing and providing training to staff as required.
- Debriefing with coordination, Headquarter (including Paediatric Advisor) and providing written report on main findings, activities, conclusions and further recommendations.

**What MSF Offers:**

- A fixed-term contract for deployment assignments and additional 21 days
- Travel, accommodation, and medical coverage during missions.
- Daily allowances in line with MSF policies.
- Access to training and professional development opportunities.

title: Chargé.e de Communication Audiovisuelle - Dakar - H/F
body:
ALIMA (The Alliance for International Medical Action) est une ONG humanitaire médicale internationale, créée en 2009. Elle offre des soins de santé de qualité aux populations vulnérables confrontées à des crises sanitaires, des [épidémies](https://alima.ngo/decouvrir/expertises/epidemies-maladies-emergentes/) ou des catastrophes naturelles.

ALIMA intervient lors des crises humanitaires, dans les [zones de conflits](https://alima.ngo/conflits-populations-deplacees/), [d’épidémies](https://alima.ngo/decouvrir/expertises/epidemies-maladies-emergentes/) et de malnutrition où les besoins médicaux sont les plus urgents. ALIMA associe des [soins d’urgence](https://alima.ngo/reponse-urgences/) à des [projets de recherche de plus long terme](https://alima.ngo/decouvrir/expertises/recherche-innovation/) pour développer de nouvelles solutions et améliorer durablement la prise en charge des populations les plus vulnérables.

8 domaines d’expertise

- [Épidémies et maladies émergentes](https://alima.ngo/decouvrir/expertises/epidemies-maladies-emergentes/)
- [Malnutrition](https://alima.ngo/decouvrir/expertises/malnutrition-aigue/)
- [Santé des femmes](https://alima.ngo/decouvrir/expertises/sante-femmes/)
- [Pédiatrie](https://alima.ngo/decouvrir/expertises/pediatrie/)
- [Santé mentale](https://alima.ngo/decouvrir/expertises/sante-mentale/)
- [Recherche et innovation](https://alima.ngo/decouvrir/expertises/recherche-innovation/)
- [Renforcement du système de santé](https://alima.ngo/decouvrir/expertises/renforcement-systeme-sante/)
- [Chirurgie](https://alima.ngo/decouvrir/expertises/chirurgie-humanitaire/)

ALIMA collabore avec des autorités sanitaires nationales et locales, des [ONG locales](https://alima.ngo/agir/nous-soutenir/devenir-partenaire/partenaires-operationnels/), des communautés, et des instituts de recherche pour bâtir des solutions humanitaires innovantes et adaptées. Son siège opérationnel à Dakar reflète son ancrage au plus près du terrain et 95 % de ses équipes viennent des pays d’intervention.

Depuis 2009, ALIMA a soigné plus de 46 millions de personnes dans [ 16 pays](https://alima.ngo/decouvrir/nos-operations/), principalement en Afrique. L’organisation se distingue par son expertise en [malnutrition](https://alima.ngo/decouvrir/expertises/malnutrition-aigue/), [pédiatrie](https://alima.ngo/decouvrir/expertises/pediatrie/), [santé des femmes](https://alima.ngo/decouvrir/expertises/sante-femmes/) et [réponse aux épidémies et maladies émergentes](https://alima.ngo/decouvrir/expertises/epidemies-maladies-emergentes/), entre autres.

Grâce à la [recherche et à l’innovation](https://alima.ngo/decouvrir/expertises/recherche-innovation/) issues de l’expérience sur le terrain, et au renforcement des capacités locales dans nos pays d’opération, ALIMA s’efforce de transformer la médecine humanitaire et de mieux protéger les populations des crises sanitaires de demain.

**PRÉSENTATION DU POSTE**

**Liens hiérarchiques et fonctionnels** :

**Superviseur hiérarchique** : Responsable de la Communication digitale

Personnels sous sa responsabilité hiérarchique : aucun

Il/elle collabore avec :

- L’équipe Communication (siège et pays)
- Les Missions dans les pays et les Desks au Siège de Dakar
- L’équipe Développement / Collecte (Sénégal, France, USA, UK, Suisse)
- L’équipe Bailleurs
- Les équipes et partenaires Recherche
- Les prestataires externes

**Enjeux du poste** :

Garantir la qualité, l'éthique et la cohérence de tous les contenus photo et vidéo d'ALIMA, de leur production à leur archivage, afin de rendre compte de l'action d'ALIMA dans le respect de la dignité des personnes accompagnées.

**Missions et objectifs** :

Conformément aux orientations stratégiques et aux priorités fixées par la Direction de la Communication, vous avez pour missions principales de :

- Monter et postproduire les vidéos d’ALIMA
- Concevoir et animer des contenus en motion design (vidéos explicatives, infographies animées, habillages…)
- Concevoir, écrire et tourner des contenus vidéos, au siège et sur le terrain
- Garantir la qualité et la cohérence des contenus vidéos et photos produits par les équipes pays et les prestataires
- Produire des photos en appui, selon les besoins
- Archiver et assurer la traçabilité des contenus audiovisuels (consentements, droits)

**Lieu du poste**

Dakar, Sénégal, siège opérationnel d'ALIMA.

Déplacements possibles pour un besoin de reportage ponctuel le justifiant.

**Activités principales**

1. Monter et postproduire les vidéos d’ALIMA

● Narration et dérushage stratégique

- Visionner, trier et dérusher les rushs (tournages en propre, équipes pays, prestataires)
- Construire un récit clair et rythmé : repérer les moments forts, structurer la narration et maintenir l’attention du spectateur du début à la fin
- Monter des formats variés : formats courts réseaux sociaux (verticaux et carrés), témoignages et reportages terrain, vidéos bailleurs et institutionnelles et formats longs

● Rythme et plans d’illustration (B-roll)

- Intégrer des plans d’illustration pertinents pour dynamiser les interviews et casser la monotonie du « face caméra »
- Privilégier les images d’ALIMA et encadrer l’usage des banques d’images (ex : photos AFP)

● Conception sonore (sound design)

- Traiter et égaliser la voix principale, nettoyer l’audio (bruits de fond, niveaux)
- Choisir des musiques adaptées au propos, ambiance voulue, avec des droits d’utilisation vérifiés
- Utiliser avec justesse les bruitages et effets sonores

● Finalisation et diffusion

- Réaliser l’étalonnage, créer et relire les sous-titres (français et anglais)
- Réaliser les exports adaptés à chaque plateforme (site, YouTube, LinkedIn, Instagram, Facebook, X , bailleurs)
- Intégrer les retours des équipes et gérer les versions successives jusqu’à validation
- Utiliser l’IA de manière encadrée (transcription, sous-titrage, nettoyage audio)

2\. Concevoir et animer en motion design

- Vidéos explicatives et pédagogiques
    - Concevoir et réaliser des vidéos explicatives animées pour rendre accessibles des sujets médicaux et humanitaires complexes (malnutrition, épidémies, recherche, innovations médicales)
    - Construire le storyboard et le découpage visuel à partir d’un script, en lien avec les chargés de communication et les équipes médicales et recherche
- Data visualisation animée
    - Transformer les données et chiffres clés d’ALIMA (rapports annuels, bilans de réponse d’urgence, résultats de recherche) en infographies et cartes animées, claires et fiables
- Habillage et identité visuelle animée
    - Créer et faire évoluer la bibliothèque d’éléments graphiques animés d’ALIMA : génériques, titres animés, bandeaux nom/fonction, transitions personnalisées, logos animés, cartons de fin et appels à l’action
    - Garantir la cohérence de l’identité visuelle animée sur toutes les productions, internes et prestataires, dans le respect de la charte graphique et de la charte vidéo d’ALIMA
    - Produire des modèles réutilisables (templates) pour accélérer la production
- Formats réseaux sociaux
    - Réaliser des formats courts animés et dynamiques : typographie cinétique, citations animées, carrousels animés, formats verticaux
    - Animer des visuels existants (photos, illustrations, captures d’écran) pour les rendre plus engageants

3\. Concevoir, écrire et tourner les vidéos

- Préparation
    - Être force de proposition sur les sujets et les angles éditoriaux
    - Écrire ou co-écrire les scripts, trames narratives et voix off avec les chargés de communication, et proposer en autonomie des scripts corporate
    - Préparer les tournages : repérages, liste de plans, questions d’interview, logistique
- Tournage
    - Tourner au siège et sur le terrain : interviews, plans d’illustration, événements
    - Mener des entretiens pertinents et en autonomie, mettre les personnes filmées à l’aise
    - Recueillir les informations de contexte (lieu, date, pays, projet, histoire de la personne, soins reçus)
- Éthique, consentement et sécurité
    - Recueillir un consentement éclairé dans une langue comprise par la personne (accord du parent ou du tuteur pour les mineurs), collecter et archiver les formulaires
    - Respecter les règles de sécurité des missions et obtenir les autorisations de tournage (autorités, sites, drone le cas échéant)

4\. Garantir la qualité et appuyer les équipes

- Être le référent vidéo des chargés de communication pays : guides de tournage (smartphone et caméra), briefs, modèles de liste de plans, retours techniques sur les rushs reçus
- Former les équipes à distance ou lors des missions, notamment à l’utilisation des templates d’habillage
- Gérer les prestataires au siège, de l’expression du besoin au paiement de la facture : cahier des charges, devis, supervision du tournage, validation, suivi des droits et crédits
    - Les commandes aux prestataires dans les pays restent gérées par les chargés de communication pays et le Responsable Communication Opérations
- Assurer une veille sur les formats, tendances vidéo et motion design, et proposer des formats innovants, notamment pour les réseaux sociaux

5\. Produire des photos

- Réaliser des photos lors des tournages, des missions et des événements (portraits, activités, siège et missions ALIMA)
- Assurer la postproduction des photos (sélection, retouche) et rédiger les légendes détaillées (projet, bailleur, contexte)
- Appliquer les mêmes règles de consentement et d’éthique que pour la vidéo

6\. Archiver, gérer les droits et le matériel

- Organiser et classer les fichiers sources, projets de montage et d’animation, éléments graphiques et exports finaux
- Enregistrer les contenus validés dans le Drive et/ou la Media Gallery (Bynder), avec légendes et tags pertinents, en coordination avec le/la Chargé.e de communication en charge de la Media Gallery
- Assurer le suivi des consentements, des droits musicaux
- Entretenir et sécuriser le matériel et le studio, tenir la fiche des entrées et sorties du matériel

## Expériences & Compétences

- Niveau d’étude
- Formation supérieure en audiovisuel, montage, motion design, cinéma ou design graphique, ou expérience professionnelle équivalente
- Expérience
    
    
    - Expérience d’au moins 5 ans en montage vidéo, dont 2 à 3 ans en motion design
    - Références techniques en conception et production de supports photos et vidéos (Portfolio obligatoire)
    - Références techniques en écriture de scripts vidéos
- Connaissances en langues
    
    
    - Excellente maîtrise en Français et bonne maîtrise en anglais
    - Excellente maîtrise des deux langues écrites (relecture des sous-titres des vidéos)
- Compétences
    
    
    - Excellente maîtrise du montage et de la narration vidéo (Premiere Pro ou DaVinci Resolve)
    - Excellente maîtrise du motion design 2D (After Effects) et de la création graphique (Illustrator, Photoshop)
    - Savoir-faire en écriture de script vidéo et de storyboards
    - Maîtrise du traitement sonore, de l'étalonnage et du sous-titrage
    - Maîtrise des suites Google Workspace et Microsoft Office
    - Bonne maîtrise de la prise de vue vidéo et photo : cadrage, lumière, prise de son, interviews et reportage terrain
    - Retouche photo (Lightroom)
- Autres qualités
    
    
    - Sens du récit, créativité et sensibilité à l'éthique de l'image
    - Autonomie, rigueur, respect des délais
    - Capacité à travailler sur plusieurs projets en même temps et à prioriser
    - Esprit d'équipe

## Conditions

- **CDI de droit sénégalais**
- **Prise de poste** : Dès que possible
- **Salaire** : selon la grille de salaire en vigueur au Siège de Dakar.
- Avantages extra contractuels :
- Cinq semaines de congés payés par an et système de jours de récupération pour les déplacements
- Couverture santé complémentaire pour l’employé et ses ayants droit.

title: Senior Compensation & Benefits Advisor, EU and Strategic Initiatives- UK or NL
country: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
body:
**Location:** UK, or NL flexible working from home (NL base location preferred)

**Status:** Full-time

**Starting salary range:** NL: € 70,920; UK: £60.030; hiring range commensurate on professional experience

[**Risk Level:**](https://library.mercycorps.org/record/47705?ln=en) ☐ **Level 3** ☐**Level 2** ☐**Level 1**

(Level 3: Frequent contact with participants, direct contact with children, access to sensitive data, and/or high level of accountability.

Level 2: Some contact with participants; unplanned non-direct contact with children.

Level 1: Likely to have no contact with participants or sensitive data)

**About Prosper Global**

Barely enough is not enough for anyone. Prosper Global is a humanitarian organization working alongside communities facing conflict, climate change, and economic hardship to meet urgent needs and create the conditions for lasting progress. Today's challenges demand new solutions, so we pair local knowledge with global resources to help communities build what's needed, test what's possible, and scale what's proven so that people everywhere can pursue a full life on their own terms. In 2026, we changed our name from Mercy Corps to Prosper Global, to reflect our belief that when every community can prosper, all of humanity moves forward.

## **The Department**

The People Team ensures that Prosper Global has the people, strategies and learning that will enable it to be a world-class, cutting edge, humanitarian organization, creating transformational change in the world. We do this through the recruitment, retention and development of the best global talent. Our aim is to drive strategic thinking and planning at all levels of the organization; create a robust body of research to guide us internally and externally and steward the organizational culture. To achieve this, we align conversations on learning; keep the organization focused on what has the greatest impact; leverage our comparative advantages in the crowded and competitive international relief and development landscape; and assure we are constantly learning from our work and the external environment.

## **The Position**

The Senior Compensation and Benefits Advisor – Europe & Strategic Initiatives designs and delivers compensation, benefits, and performance management frameworks that support a diverse workforce across European markets and globally.

This role develops and implements total rewards strategies that enhance the organization’s ability to attract, retain, and incentivize top talent from the private sector, impact investing, and tech sectors. With a strong emphasis on performance management and value creation, the role ensures that compensation and benefits structures are aligned with organizational outcomes and impact objectives. They partner closely with global teams, regional leadership, and HR team members to ensure that compensation and benefits frameworks are market-relevant and performance-driven.

Working closely with senior leadership, the role drives the design and execution of compensation and benefits frameworks and tools. They build global HR capacity and provide strategic advisory support. A strong focus is placed on data-driven decision-making, pay equity, and continuous improvement in line with evolving business and investment priorities.

The position serves as a strategic partner, strengthening cross-functional collaboration and ensuring that total rewards approaches are aligned, performance-oriented, and scalable across global operations.

## **Essential Responsibilities**

**Strategy, Planning & Continuous Improvement**

- Champion and operationalize the organization’s People Strategy, ensuring alignment between pay practices and innovation objectives.
- Partner with leadership to define and execute a forward-looking total rewards and performance management strategy, linking compensation to financial, operational, and impact performance.
- Drive continuous improvement initiatives by identifying gaps, inefficiencies, and opportunities across compensation and benefits programs and processes.
- Influence organizational and regional strategies through data-driven compensation insights that support growth, equity, and impact.
- Lead the design and implementation of scalable, globally consistent compensation and benefits frameworks and tools.
- Build and maintain strategic external partnerships.

**Compensation, Benefits & Performance Advisory**

- Familiar with different compensation structures and statutory benefits across Europe, bring working knowledge and practical experience.
- Design, implement, and refine global salary structures, grading frameworks, and pay policies aligned with market competitiveness and organizational goals.
- Lead regular market benchmarking and salary analysis to ensure competitive, equitable, and compliant pay practices.
- Drive improvements in job evaluation, role architecture, and pay-for-performance methodologies.
- Integrate compensation frameworks with performance management systems, ensuring clear links between individual performance, growth outcomes, and reward.
- Develop and harmonize benefits strategies across European jurisdictions, ensuring competitiveness, compliance, and employee well-being.
- Stay on top of employment law in European countries with Prosper Global presence, so the organization can proactively adapt.
- Provide strategic advisory support to leadership on compensation, performance calibration, workforce planning, and organizational design.

**Strategic Improvement Projects**

- Design and implement key improvement initiatives that align Prosper Global's compensation and benefits with the organization’s strategic direction, including:
    - Partner with Prosper Global Europe HR and Talent Acquisition to support strategies to attract and retain high-performing professionals across Europe from private sector and impact investing backgrounds.
    - Develop performance-related pay principles and establish incentive structures to align with organizational growth and impact metrics.
    - Support operationalizing the organization’s framework to global mobility to ensure compliance, employee retention, and equitable compensation decisions. Own and implement the organization’s global mobility workstream, including reviewing and advising on requests, with executive, HR, and legal input.
- Develop metrics, dashboards, and reporting frameworks to track performance, inform decisions, and support continuous improvement.

**Communication, Influence & Stakeholder Engagement**

- Communicate compensation and benefits initiatives clearly to internal stakeholders, strengthening understanding and engagement.
- Partner with innovations teams, HR, and leadership to ensure alignment between talent, performance and reward strategies.
- Build internal capability through coaching and guidance on compensation, benefits, and performance management best practices.
- Collaborate with Talent Acquisition to position total rewards as a competitive advantage in attracting top-tier talent in private markets.

**Personal Leadership & Organizational Values**

- Demonstrate resilience, adaptability, and professionalism in complex and dynamic environments.
- Promote innovation by encouraging new approaches to problem-solving within organizational frameworks.
- Foster a high-performing, inclusive team culture focused on learning, accountability, and innovation.
- Uphold high ethical standards and model organizational values in all interactions.

**Safeguarding Responsibilities**

● Actively learns about safeguarding and integrates it into their work, including safeguarding risks and mitigations related to their area of work.

● Practices the values of Prosper Global including respecting the dignity and well-being of participants and fellow team members.

● Encourages openness and communication in their team; encourages team members to submit reports if they have any concerns using reporting mechanisms e.g., Integrity Hotline and other options.

### **Supervisory Responsibility**

None.

### **Accountability**

**Reports Directly To:** Global Compensation and Benefits Director

**Works Directly With:** People Team, Europe HR, Talent Acquisition, and global and regional leadership

### **Accountability to Participants and Stakeholders**

Prosper Global team members are expected to support all efforts toward accountability, specifically to our program participants, community partners, other stakeholders, and to international standards guiding international relief and development work. We are committed to actively engaging communities as equal partners in the design, monitoring and evaluation of our field projects.

### **Minimum Qualification & Transferable Skills**

- 5+ years of experience managing total rewards or compensation and benefits programs at a private sector company, investment firm, or development bank.
- Familiar with different compensation structures and statutory benefits across Europe, bringing working knowledge and practical experience.
- Experience managing global programs and designing performance-related pay structures is highly preferred.
- Bachelor’s degree or equivalent in Human Resources, Business Administration or related field, preferred.
- English proficiency required.
- Project management skills including the ability to create and execute plans within established deadlines. Strong problem-solving skills, interpersonal skills, and written and verbal communication.
- Strong analytical skills and a thorough knowledge of compensation and benefit plan designs. Ability to understand how to leverage compensation and benefits programs to align with industry best practices

### **Success Factors**

The successful team member will be an avid learner, self-directed, innovative and action orientated. Furthermore, they must have the ability to work independently, employ effective time management skills, handle frequent interruptions and shift priorities, exhibit effective customer service skills and work effectively with a wide variety of individuals including team members based overseas.

They will be able to work onsite and collaborate with team members, deliver compelling designs within the guidelines of specific project objectives and interact professionally and productively with HQ and other global staff. Additionally, the individual will thrive in a fast-paced environment prone to rapid change and be willing to increase his/her responsibility level in the assigned areas.

The most successful Prosper Global team members have a positive approach, a strong commitment to teamwork and personal accountability, and the ability to be flexible and ensure effective communication is a priority in all situations.

### **Living Conditions / Environmental Conditions**

The position is based in UK or Netherlands and may require occasional travel to support country programs, which may include travel to insecure locations where freedom of movement is limited and areas where amenities are limited.

### **Ongoing Learning**

In support of our belief that learning organizations are more effective, efficient and relevant to the communities we serve, we empower all team members to dedicate 5% of their time to learning activities that further their personal and/or professional growth and development

### **Team Engagement and Effectiveness**

Achieving our mission starts with how we build our team and collaborate. By bringing together individuals with a variety of experiences, backgrounds, and perspectives, we strengthen our ability to solve complex challenges and drive innovation. We foster a culture of trust and respect, where every team member is valued for their contributions, empowered to reach their full potential, and motivated to do their best work.

We recognize that building a strong and effective team is an ongoing process, and we remain committed to learning, improving, and growing together.

**Equal Employment Opportunity**

Prosper Global is an equal opportunity employer committed to providing equal employment opportunities to all employees and qualified applicants for employment without regard to race, color, sex, sexual orientation, religion or belief, national origin, age, disability, marital status, veteran status, or any other characteristics protected under applicable law.

**Safeguarding and Ethics**

Prosper Global is committed to ensuring that all individuals we come into contact with through our work, whether team members, community members, program participants or others, are treated with respect and dignity. We are committed to the core principles regarding prevention of sexual exploitation and abuse laid out by the UN Secretary General and IASC **and have signed on to** [**the Interagency Misconduct Disclosure Scheme**](https://www.schr.info/the-misconduct-disclosure-scheme). We will not tolerate child abuse, sexual exploitation, abuse, or harassment by or of our team members. As part of our commitment to a safe and inclusive work environment, team members are expected to conduct themselves in a professional manner, respect local laws and customs, and to adhere to [Prosper Global Code of Conduct Policies](https://www.mercycorps.org/who-we-are/ethics-policies) and values at all times. Team members are required to complete mandatory Code of Conduct elearning courses upon hire and on an annual basis.

As an applicant, if you witness or experience any form of sexual misconduct during the recruitment process, please report this to Prosper Global Integrity Hotline (integrityhotline@prosperglobal.org).

title: Community Conservation Coordinator – Gabon
body:
**Report to:** Technical Director  
**Location:** Libreville, Gabon  
**Country Program**: Gabon  
**Position Type**: Full-Time  
**Collaborators:** Regional Right and Communities team, Community and Conservation Team, MEL Teams, Environment and Social Safeguards Team, relevant departments of institutional partners, notably the ANPN and the Ministry of Water and Forests, Finance, Logistics, Human Resources, and Administration departments  
**Expected Travels:** WCS project sites in Gabon (national parks: Ivindo, Lopé, Mayumba, Loango, and other sites depending on the projects)

**Job Summary**

The Community Conservation Coordinator is responsible for defining, implementing, and monitoring WCS Gabon’s community conservation strategy.

As part of WCS’s broader Rights and Communities team, he or she ensures that conservation initiatives are grounded in human rights-based approaches and aligned with WCS strategies, policies, and standards at the national, regional, and global levels.

The incumbent coordinates community activities at WCS project sites, supervises field teams, and builds strong relationships with local communities and institutional partners to foster active and inclusive participation in conservation efforts.

**Key Responsibilities**

**Development and implementation of the community conservation strategy:**

- Develop and adapt WCS Gabon’s national community conservation strategy to the local context.
- Support the development and implementation of community strategies at the site level.
- Identify priorities for community engagement and promote initiatives that strengthen community support for conservation goals.
- Contribute to the revitalization and operation of the Community-Based Local Management Committees (CCGL).
- Ensure coordination with the ANPN to guarantee alignment with national guidelines.
- Ensure consistency between community activities and other program components (biomonitoring, law enforcement, tourism, etc.).

**Coordination and Supervision of Field Teams**

- Supervise technical assistants, project managers, research assistants, and field teams involved in community activities.
- Plan and monitor the implementation of field activities.
- Monitor the implementation of activities by partners and contractors.
- Provide technical support to the teams and resolve operational challenges.

**Training and capacity building**

- Train field teams in community-based conservation approaches and outreach methods.
- Develop appropriate educational tools and materials.
- Strengthen the teams’ skills and performance through regular monitoring.

**Engagement and Community Relations**

- Build and maintain trusting relationships with local communities, community leaders, and local authorities.
- Promote inclusive and respectful community participation in conservation initiatives.
- Ensure adherence to ethical principles of respect for individuals, benevolence, and justice.
- Ensure that free, prior, and informed consent is systematically sought for any activity involving communities.
- Ensure the quality of community activities (local governance, livelihoods, environmental education).
- Ensure that community feedback is taken into account, particularly through complaint management mechanisms.

**Monitoring, Evaluation, and Reporting**

- Ensure that activities comply with WCS’s community conservation standards and national regulations.
- Contribute to the implementation of tools for monitoring and controlling activities.
- Support the design and implementation of socioeconomic studies and data collection activities.
- Produce regular reports on activities.
- Help draft funding proposals and document best practices.

**Required Qualifications and Experience**

- Master’s degree or equivalent in social sciences, rural development, conservation, natural resource management, anthropology, sociology, or a related field.
- At least 7 years of relevant professional experience, including at least 3 years in roles involving coordination, team supervision, or program/project management.
- Substantial experience in designing and implementing community-based conservation approaches, local development, or community-based natural resource governance.
- Proven experience working directly with rural communities and Indigenous peoples, including in facilitating participatory processes and multi-stakeholder consultations.
- Experience in operational planning, monitoring work plans and indicators, and supervising teams and/or implementing partners.
- A solid understanding, backed by practical experience, of rights-based approaches, inclusive participation, and the principles of FPIC, social safeguards, and grievance mechanisms.
- Experience collaborating with government agencies, civil society organizations, and/or international organizations.

**Skills and Qualities**

- Strong skills in managing, coordinating, and supporting teams, including remotely.
- Ability to translate a strategy into priorities, work plans, and operational results at the site level.
- Excellent facilitation, communication, negotiation, and constructive conflict management skills.
- Ability to analyze and synthesize information, particularly socio-economic data and information relevant to program planning.
- Very strong writing and reporting skills.
- Fluency in French; ability to work in English strongly preferred.
- Willingness to travel frequently to WCS sites in Gabon.

**Strengths**

- Professional experience in Gabon or Central Africa.
- Knowledge of protected area governance issues and community representation/consultation mechanisms.
- Experience with projects funded by international donors.
- Experience contributing to the design of projects or funding proposals.

title: Malawi Farmer Behavior & Extension Design Lead
body:
## **About One Acre Fund**

Founded in 2006, One Acre Fund equips 5.5 million smallholder farmers to make their farms more productive. Across nine countries that together are home to two-thirds of Africa's farmers, we provide high-quality farm supplies, tree seedlings, accessible credit, modern agronomic training, and a wide range of other agricultural services. On average, this model enables any farmer to increase their income and assets on supported land by more than 35 percent, while permanently improving their resilience. This is all made possible by our team of 9,000+ full-time staff, drawn from diverse backgrounds and professions. To learn more, please see our [Why Work Here](https://oneacrefund.org/careers/why-work-here) blog post.

Our Malawi program, founded in 2016, provides more than 670,000 farmers with quality farm supplies and training. Our office in Malawi is located in Zomba, in the country’s south. One Acre Fund works in Malawi’s southern region, which has the highest concentration of smallholder farmers in the country.

## **About the Role**

The Agronomy & Extension Lead will own the implementation of Malawi’s extension strategy, using HCD and SBC approaches to translate agronomic recommendations into simple, practical and adoptable support for farmers. The role will strengthen extension delivery, training and communication content, and use farmer feedback and impact data to continuously improve our approaches. They will work closely with Field Operations and Innovations to turn validated research into scalable farmer-facing solutions.

## **Responsibilities**

The role combines technical agronomy leadership with the design and management of a practical, farmer-centered extension system.

Own Malawi's agronomy and extension strategy

- Co-design and maintain a multi-year strategy aligned with Malawi’s impact priorities and farmers’ needs.
- Turn the strategy into annual OKRs, budgets, seasonal plans and clear ownership across teams.

Embed extension in Field Operations execution

- Build agronomy and extension priorities into the Field Operations seasonal calendar, training cascade, field tools and performance routines.
- Strengthen the technical capability of Field Managers, Field Officers and other delivery partners through training-of-trainers, coaching and practical support.
- Create clear feedback and support channels so field teams receive timely technical answers and can share implementation challenges and farmer responses.

Own the process of qualitative technical agronomic recommendations

- Use Human-Centred Design, farmer feedback and impact data to develop, test and refine agronomic recommendations.
- Work with Innovations, MEL and global technical teams to assess recommendations against local evidence, farmers’ realities and government guidance before they are scaled.
- Conduct formative research to understand farmers’ needs, behaviours and barriers to adoption.

Design farmer-centered extension and behavior-change interventions

- Translate technical recommendations into simple, memorable and actionable guidance for field teams and farmers.
- Develop extension approaches that use the right mix of group training, demonstrations, coaching and digital channels.
- Use the findings to design, test and improve extension approaches and communication content.
- Apply adult-learning, behavior-change and human-centered design approaches to understand barriers to adoption and ensure content works for different farmer profiles.
