Monitor adoption, learning and impact

- Analyze results across farmer groups, locations and delivery channels to identify where recommendations or delivery approaches need to change.
- Lead seasonal learning reviews and maintain clear records of lessons and decisions to continue, adapt or stop interventions or crop offerings.

Build and manage a high-performing team

- Set clear goals, roles and decision-making responsibilities, and hold the team accountable for timely, high-quality delivery.
- Coach direct reports, strengthen the team’s technical expertise and support staff to take on greater ownership.

## **Career Growth and Development**

We have a strong culture of constant learning and we invest in developing our people. You’ll have weekly check-ins with your manager, access to mentorship and training programs, and regular feedback on your performance. We hold career reviews every six months, and set aside time to discuss your aspirations and career goals. You’ll have the opportunity to shape a growing organization and build a rewarding long-term career.

## **Qualifications**

Across all roles, these are the [general qualifications we look for](https://oneacrefund.org/work-with-us/application-process/qualifications/). For this role specifically, you will have:

Technical Expertise

- A bachelor's degree in Agronomy, Crop Science, Agricultural Systems, Agricultural Extension, Sociology, Anthropology, Design or a related field;
- Experience working in the agricultural sector, ideally with smallholder farmers, is strongly preferred.
- At least 5+ years of relevant professional experience in Agricultural Extension, Human-Centred Design, Social Behaviour Change Campaigns, or Rural Marketing, with experience applying these approaches in the agricultural sector
- Demonstrated experience developing, testing or scaling agronomic recommendations or rural extension interventions.
- Experience using adult-learning, instructional-design, SBCC or human-centered design approaches is strongly preferred

Core skills

- Technical judgment: Able to assess agronomic evidence, identify limitations and translate it into responsible recommendations.
- Farmer-centered design: Able to understand farmer constraints and create practical interventions that improve understanding and adoption.
- Data and learning: Comfortable using qualitative and quantitative evidence to make decisions; strong Excel skills required, with R or Stata as an advantage.
- Strategy and project management: Able to prioritize, build critical paths and keep multiple seasonal workstreams on track.
- Communication: Able to make complex technical information simple and persuasive for field teams, farmers, leaders and external partners.
- Collaboration and influence: Able to work across Field Operations, Innovations, MEL and government-facing teams without relying solely on formal authority.
- People leadership: Able to set high standards, coach others and build a healthy, accountable team culture.

Cultural Fit & Communication

- Value Alignment: Deeply aligned with One Acre Fund values: *Farmers First*, *Work Hard*, *Grow Through Feedback*, and *Own Your Results*.
- Communication: Clear, compelling written and verbal style with a strong eye for data presentation and visual design (English required).
- Commitment: Willingness to relocate and commit to living in Africa (Malawi) for at least two years for a long-term career track.

## **Preferred Start Date**

As soon as possible

## **Job Location**

Zomba, Malawi

## **Benefits**

Health insurance, housing, and comprehensive benefits

## **Eligibility**

This role is only open to citizens or permanent residents of Kenya, Malawi, Ethiopia, Uganda, Tanzania, Nigeria, Rwanda, Burundi, Zambia and the Democratic Republic of Congo.

## **Application Deadline**

16 December 2026. Please note that we hire on a rolling basis which means that applications are reviewed and processed on a continuous basis until a hire is made.

*One Acre Fund never asks candidates to pay any money or pay for tests at any stage of the interview process. Official One Acre Fund emails will always arrive from an @*[*oneacrefund.org*](http://oneacrefund.org/) *address. Please report any suspicious communication here (globalhotline@oneacrefund.org), **but do not send applications or application materials to this email address.***

*Diversity, Equity, Inclusion (DEI), and anti-racism are deeply connected to our organization’s mission and purpose. One Acre Fund aspires to build a culture where all staff feel consistently valued, represented, and connected – so that our team can thrive as professionals, and achieve exceptional impact for the farmers we serve.*

*We are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, marital status, disability, gender, gender identity or expression. We are proud to be an equal opportunity workplace.*

title: Caseworker
body:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

This position is represented by the OPEIU union and subject to the terms and conditions of a collective bargaining agreement.

**Job Overview:** The Caseworker provides trauma-informed services to recently arrived refugees and other qualified immigrants to meet basic needs and support client achievement of self-sufficiency. The Caseworker works closely with clients, colleagues, and external parties to develop service and/or self-sufficiency plans to meet individual client needs, engaging a broad range of financial, medical, social, vocational, and other services and resources in accordance with client eligibility and program requirements. The Caseworker is expected to follow guidelines and standard practices, connecting clients to services that support wellbeing.

**Major Responsibilities:**

Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

- Coordinate timely pre- and post-arrival services to ensure each client has living essentials such as housing, food, medical care, access to transportation and community orientation
- Purchase necessary items, conduct housing set-ups, airport pick-ups, home visits, grocery orientation, bus orientation and other field-based services related to the immediate needs of newcomers. Lift, transport, drive and move items as needed for program delivery.
- Conduct intake to assess needs. Develop self-sufficiency plans and timelines in partnership with each client. Provide individualized support through direct services, referrals, and advocacy.
- Assess and monitor client progress to support their attainment of established goals. Address challenges, and to ensure that available resources are utilized.
- Detail each client interaction in accordance with program requirements. Input client information in database(s) and assist with tracking and reporting as needed.
- Collaborate effectively with coworkers and partner organizations. Build and maintain relationships with area service providers for the benefit of clients.
- Use personal, insured vehicle and/or public transportation (where available) to travel and transport clients and materials as needed throughout the service delivery area.
- Collaborate with colleagues across grants and programs, ensuring that clients access services for which they are eligible. Complete program quality assurance activities to ensure appropriate use of funds.
- Other duties as assigned.

**Job Requirements:**

**Education:** Bachelor’s degree in social work or related field of study preferred.

**Work Experience:**

- Prior experience working with refugee and/or immigrant populations required, including casework and/or pre-arrival services
- Prior experience navigating program eligibility and program requirements; ensuring services are provided and appropriately documented

**Demonstrated Skills & Competencies:**

- Strong relationship building, diplomacy, and networking skills; ability to effectively build relationships with clients, colleagues and collaborators
- Demonstrated success working and communicating effectively in a multi-cultural environment.
- Self-starter with excellent problem-solving skills combined with the proven ability to multi-task, prioritize duties, and manage time effectively.
- Attention to detail and accuracy in work product.
- Fluent in spoken and written English. Proficiency in language(s) spoken by client group strongly desired.
- Proficient in Microsoft Office applications (Word, Excel, Outlook); ability to use the internet and other digital tools for data entry, research and problem-solving purposes.
- Ability to transport, lift and move items as needed to set up homes and otherwise support new arrivals. Lifting and carrying of items 50+ lbs, including larger items such as furniture
- Valid driver’s license and access to a personal, insured vehicle.
- Ability to drive a large van or other passenger vehicles, as needed to conduct work.

**Working Environment:**

- A combination of standard office environment, remote work, and ‘field’ time within the service delivery area to perform the above outlined responsibilities. Typically, this position is based at the office 4 days/week and remotely 1 day/week, with potential field work all days.
- Requires schedule flexibility to perform weekend and/or evening work, including but not limited to airport pick-ups.

**Compensation:** (Pay Rate: $26.80/hr). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**Benefits:** IRC offers a comprehensive and competitive benefits package. Highlights include 10 paid sick leave, 10 U.S. holidays, 20-25 generous paid time off based on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163/month, dental starting at $6.50/month, and vision starting at $5/month, flexible spending accounts (healthcare, dependent care, and commuter), a 403(b) retirement savings plan with employer match (immediate vesting) along with a non-elective employer contribution based on age and years of service (3-year vesting), disability and life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program (EAP) offering confidential counseling and support services for employees and their families.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

title: Director, Finance
source: International Centre for Diarrhoeal Disease Research
body:
icddr,b is an international health research institute based in Bangladesh. Policymakers and practitioners utilise our evidence and expertise to improve health outcomes and prevent premature death and disability worldwide. In recognition of its scientific and humanitarian contributions, icddr,b has received numerous international and national awards, including

- **Gates Award for Global Health (2001):** For its pioneering contributions to global health, including the development of oral rehydration therapy.
- **Independence Award (2005):** For services rendered to the people of Bangladesh.
- **Conrad N. Hilton Humanitarian Prize (2017):** For innovative approaches to addressing health challenges in underserved communities

Since its establishment in 1960, icddr,b’s research focus has expanded beyond cholera and diarrhoeal diseases to encompass a broad range of public-health challenges in Bangladesh and globally.

Our research priorities are organised around nine public-health goals:

- Address health risks related to climate change;
- Address health risks related to gender and sexual and reproductive health and rights;
- Prevent and manage non-communicable diseases;
- Improve healthcare in urban populations and achieve universal health coverage;
- Prevent and control infectious diseases;
- Improve maternal and newborn health;
- Reduce maternal, adolescent and childhood malnutrition;
- Enhance laboratory services and support genomics research; and
- Improve hospital services and clinical research.

## **The Opportunity**

We seek an accomplished, strategic and collaborative Director, Finance to provide leadership and oversight of icddr,b’s financial strategy, operations and governance.

Reporting directly to the Deputy Executive Director, the Director, Finance will lead a multidisciplinary finance team and work closely with the Senior Leadership Team, Division Directors, Principal Investigators and donors to ensure sound financial stewardship and long-term organisational sustainability.

The successful candidate will combine strong professional expertise with integrity, sound judgement and inclusive leadership. The position will ensure effective financial planning, transparent reporting, robust internal controls and adherence to sound financial governance and applicable regulatory requirements.

## **Key Responsibilities**

**Strategic Planning and Development**

- Provide strategic leadership and overall direction for icddr,b’s Finance function, ensuring that financial strategy, resource allocation and financial management are aligned with icddr,b’s mission, research priorities and long-term institutional sustainability.
- Serve as a trusted financial adviser to the Executive Director, Deputy Executive Director, Senior Leadership Team, Finance & Audit Committee (FAC) and Board of Trustees (BOT), providing independent advice and constructive challenge on financial performance, sustainability, funding, investment, risk and major institutional decisions.
- Lead the development and implementation of icddr,b’s long-term financial strategy, multi-year financial plans, annual budgets, forecasts and scenario analyses, translating institutional and research priorities into sustainable financial plans and resource-allocation decisions.
- Provide financial leadership on major research initiatives, institutional programmes, partnerships and funding opportunities, assessing their financial implications, affordability, risks and long-term sustainability.
- Analyse funding patterns, expenditure trends and cost structures to inform strategic decisions and strengthen cost recovery.
- Anticipate changes in the research, donor funding and operating environment and advise leadership on their implications for icddr,b’s financial resilience, funding model, cost structure and future resource requirements.

**Financial Planning and Analysis**

- Lead the preparation of annual budgets, multi-year financial plans, cash-flow forecasts and scenario analyses.
- Lead organisation-wide financial planning and performance management, ensuring effective alignment of resources with icddr,b’s research, programme and institutional priorities.
- Establish consistent budgeting assumptions, guidelines and monitoring arrangements across the organisation.
- Provide financial insight and constructive challenge to Division Directors, Principal Investigators and programme leadership to strengthen resource allocation, financial planning and organisational performance.
- Establish appropriate financial performance measures and provide timely, forward-looking analysis of financial results, funding, expenditure, cost structures, cost recovery and resource utilisation to support management, FAC and BOT decision-making.
- Hold overall accountability for the financial health, integrity and stewardship of icddr,b, ensuring that financial resources are managed effectively, transparently and in accordance with approved strategy and governance arrangements.

**Financial Operations Management and Reporting**

- Oversee accounting, financial reporting, accounts payable and receivable, project finance and related financial operations.
- Ensure that financial information and management reporting provide reliable, timely and decision-useful information for management and governance oversight.
- Provide strategic leadership of icddr,b’s financial governance and control environment, ensuring appropriate policies, delegated authorities, accountability mechanisms and internal controls are established and operating effectively.
- Ensure that accounting policies, financial reporting and practices remain aligned with applicable international standards, including IPSAS, as well as relevant laws, regulatory requirements, donor obligations and icddr,b policies.
- Provide timely financial reports and analysis to the Deputy Executive Director, Executive Director, Division Directors, Board of Trustees and donors, in accordance with established reporting arrangements.
- Promote efficient, responsive and service-oriented financial support across the organisation.

**Financial Systems and Process Improvement**

- Lead the strategic evolution and modernisation of the Finance function, ensuring that its operating model, capabilities, systems and processes remain fit for icddr,b’s evolving research, funding and institutional environment.
- Set the strategic direction for Finance systems, digitalisation, automation, data and management information, ensuring these enable effective financial management, strong controls and informed organisational decision-making.
- Provide strategic oversight of icddr,b’s financial reporting framework and accounting architecture, including the effective application of IPSAS and adaptation to evolving accounting and reporting requirements.
- Sponsor and oversee major Finance transformation and continuous-improvement initiatives, ensuring that investments in systems, processes and capabilities deliver sustainable improvements in efficiency, transparency, control and service quality.
- Ensure that ERP and other financial systems provide integrated, reliable and decision-ready information across icddr,b and support effective financial governance and performance management.

**Project Fund Management**

- Provide strategic oversight of grants, contracts and collaborative research agreements, working with Principal Investigators, Division Directors and programme leadership to ensure sound financial stewardship, appropriate cost allocation and recovery, effective financial management and compliance with donor and contractual requirements.
- Support Principal Investigators and programme teams in proposal budgeting, expenditure planning, financial monitoring and project close-out.
- Ensure appropriate cost allocation, indirect-cost recovery and compliance with donor-specific financial requirements.
- Review and approve project budgets and financial transactions within delegated authority.
- Ensure timely and accurate donor financial reporting and resolve escalated financial and contractual issues.
- Promote constructive collaboration between Finance, research teams, donors and partner institutions.

**Risk Management**

- Oversee material financial risks relating to research funding, institutional sustainability, liquidity, foreign exchange, investments, financial reporting, fraud, compliance and donor obligations, ensuring significant risks are identified, escalated and appropriately managed.
- Maintain appropriate controls to prevent and detect fraud, misuse of funds and material financial misstatement.
- Ensure effective segregation of duties and compliance with delegated financial authorities.
- Oversee financial due diligence on relevant banking institutions, service providers and partners.
- Promote financial accountability, ethical conduct and risk awareness across the organisation.

**Audit and Compliance**

- Provide executive oversight of statutory, external and donor audits and work closely with Internal Oversight, while respecting its independence, to strengthen assurance and ensure timely resolution of material findings and agreed recommendations.
- Support internal audit and assurance activities while respecting the independence of the Internal Oversight function.
- Ensure timely implementation and monitoring of agreed audit recommendations.
- Maintain effective relationships with auditors, donors and relevant regulatory authorities.
- Maintain effective senior relationships with donors, auditors, regulators, financial institutions and other key external stakeholders on significant financial, contractual and regulatory matters.
- Ensure compliance with applicable taxation, regulatory and contractual obligations.

**Treasury Management**

- Oversee cash-flow forecasting, liquidity management, banking relationships and foreign-exchange exposure.
- Oversee liquidity, reserves, investments and other institutional financial resources, ensuring an appropriate balance between financial resilience, risk, return and icddr,b’s strategic priorities.
- Develop and review treasury and investment policies within approved governance arrangements.
- Oversee the prudent management of surplus funds, reserves, endowments and separation funds.
- Report regularly on liquidity, investment performance and treasury risks.

**Leadership and Team Development**

- Lead and develop the Finance function through its management structure, establishing clear accountability and performance expectations across its respective units and ensuring effective integration and collaboration across the function.
- Build a high-performing Finance leadership team with the professional capability, managerial strength and succession depth required to support icddr,b’s evolving strategic and operational needs.
- Foster a culture of integrity, accountability, collaboration, service excellence and continuous improvement across Finance.
- Position Finance as a strategic business partner to icddr,b’s scientific, research, programme and corporate leadership, providing insight, advice and constructive challenge to strengthen organisational performance, research delivery and financial sustainability.
- Lead significant organisational change within Finance and ensure the function continuously develops its capabilities in response to changing technologies, accounting standards, funding models and institutional priorities.
- Represent the Finance function at senior institutional and external forums and contribute to icddr,b-wide strategy, performance, risk and institutional decisions.

## **Qualifications and Experience:**

**Essential Requirements**

- A master’s degree in Accounting, Finance or a related discipline.
- At least 15 years of progressively responsible experience in accounting, finance or financial management, including at least five years in a senior financial leadership role with substantial responsibility for financial strategy, operations, governance and team management.
- Fellowship of a recognised professional accountancy body, FCA, FCCA, FCMA, FCPA is mandatory. Candidates must hold at least one of these designations and maintain current membership in good standing with the awarding professional body.
- Demonstrated experience managing complex, multi-million-dollar budgets and multiple funding sources in an international, donor-funded or comparably complex organisation.
- Substantial experience in financial planning and analysis, accounting, management reporting, treasury, audit, internal controls and financial risk management.
- Demonstrated experience in grant and contract financial management, including donor compliance, cost recovery and financial reporting.
- Strong working knowledge of internationally recognised accounting standards, including IPSAS and/or IFRS.
- Proven experience leading financial process improvement, organisational change and the implementation or optimisation of ERP systems.
- Demonstrated ability to advise executive leadership and communicate financial performance, risks and recommendations to governing bodies or equivalent senior decision-makers.
- Proven ability to lead and develop diverse teams and collaborate effectively with financial and non-financial stakeholders.
- Excellent written and spoken English.

**Desirable Requirements**

- Experience in an international health research institution, university, development organisation, public-health organisation or other not-for-profit institution.
- Formal training or certification in IPSAS and practical experience implementing or transitioning to an international accounting framework.
- Experience with Microsoft Dynamics 365, SAP, Oracle Financials or a comparable ERP platform.
- Experience managing endowments, institutional reserves and investment portfolios.
- Knowledge of Bangladesh’s financial, taxation and regulatory environment.
- Experience working across multiple countries, cultures or regulatory environments.

## **Key Skills**

- Analytical rigour – translates complex financial data into clear, actionable insight for financial and non-financial audiences alike;
- Sound, independent judgement – comfortable making high-stakes financial calls under time pressure or incomplete information;
- Integrity under scrutiny – upholds rigorous controls and ethical standards even under programme or donor pressure;
- Systems thinking – understands how financial decisions ripple across research operations, HR, IT and institutional risk;
- Cross-functional communication – builds trust and negotiates effectively with donors, auditors, regulators, scientists and field teams alike;
- Change leadership – drives adoption of new systems and processes (e.g. ERP, IPSAS) with genuine staff buy-in rather than top-down mandate;
- Coaching and talent development – builds bench strength and succession within the finance function itself;
- Resilience under resource constraint – sustains service quality and team morale through funding volatility or donor-driven change;
- Diplomatic acumen – navigates competing priorities between the Board, donors and scientific leadership without compromising financial discipline; and
- Hands-on digital fluency – works directly and confidently with financial systems, dashboards and data-analytics tools, not just through others.

## **Compensation**

This internationally recruited position offers a competitive salary paid in US Dollars.

The successful candidate will receive an initial three-year contract, including a one-year probationary period. Contract renewal will be subject to satisfactory performance and funding availability.

title: Director of Program Development, Quality & Learning (PQL) - Port au Prince, Haiti
body:
**Location:** Port-au-Prince, Haiti

**Position Status:** Full-time, Regular

**Language:** Required language fluency in French

[**Risk Level:**](https://library.mercycorps.org/record/47705?ln=en) X **Level 3** ☐**Level 2** ☐**Level 1**

(Level 3: Frequent contact with participants, direct contact with children, access to sensitive data, and/or high level of accountability.

Level 2: Some contact with participants; unplanned non-direct contact with children.

Level 1: Likely to have no contact with participants or sensitive data)

## **About Mercy Corps**

Mercy Corps is a leading global organization powered by the belief that a better world is possible. In disaster, in hardship, in more than 40 countries around the world, we partner to put bold solutions into action — helping people triumph over adversity and build stronger communities from within.

Now, and for the future.

## **Program/Department Summary**

Mercy Corps helps communities develop their own ideas to solve Haiti’s most daunting problems by using innovative approaches to bring Haitians new social and economic opportunities and to make their country more secure, productive and just. Established in January 2010, Mercy Corps Haiti has offices in Port-au-Prince, Jeremie, and Miragoane and more than 80 staff implementing programs in WASH, financial inclusion, economic development, agriculture, natural resource management and humanitarian response. Mercy Corps’ economic development work is guided by the principles of pro-poor development and demand driven strategies. Mercy Corps takes a progressive approach to development that leads communities and entrepreneurs from relief to sustainable livelihoods to resilience.

Mercy Corps Haiti is going through a transformational change at this moment. As a catalytic organization, our future impact will increasingly focus on **sustainability and transformative change,** supporting lasting improvements in the lives of the communities we serve. This ambition will be supported through several key drivers, including: evidence-based programming, learning generation to influence systems change, scaling impact through Mercy Corps and strategic partners, stronger knowledge management and impact measurement, expanded partnerships and alliances, greater commitment to gender equity and diversity and strategic advocacy and fundraising.

## **General Position Summary**

As a member of the Senior Management Team (SMT) in Haiti, the Director of Program Development, Quality and Learning (PQL) is responsible for driving cross-functional engagement in the development and delivery of Country Program Strategy, developing annual plans and reporting on results. S/he is responsible for ensuring development and delivery of high quality, evidence-based, innovative programs that contribute to Mercy Corps Global Strategy and Mercy Corps Haiti new strategic vision. The Director of PQL ensures that a robust monitoring, evaluation, accountability and learning (MEAL) system is in place, that the country office engages in the collection and use of evidence and that this is shared across the global organization, and that reliable data is used for decision-making. One key aspect of the role is ensuring capability building, mentoring and coaching of the Program/Project Managers in order to support program quality in line with global standards and key performance indicators. As a senior leader in the country office s/he plays a representational role with the government, donors, partners, peer agencies, and others. The Director of PQL supports strategic positioning with donors and partners and leads on project design to ensure that the country office strategy can be delivered in line with Mercy Corps vision.

As one of the most senior staff in the Country Office, the Director of Program Development, Quality and Learning must demonstrate the qualities of agile leadership. This role plays a key role in defining and pursuing the strategic direction for Mercy Corps programs in Haiti, ensuring the relevance, coherence, safety and impact of our programs. It is essential that the Director of Program Development, Quality and Learning builds and maintains strong relationships across functions within the Country Program.

## **Essential Job Responsibilities**

**STRATEGY & VISION, PLANNING & REPORTING**

- Lead the development/updating of the analysis of the country context ensuring community, partners and other stakeholders’ participation as necessary.
- Lead the SLT to develop/update and drive forward the Country Program Strategy that is in line with the global strategy.
- Provide leadership on development of the Country Annual Implementation Plan, monitoring of progress against the plan, and completion of accurate, on-time Country Annual Report of outcomes and impact, aligned with the Global Results Framework.
- Facilitate the development and pursuit of thematic and cross-cutting strategic priorities in line with the Country Program Strategy, including gender equality, to guide current and future Mercy Corps programming and Humanitarian Principles.
- Support ownership and commitment to the Country Program Strategy by all staff and departments through clear communication, regular feedback on progress and engagement of all functions in updates.
- Participate in global discussions and working groups to represent country programs, in learning for a, in strategy design and policy development.
- Support change processes and roll out new ways of working to improve achievement of the Country Program Strategy.
- Drive Innovation and thought leadership at all levels in the CO (strategy, programme, project and individual levels).

**PROGRAM DESIGN & DEVELOPMENT**

- Lead strategic resource (financial, materials & human) mobilization drive and ensure the Country Program is always resourced to drive programme design and development.
- Work with CD and SMT to set funding targets and drive implementation at all levels ensuring the entire Country Program is committed to and aware of these contributions to these targets.
- In consultation with the Country Director and Members, ensure technical engagement with donors to pre-position and prepare for opportunities, and engage in strategic positioning work directly as appropriate.
- Lead the identification of new initiatives and opportunities that respond to identified needs and the country strategy, in coordination with the Country Director and Program Managers, as well as the Regional Program Director, headquarters-based Senior Program Officer, Technical Advisors and other relevant staff.
- Play a leading role in designing innovative projects/proposals, including:
    - Engaging with technical experts as needed to ensure high quality, evidence-based designs that draw on needs assessments, learning from past programs and program standards principles.
    - Ensuring partners are identified and appropriately engaged in program design, linking with Operations as need be for assessments, especially to strengthen gender sensitivity at design stage.
    - Ensuring proposal designs and their budgets include robust MEAL plans that are aligned with the Global Results Framework and build in critical learning questions.
    - Ensuring the project budget will enable the project to be delivered as designed.
    - Incorporating community participation into design, as relevant.

**PROGRAM QUALITY AND PROGRAM TECHNICAL EXCELLENCE**

- Ensure the Country Program delivers high quality, multi-sectoral programming in both development and humanitarian contexts (as appropriate).
- Monitor and advance technical and operational quality of programmes, including conducting regular field visits to provide feedback on quality benchmarks, soliciting inputs for design of new programs and collecting ideas for innovation.
- Monitor program Key Performance Indicators and, in partnership with other functions, take steps to improve the quality programming platform to meet agreed upon standards.
- Work closely with the Director of Operations to ensure procedures are followed throughout the project cycle and across the portfolio.
- Ensure Program/Project Managers proactively and regularly communicate planned requirements for program design, learning and implementation to relevant Country Program departments/functions.
- Oversee program startup and ongoing program management and administration of teams across various field locations.
- Ensure that program implementation is responsive to communities and partners and consistent with Mercy Corps’ relevant program guidelines, principles, values, quality standards and strategic plan.
- Ensure that beneficiaries are effectively targeted according to established and well-defined criteria and processes.
- Develop partners’ MoUs and contracts and ensure that partners are delivering in accordance with the agreements.
- Support the PMs and team in the development and ongoing refinement of implementation strategies.
- Integrate community approaches, gender sensitivity and capacity building into all activities as appropriate.
- Ensure program implementation is on time, target and budget, using effective M&E systems to reach desired impacts (adaptive management).
- Create and maintain systems ensuring effective and transparent use of financial resources for timely and informative reporting in line with donor and Mercy Corps policies and procedures.
- Conduct frequent field visits to all project sites for monitoring, quality control and program staff mentoring and coaching.
- Ensure that community feedback mechanisms are in place, functioning, and clearly communicated to staff and beneficiaries.
- Review all draft reports and ensure that reports are ready for submission to HQ on time.
- Lead and coach the Program/Project Managers to enable them to successfully deliver against the Country Program Strategy.
- Ensure effective working relationships with Mercy Corps global, Member and regional technical advisors, procuring technical support as needed to support program and advocacy efforts, including during Emergencies.
- Ensure that program technical experts engage in larger communities of practice within and external to Mercy Corps, to link with the most relevant and evidence-based approaches and conduct timely and useful review of project reports to support quality reporting for Members and donors.
- Ensure that the different technical sectors of the Country Program are coordinated, integrated and support each other to optimize programs and projects.

**DRIVING EVIDENCE, MEAL AND KNOWLEDGE MANAGEMENT**

- Work to develop a monitoring system that provides timely and accurate project results by embedding MEAL across program implementation. This requires ensuring effective collaboration across MEAL staff, Technical Specialists, Technical Advisors and program implementation teams to develop logframes, indicators, implementation plans, quality benchmarks, monitoring and evaluation frameworks and related tools.
- Lead programme quality improvements by monitoring and improving Programme KPI performance, including resourcing and conducting high-quality evaluations to demonstrate outcomes and impact and ensuring that accountability mechanisms are in place for all projects so that identified actions are resolved, with critical issues escalated to senior management.
- Ensure the research, evaluation and policy work of the Country Program contributes to generation of evidence for development and improvement of program quality, sound decision making and policy influencing internally and externally.
- Establish effective program learning and knowledge management systems to support adaptive programming and innovation that improves outcomes for children through service delivery, policy & advocacy and campaigns.

**STAFF MANAGEMENT, MENTORSHIP, AND DEVELOPMENT**

- Ensure appropriate staffing of Program Development and Quality team, and engagement of additional technical support when needed to deliver quality project design and delivery.
- Ensure that staff proactively build and maintain technical, managerial and leadership skills, , providing coaching opportunities when needed.
- Create and sustain a work environment of mutual respect where team members strive to achieve excellence.
- Promote accountability, communicate expectations and provide constructive feedback via regular performance reviews.
- Supervise, hire and orient new team members as necessary.
- Provide team members with information, tools and other resources to improve performance and reach objectives.
- Contribute to country team-building efforts, help team members identify problem-solving options and ensure the integration of all team members into relevant decision-making processes.
- Be comfortable and able to manage a team remotely and with limited travel based on the security situation.

**FINANCE & COMPLIANCE MANAGEMENT**

- Ensure compliance with donor and Mercy Corps regulations related to programming.
- Review BVAs with Finance and Program managers to identify any issues and undertake any necessary budget revisions.
- Ensure program close-out begins in a timely manner to minimize any significant under or overspends at the end of the grant (i.e. final variance for all grants should be within 5%).

**INFLUENCE, ADVOCACY & REPRESENTATION:**

- Guide functions and thematic tracks to identify advocacy issues and lead them at the national level.
- Ensure Mercy Corps is represented in the relevant networks.
- Develop and / or participate in various networks for opportunities to extend the program and defend interests.
- Ensure Program issues are subject to pressure and advocacy at national and other levels.
- Ensure programming models are demonstrated/documented and scaled up in line with strategic directions.
- Undertake an in-depth analysis of the powers and policies of the country's structures, systems and networks to identify opportunities for changes in law, policy, budget and behavior at the national level that will achieve the goals and objectives strategies set by the national office.
- Lead and manage the design and implementation of the influence strategy in coordination with staff and partners, taking an integrated approach to influence.
- Revise and update the advocacy strategy according to the evolution of the context.
- Ensure strong links with programs and monitoring, evaluation, research and learning (MERL) so that advocacy and policy approaches are evidence-based.
- Monitor and report on progress in influencing and its contribution to change, including to donors where appropriate.

## **Supervisory Responsibility**

Project Directors, Program Managers, CARM Manager, MEL Manager, Safeguarding Manager, Program Development & Knowledge Manager and other staff as needed.

## **Accountability**

**Reports Directly To:** Country Director  
**Works Directly With:** All program staff, both national and expatriate in Haiti; HQ-based program, operations, recruiting, human resources, finance, and technical support teams.

## **Accountability to Participants and Stakeholders**

Mercy Corps team members are expected to support all efforts toward accountability, specifically to our program participants, community partners, other stakeholders, and to international standards guiding international relief and development work. We are committed to actively engaging communities as equal partners in the design, monitoring and evaluation of our field projects.

## **Minimum Qualification & Transferable Skills**

- BA/S or equivalent in international studies, social science, management, economics or other relevant fields. MA/S preferred.
- 7+ years of experience with European and US institutional and private donors, including proposal development.
- 5+ years overseas experience, including at least 3 years in a senior management position.
- Experience managing humanitarian relief and/or transitional programs in areas affected by insecurity and natural disasters.
- Previous experience working in Haiti or similar contexts strongly preferred.
- Proven track record in program design, proposal writing and development, and donor reporting.
- Be trained and knowledgeable in design, monitoring, and evaluation concepts and methodologies. M&E experience should include conducting assessments and surveys, program design using a logical framework approach, selecting indicators, implementing monitoring plans, coordinating evaluations and data analysis.
- Experience supervising international and national staff, starting up programs and working in difficult environments.
- Experience managing programs in relevant technical areas including Participatory Community Development, Livelihoods, Agriculture, Water and Sanitation, Economic Recovery, Women’s Empowerment and GBV programming, Peacebuilding, Civil Society Capacity Building and Youth.
- Knowledge of major donor requirements and compliance issues.
- Strong management skills with good understanding of relevant cross-cultural issues.
- Understanding of advocacy, policy, and government systems in the host country.
- Strong skills and proven experience in leading strategic planning, change management and program management processes, also from the knowledge and learning perspective.
- Strong skills and proven experience in new program development, project design and proposal writing with corporate, foundations and/or institutional donors.
- Skills in training, capability building, coaching, mentorship, problem solving, and project cycle management.
- High level of self-awareness and willingness to take feedback for growth and self-development.
- Proven experience as a team player and leader in an international organization.
- Demonstrated attention to detail, ability to follow procedures, meet deadlines and work independently and cooperatively with team members.
- History of working effectively with host country government, national and international NGO partners, and collaborating with other actors, including the private sector.
- Solid knowledge of and experience with security protocols is essential.
- **Fluency in written and oral French and English is required.**

## **Success Factors**

A successful candidate will be conscientious, with excellent judgment and will display an entrepreneurial spirit that is both creative and flexible. S/he will combine strong communication skills, creativity, initiative, participatory leadership and tactful decisiveness to assist in the development and implementation of Mercy Corps’ country strategy. Prioritizing, problem solving and simultaneous attention to detail and strategic vision are essential. The individual will be a strategic thinker able to bring ideas to implementation in growing program operations. They will have exceptional proposal development skills and an outstanding ability to design, implement and manage innovative programs that respond to current needs. An interest and ability to travel and work in remote environments, and awareness of and sensitivity to multi-cultural international development work and ability to train and facilitate dialogue among a diverse group of individuals with various skill sets and working styles is required. An even temperament and a good sense of humor are appreciated. Language proficiency in English/French is a must.

## **Living Conditions / Environmental Conditions**

Haiti is a country of 11 million people and is the poorest country in the Western Hemisphere. The country has been wracked by a series of major natural disasters since 2010 including earthquake, hurricanes, and drought. A new government is in place for the next five years which is anticipated to reduce instability, however occasional violent demonstrations and flare-ups in crime can occur. Haiti suffers from chronic high unemployment, severe environmental degradation, food insecurity, and health issues like cholera exacerbated by low levels of access to water and poor infrastructure. Nonetheless, Haiti also has great beauty including beaches and mountainous national parks. Its international airport provides daily flights to multiple destinations in the US, as well as access to DR, Canada, Paris, Cuba, Panama, Curacao, and other locations in the Caribbean.

The position is based in Port au Prince, which is estimated at around 2.5 million people. Although infrastructure is also poor in the capital, comfortable housing with water and electricity are readily available. There are many places to eat in all price ranges, as well as shops, and supermarkets which are comparable to a US supermarket. Self-drive is permitted, however driving can be challenging, and traffic is often very heavy. Housing is provided for this position.

Mercy Corps Team members represent the agency both during and outside of work hours when deployed in a field posting. Team members are expected to conduct themselves in a professional manner and respect local laws, customs and Mercy Corps' policies, procedures, and values at all times and in all in-country venues.

## **Ongoing Learning**

In support of our belief that learning organizations are more effective, efficient and relevant to the communities we serve, we empower all team members to dedicate 5% of their time to learning activities that further their personal and/or professional growth and development.

## **Team Engagement and Effectiveness**

Achieving our mission starts with how we build our team and collaborate. By bringing together individuals with a variety of experiences, backgrounds, and perspectives, we strengthen our ability to solve complex challenges and drive innovation. We foster a culture of trust and respect, where every team member is valued for their contributions, empowered to reach their full potential, and motivated to do their best work.

We recognize that building a strong and effective team is an ongoing process, and we remain committed to learning, improving, and growing together.

## **Equal Employment Opportunity**

Mercy Corps is an equal opportunity employer committed to providing equal employment opportunities to all employees and qualified applicants for employment without regard to race, color, sex, sexual orientation, religion or belief, national origin, age, disability, marital status, veteran status, or any other characteristics protected under applicable law.

## **Safeguarding & Ethics**

Mercy Corps is committed to ensuring that all individuals we come into contact with through our work, whether team members, community members, program participants or others, are treated with respect and dignity. We are committed to the core principles regarding prevention of sexual exploitation and abuse laid out by the UN Secretary General and IASC **and have signed on to the** [**Interagency Misconduct Disclosure Scheme**](https://www.schr.info/the-misconduct-disclosure-scheme)**.** We will not tolerate child abuse, sexual exploitation, abuse, or harassment by or of our team members. As part of our commitment to a safe and inclusive work environment, team members are expected to conduct themselves in a professional manner, respect local laws and customs, and to adhere to [Mercy Corps Code of Conduct Policies](https://www.mercycorps.org/who-we-are/ethics-policies) and values at all times. Team members are required to complete mandatory Code of Conduct elearning courses upon hire and on an annual basis.

As an applicant, if you witness or experience any form of sexual misconduct during the recruitment process, please report this to Mercy Corps Integrity Hotline (integrityhotline@mercycorps.org).

title: Nurse Mentor
body:
**This full-time, on-site position located in Sierra Leone.**

Mercy Ships is seeking an experienced Nurse Mentor for its work in Sierra Leone. They will develop and deliver nurse mentoring projects, in the surgical ward and/or the operating rooms, at a partner country teaching hospital. Develops and maintains strong relationships with partner country partners, providers, and government officials. This role works to enhance the partner country’s surgical system through mentoring, training, and quality improvement projects at targeted facilities, together with the existing multidisciplinary team from those facilities. The focus is on the facility and sustained system-level changes to the surgical system at the targeted facility. This role could include providing direct patient care, depending on the facility, country, and objectives of the project. This is a full-time in-country role.

**How You Will Contribute:**

- Develop, coordinate, and maintain clear lines of communication between partner country partners, hospitals, ship departments and the ETA team.
- Develop relationships with national partners, healthcare agencies, and other national or international Non-Government Organizations.
- Contribute to the development, design and review of relevant ETA projects in the designated hospital(s).
- Maintain records and perform evaluations as necessary, of all training projects and donations, as directed by the ETA Director (In-Country).  
    Document processes related to project delivery to increase the effectiveness of future projects.
- Prepare internal and final reports on ETA projects in conjunction with the ETA Director (In-Country) and International Programs in a timely manner.
- Participate in communications activities designed to promote the ETA portfolio of work among Mercy Ships’ stakeholders and supporters.
- Assist management in receiving business guests at Mercy Ships functions and receptions.
- Due to the ever-changing staffing levels and field service rotations, all staff may be reassigned to temporarily fill roles in other departments in a time of need.

**Nurse mentoring project:**  
This role is part of a long-term, in-country project.

- Adhere to strategic and educational directives from the ETA Director (In-Country) and Senior Director for ETA.
- Work alongside mentoring participants from the partner country and identify their learning needs and objectives.
- Collaborate with hospital leaders and other key stakeholders, capable of influencing change, to support the planning and implementation of contextually and culturally appropriate activities, to improve the quality of surgical and anesthesia care at the facility.
- Work alongside the partner country hospital teams to implement quality improvement projects that lead to sustainable implementation of learning and improved outcomes.
- Deliver up-to-date, culturally and environmentally sensitive, and relevant teaching and simulation that encourages participants to deliver best practices in their environment.
- Support integration of learning from ETA courses and on-ship skills sharing into the partner country hospital context, specifically into policy and process.
- Work with the ship team to select participants for on-ship skills sharing, as relevant.
- Collaborate with program partners to ensure alignment between different educational interventions for nurses.
- Collaborate with Program Design, Monitoring, Evaluation, Learning, and Data (PDMELD) team to understand the project plan, monitoring, and reporting requirements. Assist with baseline assessment at the facility level.
- Record statistics for mentoring and teaching and provide narrative reports as outlined by the PDMELD team.
- Abide by security and operational protocols established by the Country Engagement Team; take operational directives from the Country Director and CET Operations Director when in pre and post-ship phases of the program.
- Maintains alignment and upholds Mercy Ships Core Values, Code of Conduct, and follows the policies and procedures published on Compass.  
    Follows the model of Jesus and aligns with our core values by Loving God; Loving and Serving Others; Being a Person of Integrity; and a Person of Excellence in all you say and do.
- Other duties may be assigned that are not included in the information provided in this job description.

**Ideal Candidate:**

• Keen interest in building nurse capacity in resource-limited contexts through the development and deployment of training programs.  
• Experience in delivering clinical educational activities and willingness to develop own skills to ensure delivery of high-quality educational interventions.  
• Ability to adapt and be flexible, depending on resources available, external factors, and consistent change.  
• Ability to problem solve and be resilient in a resource-limited context.  
• Ability to organize and plan work effectively within a team and organizational context.  
• Able to lead and manage a diverse team through strong communication, problem solving, and planning skills.  
• Must have excellent written and oral communication skills.  
• Must possess cross-cultural awareness and sensitivity and the ability to build strong professional relationships to work in a multidisciplinary, multicultural team.  
• Commitment to developing activities and processes in collaboration with partners to ensure long term sustainability of successful interventions.  
• Supportive of Mercy Ships' mission and vision and committed to its core values.  
• Understand and apply servant leadership, work collaboratively with integrity, and demonstrate accountability.  
• Able to live in and contribute to community life, requiring stable and healthy interpersonal skills.  
• Live in-country full time.  
• Fluent in English.  
• French language skills - International B1 Level (or equivalent), B2 level strongly preferred when serving in Francophone countries.  
• Valid Driver's License from home country with International Driving Permit preferred (obtain prior to travel if necessary) and ability to drive standard (manual transmission) vehicle within a host country.

**Education and/or Experience;**

• Registered Nurse with an active license in home country required.  
• Nursing degree, equivalent to BScN or higher level.  
• At least 3 years of relevant nursing experience including recent work experience in perioperative and/or operating room nursing.  
• Or equivalent combination of experience and education.  
Successful completion of the Mercy Ships Onboarding program will be required.  
• Experience working and/or training in healthcare in resource-limited settings is required.  
• Experience in quality improvement, policy, and procedure design and implementation, and change management is strongly preferred.  
• Experience in education, curriculum design, development, and simulation preferred.  
• Additional training with the Country Engagement Team may be required, depending on project scope and duration.

title: Humanitarian Response Coordinator
body:
**Salary:** PhP65,000 –70,000/month

**Hours:** 40 hours per week (full time Monday to Friday) with occasional evening/weekend working and travel away from home

**Position type:** 11 month - fixed term contract

**Responsible to:** Programme Manager

**Direct reports:** None

**Location:** ShelterBox Operations Philippines, Cebu, Philippines (time split between warehouse and office) with national travel for disaster responses, and occasional travel to ShelterBox HQ, UK

**ROLE PURPOSE:**

The Humanitarian Response Coordinator plays a key role in strengthening ShelterBox Operations Philippines' preparedness, response and humanitarian coordination capacity. Working closely with the Programme Manager, the postholder will coordinate emergency assessments, support the delivery of humanitarian shelter responses, and help ensure programmes are implemented effectively, safely and in line with organisational and donor requirements.

The role combines emergency preparedness, response coordination, partner management and programme quality oversight. It requires a proactive and relationship-focused individual who can build strong partnerships with government agencies, community stakeholders, volunteers and humanitarian actors to ensure vulnerable communities receive timely and effective support before, during and after disasters.

As part of a small and dynamic team, the Humanitarian Response Coordinator will contribute to preparedness planning, emergency deployments, project monitoring, learning and compliance activities, helping ShelterBox deliver high quality humanitarian shelter interventions across the Philippines.

**WHO ARE WE LOOKING FOR?**

We are looking for an experienced humanitarian professional with a strong understanding of emergency response, disaster management and humanitarian programming within the Philippines.

You will have significant experience coordinating emergency responses, conducting humanitarian assessments and working collaboratively with local partners, government agencies and affected communities. You will be confident operating in challenging and dynamic environments, balancing immediate response needs with longer-term programme quality and accountability requirements.

The successful candidate will be highly organised, adaptable and solutions-focused, with excellent relationship-building skills and the ability to coordinate multiple stakeholders. You will be comfortable travelling to disaster-affected areas, leading field-based activities and supporting partners to deliver effective humanitarian shelter programmes.

This is an exciting opportunity to join a growing humanitarian organisation and play a key role in ensuring families affected by disasters receive timely, dignified and effective shelter assistance when they need it most.

DUTIES WILL INCLUDE BUT NOT BE LIMITED TO:

Emergency Preparedness & Humanitarian Coordination

- Monitor potential disaster events and humanitarian needs across the Philippines.
- Support preparedness, contingency planning and response readiness activities.
- Build and maintain effective relationships with government agencies, local partners, Rotary, volunteers and other humanitarian stakeholders.
- Support the delivery of training, orientation and capacity-strengthening activities for partners and stakeholders.

Humanitarian Response & Assessment

- Coordinate emergency shelter and multi-sector needs assessments to inform response planning.
- Deploy to disaster-affected areas to support and, where required, lead emergency response activities.
- Coordinate with local authorities, partners and community representatives to facilitate effective response operations.
- Support the development of response plans, proposals and reports.

Programme Delivery & Partner Coordination

- Work with implementing partners to ensure activities are delivered on time, to budget and in line with agreed plans.
- Monitor programme implementation and identify risks, challenges and opportunities for improvement.
- Provide technical guidance and day-to-day support to partners delivering humanitarian shelter interventions.
- Support partner capacity strengthening through coaching, mentoring and knowledge sharing.

Shelter Programming & Quality Assurance

- Support the design, implementation and monitoring of humanitarian shelter and settlements programmes.
- Promote adherence to humanitarian principles, technical standards, safeguarding requirements and accountability to affected populations.
- Contribute to the identification of appropriate shelter solutions that meet the needs of disaster-affected communities.

Monitoring, Evaluation, Learning & Compliance

- Support project monitoring, evaluation, accountability and learning activities.
- Ensure project documentation, monitoring data and compliance requirements are completed accurately and on time.
- Contribute to donor reporting, lessons learned and continuous improvement activities.
- Support audits, evaluations and donor visits as required

General Responsibilities

- Provide regular updates on programme progress and key developments.
- Support the Critical Incident Management Team as required.
- Contribute to ShelterBox communications and fundraising activities where appropriate.
- Adhere to organisational policies and procedures, including safeguarding, safety and security requirements.
- Represent ShelterBox Operations Philippines professionally with partners, stakeholders and communities.
- Undertake any other duties commensurate with the level of the role

***Please note: We reserve the right to close this vacancy early if we receive a high volume of applications. We therefore encourage you to submit your application as soon as possible. Please ensure your application is completed in full and you read the applicant guidance on our website before applying.***

title: PIR Caseworker
body:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

***This position has an end date of September 30, 2027.***

**Job Overview:** The Caseworker provides trauma-informed services to refugees and other qualified immigrants to support a positive resettlement experience and the achievement of client self-sufficiency . The Caseworker works closely with clients, colleagues, and external parties to develop service and/or self-sufficiency plans to meet individual client needs and preferences utilizing a broad range of financial, medical, social, vocational, and other services and resources in accordance with client eligibility and program requirements.

**Major Responsibilities:**

Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

- Coordinate timely pre- and post-arrival services to ensure each client has essentials such as airport pick up upon arrival, initial and permanent housing, food, medical care, access to transportation, and is oriented to their new environment.
- Conduct intake services with clients to assess needs. Develop individualized self-sufficiency plans and SMART goals in partnership with each client.
- Provide services that are relevant to the client’s goals, including the distribution of direct financial assistance, applications for public benefits, referrals to medical and mental health services, and housing. Ensure active clients receive at meaningful interactions over the course of the service delivery period in accordance with program requirements.
- Assess and monitor client progress to support their attainment of established goals, address challenges, and to ensure that available resources are utilized.
- Detail each client interaction in accordance with program requirements. Input client information in ETO and assist with tracking and reporting as needed.
- Collaborate effectively with coworkers and partner organizations. Build and maintain relationships with area service providers for the benefit of clients.
- Use personal, insured vehicle and/or public transportation (where available) to travel and transport clients and materials as needed throughout the service delivery area.
- May train and lead the activities of volunteers and interns.
- Other duties as assigned.

**Job Requirements:**

**Education:** Bachelor’s degree in social work or related field of study preferred.

**Work Experience:**

- Relevant professional experience in human services field required; minimum of 2 years’ experience strongly preferred.
- Experience working with refugee and/or immigrant populations strongly preferred.

**Demonstrated Skills & Competencies:**

- Ability to learn to navigate or familiarity with database systems such as IRIS and Efforts to Outcomes (ETO)
- Strong relationship building, diplomacy, and networking skills; ability to effectively build internal and external relationships.
- Demonstrated success working and communicating effectively in a multi-cultural environment.
- Self-starter with excellent problem-solving skills combined with the proven ability to multi-task, prioritize duties, and manage time effectively.
- Attention to detail and accuracy in work product.
- Fluency in English, both spoken and written; proficiency in language(s) spoken by IRC’s clients is desired; including Dari, Farsi, and/or Pashto.
- Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications (Word, Excel, Outlook); ability to use the internet and other digital tools for data entry, research and problem-solving purposes.
- Valid driver’s license and access to a personal, insured vehicle.

**Working Environment:**

- A combination of standard office environment, remote work, and ‘field’ time within the service delivery area to perform the above outlined responsibilities.
- May require occasional weekend and/or evening work.

**Compensation:** ($21 - $23). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**Benefits:** IRC offers a comprehensive and competitive benefits package. Highlights include 10 paid sick leave, 10 U.S. holidays, 20-25 generous paid time off based on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163/month, dental starting at $6.50/month, and vision starting at $5/month, flexible spending accounts (healthcare, dependent care, and commuter), a 403(b) retirement savings plan with employer match (immediate vesting) along with a non-elective employer contribution based on age and years of service (3-year vesting), disability and life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program (EAP) offering confidential counseling and support services for employees and their families.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

title: WASH&Shelter/NFI _only national staff
source: Polish Humanitarian Action - Polska Akcja Humanitarna
body:
Polish Humanitarian Action (PAH) is currently looking for **Shelter/WASH Manager** to support implementation of the projects.

General information:

- Organization: Polish Humanitarian Action (PAH), Warsaw-based international non-governmental organization with representation office in Ukraine
- Position: Shelter/WASH Manager
- Location: Kyiv with regular field visits
- Job terms: full-time
- Type of job: employment contract
- Starting date: ASAP
- Duration: 12 months (3 month of approbation period) with possibility for extension

*We encourage qualified candidates to apply as soon as it is possible as the applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis.*

**About PAH:**

Polish Humanitarian Action (PAH) is an international non-governmental organization providing humanitarian and development aid worldwide since 1992. So far, the interventions have been carried out in 46 different countries. By possessing long-standing expertise in the implementation of projects in WASH, FSL, Protection, as well as Nutrition and Education, PAH concentrates its global activities on ensuring sustainable development of regions suffering from consequences of armed conflicts, natural disasters, climate change and others humanitarian crises.

PAH has been present in Ukraine since August 2014 delivering humanitarian aid to the most vulnerable of the conflict-affected population. PAH provides assistance to internally displaced people, elderly, children and other vulnerable population groups. PAH is currently working in the sectors of FSL, protection, WASH and Shelter. For more information, please refer to: [Homepage - Polska Akcja Humanitarna](https://robota.ua/redirect?event_name=url_click&redir_token=eyJPcmlnaW5hbFVybCI6Imh0dHA6Ly93d3cucGFoLm9yZy5wbC8iLCJWYWNhbmN5SWQiOjEwMTY5MDcxfQ==)

**Key Duties and Responsibilities:**

**Programme Management and Technical Leadership**

- Lead the planning, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of WASH and Shelter/NFI assistance programmes in line with humanitarian standards and PAH guidelines.
- Contribute WASH/Shelter-NFI technical expertise to multi-sector needs assessments (MSNAs) and lead sector-specific needs assessments when required, translating findings into clear, prioritised programme recommendations.
- Lead the technical design of concept notes, proposals and project modifications with WASH/Shelter-NFI component;
- Develop detailed work plans, budgets and procurement plans for WASH and Shelter/NFI interventions in close coordination with the logistics department, ensuring efficient and effective use of resources.
- Contribute to the development and revision of the Country Programme Strategy, ensuring WASH/Shelter-NFI priorities, geographic focus, localisation approach and emergency-to-recovery pathways are clearly and realistically reflected.

 **Partner Coordination and Technical Support**

- Serve as the WASH/Shelter-NFI technical focal point for implementing partners; review partner assessments, designs, bills of quantities, technical specifications, work plans, and narrative reporting.
- Provide timely technical guidance, coaching and capacity-strengthening support to partners on WASH/Shelter-NFI programming methodologies, resource management and reporting requirements.
- Oversee partner implementation of WASH/Shelter-NFI activities, ensuring compliance with sectoral technical and donor requirements; escalate material risks promptly and track corrective actions to closure.

 **Quality Assurance, Tools and Monitoring**

- Review technical assessments, designs, specifications, BoQs, tender technical documentation, samples/materials, construction or installation quality, and commissioning/handover documentation for direct and partner-led activities.
- Define and maintain a risk-based technical monitoring framework and tools for direct and partner-led WASH/Shelter-NFI activities, coordinating monitoring planning with Area Managers, Project Leads, Partnership and MEAL teams.
- Develop and institutionalise practical WASH/Shelter-NFI tools, checklists, SOPs and a standard project-file and document-management structure, in coordination with Programme, Logistics, MEAL, Grants and Partnership teams.
- Participate in project reviews, field monitoring, troubleshooting and lessons-learned processes; use monitoring data to inform programme adjustments, identify best practices and contribute to organisational learning.

 **Financial Management**

- Monitor budget expenditure, identify variances and take corrective action as necessary to ensure financial accountability and transparency.
- Provide continuous review of partners' financial and programmatic performance and implementation.
- **Reporting and Representation**
- Prepare timely and accurate reports for donors, government partners and other stakeholders, highlighting programme achievements, challenges and lessons learned.
- Represent PAH in relevant national WASH, Shelter/NFI and technical coordination forums and cluster meetings, advocating for the sector and sharing useful updates and opportunities internally.
- Identify and pursue documented strategic or technical engagement opportunities with clusters, authorities, other NGOs, technical institutions and prospective partners.

 **Team Management and Capacity Strengthening**

- Lead the WASH/Shelter-NFI team, including hiring and management of staff, performance reviews and goal-setting, and development of supportive relations with subordinates.
- Ensure direct reports have clear objectives, regular documented check-ins and timely feedback, coordinating constructively with Area Managers and other functions.
- Maintain a practical capacity-development approach for PAH WASH/Shelter-NFI staff and implementing partners, delivering targeted coaching or learning sessions based on identified performance gaps.
- Maintain an effective management flow for the function, including clear priorities, realistic work planning, a live work plan/action tracker, and concise monthly reporting to the Head of Programmes.

 **Shelter/WASH Manager will be selected based on the qualification requirements described below:**

- Higher professional education in the relevant field of study (master’s degree, specialist);
- Professional experience of more than 7 years;
- At least 3 years of work experience in international or local NGO;
- Excellent verbal and written communication skills in English (at least upper-intermediate level) and Ukrainian;
- Understanding of the context in Ukraine;
- Understanding of international humanitarian work;
- Good interpersonal skills;
- Good working knowledge of Microsoft Office and Google Apps;
- Good organizational skills and discretion with confidential information;
- Proven ability to handle challenging workload;
- Ability to work independently and proactively.

**What PAH offers:**

- Opportunity to gain experience in a professional and flexible international NGO, one of the largest organizations in Central and Eastern Europe.
- Work in a dynamic and motivated team.
- Voluntary medical insurance fully covered by the organization.
- Free English language courses and other opportunities for professional growth.
- Full social benefits package in accordance with Ukrainian legislation.
- Flexible work arrangements.
- Access to confidential psychological support sessions when needed.
- Additional days off in observance of public and religious holidays in Ukraine.

**Equal Opportunities and Non-Discrimination**

Our organization adheres to the principles of equality, respect for human dignity, and non-discrimination in accordance with the legislation of Ukraine.

We do not tolerate discrimination based on age, sex, gender identity, marital status, pregnancy, parental status, disability, health condition, race, skin color, ethnic or national origin, citizenship, language, religion or other beliefs, sexual orientation, or any other characteristic.

All candidates are assessed solely on the basis of their professional competencies and alignment with the position requirements.

 **Employment of Persons with Disabilities**

The organization is open to employing persons with disabilities and ensures equal opportunities to participate in the recruitment process.

If needed, we are ready to:

- provide reasonable workplace accommodation.
- adapt the recruitment process.
- consider flexible working hours or remote work arrangements;
