title: Health Coordinator
body:
**CONTEXTE**

Le 15 mai 2026, la République démocratique du Congo (RDC) a déclaré sa dix-septième épidémie d'Ebola après la confirmation de cas dans la province de l'Ituri. L'épidémie s'est depuis étendue à d'autres zones touchées et à risque, ce qui accroît la pression sur un système de santé déjà fragile. La réponse se déroule dans un contexte humanitaire complexe, marqué par les conflits, les déplacements de population, un accès limité aux services de santé et des lacunes persistantes en matière de prévention et de contrôle des infections (PCI), d'eau, hygiène et assainissement (EHA), de surveillance, de systèmes de référencement et de fournitures médicales essentielles. Ces difficultés augmentent le risque de transmission liée aux soins de santé et de perturbation des services de santé essentiels.

L'IRC a lancé une réponse intégrée à l'épidémie d'Ebola en collaboration avec le ministère de la Santé et les structures de réponse nationales, provinciales et de zone de santé concernées, notamment le COUSP, les Divisions provinciales de la santé (DPS), les équipes cadres des zones de santé (BCZ), les formations sanitaires et d'autres partenaires de la réponse. La réponse de l'IRC réunit les secteurs Santé, PCI/EHA, Communication sur les risques et engagement communautaire (CREC), Protection, et Santé mentale et soutien psychosocial (SMSPS). La réponse sanitaire vise à renforcer la capacité des formations sanitaires à détecter et référer en toute sécurité les cas suspects d'Ebola, à améliorer la PCI et la sécurité des patients, à renforcer la surveillance et les filières de référencement au niveau des formations sanitaires, et à soutenir la continuité en toute sécurité.

**APERÇU DU POSTE**

Le/la Coordinateur(trice) Santé assure le leadership technique global et la supervision programmatique de la réponse santé de l'IRC à la maladie à virus Ebola (MVE) en RDC. Rattaché(e) au Directeur adjoint des programmes (DDP) Ebola, le poste est chargé de veiller à ce que la réponse santé de l'IRC soit techniquement solide, opérationnellement réalisable, suivie par rapport aux résultats convenus, et alignée sur le ministère de la Santé (MoH), les structures nationales de réponse à la MVE et les normes de l'IRC.

Le/la Coordinateur(trice) Santé assure la direction technique de la programmation MVE au niveau des formations sanitaires, notamment la prévention et le contrôle des infections (PCI), le dépistage, le triage et l'isolement temporaire, la surveillance au niveau des formations sanitaires, la prévention de l'exposition professionnelle et la continuité en toute sécurité des services de santé essentiels. Le poste supervise directement les Responsables PCI seniors et assure la supervision technique, le mentorat et l'assurance qualité auprès des équipes PCI santé dans l'ensemble des sites de réponse. Le rôle travaille en étroite collaboration avec les équipes EHA, CREC et Protection afin de garantir une réponse intégrée et redevable.

**PRINCIPALES RESPONSABILITÉS**

**Leadership technique et qualité des programmes**

- Assurer le leadership stratégique et technique global de la réponse santé MVE de l'IRC, en traduisant l'épidémiologie de l'épidémie, les priorités de la réponse et les données de terrain en priorités programmatiques claires et en orientations techniques.
- Veiller à ce que les interventions de santé soient mises en œuvre conformément aux protocoles du MoH, aux directives nationales de réponse à la MVE, aux engagements envers les bailleurs et aux normes techniques de l'IRC.
- Assurer la supervision technique des mesures de prévention et de réponse à la MVE au niveau des formations sanitaires, y compris le dépistage et le triage, l'isolement temporaire, la circulation des patients, les précautions standard et liées à la transmission, l'hygiène des mains, le nettoyage et la désinfection environnementaux, la gestion des déchets biomédicaux, l'utilisation des EPI et la prévention de l'exposition professionnelle.
- Veiller à ce que les formations sanitaires appuyées par l'IRC puissent identifier, isoler et référer en toute sécurité les cas suspects de MVE tout en maintenant un accès sûr aux services de santé essentiels et en réduisant les risques de transmission liée aux soins.
- Orienter l'élaboration, l'adaptation et l'application des protocoles techniques, procédures opérationnelles standard (POS), listes de contrôle, aide-mémoires, outils d'évaluation et démarches d'amélioration de la qualité pour la réponse MVE.
- Veiller à ce que les priorités programmatiques et l'appui aux formations sanitaires soient fondés sur les risques et réactifs à l'évolution de l'épidémiologie, aux risques au niveau des formations sanitaires, aux expositions du personnel soignant, aux tendances d'utilisation des services et aux lacunes identifiées en matière de PCI/EHA.
- Fournir une orientation technique lors d'incidents cliniques ou de PCI significatifs, veiller à une escalade et un suivi appropriés, et appuyer l'adaptation des programmes sur la base des enseignements tirés.

**Gestion des programmes, suivi et amélioration de la qualité**

- Superviser la mise en œuvre des programmes santé/MVE de l'IRC par rapport aux plans de travail approuvés, aux cadres de résultats, aux indicateurs de performance, aux plans de dépenses et aux engagements envers les bailleurs, en veillant à des mesures correctives rapides lorsque la mise en œuvre s'écarte des objectifs.
- Effectuer des visites de terrain et des revues techniques régulières afin d'évaluer la qualité des programmes, d'encadrer les équipes, de vérifier la mise en œuvre et de suivre les mesures correctives convenues.
- Travailler avec les équipes MEAL afin de garantir la mise en place et l'utilisation cohérente de systèmes de suivi, de bases de données, d'indicateurs et de processus de qualité des données appropriés dans l'ensemble de la réponse santé.
- Examiner et analyser les données programmatiques, les scores d'évaluation PCI, les données de surveillance et de dépistage, les tendances d'utilisation des services, les résultats de formation et de mentorat, les événements d'infection/exposition du personnel soignant et les informations sur les intrants, afin d'orienter les décisions et l'amélioration des programmes.
- Veiller à la production en temps voulu de mises à jour programmatiques, de rapports internes, de rapports aux bailleurs et de contributions techniques aux rapports de situation précis et de haute qualité, documentant clairement les réalisations, les lacunes, les risques, les mesures correctives et les priorités.

**Supervision, leadership et développement du personnel**

- Superviser directement les Responsables PCI seniors et les autres membres du personnel de santé senior assignés, en définissant des priorités claires, en évaluant la performance et en garantissant la redevabilité en matière de qualité et de mise en œuvre des programmes.
- Assurer une supervision technique, un coaching et un mentorat réguliers auprès des Responsables PCI seniors et garantir des normes et approches techniques cohérentes dans l'ensemble des sites de réponse.
- Diriger le recrutement des postes clés en santé/MVE en coordination avec le DDP, les RH et la direction de terrain.
- Identifier les lacunes de capacité et garantir une formation technique structurée, un mentorat et un développement professionnel pour les équipes santé.
- Veiller à ce que des mesures de devoir de diligence appropriées soient appliquées pour les équipes travaillant en contexte d'épidémie, y compris le respect des protocoles de sécurité du personnel, la prévention de l'exposition et le signalement des incidents

**Développement des activités, gestion des subventions et supervision budgétaire**

- Participer activement à l'élaboration des notes conceptuelles et des propositions de réponse à Ebola, en assurant le leadership technique pour l'analyse des besoins, la conception des programmes, les paquets d'activités, les indicateurs, les cibles, les approches de mise en œuvre et les notes techniques narratives.
- Travailler avec les équipes Subventions, Finance, Opérations, MEAL et techniques afin d'élaborer des budgets de proposition réalistes, des structures de dotation en personnel, des besoins en approvisionnement et des plans de mise en œuvre alignés sur la conception du programme.
- Superviser la composante santé de la mise en œuvre des subventions et assumer la responsabilité de la gestion du budget du programme, y compris l'examen régulier du budget par rapport aux dépenses réelles (BvA), des plans de dépenses, des taux de consommation budgétaire, des prévisions et des écarts identifiés.
- Veiller à ce que les équipes santé maintiennent des plans d'approvisionnement et des prévisions actualisés pour les EPI, les intrants PCI, les fournitures médicales, les équipements et autres intrants programmatiques, en lien avec les plans d'activités et de dépenses.
- Veiller à ce que la quantification soit fondée sur le type de formation sanitaire, le volume de services, le niveau de risque, les données de consommation et les plans programmatiques, avec une action précoce pour éviter les ruptures de stock ou une utilisation inappropriée.
- Contribuer aux réunions de revue des subventions, aux rapports aux bailleurs et à la clôture des programmes, en veillant à l'alignement des livrables techniques, des dépenses et des résultats programmatiques.

**Coordination et représentation**

- Représenter l'IRC dans les forums de coordination pertinents aux niveaux national, provincial et de zone de santé, y compris le Cluster Santé et les structures techniques de réponse à la MVE.
- Entretenir des relations de travail constructives avec le MoH, les DPS, les autorités des zones de santé, la direction des formations sanitaires, les agences des Nations Unies, les bailleurs, les ONG et les autres partenaires de la réponse.
- Renforcer la qualité des activités de PCI par une supervision formative régulière avec les DPS et les zones de santé.

**Partenariats**

- Servir de point focal technique santé de l'IRC pour les partenariats appuyant la réponse à la MVE en Ituri et au Nord-Kivu, en travaillant en collaboration avec les responsables techniques des partenaires.
- Contribuer à la planification technique conjointe, à la revue et à l'adaptation de la réponse, en veillant à ce que les activités santé de l'IRC soient complémentaires à celles des partenaires et alignées sur les priorités convenues de la réponse.
- Représenter l'IRC dans les discussions techniques pertinentes avec les partenaires et veiller à ce que les actions techniques convenues concernant l'IRC soient communiquées et suivies en interne.

**Sécurité, sauvegarde et redevabilité**

- Travailler avec le service Sécurité et la direction de terrain pour surveiller les risques affectant les équipes santé et la mise en œuvre des programmes, et veiller à ce que les incidents ou préoccupations soient signalés et traités rapidement.
- Promouvoir une programmation centrée sur les clients et redevable, y compris la sensibilisation et l'utilisation appropriée des mécanismes de retour d'information et de plainte dans les services appuyés.
- Intégrer l'analyse des risques de sauvegarde et les mesures d'atténuation des risques pertinentes dans la conception et la mise en œuvre des projets.
- Maintenir à jour une cartographie multisectorielle des services et une filière de référencement pour la réponse aux violences. (Ceci sert des objectifs programmatiques mais sous-tend également les procédures opérationnelles standard de l'IRC pour la réponse à tout préjudice lié à la sauvegarde.)

**PROFIL RECHERCHÉ**

- Professionnel(le) de santé ayant une solide formation en santé publique (un master en santé publique serait un atout).
- Au moins 3 à 5 ans d'expérience progressivement responsable dans la programmation santé humanitaire ou d'urgence, y compris la gestion de programmes de santé complexes et la supervision de personnel technique senior.
- Une expérience opérationnelle avérée dans la réponse à la maladie à virus Ebola, à une autre fièvre hémorragique virale, ou à une épidémie de maladie infectieuse comparable est fortement souhaitée.
- Compétences avérées en leadership, communication et facilitation.
- Expérience de la gestion d'équipes multidisciplinaires sur plusieurs sites de terrain, avec de solides compétences en coaching, gestion de la performance et résolution de problèmes.
- Maîtrise de Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint et des outils courants de suivi de programme.
- La maîtrise du français est requise, avec un bon niveau d'anglais ; la connaissance des langues locales pertinentes est un atout.

**ENVIRONNEMENT DE TRAVAIL**

- Le poste nécessite des déplacements réguliers vers les formations sanitaires appuyées par l'IRC, les zones de santé et les sites de réponse en RDC.
- Le rôle peut nécessiter des visites dans des environnements cliniques, y compris des zones de dépistage, strictement conformément aux protocoles de PCI et de sécurité approuvés.
- Le poste exige une flexibilité pour répondre à l'évolution rapide des conditions épidémiologiques, opérationnelles et sécuritaires.

**Employeur garantissant l'égalité des chances** : L'IRC est un employeur garantissant l'égalité des chances. L'IRC évalue tous les candidats sur la base du mérite, sans distinction de race, de sexe, de couleur de peau, d'origine nationale, de religion, d'orientation sexuelle, d'âge, de situation matrimoniale, de statut d'ancien combattant, de handicap ou de toute autre caractéristique protégée par la législation en vigueur.

**Normes professionnelles** : Tous les collaborateurs de l’International Rescue Committee (IRC) doivent adhérer aux valeurs et principes fondamentaux énoncés dans le document « IRC Way – Normes de conduite professionnelle ». Nos normes sont l’intégrité, le service, l’égalité et la responsabilité. Conformément à ces valeurs, l’IRC met en œuvre et applique des politiques relatives à la protection des personnes, aux conflits d’intérêts, à l’intégrité financière, au signalement des irrégularités et à la protection contre les représailles. L’IRC s’engage à prendre toutes les mesures préventives nécessaires et à créer un environnement où chacun se sent en sécurité, ainsi qu’à prendre toutes les mesures nécessaires et correctives en cas de préjudice. L’IRC constitue des équipes de professionnels qui favorisent la réflexion critique, le partage des responsabilités, le débat et l’objectivité afin d’offrir les meilleurs services possibles à nos bénéficiaires.

**BACKGROUND**

On 15 May 2026, the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) declared its seventeenth Ebola outbreak following confirmation of cases in Ituri Province. The outbreak has since expanded to other affected and at-risk areas, placing additional pressure on an already fragile health system. The response is unfolding in a complex humanitarian context characterized by conflict, population displacement, limited access to health services, and persistent gaps in infection prevention and control (IPC), WASH, surveillance, referral systems, and essential medical supplies. These challenges increase the risk of healthcare-associated transmission and disruption of essential health services.

IRC has launched an integrated Ebola response in collaboration with the Ministry of Health and relevant national, provincial, and health zone response structures, including the COUSP, Provincial Health Divisions (DPS), Health Zone management teams (BCZ), health facilities, and other response partners. IRC’s response brings together Health, IPC/WASH, Risk Communication and Community Engagement (RCCE), Protection, and Mental Health and Psychosocial Support (MHPSS). The health response focuses on strengthening the capacity of health facilities to safely detect and refer suspected Ebola cases, improving IPC and patient safety, strengthening facility-based surveillance and referral pathways and supporting the continuity of safe.

**POSITION OVERVIEW**

The Health Coordinator provides overall technical leadership and program oversight for IRC’s Ebola Virus Disease (EVD) health response in DRC. Reporting to the Ebola Deputy Director of Programs (DDP), the position is responsible for ensuring that IRC’s health response is technically sound, operationally feasible, monitored against agreed results, and aligned with Ministry of Health (MoH), national EVD response structures and IRC standards.

The Health Coordinator leads the technical direction of the facility-based EVD programming, including Infection Prevention and Control (IPC), screening and triage and temporary isolation, facility-based surveillance, occupational exposure prevention and safe continuity of essential health services. The position directly supervises Senior IPC Managers and provides technical oversight, mentoring and quality assurance to health IPC teams across response locations. The role works closely with WASH, RCCE and Protection teams to ensure an integrated and accountable response.

**MAJOR RESPONSIBILITIES**

**Technical Leadership and Program Quality**

- Provide overall strategic and technical leadership for IRC’s EVD health response, translating outbreak epidemiology, response priorities and field evidence into clear program priorities and technical direction.
- Ensure health interventions are implemented in accordance with MoH protocols, national EVD response guidance, donor commitments and IRC technical standards.
- Provide technical oversight of facility-based EVD prevention and response measures, including screening and triage, temporary isolation, patient flow, standard and transmission-based precautions, hand hygiene, environmental cleaning and disinfection, healthcare waste management, PPE use and occupational exposure prevention.
- Ensure IRC-supported health facilities can safely identify, isolate and refer suspected EVD cases while maintaining safe access to essential health services and reducing healthcare-associated transmission risks.
- Guide development, adaptation and application of technical protocols, SOPs, checklists, job aids, assessment tools and quality-improvement approaches for the EVD response.
- Ensure program priorities and facility support are risk-based and responsive to evolving epidemiology, health-facility risks, healthcare-worker exposures, service-utilization trends and identified IPC/WASH gaps.
- Provide technical guidance during significant clinical or IPC incidents, ensure appropriate escalation and follow-up, and support program adaptation based on lessons learned.

**Program Management, Monitoring and Quality Improvement**

- Oversee implementation of IRC health/EVD programs against approved work plans, results frameworks, performance indicators, spending plans and grant commitments, ensuring timely corrective action where implementation is off track.
- Conduct regular field visits and technical reviews to assess program quality, mentor teams, verify implementation and follow up agreed corrective actions.
- Work with MEAL teams to ensure appropriate monitoring systems, databases, indicators and data-quality processes are in place and consistently used across the health response.
- Review and analyze program data, IPC assessment scores, surveillance and screening data, service-utilization trends, training and mentorship results, healthcare-worker infection/exposure events and commodity information to guide decisions and program improvement.
- Ensure timely, accurate and high-quality program updates, internal reports, donor reports and technical inputs to situation reports, clearly documenting achievements, gaps, risks, corrective actions and priorities.

**Staff Supervision, Leadership and Development**

- Directly supervise Senior IPC Managers and other senior health staff as assigned, setting clear priorities, reviewing performance and ensuring accountability for program quality and delivery.
- Provide regular technical supervision, coaching and mentoring to Senior IPC Managers and ensure consistent technical standards and approaches across response locations.
- Lead recruitment of key health/EVD positions in coordination with the DDP, HR and field management.
- Identify capacity gaps and ensure structured technical training, mentorship and professional development for health teams.
- Ensure appropriate duty-of-care measures for teams working in outbreak settings, including adherence to staff safety protocols, exposure prevention and incident reporting

**Business Development, Grant Management and Budget Oversight**

- Participate actively in development of Ebola-response concept notes and proposals, providing technical leadership for needs analysis, program design, activity packages, indicators, targets, implementation approaches and technical narratives.
- Work with Grants, Finance, Operations, MEAL and technical colleagues to develop realistic proposal budgets, staffing structures, procurement requirements and implementation plans aligned with program design.
- Oversee the health component of grant implementation and maintain responsibility for program budget management, including regular review of Budget versus Actuals (BvA), spending plans, burn rates, forecasts and identified variances.
- Ensure health teams maintain updated procurement plans and forecasts for PPE, IPC commodities, medical supplies, equipment and other program inputs, with appropriate linkage to activity and spending plans.
- Ensure quantification is informed by facility type, service volume, risk level, consumption data and program plans, with early action to prevent stock-outs or inappropriate use.
- Contribute to grant review meetings, donor reporting and program close-out, ensuring technical deliverables, expenditure and program results remain aligned.

**Coordination and Representation**

- Represent IRC in relevant national, provincial and Health Zone coordination forums, including Health Cluster and EVD-response technical structures.
- Maintain constructive working relationships with the MoH, DPS, Health Zone authorities, health-facility leadership, UN agencies, donors, NGOs and other response partners.
- Strengthen the quality of IPC activities through regular supportive supervision with the DPS and Health Zones.

**Partnerships**

- Serve as IRC’s health technical focal point for partnerships supporting the EVD response in Ituri and North Kivu, working collaboratively with partner technical leads.
- Contribute to joint technical planning, review and adaptation of the response, ensuring IRC’s health activities are complementary to those of partners and aligned with agreed response priorities.
- Represent IRC in relevant partnership technical discussions and ensure agreed technical actions relevant to IRC are communicated and followed up internally.

**Safety, Safeguarding and Accountability**

- Work with Safety and Security and field leadership to monitor risks affecting health teams and program delivery and ensure incidents or concerns are promptly reported and addressed.
- Promote client centered and accountable programming, including awareness and appropriate use of feedback and complaint mechanisms in supported services.
- Build safeguarding risk analysis and relevant risk mitigation measures into project design and implementation.
- Maintain updated, multisector service mapping and referral pathway for violence response. (This serves programming purposes but also underpins IRC's standard operating procedures for response to all safeguarding harm.

**REQUIRED PROFILE**

- Health professional with a strong public health background (MPH desirable).
- At least 3- 5 years of progressively responsible experience in humanitarian or emergency health programming, including management of complex health programs and supervision of senior technical staff.
- Demonstrated operational experience in Ebola Virus Disease, another viral haemorrhagic fever, or comparable infectious-disease outbreak response is strongly preferred.
- Demonstrated leadership, communication, and facilitation skills.
- Experience managing multidisciplinary teams across multiple field locations, with strong coaching, performance-management and problem-solving skills.
- Proficiency in Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint and routine program monitoring tools.
- Fluency in French is required with strong English proficiency; relevant local languages are an asset.

**WORKING ENVIRONMENT**

- The position requires regular travel to IRC-supported health facilities, Health Zones and response locations in DRC.
- The role may require visits to clinical environments, including screening areas, strictly in accordance with approved IPC and safety protocols.
- The position requires flexibility to respond to rapidly changing epidemiological, operational and security conditions.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

title: Employment Specialist
body:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

***This position has an end date of September 30, 2027.***

**Job Overview:** The Employment Specialist in Iowa assists newly arrived refugees and other qualified immigrants to attain self-sufficiency through employment by guiding them through employment preparation, coordinating job placements, and other career advancement services.

**Major Responsibilities:**

Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

- Conduct intake, assessment and provide program orientation to clients eligible for employment services. Develop comprehensive employment plans and budget strategies for each employable adult. Provide job readiness and job search coaching and connect clients with job opportunities.
- Develop and cultivate long-term relationships with area employers and staffing agencies to identify appropriate employment opportunities for clients.
- Assist clients and employers as necessary with post-placement issues and continuing employment needs.
- Monitor client job performance, wage levels, and related metrics.
- Detail each client interaction in accordance with program requirements. Input client information in database(s) and assist with tracking and reporting as needed.
- Collaborate effectively with coworkers and partner organizations. Build and maintain relationships with area service providers for the benefit of clients.
- Use personal, insured vehicle and/or public transportation (where available) to travel and transport clients and materials as needed throughout the service delivery area.
- May train and lead the activities of support staff, volunteers, and interns.
- Other duties as assigned.

**Job Requirements:**

**Education:** Bachelor’s degree in social work or related field of study preferred.

**Work Experience:**

- Relevant professional experience in workforce development field required; minimum of 2 years’ experience strongly preferred.
- Experience working with refugee and/or immigrant populations strongly preferred.
- Experience with job placement and job readiness training a plus.

**Demonstrated Skills & Competencies:**

- Strong relationship building, diplomacy, and networking skills; ability to effectively build internal and external relationships.
- Demonstrated success working and communicating effectively in a multi-cultural environment.
- Self-starter with excellent problem-solving skills combined with the proven ability to multi-task, prioritize duties, and manage time effectively.
- Attention to detail and accuracy in work product.
- Proficient in English, both spoken and written; proficiency in language(s) spoken by client group is desired
- Proficient in Microsoft Office applications (Word, Excel, Outlook); ability to use the internet and other digital tools for data entry, research and problem-solving purposes.
- Valid driver’s license and access to a personal, insured vehicle.

**Working Environment:**

- A combination of standard office environment, remote work, and ‘field’ time within the service delivery area to perform the above outlined responsibilities.
- May require occasional weekend and/or evening work.

**Compensation:** ($21.00/hr - $22.80/hr). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law***.***

**US Benefits:** We offer a comprehensive and highly competitive set of benefits. In the US, these include: 10 sick days, 10 US holidays, 20-25 paid time off days depending on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $143 per month, dental starting at $6.50 per month, and vision starting at $5 per month, FSA for healthcare and commuter costs, a 403b retirement savings plans with immediately vested matching, disability & life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program which is available to our staff and their families to support counseling and care in times of crisis and mental health struggles.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

title: Research Manager for Afghanistan, based in Kabul
body:
## BACKGROUND ON IMPACT AND REACH

IMPACT Initiatives is a humanitarian NGO, based in Geneva, Switzerland. The organisation manages several initiatives, including the REACH Initiative. The IMPACT team comprises specialists in data collection, management and analysis, GIS and remote sensing. IMPACT was launched at the initiative of ACTED, an international NGO with headquarters based in Paris and presence in thirty countries. The two organizations have a strong complementarity formalized in a global partnership, which allows IMPACT to benefit from ACTED’s operational support in its fields of intervention.

### We are currently looking for a Research Manager to scope out and set-up a new Research Team focussing on the Economy, Markets, and Livelihoods

**Department**: IMPACT

**Position**: Research Manager

**Contract duration**: 4 months

**Starting Date**: 1st December 2026 (preferred); 1st January 2027 (latest)

**Location**: Kabul, Afghanistan.

## COUNTRY PROFILE

The humanitarian response in Afghanistan remains one of the largest in the world, with 21.9 million people identified as in need of assistance in the 2026 Humanitarian Needs and Response Plan. The country is particularly vulnerable to climate change, with drought conditions affecting agriculture and livelihoods. Natural disasters, including flooding and earthquakes, remain prevalent – often causing displacement, damaging and destroying shelter and services, and disrupting livelihoods. Conflict remains a risk, with recent increase in conflict activity between Afghanistan and Pakistan. With millions of refugees in neighbouring countries, including Iran and Pakistan, forced return of refugees is also a driver of needs in the country.

Alongside this, since the De facto Authorities took control of the government in 2021, a range of restrictive policies have significantly restricted the rights of women and girls in society – leading to increased marginalisation and protection risks. The economic situation remains poor and authorities lack resources to run effective public services, with reliance on humanitarian assistance. As the USA was a major aid donor in Afghanistan, their withdrawal of all aid funding had a significant effect, for example on the closures of health centres. With political positioning of donor governments restricting a full development approach, a basic human needs response is increasingly complementing the humanitarian response across Afghanistan.

Against this backdrop, IMPACT Initiatives is planning a range of research activities to support an evidence- and needs-based humanitarian response. The IMPACT Deputy Country Representative (DCR) supports the Country Representative (CR) in overseeing programme strategy and implementation internally, as well as external representation of IMPACT.

## POSITION PROFILE

Following the development of our new Country Strategy, IMPACT Afghanistan is planning to establish a new research team with the aim of providing relevant information to humanitarian and basic human needs stakeholders linked to the economy, markets and livelihoods in Afghanistan.

IMPACT Afghanistan is therefore seeking an experienced Research Manager with knowledge of assessment and analysis, to scope out a programme of work for this new team, through internal and external consultations. The Research Manager will be responsible for drafting concept notes and research ToRs that can be used to solicit funding for the start-up of the team.

The Research Manager will be responsible for building an understanding of the relevant aid strategies existing in Afghanistan and identifying relevant data and research gaps that could be filled. This will involve connections with international and national NGOs (including members of Cash Consortium of Afghanistan), the UN, and donors. The Research Manager will review existing research in Afghanistan (including the MSNA and Joint Market Monitoring Initiative) and also connect across IMPACT to understand similar research being conducted elsewhere that could be adapted for the Afghanistan context.

## RESPONSIBILITIES

The Research Manager’s responsibilities will include:

***CONTEXTUAL UNDERSTANDING***

- Assess relevant strategic, analytical, and operational documents to develop an understanding of the current priorities relating to the economy, markets and livelihoods for the aid response in Afghanistan.
- Mapping existing IMPACT data, other research, and other relevant information sources to understand relevant areas for potential assessment and research.
- Connecting with national and international NGOs, UN colleagues, and the donor community to understand their priorities and to identify where IMPACT research could support their programmes and strategies.
- Provide SMT and other staff members with key updates from these efforts.

***DEPARTMENT STRATEGY DEVELOPMENT***

- Engage with IMPACT colleagues in HQ and in other country programmes to identify existing assessment and research tools that could be adapted for Afghanistan.
- Develop a series of concept notes that can be shared with prospective partners or donors, to seek funding for the set-up for the new team.
- Develop/draft relevant research ToRs, enabling technical discussion and approval of potential research projects.
- Develop a light-touch team strategy that could subsequently be further developed based on the eventual set-up and staffing of research activities.
- Coordinate with staff in the Cash Consortium of Afghanistan to identify potential assessment and research opportunities for the future of the Consortium.

***RESEARCH MANAGEMENT***

- As necessary, support the Humanitarian Coordination and Monitoring Unit in the delivery of research and analysis linked to Joint Market Monitoring Initiative and the Cash Consortium of Afghanistan.
- As required, work with the cross-cutting analysis team to support the develop of analysis products linked to the economy, markets, and livelihoods, which can better position IMPACT Afghanistan in this thematic field.

The Research Manager will maintain the strictest confidentiality on all data collected and related processes. They will actively take measures to prevent the unauthorized sharing of any information and data belonging to IMPACT and its partners or collected during his/her assignment with IMPACT.

## REQUIREMENTS

- **Work experience** Demonstratable relevant working experience in a humanitarian setting, such as programme management, evaluation and assessments. Experience working with development responses is an advantage;
- **Thematic experience** Able to showcase experience in working with economy and market data in an aid environment’
- **Research skills** Excellent quantitative and qualitative research design, data collection, and data analysis experience required;
- **Familiarity with aid system** Good understanding of the aid system and the research community.
- **Management experience** Demonstrated team management skills, including remote management;
- **Experience in geographical region** Past experience in the region/supporting is desirable;
- **Communication/reporting skills** Excellent communication and drafting skills for effective reporting and reviewing;
- **Cross-cultural work environment** Ability to operate in a cross-cultural environment requiring flexibility and work independently;
- **Academic qualifications** A Master’s degree in a relevant discipline is preferred. However, significant relevant work experience can be considered.
- **Software skills** Proven knowledge of the Microsoft Office Suite, to include Word, Excel, and PowerPoint. Familiarity with R, SPSS and/or STATA or other statistical analysis software an asset
- **Security environment** Ability to operate in a complex and challenging security environment.
- **Language skills** Fluency in English required, competency in Dari or Pashto is an asset.

## COMPENSATION & BENEFITS

- For this position, salary between 3’050€ and 3’100 monthly before income tax), etc as well as a monthly living allowance of 300 USD *NB - IMPACT salaries are strictly determined by our salary grid depending on the grade of the position and the level of education of staff. A location-dependent security and/or isolation adjustment is then applied as a recognition that some staff are required to work in difficult places where living and working conditions are much more difficult than elsewhere.*
- Accommodation and food provided in the guesthouse.
- Affiliation to French Social security (CFE) + health Complementary (Mobility Benefits) + Repatriation assistance (SOS International) + Private Pension Fund.
- Flight tickets every six months & visa fees covered (in-country travel costs and professional expenses are fully covered).
- R&R after eight weeks, flight ticket up to 500$ + 200$ of living allowance
- Contribution to the transportation of luggage: between 20 and 100 kgs, depending on the length of the contract (+ luggage and personal property insurance)
- Annual leave of 36 days per year. Public holidays of the country of assignment. Family/compassionate leave when applicable.
- Predeparture induction - three days at IMPACT Initiatives’ HQ in Geneva + one week pre-departure training in ACTED HQ in Paris, including a 4-days in situ security training (depending on previous inductions and security trainings taken);
- IMPACT prioritizes the psychological safety of its staff and the health insurance provided covers, among others, up to 1000 € per year of psychosocial counselling fees.

title: Accounting & Audit Intern for HQ, based in Geneva
body:
## BACKGROUND ON IMPACT AND REACH

IMPACT Initiatives is a humanitarian NGO, based in Geneva, Switzerland. The organisation manages several initiatives, including the REACH Initiative. The IMPACT team comprises specialists in data collection, management and analysis, GIS and remote sensing. IMPACT was launched at the initiative of ACTED, an international NGO whose headquarter is based in Paris and is present in thirty countries. The two organizations have a strong complementarity formalized in a global partnership, enabling IMPACT to benefit from ACTED’s operational support on its fields of intervention.

**Position:** Accounting and Audit Intern

Under the supervision of the Deputy Head of Finance, the Accounting and Audit Intern is responsible for supporting the Finance & Admin Unit from Geneva in the monthly tasks of the accounting cycle, in the collection, control and preparation of supporting documentation for external audits, while maintaining the databases up to date.

## **REQUIREMENTS**

NB – IMPACT salaries are strictly determined by our salary grid depending on the grade of the position and the level of education and experience of staff. A contribution to medical insurance of 520 CHF per month is already included in the salary figure.
- Insurance covering professional and non-professional accidents throughout the period of employment with IMPACT
- Health insurance, life insurance and repatriation assistance in case of field visits/temporary deployments
- Enrolment in IMPACT Initiatives Research Foundational Learning Programme within the first 3 months from the start of contract.

title: Education Content Manager
body:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**SCOPE**

Education is central to that mission. The IRC works to ensure that even the hardest-to-reach children in the most challenging places are able to go to school and thrive, defining success through education outcomes spanning infancy to young adulthood: access to safe, functional and responsive education across all ages; early childhood learning and nurturing care; primary school-aged learning; post-primary learning; safety in school; and gender equality across all education outcomes. Delivering on these outcomes at scale increasingly depends on innovation - including the thoughtful use of education technology to strengthen the quality of teaching and learning and to extend support to teachers and learners who are otherwise out of reach.

To meet the sector's toughest education challenges, the IRC's Education Technical Unit (TU) collaborates with the Airbel Impact Lab - the IRC's research and innovation department - to design, test, and scale innovative solutions that reach last-mile teachers and learners. A flagship example is aprendIA, an AI-powered teacher professional development program delivered via low-tech, widely accessible channels to support teachers working in under-resourced, crisis-affected, and multilingual classrooms.

The Education Content Manager plays a central role in supporting content and pedagogy quality assurance across this work. Sitting at the intersection of pedagogy, quality assurance, and content development, the Manager helps ensure that what teachers experience is pedagogically sound, contextually appropriate, and safe. In the near term, the bulk of this role will focus on aprendIA; over time it may extend to the IRC's broader portfolio of teacher support and education innovation initiatives as priorities evolve.

**Major Responsibilities:**

Working under the direction of the Education Advisor and in support of senior technical staff, the Education Content Manager focuses on execution, quality, and content development - rather than setting technical strategy or leading external representation - across the following areas:

**Testing, quality assurance & troubleshooting for digital & AI-enhanced programming**

- Conduct regular testing of digital course flows, prompt responses, and chatbot behaviors - assessing accuracy, clarity, pedagogical alignment, and cultural appropriateness.
- Communicate testing notes with developer(s) on the team and collaborate on solutions that maintain pedagogical quality.
- Red-team digital content to identify edge cases, problematic outputs, and safety gaps.
- Maintain clear, actionable QA logs that track issues, findings, and resolution status across the initiatives supported.
- Synthesize findings into prioritized recommendations, distinguishing content fixes from product or design fixes, and flag where testing results suggest content may not be achieving its intended learning purpose.
- Review usage, completion, and engagement data findings alongside QA findings to surface early signals of whether content is supporting teacher learning and uptake, flagging patterns for senior technical and MEAL colleagues.
- Troubleshoot content-related issues flagged by country teams or surfaced through data and program monitoring, and support testing of new features, materials, and content updates ahead of release.
- Review and quality-assure teaching and learning content and materials across TU projects as requested, checking for pedagogical soundness, evidence alignment, and contextual fit.

**Capturing process & learning**

- Refine quality frameworks and rubrics for evaluating digitally delivered pedagogical content, including dimensions such as context fit and alignment with evidence-based practice.
- Document QA and content-development processes, criteria, and lessons learned for internal use and external sharing.
- Connect testing and QA insights to available evidence on teacher engagement, classroom practice, and learner outcomes, contributing to the team’s understanding of what is driving impact in digital an AI-enabled teacher support.
- Support senior technical and MEAL colleagues in translating content and QA insights into evaluation questions and learning agenda priorities, so that testing feeds directly into how the team understands outcomes and impact.
- Contribute to accessible knowledge products (e.g. blog posts, working papers, briefs) that articulate what quality looks like in technology-enabled and conventional teacher professional development, in support of the team's thought leadership and external engagement.
- Support presentations, funder updates, and partner briefings that draw on QA findings and learning across projects.
- Adapt and apply quality frameworks and documentation practices to other TU content and teacher-support materials as requested.

**Content development**

- Work alongside government, local partners and local content creators to develop and adapt content for programs, ensuring alignment with local curriculum, global best practices and user interface (UI) requirements.
- Draft and refine short, structured course content for digital modalities, aligned with strategy, templates, and evidence-based pedagogy.
- Develop one-off or thematic modules in response to identified needs (e.g. managing test anxiety during exam periods; supporting children with learning difficulties in large classes).
- Review and refine content deliverables such as quiz questions and strategy descriptions, and support localization review for new cultural and operational contexts.
- Develop and adapt teaching and learning materials for other TU teacher-support and innovation initiatives as requested, drawing on existing IRC resources, established course outlines, and context-specific input.
- Propose alternative formats through which courses and learning games can still qualify as recognized coursework (completion criteria, evidence of learning, assessment logic) while deliberately departing from the conventional module-and-assessment structure, grounded in how educators actually engage in low-connectivity, messaging-based, time-constrained settings.

**Broader innovation & cross-TU support**

- Support senior technical staff in scoping and needs assessment for new deployments, contexts, and delivery modalities.
- Provide flexible content, quality assurance, and documentation support across the Education TU and its collaboration with the Airbel Impact Lab as organizational priorities evolve.

**Key Working Relationships:**

**Department:** Education Technical Unit; AcceleratED team

**Reports to**: Education Advisor for Foundational Learning & Content Innovation

**Works closely with**: AcceleratED team, including product and developer colleagues, as well as education technical advisors and country program teams

**Other Internal and/or external contacts:**

- **Internal:** Airbel Impact Lab colleagues, Education Technical Unit staff, country program teams supporting deployment and localization of education programming
- **External:** Subject-matter experts, consultants, and country-level partners engaged for content development, review, and localization, in coordination with senior technical staff.

**Job Qualifications:**

**Required**

- Master's degree in International Education or a related field (or a Bachelor's degree with equivalent additional professional experience).
- Classroom teaching experience.
- International experience, ideally in low-resource, crisis- or conflict-affected contexts.
- Experience developing education or teacher professional development content grounded in evidence-based pedagogy.
- Strong analytical skills and a demonstrated eye for detail, with the ability to test, evaluate, and troubleshoot content systematically.
- Excellent writing skills, including the ability to produce clear, concise, audience-ready content and documentation.
- Ability to work independently and productively in a fast-paced, collaborative, cross-functional, and geographically dispersed team.
- Ability to apply a diversity and inclusion lens to work, and excellent interpersonal and communication skills across a multicultural environment and multiple time zones.
- Commitment to the mission and values of the IRC.
- Proficiency in spoken and written English.

**Desirable**

- Strong interest in, or experience with, EdTech and the use of AI in education, particularly in low-tech modalities.
- Experience creating, adapting, or localizing content for multilingual or humanitarian contexts.
- Familiarity with teacher professional development frameworks and classroom observation or quality instruments.

***Travel***:

- Up to 20% travel for 1-3 weeks each time to assigned countries, including crisis- and conflict-affected contexts, in line with IRC’s security policies.

**Compensation:** ($68,000 - $74,000). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**Benefits:** IRC offers a comprehensive and competitive benefits package. Highlights include 10 paid sick leave, 10 U.S. holidays, 20-25 generous paid time off based on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163/month, dental starting at $6.50/month, and vision starting at $5/month, flexible spending accounts (healthcare, dependent care, and commuter), a 403(b) retirement savings plan with employer match (immediate vesting) along with a non-elective employer contribution based on age and years of service (3-year vesting), disability and life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program (EAP) offering confidential counseling and support services for employees and their families.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

title: Software Developer
body:
**Description**

The **Pacific Community** (SPC) is the principal scientific and technical organisation in the Pacific region, supporting development since 1947. We are an international development organisation owned and governed by our 27 country and territory members. In pursuit of sustainable development to benefit Pacific people, our unique organisation works across more than 25 sectors. We are known for our knowledge and innovation in such areas as fisheries science, public health surveillance, geoscience, and conservation of plant genetic resources for food and agriculture.

The **Fisheries, Aquaculture and Marine Ecosystems (FAME)** division is composed of three programmes: the Coastal Fisheries and Aquaculture Programme (CFAP); the Oceanic Fisheries Programme (OFP); and the Marine Ecosystems Programme (MEP). The Director’s Office provides implementation support and strategic direction across the three programmes and cross-cutting projects. Working with all 22 PICTs, SPC FAME has strong partnerships with regional, sub-regional and national entities working in the marine sector. SPC FAME staff are based in New Caledonia, Fiji, Federated States of Micronesia, Solomon Islands, and Tonga, with most of the staff being based in New Caledonia.

The **Software Developer** will design, develop, maintain, and support Full-stack fisheries information and database management systems for both SPC and WCPFC member countries; develop, maintain, and enhance OFP mobile applications; develop and maintain data integration and workflow infrastructure to support fisheries and climate science programmes; provide technical support and training to National Fisheries staff and SPC personnel on system functionality, data workflows, and data management processes and contribute to the design and implementation of new technologies and data collection tools that support emerging fisheries research and climate change initiatives.

The key responsibilities of the role include the following:

**Information systems and application development**

- Develop and maintain fisheries database management systems, in particular, the Tufman2 tuna fisheries database management system
- Develop and maintain mobile applications used to collect tuna fisheries and environmental data to support fisheries and climate-related research
- New functionality is delivered in response to business, scientific, and operational requirements

**Data management and scientific data collection**

- Design, develop, document and maintain the regional tuna fisheries database systems for the registration, entry, importing and querying of data
- Data integration, validation, and workflow processes are maintained and improved

**WCPFC and SPC members support and collaboration**

- Technical support is provided to SPC staff, member countries, and regional partners
- Train and support national staff in the use of fisheries database management systems and mobile applications

For a more detailed account of the key responsibilities, please **refer to the online job description**.

**Key selection criteria**

**Qualifications**

- Specialized degree in IT, computing, science, or mathematics or equivalent body of knowledge and experience.

**Technical expertise**

- At least 4 years’ experience as software developer in web application and data workflow developments, using languages such as C#, JavaScript and Python
- At least 4 years’ experience administrating SQL databases
- At least 4 years’ experience with Git and CI/CD
- Demonstrated experience in the design and development of mobile device applications
- Experience as an Analyst, working with the client to get their information system requirements

**Language skills**

- Good communications skills (English)

**Interpersonal skills and cultural awareness**

- Ability to work and travel in a multicultural and multilingual environment

**Salary, terms and conditions**

**Contract Duration** – This contract is budgeted for 3 years and is subject to renewal depending on funding and performance.

**Remuneration** – the **Software Developer** is a band 10 position in SPC’s 2026 salary scale, with a starting salary range of SDR (special drawing rights) 3,727-4,562 per month, which converts to approximately XPF 537,766-658,322 (USD 4,994-6,114; EUR 4,506-5,517). SPC salaries are not presently subject to income tax in New Caledonia. An offer of appointment for an initial contract will normally be made in the lower half of this range, with due consideration given to experience and qualifications. Progression within the salary scale will be based on annual performance reviews.

**Benefits for Staff in a position advertised internationally (EPAI) whose duty station is Noumea** – SPC provides housing support in Noumea. Establishment and repatriation grant, removal expenses, airfares, home leave travel, health and life and disability insurances and education allowances are available for eligible employees and their eligible dependents. Employees are entitled to 25 working days of annual leave per annum and other types of leave, and access to SPC’s Provident Fund (contributing 8% of salary, to which SPC adds a 10% contribution).

**Languages** – SPC’s working languages are English and French.

**Recruitment principles** – SPC’s recruitment is based on merit and fairness, and candidates are competing in a selection process that is fair, transparent and non-discriminatory. SPC is an **equal-opportunity employer**, and is committed to cultural and gender diversity, including bilinguism, and will seek to attract and appoint candidates who respect these values. Due attention is given to gender equity and the maintenance of strong representation from Pacific Island professionals. If two interviewed candidates are ranked equal by the selection panel, preference will begiven to the **Pacific Islander**. Applicants will be assured of complete confidentiality in line with SPC’s private policy.

title: Agriculture, Market Systems and Climate Finance Senior Advisor, VisionFund International
body:
**Agriculture, Market Systems and Climate Finance Senior Advisor, VisionFund International**

VisionFund International is World Vision’s microfinance provider serving vulnerable clients through loans, savings, and insurance. We enable families to grow their livelihoods in hard to reach, rural locations in 28 countries so that caregivers can create secure futures for their children.

We believe in brighter futures for children; empowering families to create incomes and jobs; unlocking economic potential for communities to thrive.

Join VisionFund as we seek to end intergenerational poverty through microfinance.

**Here’s where you come in:**

As **Agriculture, Market Systems and Climate Finance Senior Advisor**, you will serve as the technical lead and focal point internally and externally for these three important, connected, and strategic areas of intervention for VisionFund. You will provide technical advice on current best practices, support the development of related products, guide strategy and organisational positioning, and support resource development and programme management for related Agricultural, Climate, and Market Systems initiatives and grants.

You will manage the CrediEnterprise credit product pilot project in nine countries in Africa and Central America as part of the THRIVE 2030 programme, ensuring it delivers on its targets while coordinating with and reporting to World Vision partners. You will oversee grant reporting, project management, operational delivery, capacity building of national staff, and integration of this component with other interventions within the THRIVE 2030 programme.

You will provide technical leadership to position VisionFund for institutional funding to support its growing Agricultural, Climate, and Market Systems interventions globally. You will support donor pre-positioning, grant writing, and the Resource Development team with technical content throughout proposal development processes.

**Technical Advisory**

You will provide technical advice to VisionFund Operations and MicroFinance Institutions across the network on Agricultural, Market Systems, and Climate industry best practices. You will lead VisionFund’s Internal Climate Financing working group, using your knowledge and experience to shape VisionFund strategy, products, and market positioning. You will also represent VisionFund in technical working groups, including Environmental and Climate Action forums, to communicate VisionFund strategy and strengthen brand visibility within the World Vision partnership.

**Resource Development**

You will support resource development activities for Agricultural, Climate, and Market Systems initiatives through grant writing, review, and donor positioning. You will provide technical advice and content for new and existing grant applications, lead VisionFund’s positioning with agricultural, climate, and market systems-focused donors and opportunities, and leverage learnings from the implementation of CrediEnterprise under THRIVE 2030 to pursue additional institutional funding.

You will represent the organization in technical grant calls and donor visits as needed, establish a mechanism for tracking ESCA climate-finance engagements and opportunities, and provide technical advisory support for the implementation of new and ongoing institutional funding in partnership with the Resource Development and Operations teams. You will also lead sector learning, evidence documentation, and dissemination to support VisionFund’s positioning and acquisition activities.

**Operational Delivery**

You will oversee the implementation of CrediEnterprise as part of the THRIVE 2030 programme and other relevant Agricultural, Climate, and Market Systems projects. You will manage CrediEnterprise implementation to achieve THRIVE 2030 targets, working closely with MFI Country Managers and World Vision field offices. You will supervise product training rollout and provide ongoing coaching and mentoring to MFI staff.

You will support the gathering of commodity profiles for the agrocalculator, lead the replication of standard tools and processes developed by Operations into CrediEnterprise projects, and ensure CrediEnterprise figures are accurately reflected in core banking and impact tracking systems. You will monitor performance metrics, assess progress, resolve implementation bottlenecks, and agree on corrective actions with MFIs, escalating issues to Regional and Operational Directors as needed.

You will ensure quality control of MFI partnerships supporting CrediEnterprise implementation, ensure integration with other financial products such as insurance and savings, and maintain coordination and differentiation between Savings Group linkage and the CrediEnterprise product. You will support MFIs in recruiting and developing Agri and Business Development Officers, provide training on THRIVE 2030, monitoring and evaluation, and reporting standards, and build the capacity of CrediEnterprise managers to use the e-THRIVE platform and other World Vision digital platforms for decision-making.

**Programme Reporting and Knowledge Management**

You will lead market systems, agricultural, and climate finance reporting, particularly for CrediEnterprise THRIVE 2030 programme reporting, learning, and knowledge management. You will establish a structured monitoring and evaluation framework, in collaboration with the VFI Global Impact team, to track product performance, gather field data, and assess client feedback.

You will coordinate technical input into VisionFund’s quarterly DME and narrative reporting for THRIVE 2030 quarterly AP and donor progress reports, aligned with THRIVE DME indicators. You will review quarterly THRIVE 2030 market systems reports to identify opportunities to scale CrediEnterprise financing across THRIVE countries and participate in regular country-specific quarterly THRIVE report reviews.

You will develop annual priorities, implementation plans, and budgets for the function in alignment with available resources. You will also develop case studies, implementation briefs, and other learning products to support Community of Practice learning.

**Requirements include:**

- 10 years' experience agri, climate and market systems finance, preferably in Africa
- Agricultural Economics or relevant agricultural degree (or equivalent practical experience). Post-graduate level degree
- Proven experience in market systems and agricultural lending i.e. understands farmer value chains production cycles and cashflows
- Able to communicate the fundamentals of market systems and climate resilience
- Proven ability to implement projects - action oriented, proven ability to implement and follow up
- Good communication skills with staff and partners
- Demonstrated experience in partnering, grant applications, reporting and other writing skills
- Experience across a range of countries (not limited to one or two places is a plus)
- Experience of Value chain/market systems financing or finance to agricultural cooperatives
- Demonstrated experience of working on and or designing programs with a climate change component
- Working level proficiency of written and verbal English. Spoken and written Spanish or French will be a plus

**Travel and/or Work Environment Requirement:** The position requires ability and willingness to travel domestically and internationally up to **35%** of the time.

title: Job Counselor
body:
**BACKGROUND**

The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world’s worst humanitarian crises and helps people to survive and rebuild their lives. Founded in 1933, the IRC offers lifesaving care and life-changing assistance to refugees forced to flee from war or disaster. At work today in over 40 countries, the IRC aims to restore safety, dignity and hope to millions who are uprooted and struggling to endure. In response to the arrival of refugees in Greece in 2015, the IRC has been offering SMS, WASH and Protection services. Among others, through its child protection programs, the IRC has been offering individual support through case management to vulnerable children and their families, non-formal educational activities for children through Safe Healing and Learning Spaces and emergency accommodation and protection to unaccompanied children.

**SCOPE OF WORK**

Since 2017, IRC Hellas supports vulnerable youth refugee and host communities in Athens to access income generation through employment and self-employment services and skills-building activities, directly and in collaboration with partners. Building on this experience, IRC Hellas, with the support of UNHCR and in partnership with the Municipality of Thessaloniki, is implementing the Youth Empowerment and Self-Reliance project for the third year to promote socio-economic equal access for vulnerable youth in Thessaloniki.

To support with the implementation of the project, IRC Hellas is recruiting a Job Counselor, to be responsible for the day-to-day implementation of employability activities, including service mapping, stakeholder engagement, job counseling and Job Readiness Trainings.

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES**

Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

- Organize needs assessment and service mapping activities related to employability and skills development programming for youth;
- Participate in stakeholder engagement activities;
- Support the project implementation by designing, organizing and leading Job Readiness Trainings and information sessions for youth;
- Support the project implementation by providing individual employment support/job counseling for youth;
- Proactively working to identify issues related to clients’ participation and report them to the Project Manager.
- Ensuring relevant project data is accurately collected and updated on a weekly and monthly basis.
- Coordinate closely with the team to ensure effective implementation of the provided activities;
- Participate in regular team meetings;
- Ensure regular reporting from the projects is compiled and reports are submitted to the Senior Livelihoods Manager on a weekly/monthly basis;
- Any other task designated by the Project Manager as requested.

**REQUIREMENTS**

BA/BS Degree in social sciences, education, project management, and/or related certification required. Master’s degree or additional certification in Job Counseling is strongly preferred.

- Minimum 2 years’ experience in training, employment support, counseling or project management, primarily in relation to refugee protection. NGO experience preferred.
- Strong interest in supporting refugees and vulnerable populations (experience supporting youth a plus)
- Demonstrated understanding and ability to maintain confidentiality and respect for clients and partners
- Good interpersonal and strong negotiation skills essential with experience in conflict resolution desirable
- Excellent verbal communication skills
- Strong liaison and diplomatic skills
- Punctuality and attention to detail
- Computer skills, in particular Excel
- Fluency in both Greek and English is mandatory

**WORK ENVIRONMENT**

**Working hours:** 9:00-17:00

**Travel and other requirements:** Occasionally to other areas of IRC programs in Greece.

**Disclaimer Clause:** This job description is not an exhaustive list of the skills, effort, duties and responsibilities associated with position.

Due to the expected high number of applications, only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

**Compensation:** (Pay Rate: €1,631/month). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

title: Training Officer
body:
*This position is contingent on receipt of grant funding.*

**Job Overview**

The International Rescue Committee (IRC) is one of the leading providers of high-quality programming for refugees resettling to the United States. The IRC is committed to developing innovative programs that respond to the refugees’ unique strengths and needs, using our learning and experience to shape policy and practice, and highlighting and promoting best practices in refugee services provision.

The IRC is seeking a Training Officer for Switchboard, a project that provides training and capacity-building services to service providers in the United States, including resettlement agencies and affiliates, state agencies, ethnic community-based organizations, and others. More information about Switchboard can be found at [www.SwitchboardTA.org](https://reliefweb.int/file:///C:/Users/TigestCo/AppData/Local/Microsoft/Olk/Attachments/ooa-fefcb179-4b91-4707-b044-59e9496f57fe/69780562696ebcadf2340c5c93711aeb96e9493d8b84ea912d714b7dd9c61fdb/www.SwitchboardTA.org).

The Training Officer will be responsible for leading the development and delivery of capacity-building initiatives related to newcomer and refugee services. This role includes providing training and technical assistance to service providers to support them in addressing the general resettlement and case management needs of refugees and newcomers. This role requires prior direct service experience working with clients, subject matter experts, and/or partners to develop culturally responsive service plans to address individual and family client needs utilizing a broad range of approaches, including client-centered, strength-focused, and trauma-informed to meet the social, safety and stability of newcomers.

This staff will be responsible for producing and maintaining high-quality performance by collaborating with experts, designing effective resources, and facilitating learning experiences that contribute to improving outcomes for children, adults, and families.

**Major Responsibilities:**

**Training and Technical Assistance**

- Develop and deliver training related to refugee and newcomer services, to include webinars, self-paced, e-learning courses, online certificate courses, in-person training, etc.
- Provide consultation, guidance, and recommended resources via email and/or virtual meetings to refugee service providers across the U.S., in response to questions and technical assistance requests
- Produce written learning resources including blog posts, information guides and toolkits
- Incorporate feedback from internal and external reviewers
- Lead development of multimedia resources, including e-learning modules, videos, and podcasts, in collaboration with colleagues across teams
- Coordinate a monthly community of practice focused on refugee and newcomer emerging topic needs

**Project Management**

- Contribute to the creation of Switchboard’s annual training and technical assistance (TTA) workplan.
- Ensure related trainings and learning resources are developed and delivered on time and on budget.
- Use effective communication and collaborative skills with a wide range of stakeholders
- Manage external subject matter expert/consultant relationships and project plans as they contribute to the development of related TTA.

**Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E)**
