title: Medical Coordinator (F/M) - Afghanistan
body:
Do you want to join a committed, activist-driven organization and take meaningful action for social justice?

For over 40 years, Médecins du Monde has been delivering healthcare to the most vulnerable, challenging barriers to access, and driving long-term change in health policies.

In France and across nearly 30 countries, our work is built around six core missions:

- Sexual and reproductive health and rights (including access to safe abortion)
- Migration, exile, human rights and health
- Harm reduction
- Health and the environment
- Healthcare systems
- Humanitarian spaces

## MdM in Afghanistan

Médecins du Monde re-opened its mission in Afghanistan in 2021 and currently implements programmes in primary healthcare, sexual and reproductive health and rights (SRHR), mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS), nutrition and harm reduction through a combination of direct implementation and partnerships with local organizations. The mission operates in a complex environment marked by restrictions imposed by de facto authorities, constraints affecting women’s participation and access to services, evolving humanitarian needs and significant challenges for the health system. Current programmes are implemented in Wardak, Farah and Nimroz provinces and place a strong emphasis on community engagement, quality of care and access to essential health services.

## About the role

You will join the mission at a pivotal moment. Beyond ensuring the quality and relevance of medical activities, you will play a key role in strengthening the mission’s medical leadership, supporting teams, reinforcing SRHR priorities and helping to structure programmes, partnerships and ways of working in line with Médecins du Monde’s values and standards. Working closely with the General Coordinator, HQ Health Advisor and programme teams, you will contribute directly to improving access to quality healthcare for vulnerable populations across Afghanistan.

## What you'll do

? Define, drive and monitor the mission's medical strategy and ensure its alignment with MdM's global priorities, with a particular focus on SRHR.

? Ensure the quality, relevance and effectiveness of health, nutrition, MHPSS and SRHR activities across all programmes.

? Lead, support and develop medical teams through coaching, capacity-building and performance management.

? Analyse programme performance and medical data to guide decision-making and continuous improvement.

? Design new projects, contribute to donor proposals and support the mission's strategic development.

? Represent MdM with health authorities, humanitarian actors, partners and community stakeholders.

? Adapt programmes and priorities in response to contextual changes, population needs and humanitarian emergencies.

## Who you'll work with

You will report directly to the General Coordinator and maintain a strong functional relationship with the Health Advisor based at headquarters. You will supervise a technical medical team of two to three people and work closely with programme managers, medical supervisors, support departments and local partners across the mission. The position also requires regular interaction with health authorities, UN agencies, humanitarian coordination mechanisms and community representatives.

## What you'll gain

- Develop advanced leadership skills in one of the world's most complex humanitarian contexts.
- Strengthen your expertise in SRHR programming, community-based health approaches and health system strengthening.Gain significant experience in humanitarian negotiation, representation and stakeholder engagement
- Contribute to meaningful, high-impact programmes supporting vulnerable communities while helping shape the future strategic direction of the mission.
- Propose and develop projects relating to women’s rights and health, in collaboration with local organisations.

### REQUIREMENTS

## You are the right match if you:

- Demonstrate a strong commitment to human rights, non-discrimination and respectful engagement, even in sensitive contexts where values, beliefs or lifestyles differ significantly from your own.
- Can provide strategic medical leadership and bring structure, clarity and direction to complex health programmes.
- Lead teams through trust, listening, accountability and collaboration while fostering a healthy and inclusive work environment.
- Have successfully strengthened the quality, relevance and impact of SRHR or public health programmes.
- Build productive relationships and negotiate effectively with authorities, partners and diverse stakeholders in challenging environments.
- Remain calm, analytical and decisive when responding to emergencies, operational constraints or rapidly changing contexts.

## This role may not suit you if:

- You favour directive or individualistic approaches over collaboration, dialogue and collective problem-solving.
- You struggle to provide constructive management, clear communication and respectful feedback.
- You are uncomfortable representing humanitarian principles and advocating for vulnerable populations in sensitive environments.
- You prefer highly structured and predictable settings over complex and evolving humanitarian contexts.
- You are not aligned with Médecins du Monde's values, principles and activist approach.

## Recruitment process

Apply soon! If shortlisted, you will first meet with our HR team. Technical and managerial interviews, which may include practical case studies, will follow.

Please note: as part of our anti–money laundering and counter-terrorism policy, international background checks may be conducted. Data is processed confidentially and securely. More info: [https://www.medecinsdumonde.org/en/working-internationally/](https://www.medecinsdumonde.org/en/working-internationally/)  
All successful candidates must provide a criminal record extract (B3).

## Ready to apply?

We only need your CV and a cover letter.

If this role sounds like the right fit for you, apply now – we'd love to hear from you!

### **EMPLOYMENT CONDITIONS**

**Contract & status:**

- Gross monthly salary: € 3,664
- Fixed-term contract (6 months), starting as soon as possible
- Single posting

**Work environment:**

- Position based in Kabul, Afghanistan
- Regular field visits

**Benefits:**

- 13th-month salary (for employees with more than 6 months’ seniority)
- Expatriation allowance: 10% of gross monthly salary
- Coverage of travel (home – mission), visas, and vaccinations
- Accommodation: in a guesthouse with other expatriates initially, with the possibility of individual housing later on
- Health insurance (50% covered by MdM and 50% by the employee)
- Repatriation insurance
- MdM promotes training and internal mobility

**Essentials:**

- 5 weeks paid leave + 22.5 RTT days per year
- More info: [https://www.medecinsdumonde.org/en/working-internationally/](https://www.medecinsdumonde.org/en/working-internationally/)

**Our commitment to diversity and inclusion**

MdM is committed to the inclusion of people with disabilities and to fighting all forms of discrimination.  
If you are officially recognized as a person with a disability and/or require workplace accommodations, please let us know.

title: Senior Health Technical Lead/Specialist
body:
**BACKGROUND**

The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGOs), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities, helping people survive, reclaim control of their futures, and strengthen their communities.

The IRC was present in Sudan from 1981 to 2009. In November 2019, the IRC re-registered in Sudan and, with the wider IRC-led Consortium (CARE International, Catholic Relief Services, Medical Teams International, Relief International, and local partners), currently delivers integrated health and nutrition services across 11 states, supporting 640 health facilities and service delivery points nationwide and reaching over four million beneficiaries in 2025.

Since the outbreak of war in April 2023 between the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) and the Rapid Support Forces (RSF), the country has spiraled into relentless violence, institutional collapse, and mass displacement, and is facing one of the most complex and devastating humanitarian crises in the world today. More than 30 million people now require humanitarian assistance, and around 25 million people face acute food insecurity, including 770,000 children suffering from severe acute malnutrition.

The project is expected to run for the duration of the World Bank-financed award (exact start date and duration to be confirmed on award).

**Senior Health Technical Lead Scope of Work**

The IRC is seeking a Senior Health Technical Lead for an upcoming World Bank-funded health project in Sudan. The project is intended to restore access to a basic package of health and nutrition services and preserve the main elements of essential public health functions in Sudan.

The project is expected to run from February 2027 for 3 years.

The Senior Health Technical Lead provides technical leadership and quality assurance across SHARE II's health and nutrition service delivery and health system strengthening activities including primary health care and hospital services, nutrition programming (CMAM/IYCF), communicable and non-communicable disease management, reproductive, maternal and newborn health, disease surveillance and outbreak preparedness, health information systems (DHIS2/EWARS/HMIS), and facility-level WASH and infection prevention and control. They will ensure service delivery is technically sound, aligned with national health strategies and World Bank requirements. SHARE II will sustain and maintain SHARE I’s existing footprint in delivering a basic package of health services to 420 PHCs and 10 hospitals and also expand access to essential health services in prioritized high-need localities. The project will be delivered nationwide across multiple states including RSF and SAF controlled areas and many areas with severe to catastrophic health needs.

The postholder will lead facility readiness assessments and IPC protocols; oversees nutrition programming and evidence generation; supports health workforce strengthening, referral pathways, and differentiated delivery models; and provides technical guidance on DHIS2/HMIS, disease surveillance, outbreak preparedness and emergency response, climate-resilient facility and WASH improvements, laboratory and blood systems, digital health, and supply chain/pharmaceutical management, coordinating closely with Consortium partners.

The Senior Health Technical Lead represents the IRC-led consortium in relevant technical coordination mechanisms (Health, Nutrition and WASH Clusters, Strategic Advisory Group, technical working groups), liaising with WHO, UNICEF, and Federal/State Ministries of Health, and reinforcing government-led systems. They ensure technical activities comply with World Bank Operational Policy 7.30, the Procurement Regulations, and the Environmental and Social Framework, including SEA/SH prevention and response; supports the Third-Party Monitoring mechanism, IRC's Community Feedback Mechanisms and the project's Grievance Redress Mechanism; and supports continuity of SRH and GBV services across the Consortium.

The Senior Health Technical Lead supports the phased, consultative handover of SHARE I sites into SHARE II, ensuring continuity of services, staffing, incentives, commodities and data systems during transition, and contributes to sustainability and responsible exit planning, including integration into MoH plans. The Senior Health Technical Lead provides technical inputs to project reporting, including results framework/indicator tracking for submission to the Project Director and the World Bank, and supports capacity building of MoH and local partner staff consistent with IRC's Partnership Excellence for Equality and Results System (PEERS).

**Requirements**

- Medical degree (MD/MBBS) or an advanced degree (Master's) in public health, health systems management, or a related field.
- Minimum 10-15 years' progressive experience in health systems strengthening and/or PHC and hospital service delivery programming, including significant experience in Sudan or comparable fragile, conflict-affected, or access-constrained settings.
- Demonstrated technical expertise in health and nutrition and relevant technical areas including PHC/hospital service delivery, nutrition (CMAM/IYCF), communicable and non-communicable disease management, reproductive/maternal/newborn health, GBV/SRH, mental health, disease surveillance and outbreak response and health information system.
- Prior experience on large health and nutrition projects financed by the World Bank or other major institutional donors; familiarity with health cluster coordination.
- Experience working with, or through, Ministry of Health structures and health-sector coordination mechanisms (Health Cluster, WHO, UNICEF).
- Strong data analysis, facility assessment (HeRAMS), and technical report writing skills, and demonstrated experience supporting multi-partner consortium coordination.
- Fluency in English required; Arabic strongly preferred, given the requirement for field-facing engagement with MoH/SMoH counterparts and communities.
- Ability to travel to field locations across Sudan, including hard-to-reach and access-constrained areas, and to operate effectively under insecure or volatile conditions, in line with IRC and UNDSS security protocols.

Please note that this position will be contingent on the outcome of the bid.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

title: Youth Education Specialist (YESOL)
body:
This position is represented by the OPEIU union and subject to the terms and conditions of a collective bargaining agreement.

**Background/IRC Summary:**  
The International Rescue Committee responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic well-being, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is at work in over 40 countries and 25 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. Since 1999, the IRC has developed partnerships with New York City public schools, community-based organizations and local colleges and universities to support the positive development of refugee youth and their communities in New York City. The Education and Learning Program provides year-round programming working directly with refugee youth, their parents and families, and their schools.

**Job Overview/Summary:**  
The Youth Education Specialist (YESOL) will work closely with the Youth Programs Supervisor to support high-quality programming for refugee and immigrant youth in New York City. The specialist will be working on a team that works on youth programs including, but not limited to, Youth Tutoring, online Youth English for Speakers of Other Languages (YESOL) classes, Leaders in Training (LIT), a college access and career readiness program for high school juniors and seniors, World Explorers, a cultural awareness program, and sports programming. During the annual Newcomer Youth Summer Academy (NYSA), the Youth Education Specialist will provide logistical support to teaching staff, coordinate instructional coaching, coordinate classroom assessment materials, and collect, enter, and analyze assessment data, ensuring the overall day-to-day classroom needs of the Academy are met. The specialist will also support with instruction and field trips during Mini-NYSA programs, which occur during school breaks in the middle of the school year.

**Major Responsibilities:**

This position will lead Youth English for Speakers of Other Languages (YESOL) classes:

**Curriculum Preparation**

- Create and improve YESOL curriculum to meet the needs of current student population, including academic English and test preparation
- Prepare slideshows for each class
- Update syllabi for each group as semester progresses

**Intake and Assessment**

- Manage new referral and contact information, outreach to potential families and students
- Administer baseline, midline and endline English assessments, coordinate intake process
- Collaborate with parents and teachers to identify specific student needs

**Teach YESOL Classes**

- 2-3 groups of Middle School: Beginner and Intermediate
- 2 groups of High School: Beginner and Intermediate
- Additional groups based on student need and program capacity

**YESOL Program Monitoring & Evaluation**

- Track class attendance and document daily individual and class case notes
- Gather qualitative data of program impact through student surveys and staff observations
- Synthesize and present data for annual reports

**Intern Management**

- Recruit and hire Youth ESOL interns
- Delegate weekly tasks and review submitted projects and tasks
- Provide opportunities for leadership and professional development

**Saturday Parent ESOL Classes**

- Take lead on managing ESOL classes for parents of youth programs students

**Mini Newcomer Youth Spring Academy (Mini NYSA) and Newcomer Youth Summer Academy (NYSA) Support** — direct responsibility for the academic program

- Support NYSA program planning, including staff and volunteer recruitment, hiring, and training
- Plan and instruct lessons on ESOL and other topics to groups of up to 25 students
- Participate in all Meet & Greets, staff trainings, program meetings, and staff development activities thereafter
- Assist the Dean of Instruction in the implementation and analysis of various student assessment initiatives, including but not limited to content area assessments, progress reports, and report cards
- Monitor submission of, enter, and analyze student assessment data
- Assist in the timely production and dissemination of necessary assessments and resources for all teaching staff
- Assist in the coordination and set up of caregiver-teacher conferences
- Assist in the coordination and implementation of school-wide Multi-Tiered Systems of Support (MTSS)
- Lead the coordination and implementation of all staff-appreciation events and initiatives
- Lead groups of students for off-site field trips
- Perform other duties as assigned

**Key Working Relationships:**

- Position reports to: Youth Programs Supervisor
- Position directly supervises: Interns
- Other internal and/or external contacts: Other youth program staff

**Job Requirements:**

- Bachelor's degree in education or relevant field; Master's degree candidate in education preferred
- Must be available for Saturdays to run programming
- Strong command of Microsoft Suite, G Suite, Canva, and other digital platforms required
- Classroom teaching experience preferred (both in-person and online, especially TESOL experience)
- Experience with data collection and analysis
- Strong organizational skills and meticulous attention to detail
- Strong written and oral communication skills
- Cultural competence and cross-cultural or overseas experience required
- Experience working with immigrant populations, highly desirable
- Ability to work independently and as part of a team
- Ability to work in a fast-paced environment, adapting programming to shifting client needs and relevant government policy changes
- Fluency in written and spoken English required. Second language proficiency in relevant language highly desirable (including Spanish, French, Dari, Farsi, Pashto, Arabic, Tibetan, Russian, Haitian Creole, Ukrainian, Mandarin, etc.)
- Flexibility to work on Saturdays and evenings based on program requirements

**Working Environment:**

- All applicants must be based in or willing to work from our New York City office
- The IRC NYC RAI office currently operates on a hybrid schedule (3 days in office, 2 remote)
- During Mini-NYSA and NYSA, the specialist is expected to work in-person Monday–Friday at a centrally located public school in New York City
- During school-year programming, the specialist will be expected to work Tuesday–Saturday
- Online ESOL classes during the school year take place after school hours; specialists should expect school-year hours of 11am–7pm, Tuesday–Friday
- Saturdays are in-person at the IRC office from 9am–5pm

***This position is expected to end on August 31, 2027.***

**Compensation:** (Pay Rate: $27.50/hr). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**US Benefits:** We offer a comprehensive and highly competitive set of benefits. In the US, these include: 10 sick days, 10 US holidays, 20-25 paid time off days depending on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163 per month, dental starting at $6.50 per month, and vision starting at $5 per month, FSA for healthcare and commuter costs, a 403b retirement savings plans with immediately vested matching, disability & life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program which is available to our staff and their families to support counseling and care in times of crisis and mental health struggles.

title: (Senior) Research Officer for Nigeria, Based in Dakar
Coordinateur logistique voltigeur - Worldwide (F/H)
body:
Vous souhaitez intégrer une association militante et agir concrètement pour plus de justice sociale ?

Médecins du Monde agit depuis plus de 40 ans pour soigner les populations les plus vulnérables, dénoncer les entraves à l’accès aux soins et faire évoluer durablement les politiques de santé.

En France et dans près de 30 pays, nos actions s’articulent autour de six combats politiques :

- droits et santé sexuels et reproductifs (dont le droit à l’avortement)
- migration, exil, droits et santé
- réduction des risques
- santé environnement
- droits et système de santé
- espaces humanitaires

## **Pourquoi nous avons besoin de vous**

Les interventions d’urgence face aux crises, conflits, catastrophes naturelles, sont l’un des axes prioritaires d’intervention pour Médecins du Monde. Notre indépendance financière, la force de nos partenariats, l'implication et la flexibilité de nos équipes sont autant d’éléments clés pour apporter une réponse efficace à ces catastrophes.

Le mandat de la Cellule Urgence est d’intervenir en priorité sur les urgences et crises qui surviennent dans les pays où MdM est déjà opérationnel (30 pays). La réponse d’urgence dans les pays où MdM n’est pas présent est systématiquement considéré si l’accès au continuum de soins est interrompu et si les capacités du pays et des acteurs sur place sont dépassées.

MdM fournit également un appui et une expertise opérationnelle et technique aux missions des pôles géographiques sur leurs réponses d’urgences.

Vous faites partie de l’équipe voltigeur.euse.s de la Cellule Urgence qui est donc déployée dans les contextes d’urgence pour lancer de nouvelles interventions et/ou renforcer les équipes existantes. Vous pouvez également être déployé.e pour participer à des missions exploratoires, participer à l’ouverture de nouvelles missions et/ou de nouvelles bases, appuyer les opérations/missions existantes MdM à travers du « gap-filling » ou appuyer la mise en œuvre d’activités spécifiques liées aux activités logistiques (ex : formation, préparation, etc.).

## **Vos missions**

Vos principales responsabilités sont :

- Piloter la stratégie logistique de la mission et en assurer la mise en œuvre
- Coordonner et superviser l’ensemble des activités logistiques : chaîne d’approvisionnement, parc de véhicules, gestion des stocks, équipements, bâtiments, infrastructures informatiques, moyens de communication et énergie
- Animer et renforcer les capacités de l’équipe
- Appuyer également le/la coordinateur·rice général·e dans le suivi des procédures de sécurité
- Veiller au respect et à la bonne application des procédures MdM et bailleurs, et contribuer à garantir la qualité, l’efficacité et la conformité des services logistiques au sein de la mission, tout en œuvrant à la prévention et à la lutte contre la fraude et la corruption

Le partage du temps de travail entre le terrain et le siège est évaluée à 80%-20%.

La durée d’un déploiement sur le terrain est de trois 3 mois maximum, et est suivie par un temps de récupération.

## **Vos collègues**

Vous travaillez sous la responsabilité du responsable de la Cellule urgences basé au siège. Lorsque vous êtes déployé.e sur le terrain, vous reportez directement au/à la coordinateur.rice général.e de la mission. Vous avez un lien fonctionnel avec le/la référent.e logistique basé.e au siège. Vous collaborez avec les coordinateur.rice.s support ainsi qu'avec le/la chargé.e d'accès humanitaire & risques et les équipes programme.

## PROFIL

**Vous êtes la bonne personne si :**

- Vous avez une formation supérieure bac+2 type achat ou logistique
- Vous justifiez d'une expérience professionnelle de 5 ans (dont minimum 1 an sur un poste en coordination logistique dans le milieu humanitaire ou de minimum 2 ans d'expérience en tant que logisticien)
- Vous avez une solide résistance au stress et une capacité à vous adapter dans des contextes sécuritaires complexes
- Vous maitrisez le Pack Office
- Vous maitrisez l’anglais et le français couramment à l’écrit comme à l’oral

**Ce poste n'est pas pour vous si :**

- La flexibilité et l’adaptabilité ne comptent pas parmi vos principales qualités ; les déplacements fréquents ainsi que les changements réguliers d’équipe vous posent des difficultés
- Vous craignez de ne pas vous retrouver dans les valeurs et le positionnement militant de Médecins du Monde.

## Les prochaines étapes

Si votre candidature est sélectionnée, nous vous contacterons pour vous proposer un entretien RH avec notre chargée de recrutement. Puis viendront l'entretien technique et managérial (auquel des cas pratiques pourront éventuellement être intégrés).

Dans le cadre de la lutte contre le blanchiment et le financement du terrorisme, des vérifications d’antécédents sur listes internationales pourront être effectuées. Les données sont traitées de façon confidentielle et sécurisée. Plus d’infos : [http://bit.ly/3CSThBs](http://bit.ly/3CSThBs)

Un extrait de casier judiciaire (B3) sera demandé à toute personne recrutée.

## Nous attendons votre candidature

Nous n’avons besoin que de votre CV et de votre lettre de motivation.

Si vous pensez correspondre à ce poste, n’attendez plus, postulez !

## VOS CONDITIONS D'EMPLOI

**Contrat & statut :**

- CDD à pourvoir dès que possible et jusqu'au 31/12/2026
- Salaire brut mensuel de 3 392 €
- Statut : agent de maitrise
- Poste à temps plein

**Les avantages :**

- Télétravail ponctuel
- 13e mois (pour les salarié.e.s ayant plus de 6 mois d’ancienneté)
- Prime de déplacement terrain de 198,18€ brut/mois au prorata du temps de présence sur le terrain
- Au siège, tickets restaurants d’une valeur unitaire de 10€ (participation à hauteur de 60% de MdM, 40% salarié.e) et sur le terrain via une allocation forfaitaire de restauration fixée en fonction du pays
- Au siège, remboursement du titre de transport en commun à 50% (abonnement mensuel) et prise en charge à 100% des allers-retours siège-terrain
- Logement pris en charge sur le terrain à 100%
- Mutuelle prise en charge à 100%
- MdM favorise la formation et la mobilité interne

**Les indispensables :**

- 5 semaines de congés + 22,5 RTT par an
- Engagement fort en faveur de l’inclusion et de la lutte contre toutes les discriminations
- Plus d’infos : [https://bit.ly/3x5MezL](https://bit.ly/3x5MezL)

**Cadre de travail :**

- Poste basé au siège à Saint-Denis (20% du temps) et sur les terrains internationaux (80% du temps)
- Déploiement sur le terrain pas avant 1 mois d’intégration
- Travail sur écran, en open space
- Communication orale et téléphonique
- Posture assise prolongée

**Diversité et inclusion**

MdM s’engage pour l’insertion des personnes en situation de handicap et lutte contre toutes les discriminations.

Si vous bénéficiez d’une reconnaissance de la qualité de travailleur.se handicapé.e et/ou si vous avez besoin d’un aménagement de poste, n’hésitez pas à nous en faire part.

title: International Education Expert
body:
**About STOOS**

STOOS is an international research and consulting firm providing **evaluations, assessments, research, capacity building and project management** services across humanitarian and development settings. We work with NGOs, international organizations and other partners to generate evidence, strengthen programmes and improve outcomes for communities across the Middle East, Africa, Eastern Europe and beyond.

STOOS invites applications from experienced **international Education Experts** to collaborate on education-related consultancy assignments. **Experts based in any country are welcome to apply.** Assignments will be **primarily remote**, with occasional travel depending on project requirements and agreed availability.

**Role Overview**

The Education Expert will provide technical and strategic support to education assignments, drawing on substantial experience in **managing and implementing education projects internationally**. The role will include contributing to programme design, evaluations, assessments, research and capacity building, working closely with STOOS teams, clients and national partners.

We are particularly interested in experts who combine **practical programme management experience with strong research, evaluation and analytical skills**, and can translate evidence into feasible recommendations for education programming.

**Key Responsibilities**

- **Programme design and technical support:** Contribute to education strategies, theories of change, results frameworks and implementation approaches that improve access, quality, equity and learning outcomes.
- **Project management and implementation:** Provide guidance on work planning, implementation quality, partner coordination, monitoring and adaptive management.
- **Evaluations, assessments and research:** Lead or contribute to education evaluations, needs assessments, feasibility studies and thematic research, including methodology development, sampling and research tool design.
- **Technical analysis:** Assess issues relating to formal and non-formal education, teacher development, inclusive education, education systems and **Education in Emergencies (EiE)**.
- **Data analysis and reporting:** Review programme documentation, analyse qualitative and quantitative findings, and produce clear reports with practical recommendations.
- **Stakeholder engagement:** Facilitate consultations, interviews and workshops with education authorities, donors, implementing partners, teachers, learners and community representatives.
- **Capacity building:** Develop training resources and strengthen the capacities of project teams, local partners and researchers through coaching and technical guidance.
- **Quality assurance and safeguarding:** Ensure deliverables meet agreed standards and integrate **child safeguarding, research ethics, gender equality, disability inclusion and conflict sensitivity**.
- **Proposal development:** Contribute technical inputs to education-related proposals, including approaches, methodologies, workplans and deliverable frameworks.

**Required Qualifications and Experience**

**Education**

- A **Master’s degree or higher in Education, International Education, Education Policy, International Development** or a closely related discipline.

**International Professional Experience**

- **At least eight years of professional experience in managing and implementing education projects internationally**, including work across different country contexts.
- Demonstrated responsibility for education programme planning, delivery, team or partner coordination, monitoring and quality assurance.
- Experience working with **international NGOs, UN agencies, donors, government institutions or international consulting organizations**.
- Strong understanding of challenges affecting education access, participation, retention and learning outcomes, particularly for marginalized and crisis-affected populations.
- Demonstrated experience conducting or contributing to **education evaluations, assessments or research**, using qualitative and quantitative methods.
- Experience translating programme evidence into actionable recommendations for implementing organizations, policymakers and development partners.

**Technical and Collaboration Skills**

- Strong analytical skills and the ability to produce **clear, well-structured reports**.
- Ability to develop research tools, review data quality and synthesize findings from multiple sources.
- Proven ability to collaborate with **multicultural teams and national partners**, including through remote working arrangements.
- Strong organizational skills, responsiveness and the ability to deliver high-quality outputs within agreed deadlines.
- Commitment to safeguarding, ethical research and culturally appropriate engagement with children, young people and communities.

**Languages**

- **Fluency in English is mandatory**, including excellent speaking, analytical writing and report-writing skills.
- **Proficiency in additional languages is an asset.**

**Areas of Expertise of Particular Interest**

Applicants may bring expertise in one or more of the following areas:

- **Education in Emergencies** and education in conflict or displacement settings.
- Inclusive education, disability inclusion and gender-responsive programming.
- Teacher professional development, pedagogy and teaching quality.
- Foundational literacy and numeracy, learning assessment and learning recovery.
- Non-formal education, accelerated education and pathways back into formal schooling.
- Education systems strengthening, policy analysis and institutional capacity development.
- Early childhood education and development.
- Integration of child protection, psychosocial support and wellbeing within education programmes.

**Working Arrangements**

Engagements will be **consultancy-based and linked to specific assignments**. Most activities—including document review, methodology development, remote consultations, analysis, reporting and technical coordination—will be undertaken remotely.

The scope, duration, level of effort and fees will be agreed for each assignment. Where travel is required, arrangements will be discussed in advance.

title: Recruitment for Multiple (Senior) Analyst Positions Across Multiple Regions & Countries: Acute Needs Analysis, Multiple Locations
body:
*Veuillez trouver la version française ci-dessous*

*PLEASE NOTE: This is a global call for applications to fill multiple Analyst and Senior Analyst vacancies hosted across various IMPACT country offices in Latin America & the Caribbean (LAC), Middle East & North Africa (MENA), and Sub-Saharan Africa. Candidates should indicate their preferred analysis context (see table below) on the application form. In your cover letter, please provide your motivation for the top 3 analysis context preferences you select on the application form*

## **BACKGROUND ON IMPACT AND REACH**

Founded in 2010 and headquartered in Geneva, [IMPACT Initiatives](https://www.impact-initiatives.org/what-we-do/) is a leading applied research organization and the largest independent provider of data in crisis-affected contexts. Through our initiatives—REACH, AGORA, and PANDA—we enable humanitarian and other aid actors to make better, evidence-based decisions by delivering timely, relevant, and methodologically rigorous data and analysis. Our extensive presence across crisis-contexts allows us to collect data directly from crisis-affected people wherever needed, including among the most vulnerable and hard-to-reach. [REACH](https://www.impact-initiatives.org/what-we-do/reach/), initiative of IMPACT, strengthens evidence-based humanitarian decision-making through efficient data collection, management, and analysis – before, during, and after an emergency.

All of IMPACT’s programs are implemented in support of humanitarian coordination structures. IMPACT’s team comprises specialists in data collection, management, and analysis, as well as experts in humanitarian response, GIS, and remote sensing.

### We are currently looking for various (Senior) Analysts – Acute Needs Analysis to support our teams in multiple locations.

**Position:** (Senior) Analyst – Acute Needs Analysis

**Contract duration**: Up to 6 months

**Starting Date**: Mid-September 2026

**Location**: Multiple country office locations across **LAC**, **MENA**, **Sub-Saharan Africa** (see below location preference to be indicated on applicant form).

### POSITION PROFILE

In response to the shifting humanitarian financing landscape, IMPACT is placing greater emphasis on producing **comparable, decision-oriented analysis products to inform humanitarian prioritization.** This position will be working on the second round of the Acute Needs Analysis (ANA) - a flagship analytical output that summarizes available data to provides a concise, actionable understanding of **risk of loss of life** across geographies and population groups within a crisis **in order to feed into key decision-points, such as the HPC and donor allocations.**

The **(Senior) Analyst – Acute Needs Analysis** will be responsible for producing this analytical product at country level. This includes reviewing and synthesizing data, conducting structured analysis using IMPACT’s global analytical guidance, and producing a short, high-impact external brief. The analyst will work closely with GIS, data, and design colleagues to incorporate visual elements into the final output. The final analytical product will play a key role in informing humanitarian prioritization decisions.

### RESPONSIBILITIES

#### DEVELOPMENT OF ANALYTICAL PRODUCT - ACUTE NEEDS ANALYSIS

- Lead the implementation and delivery of the analysis project at the country level, in coordination with the HQ programme team.
- Align the rollout with global schedules and ensure adherence to IMPACT’s analytical standards.
- Develop and maintain a strong stakeholder mapping and a network of collaborators at country level to enhance contextual understanding / monitoring.
- Ensure development of user-centered products and, where relevant, support joint analysis with relevant stakeholders.

#### DATA REVIEW AND CONSOLIDATION

- Collect and synthesize relevant secondary data from REACH assessments, UN agencies, INGOs, and public datasets (e.g., OCHA, FEWS NET, IPC), including via building and maintaining necessary relationships.
- Evaluate data reliability and identify critical gaps.
- Support decisions on the need for targeted, light-touch primary data collection.

#### ANALYTICAL PROCESS AND INTERPRETATION

- Apply IMPACT’s global analytical guidance to produce structured, consistent, and context-relevant analysis of acute needs analysis.
- Use defined frameworks (e.g. Risk of Excess Mortality) to identify areas at risk of large-scale loss of life and estimate the number of people experiencing life-threatening conditions
- Clearly document assumptions, limitations, and analytical reasoning.

#### OUTPUT PRODUCTION AND DISSEMINATION

- Draft the Acute Needs Analysis brief using standardized global templates and language.
- Collaborate with GIS and design colleagues to include maps, caseload tables, and other visual aids.
- Ensure internal review and validation of the product before dissemination.
- Present findings to clusters, working groups, and donors as needed.
- As needed, support the development of Global Key Messages based on country level findings.

#### LEARNING, INNOVATION, AND QUALITY ASSURANCE

- Participate in lessons-learned reviews and propose improvements to global analysis processes and guidance.
- Contribute to organisational learning on running analysis workstreams and contribute to reflections and development of additional analytical workstreams, in collaboration with country and global counterparts.
- Support internal knowledge sharing and analytical training at the country level.
- Stay updated on sectoral best practices and innovations in humanitarian analysis.
- The (Senior) Analyst will maintain the strictest confidentiality on all data collected and related processes. They will actively take measures to prevent the unauthorized sharing of any information and data belonging to IMPACT and its partners, or collected during his/her assignment with IMPACT.

### REQUIREMENTS

Note, roles can be at Senior Analyst or Analyst level, based on the experience of the candidate.

#### REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

- **3** **years of relevant working experience** in a humanitarian setting, such as analysis, assessments, monitoring and evaluation and research design etc. with direct in-country experience;
- **Excellent academic qualifications**, including a master’s degree or equivalent in a relevant discipline (e.g. international development studies / international relations, humanitarian response, data science, political science, etc.);

#### TECHNICAL SKILLS:

- **Excellent analytical and critical thinking skills** with experience of interpreting complex data and producing clear, actionable insights.
- **Strong writing skills** and experience producing clear, concise briefs for external audiences.
- **Proficiency in Excel**, with experience of an additional analytical tool (e.g. PowerBI, SPSS, R, STATA, or Python) and an understanding of basic GIS processes and outputs an asset.
- **Familiarity with different qualitative and quantitative research methods**, with the ability to evaluate the quality of different data sources.
- **Understanding of humanitarian coordination systems**, including HPC and inter-agency needs analysis and assessments.
- **Contextual knowledge** is an asset. Please highlight in your application if you have experience working in one or more of the potential contexts listed below

#### COMMUNICATION AND ORGANIZATIONAL SKILLS

- **Ability to manage complex workflows** and deliver high-quality outputs under tight deadlines.
- **Experience engaging with external stakeholders** (e.g. clusters, donors, UN agencies).
- **Fluency in English required**; additional languages required based on location (see ‘Additional Requirements’).
- **Comfortable working** in cross-cultural, fast-paced environments.
- **Sound judgment and emotional intelligence** in high-pressure or sensitive situations, strong interpersonal awareness and the ability to respond constructively to feedback and shifting priorities.
- **Please indicate in the applicant form if you have completed a HEAT training.**

#### ANALYSIS CONTEXT LOCATIONS AND ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS

The exact locations where the ANA will be conducted in 2026 will be confirmed pending funding The below is a tentative *list of possible* crises to be analysed.

### COMPENSATION & BENEFITS

- For this position, depending on the seniority of the role and the location salary between 2’100 CHF and 3'120 CHF monthly (before income tax), etc as well as a monthly living allowance of 300 USD
- *NB - IMPACT salaries are strictly determined based on our salary grid, which takes into account both the grade of the position and the staff member’s level of education. In addition, a location-specific security and/or isolation allowance may be applied to acknowledge the challenging living and working conditions in certain duty stations.*
- Accommodation and food provided in the guesthouse.
- Enrolment in Swiss private pension fund (Swisslife – approx. 9.975% of staff gross salary, employer-funded in addition to gross salary), MSH health insurance, life insurance and ISOS repatriation assistance.
- Flight tickets at the beginning and at the end of the contract & visa fees covered (in-country travel costs and professional expenses are fully covered).
- Contribution to the luggage transportation: 23 kg of luggage allowance (+ luggage and personal property insurance)
- Annual leave of 36 days per year. Public holidays of the country of assignment. Family/compassionate leave when applicable.
- IMPACT prioritizes the psychological safety of its staff and the health insurance provided covers, among others, up to 1000 € per year of psychosocial counselling fees.

### \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_

*VEUILLEZ NOTER : il s’agit d’un appel à candidatures global visant à pourvoir plusieurs postes d’Analyste et d’Analyste Senior au sein de différents bureaux pays d’IMPACT en Amérique latine et aux Caraïbes (ALC), au Moyen-Orient et en Afrique du Nord (MENA), ainsi qu’en Afrique subsaharienne. Les candidat·e·s sont invité·e·s à indiquer leur contexte d’analyse préféré (voir tableau ci-dessous) sur le formulaire de candidature. Dans votre lettre de motivation, veuillez indiquer les raisons de vos trois principales préférences de contexte d'analyse sélectionnées sur le formulaire de candidature.*

## CONTEXTE SUR IMPACT ET REACH

Fondée en 2010 et basée à Genève, [IMPACT Initiatives](https://www.impact-initiatives.org/what-we-do/) est une organisation de recherche appliquée de référence et le principal fournisseur indépendant de données dans les contextes de crise. À travers ses initiatives (REACH, AGORA et PANDA), IMPACT permet aux acteurs humanitaires et autres acteurs de l’aide de prendre de meilleures décisions fondées sur des données probantes, en leur fournissant des données et analyses rigoureuses, pertinentes et livrées en temps utile. Notre présence étendue dans les contextes de crise nous permet de collecter des données directement auprès des populations affectées, y compris les plus vulnérables et les plus difficiles à atteindre. [REACH](https://www.impact-initiatives.org/what-we-do/reach/), une initiative d’IMPACT, renforce la prise de décision humanitaire fondée sur des données probantes grâce à une collecte, une gestion et une analyse efficaces des données, avant, pendant et après une urgence.

L’ensemble des programmes d’IMPACT est mis en œuvre à l’appui des structures de coordination humanitaire. L’équipe d’IMPACT est composée de spécialistes en collecte, gestion et analyse de données, ainsi que d’expert·e·s en réponse humanitaire, SIG et télédétection.

### Nous recherchons actuellement plusieurs (Senior) Analystes en Besoins Aigus pour rejoindre nos équipes dans plusieurs lieux d’affectation.

**Poste :** (**Senior) Analyste en Besoins Aigus (ANA)**

**Durée du contrat** : Jusqu’à 6 mois

**Date de début** : Mi-septembre 2026

**Lieu** : Plusieurs bureaux pays en **ALC**, **MENA** et en **Afrique subsaharienne** (voir ci-dessous la localisation à indiquer sur le formulaire de candidature).

### PROFIL DU POSTE

Face à l’évolution du paysage du financement humanitaire, IMPACT met davantage l’accent sur la production de **produits d’analyse comparables et orientés vers la décision, au service de la priorisation humanitaire.** Ce poste portera sur le deuxième cycle de l’Analyse des Besoins Aigus (ANA), un produit analytique phare qui synthétise les données disponibles afin de fournir une compréhension claire et exploitable du **risque de perte de vies humaines** à travers les zones géographiques et les groupes de population au sein d’une crise, **afin d’alimenter des points de décision clés, tels que le HPC et les allocations des bailleurs de fonds.**

L’**Analyste (Senior) en Besoins Humanitaires Aigus** sera chargé·e de produire ce produit analytique au niveau pays. Cela inclut la revue et la synthèse des données, la conduite d’une analyse structurée à l’aide des orientations analytiques globales d’IMPACT, ainsi que la production d’une note externe courte et à fort impact. L’analyste travaillera en étroite collaboration avec les équipes Data, SIG et design pour intégrer des éléments visuels au produit final. Le produit analytique final jouera un rôle clé dans les décisions de priorisation humanitaire.

### RESPONSABILITÉS

#### ÉLABORATION DU PRODUIT ANALYTIQUE : BESOINS HUMANITAIRES AIGUS

- Piloter la mise en œuvre et la livraison du projet d’analyse au niveau pays, en coordination avec l’équipe programme du siège.
- Aligner le déploiement sur les calendriers globaux et veiller au respect des standards analytiques d’IMPACT.
- Développer et entretenir une cartographie solide des parties prenantes ainsi qu’un réseau de collaborateur·rice·s au niveau pays afin de renforcer la compréhension du contexte et le suivi.
- Assurer le développement de produits centrés sur les utilisateur·rice·s et, le cas échéant, appuyer les analyses conjointes avec les parties prenantes concernées.
- REVUE ET CONSOLIDATION DES DONNÉES
- Collecter et synthétiser les données secondaires pertinentes issues des évaluations REACH, des agences des Nations Unies, des ONG internationales et des bases de données publiques (par ex. OCHA, FEWS NET, IPC), notamment en développant et entretenant les relations nécessaires.
- Évaluer la fiabilité des données et identifier les lacunes critiques.
- Appuyer les décisions relatives à la nécessité d’une collecte de données primaires ciblée et légère.

#### PROCESSUS ANALYTIQUE ET INTERPRÉTATION

- Appliquer les orientations analytiques globales d’IMPACT afin de produire une analyse structurée, cohérente et adaptée au contexte des besoins humanitaires aigus.
- Utiliser des cadres définis (par ex. le risque de surmortalité) pour identifier les zones à risque de pertes de vies humaines à grande échelle et estimer le nombre de personnes en situation de menace vitale
- Documenter clairement les hypothèses, les limites et le raisonnement analytique.

#### PRODUCTION ET DIFFUSION DES LIVRABLES

- Rédiger la note de l’Analyse des Besoins Aigus à l’aide des modèles et du langage standardisés au niveau global.
- Collaborer avec les équipes SIG et design afin d’intégrer cartes, tableaux de caseload et autres supports visuels.
- Assurer la revue et la validation internes du produit avant sa diffusion.
- Présenter les résultats aux clusters, groupes de travail et bailleurs de fonds selon les besoins.
- Selon les besoins, appuyer le développement des messages clés globaux sur la base des résultats au niveau pays.

#### APPRENTISSAGE, INNOVATION ET ASSURANCE QUALITÉ

- Participer aux revues de leçons apprises et proposer des améliorations aux processus et orientations d’analyse globaux.
- Contribuer à l’apprentissage organisationnel sur la conduite des chantiers d’analyse et participer aux réflexions et au développement de nouveaux chantiers analytiques, en collaboration avec les équipes pays et le siège.
- Appuyer le partage interne de connaissances et les formations analytiques au niveau pays.
- Se tenir informé·e des bonnes pratiques sectorielles et des innovations en matière d’analyse humanitaire.
- L’(Senior) Analyste maintiendra la plus stricte confidentialité sur l’ensemble des données collectées et des processus associés. Il/elle prendra activement des mesures pour prévenir tout partage non autorisé d’informations et de données appartenant à IMPACT et à ses partenaires, ou collectées au cours de sa mission avec IMPACT.

### PROFIL REQUIS

À noter : le poste peut être pourvu au niveau Analyste ou Analyste Senior, en fonction de l’expérience du/de la candidat·e.

#### QUALIFICATIONS REQUISES

- **3** **ans d’expérience professionnelle pertinente** dans un contexte humanitaire, telle que l’analyse, les évaluations, le suivi-évaluation et la conception de recherche, etc. avec une expérience directe sur le terrain ;
- **D’excellentes qualifications académiques**, comprenant de préférence un master ou équivalent dans une discipline pertinente (par ex. études du développement international / relations internationales, action humanitaire, data science, sciences politiques, etc.) ;

### COMPÉTENCES TECHNIQUES :

- **D’excellentes compétences analytiques et de réflexion critique**, avec une expérience de l’interprétation de données complexes et de la production de résultats clairs et exploitables.
- **De solides compétences rédactionnelles** et une expérience dans la production de notes claires et concises destinées à des publics externes.
- **Maîtrise d’Excel**, avec une expérience d’un outil d’analyse supplémentaire (par ex. PowerBI, SPSS, R, STATA ou Python) ; une compréhension des processus SIG de base et de leurs livrables est un atout.
- **Bonne connaissance des différentes méthodes de recherche qualitatives et quantitatives**, avec la capacité d’évaluer la qualité de différentes sources de données.
- **Compréhension des systèmes de coordination humanitaire**, y compris le HPC et les analyses et évaluations des besoins inter-agences.
- **La connaissance du contexte** est un atout. Merci de préciser dans votre candidature si vous avez une expérience de travail dans l’un ou plusieurs des contextes potentiels listés ci-dessous

#### COMPÉTENCES EN COMMUNICATION ET EN ORGANISATION

- **Capacité à gérer des flux de travail complexes** et à produire des livrables de qualité dans des délais serrés.
- **Expérience de collaboration avec des parties prenantes externes** (par ex. clusters, bailleurs de fonds, agences des Nations Unies).
- **Maîtrise de l’anglais requise** ; des langues supplémentaires peuvent être requises selon la localisation (voir « Exigences supplémentaires »).
- **À l’aise pour** travailler dans des environnements interculturels et à rythme soutenu.
- **Bon jugement et intelligence émotionnelle** dans des situations sous pression ou sensibles, solide sens relationnel et capacité à réagir de manière constructive aux retours et aux priorités changeantes.
- **Merci d’indiquer dans le formulaire de candidature si vous avez suivi une formation HEAT.**

#### CONTEXTES D’ANALYSE, LOCALISATIONS ET EXIGENCES SUPPLÉMENTAIRES

Les localisations exactes où l’ANA sera menée en 2026 seront confirmées sous réserve du financement. Voici une *liste provisoire* des crises susceptibles d’être analysées.

### REMUNERATION ET AVANTAGES

- Pour ce poste, selon le niveau de séniorité et la localisation, le salaire mensuel se situe entre 2’100 CHF et 3’120 CHF (avant impôt sur le revenu), etc., ainsi qu’une allocation de subsistance mensuelle de 300 USD
- *NB : les salaires d’IMPACT sont strictement déterminés selon notre grille salariale, qui prend en compte à la fois le grade du poste et le niveau d’éducation du/de la salarié·e. Une allocation de sécurité et/ou d’isolement spécifique à la localisation peut également être appliquée afin de tenir compte des conditions de vie et de travail difficiles dans certains lieux d’affectation.*
- Hébergement et repas fournis en guesthouse.
- Affiliation à la caisse de pension privée suisse (Swisslife, environ 9,975 % du salaire brut, financé par l’employeur en plus du salaire brut), assurance santé MSH, assurance vie et assistance de rapatriement ISOS.
- Billets d’avion au début et à la fin du contrat, ainsi que frais de visa pris en charge (les frais de déplacement dans le pays et les dépenses professionnelles sont intégralement couverts).
- Contribution au transport des bagages : franchise de 23 kg (+ assurance bagages et effets personnels)
- 36 jours de congés annuels par an. Jours fériés du pays d’affectation. Congé familial/pour raisons personnelles lorsque applicable.
- IMPACT accorde une priorité à la sécurité psychologique de son personnel ; l’assurance santé fournie couvre, entre autres, jusqu’à 1000 € par an de frais de soutien psychosocial.

title: MEL Lead (FCDO GOAL)
body:
**About the GOAL Opportunity**

The International Rescue Committee (IRC) is preparing to bid for FCDO's Girls and Out-of-School Children: Action for Learning Programme (GOAL) Long-Term Technical Assistance (LTTA) contract in Pakistan, following release of FCDO's Terms of Reference (ITT 7863). GOAL builds on more than a decade of UK-funded education reform in Punjab and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP), delivered through the Punjab Education Support Programme (PESP, 2013–2022) and the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Education Sector Programme (KESP, 2012–2022), and on two live GOAL components: the Bridging Technical Assistance grant (B-TAG, ending March 2027) and the ILMpact remedial learning grant (ending September 2026), both of which the incoming Supplier will need to review and build on during inception.

The LTTA contract will run for up to 38 months (December 2026 – January 2030), comprising a 4-month inception period, a 32-month implementation period, and a 2-month closure phase, with a budget of up to £13 million and an extension option of up to £6.5 million and 18 months at FCDO's discretion. It will deliver systems-strengthening, politically informed technical assistance to provincial education departments in Punjab and KP, with Sindh included as a limited, capped scope (up to £1 million) focused on scoping, needs analysis and possibly Teacher Licensing support; the remaining budget is split equally between Punjab and KP.

The programme's three outcomes are:

- **Foundational Learning (30%):** strengthened provincial delivery of early and inclusive Foundational Learning.
- **Teacher Professionalisation (40%):** improved teacher professionalisation, including standards, licensing, and performance and support systems.
- **Education Financing Governance (30%):** improved governance and accountability of education financing, including public financial management and innovative financing.

The Terms of Reference place strong emphasis on systems thinking and a Thinking and Working Politically (TWP) approach, including a 'coalitions for change' lens that looks beyond government departments to civil society, philanthropy and the private sector, and on strengthening how provincial governments manage the rapid growth of outsourced and Public-Private Partnership (PPP) schools across Punjab and KP. Equity, inclusion and safeguarding are cross-cutting requirements throughout.

FCDO requires a lean Core Team of a Project Director (the only role not required to be full-time; at least 20% of days in Pakistan), a Team Leader, a Technical Assistance Lead, two Outcome Leads (one covering teaching and learning, one covering PFM and innovative financing), and two Provincial Leads (Punjab and KP) from contract commencement, with a third for Sindh only if FCDO later approves a Sindh implementation phase. The named Table 1 Core Team positions must be full-time and exclusive to the contract; any additional Core Team positions a bidder proposes do not have to be full-time, but are still subject to the same exclusivity requirement while engaged. IRC is proposing to strengthen this structure with a dedicated MEL Lead. FCDO's Terms of Reference confirm that GOAL's programme-wide MEL component is not being separately procured, and para 13.5 explicitly invites bidders to propose additional Core Team expertise beyond FCDO's named positions — this role is IRC's response to that invitation, not a named Table 1 position.

**Background of the role:**

The MEL Lead is a core team position responsible for the production, budgeting and implementation of the programme's Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning (MEL) strategy. The MEL strategy must set out the approach to data collection, management and analysis; evidence use and generation; use of innovation and technology; Value for Money (VFM); and dissemination — and must align with the Theory of Change, logframe and VFM monitoring for the overall GOAL programme.

The MEL Lead will report to the Team Lead, working closely with the Technical Assistance Lead to ensure MEL evidence informs technical decision-making, and with the GESI Specialist to ensure GESI-disaggregated data collection and analysis.

**Roles and Responsibilities**

- Lead production of the programme's MEL strategy covering data collection/management/analysis, evidence use and generation, use of innovation and technology, VFM, and dissemination, aligned with the Theory of Change, logframe and VFM monitoring for the wider GOAL programme.
- Propose and apply MEL methodologies and methods capable of capturing progress in systems thinking and Thinking and Working Politically (TWP) — for example Developmental Evaluation or Systems Thinking MEL, using methods such as outcome mapping or process tracing — rather than relying on conventional summative M&E alone.
- Lead development and updating of the programme's logframe and maintain the change log recording all logframe amendments throughout the life of the contract.
- Establish required quantitative and qualitative baseline data before the end of the inception period, in collaboration with SED Punjab, ESED KP and other GOAL component partners, drawing on existing B-TAG, ILMpact, DARE-RC and RSPN knowledge products rather than starting from scratch.
- Design monitoring activities that are real-time wherever possible, use community-driven modes of monitoring and appropriate technology, integrate into government systems rather than creating parallel ones, and remain accessible and easy to understand by all partners.
- Ensure the MEL system can track plausible contribution pathways to FCDO's wider education portfolio milestones — for example, the Foundational Learning milestone of a 5% increase in Grade 5 reading in Urdu and English in KP and Punjab by 2029 against the 2023 ASER baseline — using agreed indicators and available data sources including Annual School Census data, ASER and relevant provincial/national assessments.
- Propose an incremental, additive approach to evaluation that builds up a picture over the life of the contract, rather than relying on a single summative report at the end of the TA.
- Own the evidence base for KPI 5 (acting on lessons learnt), ensuring lessons from partners are systematically captured, analysed and reflected in quarterly reporting and adaptive management decisions; contribute quality-assured MEL and logframe products that support KPI 2 (quality of implementation deliverables).
- Lead preparation of the annual MEL Strategy document and annual Results KPIs reporting, and contribute the MEL sections of the Exit Plan (first drafted in the inception phase, updated annually, finalised January 2029) and of quarterly Progress Reports to FCDO and to SED Punjab/ESED KP/SELD Sindh.
- Ensure MEL data collection is disaggregated by gender, disability, poverty and geography, working closely with the GESI Specialist to identify and target the most marginalised children.
- Track and report on Value for Money, supporting the Team Lead's quarterly financial and progress reporting and the programme's fee-retention/KPI-linked payment model.
- Build the MEL capacity of provincial government counterparts as part of the programme's systems-strengthening approach, consistent with the ToR's expectation that TA strengthens government routines rather than substituting for them.

**Qualification, experience and Skills will include:**

**Essential:**

- Advanced degree in monitoring and evaluation, statistics, social science, education, or a related field.
- Substantial senior MEL leadership experience (indicatively 8-10+ years) on FCDO- or similarly funded, complex donor programmes, ideally involving adaptive, politically informed programming.
- Demonstrated expertise in adaptive/developmental MEL methodologies (e.g. Developmental Evaluation, Systems Thinking MEL) and methods (e.g. outcome mapping, process tracing), rather than conventional logframe-only M&E.
- Strong experience developing and managing logframes, Theories of Change, and Value for Money monitoring frameworks nested within a wider programme logframe.
- Experience with KPI-linked, fee-retention payment structures and donor reporting requirements, ideally FCDO's.
- Experience with education data systems and sources (e.g. EMIS, Annual School Census, ASER) in Pakistan or a similar context strongly preferred.
- Experience building MEL capacity within government counterparts.
- Excellent written and spoken English; Urdu and/or other relevant regional languages an advantage.

**Collaboration with Other Team Members**

- **Team Lead:** provide regular MEL evidence and VfM reporting to inform programme management and donor reporting.
- **Technical Assistance Lead:** ensure MEL findings inform technical decision-making and quality assurance across outcome areas.
- **Outcome Leads (Teaching & Learning; PFM & Innovative Financing) and Provincial Leads:** coordinate data collection, monitoring and process evaluation across outcome areas and provinces.
- **GESI Specialist:** ensure MEL data and analysis are disaggregated by gender, disability, poverty and geography to identify and target the most marginalised children.
- **SED Punjab / ESED KP:** support provincial government counterparts to strengthen their own MEL and data systems, in alignment with DARE.

*This JD reflects FCDO's Terms of Reference for the GOAL LTTA contract (ITT 7863) and associated bidder clarifications, and remains subject to change until contract award. This position is contingent on the outcome of the bid.*

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

title: Program Officer, Instructional Design & Multimedia
body:
*This position is contingent on receipt of grant funding.*

**Job Overview:**

The International Rescue Committee (IRC) is one of the leading providers of high-quality programming for refugees resettling to the United States. The IRC is committed to developing innovative programs that respond to the refugees’ unique strengths and needs, using our learning and experience to shape policy and practice, and highlighting and promoting best practices in refugee services provision.

The IRC is seeking a Program Officer for Instructional Design and Multimedia for Settle In, a program providing information and support for newcomers in multiple languages through its website (SettleInUS.org), mobile app, and social media platforms. More information on Settle In can be found on https://www.settleinus.org.

This position designs and produces the learning experiences newcomers encounter across Settle In’s platforms. The role combines two areas of practice: instructional design—structuring multilingual, self-paced learning journeys that help newcomers build knowledge over time—and multimedia production—creating videos, graphics, and other assets that support the full range of Settle In content.

**Major Responsibilities:**

- Design multilingual, self-paced learning journeys for newcomer audiences, including learning objectives, sequencing, knowledge checks, and reinforcement. Apply instructional design, adult learning principles, plain language standards, and translation-ready structure so that content is usable by newcomers with varying levels of literacy, digital literacy, and prior exposure to U.S. systems.
- In partnership with Switchboard’s Senior Program Officer, Instructional Design, establish instructional design standards for Settle In content and review materials developed by team members, subject matter experts, and contractors against those standards.
- Incorporating Switchboard’s established instructional design standards, recommend and implement improvements to Settle In’s instructional design practice, and update previously developed Settle In learning resources on an established review cycle.
- Create compelling, in-language multimedia content, including short-form video, infographics, motion graphics, and social media assets.
- Manage post-production of all finalized work, including Adobe Premiere project organization, color correction and grading, sound design, motion graphics, music editing, sequencing, export and compression for multiple platforms, and archiving.
- Coordinate with the multilingual Digital Community team on content creation, voiceover, subtitling, and translation review, and advise colleagues on audio and video recording tools and practices.
- Ensure final products are easy to understand, culturally appropriate, linguistically and factually accurate, accessible across web and mobile, and aligned with Settle In standards, newcomer needs, and funder requirements.
- Ensure all learning experiences and multimedia content meet accessibility standards (e.g., captions, alt text, screen-reader compatibility)
- Maintain visual and instructional consistency across Settle In's platforms (website, mobile app, social media)
- Coordinate and incorporate feedback across teams and projects and participate in user testing and other methods for optimization of content.
- Manage production timelines across concurrent projects and coordinate the work of external contractors, including videographers, designers, and translation vendors.
- Use platform data and user insights to set measurable goals for content and assess performance, and contribute to project reports, including monthly activity updates and performance monitoring reports.

*Other duties as assigned.*

**Job Requirements:**

- Bachelor’s degree in instructional design, education, communications, or other relevant field (or equivalent experience).
- Minimum four years of professional experience combining instructional design and multimedia production, including creating multilingual digital content for diverse populations.
- Demonstrated experience designing self-paced learning for adult audiences, including experience with e-learning tools.
- Excellent command of video editing (Adobe Premiere) and graphic design software (Adobe InDesign, Canva), and knowledge of social media platforms, especially Facebook.
- Working knowledge of plain language principles and digital accessibility standards.
- Experience contributing to project M&E (data collection, management, and reporting).
- Ability to manage complex projects on strict timelines, with excellent written and oral communication skills and strong attention to detail.
- Fluency in at least one of Settle In’s supported languages (Dari, Pashto, Spanish, and Haitian Creole) preferred.
- Previous experience working with refugee resettlement or other immigration pathways, and familiarity with ORR-funded programs.
- Ability to translate complex or technical information into clear, visual, and easy-to-understand learning content
- Experience engaging with external subject matter experts, consultants, or production vendors.

**Working Environment:**  This position is a remote working environment. Required domestic travel up to 20%.

**Compensation:** (Pay Rate: $80,000 - $85,000/yr). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**US Benefits:** We offer a comprehensive and highly competitive set of benefits. In the US, these include: 10 sick days, 10 US holidays, 20-25 paid time off days depending on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163 per month, dental starting at $6.50 per month, and vision starting at $5 per month, FSA for healthcare and commuter costs, a 403b retirement savings plans with immediately vested matching, disability & life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program which is available to our staff and their families to support counseling and care in times of crisis and mental health struggles.

title: Case Coordination Caseworker
body:
**Job Overview:** The Caseworker provides trauma-informed services to refugees and other ORR qualified immigrants to support a positive integration experience and the achievement of client self-sufficiency. The Caseworker works closely with clients, colleagues, and external parties to develop service and/or self-sufficiency plans to meet individual client needs and preferences utilizing a broad range of financial, medical, social, vocational, and other services and resources in accordance with client eligibility and program requirements.

**Major Responsibilities:**

Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

- Conduct intake services with clients to assess needs. Develop self-sufficiency plans and timelines in partnership with each client. Provide individualized support through direct services, referrals, and advocacy.
- Receive referrals for case management for ORR-eligible and TANF-eligible clients and participate in any needed case conference meetings to assure continuity of care.
- Assess client needs, creates Family Self-Sufficiency Plans (FSSPs) and Individual Employability Plans (IEPs), focusing on removing employment barriers, stabilizing, and obtaining and retaining employment.
- Assess and monitor client progress to support their attainment of established goals, address challenges, and to ensure that available resources are utilized. Follow up with any referrals made to other programs.
- Detail each client interaction in accordance with program requirements. Input client information in database(s) and assist with tracking and reporting as needed.
- Collaborate effectively with coworkers and partner organizations. Build and maintain relationships with area service providers for the benefit of clients.
- Use personal, insured vehicle and/or public transportation (where available) to travel and transport clients and materials as needed throughout the service delivery area.
- May train and lead the activities of volunteers and interns.
- Conduct outreach to case management staff, refugee-serving agencies, ethnic community-based organizations, and others to inform service providers and refugees of programs and services.

- Provide comprehensive case management services, including assisting with benefits applications as appropriate.

- Ensure all family data is entered into data management system in a timely manner.

***Demonstrated Skills and Competencies:***

- Computer proficiency with an emphasis on Microsoft Office applications (Word, Excel, Teams, Outlook).

***Certificates or Licenses:***

**Working Environment*****:***

Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability.
