title: Grants and Reporting Coordinator
body:
**Country Programme:** Ukraine

**Contract Length:** 1 year with possible extension

**Base:** Kyiv

**Starting date:** November 2026

**Line Manager:** Head of Grants and Rerporting

**People in Need** (PIN) is a Czech-based international non-governmental organization (NGO) that has provided humanitarian and development assistance across more than 20 countries since 1992. Today, PIN stands as one of the largest organizations of its kind in Central and Eastern Europe, supporting vulnerable communities in Asia, Africa, the Middle East, and Eastern Europe. PIN empowers civil society, advocates for human rights, and promotes social inclusion both at home and abroad.

## **About the Ukrainian Programme of People in Need:**

People in Need (PIN) began operations in Ukraine in 2003 with human rights programs and expanded to humanitarian assistance in 2014. With the full-scale invasion in February 2022, we significantly scaled up our programming across the country. Since then, PIN has reached almost 4 million people, working with a network of local partner organizations.

Today, PIN has its offices and teams in 8 oblasts in Ukraine with more than 500 local and international staff working in Lvivska, Kyivska (head office), Sumska, Kharkivska, Dnipropetrovska, Mykolaivska and Khersonska, Zaporizka, and Donetska oblasts.

PIN's assistance addresses both immediate and longer-term needs of war-affected people, focusing on safe water and sanitation, shelter repairs, protection services, and education in emergencies. Our recovery programming delivers more systemic solutions, including support to district heating systems and renewable energy initiatives.

PIN also provides comprehensive assistance to veterans and their families, including business grants and mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS), strengthens the quality of education in schools, and advances systemic improvements in social care for the most vulnerable. Funding comes from a diverse range of institutional and private donors.

## **About the role:**

As a member of the Country Programme (CP) and specifically a team member of the Grants and Reporting Unit, with the support of the Head of Grants and Reporting (HoGR), the Grants and Reporting Coordinator (GC) will oversee assigned grants’ implementation progress, particularly in relation to approved proposal and in compliance with donor’s rules and procedures. The GC will report on their assigned project/s in close collaboration with relevant teams. The Grants and Reporting Coordinator will act as a Grants Focal Point (GFP) as assigned during the proposal development, will support or lead the proposal development and project modification processes, and may act as a focal point for external liaison, including representing PIN vis-à-vis donors and in other coordination forums as assigned. Other tasks may be assigned by the HoGR as deemed necessary.

## **Main Duties & Responsibilities:**

**Program Coordination and Grants Management:**

- Maintains an internal tracking database of her/his assigned grants/donors, reporting timelines, project milestones/targets and modifications. Ensures comprehensive grant files, donor guidelines and resources are maintained, updated and available for use.
- Coordinates with Area Managers and Area teams, Programme Coordinators,
- MEAL, Technical Leads, as well as Advocacy and Communication, Procurement, Finance, Database, Partnership units, and Security department as well as Headquarters (HQ) focal points to ensure accurate tracking and reporting of programmatic adjustments throughout the project life cycle.
- Advises teams and partners, where needed, on donor’s compliance, rules and requirements in coordination with other relevant units.
- Prepares and leads the kick off, project review, and close out meetings, and participates in other project/grant-related meetings e.g. Lessons Learned meeting. Prepares documents and collects information from relevant Finance, Logistics/Procurement, Partnership (PI), MEAL, Comms and Advocacy, Security, Data and Programme teams in order to facilitate regular project review meetings.
- Prepares regular updates for key donors on project progress, achievement highlights and challenges as well as shares briefing notes, other project and communication materials with respective donors
- Provides information to relevant staff members on reporting timelines of the assigned project/s. Ensures relevant staff are provided with timely information and materials – including guidelines, templates and examples – to develop quality reporting contributions. Acts as a focal point for collection, compilation, review, quality control and editing of both quantitative and qualitative internal and donor reporting.
- Prepares all donor narrative reports and coordinates necessary clearances and submission of reports and necessary annexes; and flags inconsistencies, if identified to the Finance Department to ensure that financial and narrative reports are aligned.
- In collaboration with technical leads, ensures that all reports are in-line with the assigned donor/s requirements in structure and content, including mainstreaming issues such as protection, gender, do no harm, and conflict sensitivity.
- Works with Data team to report on all quantitative figures; flags any discrepancies if identified, to Data team; utilises dashboards and databases as primary source of information, working with Area teams to provide qualitative information where dashboards have gaps.
- In coordination with the PI and Technical Leads, reviews all MEAL products that will be submitted to the donor to ensure alignment with reports and donor communication.
- Prepares Modification Request, No-cost Extension, and/or Cost Extension packages in coordination with relevant departments. Supports finalisation of relevant project-related documents prepared by other departments, such as Evaluation Terms of References (ToRs), Third Party Monitoring (TPM) plans, etc. and coordinates with TPM organizations contributing to planning monitoring visits.
- Undertakes regular field visits to gain in-depth understanding of the context and implementation.
- Coordinates donor-related field visits as needed.

**Fundraising and Resource Mobilization:**

- Proactively supports in monitoring and analysis of new funding opportunities for PIN in Ukraine through relevant open sources (donor websites, humanitarian assistance portals), clusters, and bilateral consultation and scoping with existing and potential donors.
- Working in close collaboration with Technical Leads, Programme Coordinators and Area teams, as well as other relevant units and departments, acts as a GFP and/or Proposal Lead, as assigned; supports preparation for Go-No-Go and proposal kick-off preparation meetings, proposal development workplan/timelines; leads development of concept notes, proposals (including supporting the design of logical frameworks, targets, and budgets); ensures updated and current templates are available for narrative, finance, and other parts or annexes.
- Leads proposal modifications and situation analyses – including modifications in logical frameworks, targets, and budgets.
- As assigned, creates and shares a folder on SharePoint for the internal proposal preparation, creates a Teams chat for relevant colleagues, and were helpful organizes sectoral design chats/discussions.
- As assigned, creates the [Resource Folder in ELO](https://elo.pinf.cz/ix-CZE/plugin/de.elo.ix.plugin.proxy/web/?useSSO=true#/archive/(A5A8F0FF-3B32-48C6-A732-71520F4FB7B6)/) (PIN’s internal system) and initiates the workflow.
- Follows-up on relevant action items from Ukraine Fundraising and Resource Mobilization meetings, as well as other meetings, ensuring timely completion of relevant tasks.

**Internal and External Coordination:**

- Communicates with relevant donors and represents PIN at the appropriate level of representation.
- Participates in meetings with HQ and other coordination meetings as requested by the line manager.
- Coordinates with focal points from Finance, Data team, MEAL, Programme Quality, and Area teams during proposal development and reporting periods as well as partners, as needed.
- Coordinates with communications team to ensure that relevant communication materials (human interest stories, videos, etc.) are developed for projects as per workplan and donors’ requirements; as well as ensures distribution of readily available communication materials to donors.
- Acts as the main project focal point for respective donors.

## **Requirements:**

- At least 3 years of experience working in a humanitarian and/or development organization, including at least 2 years of experience in grants development.
- Demonstrated experience leading the development and coordination of successful large-scale project proposals for key institutional donors, including DoS, ECHO, FCDO, SDC, BMZ, UN agencies, GAC, and others.
- Proven experience leading the preparation and submission of interim and final donor reports, with a strong understanding of donor requirements, compliance standards, and grant management processes.
- Strong knowledge of all stages of the project and programme cycle, including humanitarian programming quality standards, monitoring, evaluation, accountability and learning (MEAL), and data management.
- Experience working in complex and volatile humanitarian contexts. Familiarity with the humanitarian context in Ukraine is an advantage.
- Excellent organizational, analytical, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to manage multiple tasks, prioritize competing deadlines, and work effectively under pressure.
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English, including outstanding report writing and editing abilities, and the capacity to collaborate effectively with internal teams and institutional donors. Knowledge of Ukrainian and/or Russian is an advantage.

## **We offer:**

- Working environment in a well-established humanitarian organization in a challenging context;
- **Starting Salary** based on PIN’s salary scale and HR policies, between 2600-2800 EUR;
- **Additional allowances include**:
    - Monthly Subsistence Allowance of 1440 EUR;
    - Monthly Hardship Allowance of 400 EUR;
    - Accommodation provided by PIN/Monthly Housing Allowance up to 1000 EUR;
- **Time off and Rest:**
    - 25 days of holiday annually;
    - 10 sick days
    - Rest & Recreation (R&R) policy in place: 3x 5 days of leave per year with 350 Eur lump sum allowance per each leave.
- **Travel benefits:**
    - Reimbursement of travel expenses with travel to the country of residence once every 6 months of work;
    - Reimbursement of costs of visas and vaccinations; assistance with the visa application procedure;
    - Reimbursement for the medical check-up before and after the deployment;
    - Travel health insurance covering medical care, incl. the repatriation;
- **Health and Well-being:**
    - 24/7 Medical Support available online;
    - Free psychological consultations available online;
- **Professional Development:** Free access to e-learning platforms and PIN Learning Hub; PIN’s global Induction Training, and tailored capacity-building opportunities, including Hostile Environment Awareness Training (HEAT);

## **Security situation in Ukraine**

Humanitarian workers continue to operate throughout Ukraine, although the front-line areas are being shelled almost constantly, and main cities are being targeted with missiles and UAVs quite regularly. PIN security SOPs require PIN staff to proceed to shelter should the risk level be assessed by the Security Department as the highest (launch of missiles or drones) and remain there until the air raid siren is cancelled, which cumulatively can be several times a week, occasionally for several hours at a time (although shorter periods are as well occurring). While air strikes that were targeting energy, infrastructure have finished after winter, they have succeeded in reaching their goals and are likely to resume in late autumn/winter. At the moment military and civilian objects are being targeted, including the west of Ukraine. While Kyiv enjoys relatively strong air defence systems that are intercepting most of the missiles and UAVs, other regions are covered much less significantly which results in bigger damage. Outside of the areas in the vicinity to the contact line, services such as medical care, shops, public transportation as well as restaurants or leisure facilities remain operational.

*People in Need is committed to preventing any type of unwanted behaviour at work including sexual harassment, exploitation and abuse, lack of integrity and financial misconduct and is committed to promoting the welfare of children and adults with whom People in Need involved. People in Need expects all staff to perform job duties and responsibilities in accordance with People in Need code of conduct and key policies (available at:* [*https://www.peopleinneed.net/key-policies-4142gp*](https://www.peopleinneed.net/key-policies-4142gp)*). People in Need Staff will undertake the appropriate level of training.*

*All offers of employment will be subject to satisfactory references and appropriate screening checks, which can include criminal records and terrorism finance checks.*

*We are committed to ensuring diversity and gender equality within our organization and encourage applicants from diverse backgrounds to apply.*

title: Financial Capabilities Coordinator
body:
**Job Overview:** Under the supervision of the Senior Program Manager, the IRC seeks a Financial Capabilities Coordinator to support the development and implementation of career pathways services in its Economic Empowerment program for refugees and other immigrants in Tucson. This position is responsible for assisting clients in developing plans that help them reach their goals and achieve financial stability, and for ensuring IRC achieves program targets relating to enrollment, economic empowerment outcomes, and connection to community benefits and resources. The Coordinator is to tangibly connect working clients on their journey to a higher paying job to resources and certifications. It is expected to focus services in a one-on-one career counseling format in tandem with conducting classes and workshops on topics such as budgeting, credit building, banking, and financial products.

**Responsibilities: Include, but are not limited to:**

**Client Services:**

- Assist clients in assessing and resolving current financial challenges, while providing a wide lens on their financial health to shift the approach to proactive financial management
- Administer intake and assessment for enrolled participants and co-develop an Individualized Career Development Plan (ICDP) with each participant to guide training, employment, and follow-up activities.
- Coordinate case-managed wraparound supports, including interpretation, transportation and childcare stipends, work supplies, and emergency assistance, tied to each participant's documented barriers and ICDP.
- Connect participants to local occupational training, apprenticeships, or certification programs, and to employer partners for job upgrades or career-related employment.
- Conduct 6- and 12-month follow-up with participants and, when applicable, their employers to assess job retention, wages, advancement, job quality, benefits, and household financial stability.
- Ensure that changes (new job, new benefit, and change in credit score) are properly documented in relevant systems.
- Capture client success stories
- Develop workshop materials or tailor existing materials to meet the needs of the community. Workshop topics may include the following: budgeting, savings, banking products, credit building, and identity theft.

**Program Coordination:**

- Ensure compliance with all policies, procedures, and protocols of the agency.
- Ensure that information required for program eligibility for all career programs and reporting purposes is collected and that accurate records are maintained, including case files and client data entry.

- Build and maintain partnerships with community-based organizations, career service providers, and small business and corporate entities for advanced career opportunities;
- Coordinate corporate and employer engagement opportunities and events.
- Participate in program meetings and staff development activities.
- Coordinate quality assurance efforts by conducting periodic case file and electronic data reviews.
- Produce high-quality program reports for IRC headquarters and funders and ensure programs fulfill funder and agency requirements.
- Other duties as assigned.

**Job Requirements:**

- 2+ years of related professional experience in financial capabilities and/or career development
- Experience in a non-profit setting and/or financial coaching services a plus
- Experience working in a diverse, and non-traditional setting with diverse staff and client base
- Self-starter with excellent problem-solving skills combined with the proven ability to multi-task, prioritize duties, and manage time effectively.
- Excellent verbal and written communication skills and an overall ability to be clear and concise in all communications
- Exceptional organizational skills with proven attention to detail.
- Demonstrated ability to work effectively as a team member in a multi-cultural environment.
- Proficient in Microsoft Office applications (Word, Excel, Outlook)
- Fluent in English, both spoken and written; bilingual ability preferred. Preferably in Spanish, Kinyarwanda, Arabic, or Dari.
- Demonstrated ability to work effectively with stakeholders at all levels

**Working Environment:**

title: Marketing and Business Development Intern
body:
***Marketing and Business*** ***Development Intern***

**Reporting to:** SBC Design and Partnerships Officer

**Start date:** 1 February 2026

**Duration:** 12 Months

**Location:** The position will be based in Amman, Jordan. Please note that MAGENTA’s teams work from home with in-person meetings and events as required, including regular colocation with colleagues in hubs.

**Remuneration:** A stipend of 1,000.00 USD per month

MAGENTA is a leading Social and Behavioural Change (SBC) agency that specialises in understanding human decision-making processes in order to design solutions for relevant and impactful solutions to some of the most challenging problems of our time. We implement programmes across the Middle East & North Africa, Africa, Asia, Latin America and the Caribbean using the latest in behavioural science principles and a rigorous approach to research, strategy, campaign design and implementation.

Our client base includes UN agencies, INGOs, the FCDO, the US government and the private sector. We aim to amplify the voices of local actors while bringing international expertise and methodological rigour. To do so, we partner with civil society, creative agencies, media and academics to design innovative, relevant and impactful solutions to some of the most challenging problems of our time. Whether we are aiming to shift parenting practices to improve children’s outcomes or to understand how social norms underpin corruption, we always go the extra mile to ensure we can create positive impact for some of the most underserved populations in the world.

MAGENTA is made up of five business units and three operating departments: Middle East & North Africa, Asia, Africa, Latin America & the Caribbean, the MAGENTA Lab, Corporate Services, Growth & Marketing and Technical & Programme.

The Marketing and Business Development Intern will play an important role in supporting MAGENTA’s marketing and new business efforts. This internship offers an opportunity to gain hands-on experience in a dynamic and mission-driven environment.

***RESPONSIBILITIES***

**Marketing and Communications**

- Manage and expand MAGENTA’s social media presence (LinkedIn and Facebook), including planning, creation, and scheduling of posts, monitoring engagement metrics, and pinpointing areas for content enhancement.
- Contribute to developing and designing compelling marketing materials, including case studies, capability statements, brochures, and bi-monthly newsletter.
- Ensure that MAGENTA’s marketing collateral is kept up-to-date across four languages, and implement updates and edits as required.
- Maintain strict compliance with the company’s branding directives across all marketing materials and communications, maintaining a consistent visual and messaging identity.
- Maintain and update MAGENTA’s website, ensuring it accurately reflects the most recent projects, initiatives, and team.
- Maintain MAGENTA’s databases including YouTube channel, tender monitoring tracker, past performance database, close-out tracker, and contact lists.
- Generate routine reports detailing marketing performance, including website traffic, social media engagement, and provide recommendations for enhancement.
- Research and monitor thought leadership opportunities and support program teams to prepare and submit applications to conferences, summits, and other thought leadership events.
- Provide occasional training and guidance to MAGENTA teams on how to use Canva and YouTube platforms for marketing and business development tasks.

**Business Development**

- Facilitate proposal development by conducting research on thematic areas related to specific bids, donor strategies, and competitor analysis.
- Collaborate with bid writing teams by providing desk research support and helping draft proposal sections as required.
- Support programme teams on proposal submissions by gathering and uploading necessary documents, formatting proposals, and providing additional technical support as required.
- Monitor business development platforms to identify relevant tenders to be shared with the programme teams twice a week.

***REQUIREMENTS***

**Education:**

- Recently completed a bachelor’s or master’s degree programme, ideally in a field related to international development, business development, or marketing.

**Experience:**

- Prior marketing-related and or business development internships, coursework, or relevant extracurricular activities preferred.
- Impeccable written and verbal communication skills in English and Arabic. One additional MAGENTA language (French or Spanish) is highly desirable.
- Strong organisational, writing, formatting, and presentation skills.
- A creative mindset for generating innovative marketing ideas and content.
- Basic understanding of analytics tools and data interpretation.
- Familiarity with digital marketing concepts, including conducting social media analytics and SEO.
- Familiarity with social media content creation and digital communication trends.
- Ability to follow branding guidelines and maintaining brand consistency.
- Ability to manage multiple tasks, meet deadlines and prioritise tasks as needed.
- Ability to work effectively in a team.
- Proficiency with Office tools, especially Word, PowerPoint, and Excel.
- Proficiency with Canva or other online graphic design tools.
- Demonstrated curiosity about AI and emerging technologies, with hands-on experience applying them to real work - e.g. using AI for research synthesis, drafting, data analysis, workflow automation, or "vibe coding" simple tools/prototypes - and a track record of proactively teaching yourself new digital skills
- Flexibility to changing needs and priorities.

***COMPETENCIES***

The following are key competencies required for this position.

• Innovative

• Reliable

A fast, self-directed learner who actively builds new skills rather than waiting to be trained - comfortable experimenting with AI, no-code and "vibe coding" tools to solve problems and work smarter

***CULTURAL FIT***

• Demonstrated adherence to MAGENTA’s core values:

Curiosity: Challenge the obvious, reflect and then act.

Transparency: Hold yourself and those around you accountable

Authenticity: Walk the talk

Innovation: Think bold, think big, think broad

• Good sense of humour, personable and demonstrated ability to build networks.

• Entrepreneurial spirit and willingness to get hands dirty.

***WORKING CONDITIONS***

MAGENTA has a flexible working policy which promotes periods of remote working in the year.

The chosen candidate must be available to work across different time zones and be flexible with working hours based on project needs.

*MAGENTA is committed to creating a diverse work environment. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, colour, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, genetics, disability, or age.*

title: Project Quality, Reporting and Implementation Advisor
body:
**Country Programme:** Angola

**Contract Length:** 1 year, with the possibility of extension

**Base**: Luanda, Angola

**Starting date:** upon agreement

**Line Manager:** Country Director for Angola

**People in Need** (PIN) is a Czech-based international non-governmental organization (NGO) that has provided humanitarian and development assistance across more than 20 countries since 1992. Today, PIN stands as one of the largest organizations of its kind in Central and Eastern Europe, supporting vulnerable communities in Asia, Africa, the Middle East, and Eastern Europe. PIN empowers civil society, advocates for human rights, and promotes social inclusion both at home and abroad.

**About the Angola Programme of People in Need:**

**PIN has been in Angola since 2006**, initially through education projects and subsequently expanding its programming across agriculture and livelihoods, water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH), community health and nutrition, gender, civil society strengthening, child protection and human rights. Over the years, PIN has worked across several provinces, including Bié, Huambo, Huíla, Namibe, Luanda, Uíge, Moxico and Kwanza Sul. Today, PIN’s work in Angola combines longer-term development and resilience building with support to communities affected by climate-related and other shocks, with particular expertise in climate-resilient livelihoods, WASH, nutrition, civil society strengthening and inclusive governance.

**PARS Programme**

PIN is the executing entity for the **PARS Angola project**, "**Promoting climate adaptation and resilience through innovation and entrepreneurship for green jobs in Angola**". A **five-year project** funded by the **Global Environement Fund (GEF)** and iimplemented in partnership with the **Angolan Ministry of Environment** and **UNIDO**. The project is part of the six-country GEN-funded PARS programme and aims to reduce climate vulnerability and strenghten the resilience of communities in Angola´s southern and coastal provinces by promoting innovation, technology transfer and private-sector-led adaptation solutions through support of Angolan MSMEs.

## **About the role:**

The Project Quality, Reporting and Implementation Advisor supports the effective and high-quality implementation of the **PARS Angola – Promoting climate adaptation and resilience through innovation and entrepreneurship for green jobs in Angola** project implemented by People in Need (PIN) in partnership with the Ministry of Environment of Angola and UN Industrial Development Organization (UNIDO).

The position provides dedicated support to the PARS Angola Project Management Unit (PMU), with a particular focus on **project cycle management, planning, monitoring of implementation, donor reporting, documentation and compliance**, complemented by operational support required for timely project delivery.

The Advisor works closely with the Project Manager to ensure that activities, outputs, targets, budget, procurement and implementation milestones remain aligned; that implementation progress and risks are systematically tracked; and that reporting to UNIDO is timely, accurate, evidence-based and compliant with the Project Document, Implementing Partner Agreement, Terms of Reference and Operational Guidelines.

The position also helps maintain effective coordination between programme, MEAL, finance, procurement, logistics and other support functions involved in project implementation.

## **Main Duties & Responsibilities:**

- **Project Cycle Management, Planning and Coordination**
    - Support the PMU in the day-to-day coordination and follow-up of project implementation across all PARS Angola components.
    - Support preparation and regular updating of Annual Work Plans, reporting-period workplans, implementation schedules and other project management tools.
    - Maintain an integrated project implementation tracker covering activities, deliverables, indicators, procurement and other milestones, responsible persons and deadlines.
    - Regularly follow up with technical and support teams on agreed actions, deliverables and implementation deadlines; identify delays, bottlenecks or non-compliance with agreed processes; seek timely clarification and corrective action from responsible colleagues; and escalate unresolved or recurring issues to the Head of Programmes and/or Country Director, as appropriate.
    - Support the organization and preparation of regular internal project coordination and review meetings.
    - Support preparation for bi-weekly coordination meetings with UNIDO and monthly implementation reviews, including consolidation of information on implementation progress, budget execution, procurement and recruitment, safeguards, risks and upcoming priorities.
    - Support preparation and follow-up of Project Steering Committee meetings, including background documents, presentations, minutes and agreed actions.
    - Support coordination across programme, MEAL, Finance, Procurement/Logistics and other relevant functions to ensure that implementation remains aligned with approved workplans and project requirements.
- **Reporting and Documentation**
    - Coordinate the internal process for preparation of project reports and ensure that inputs are requested, received and consolidated according to agreed internal deadlines.
    - Draft and/or consolidate technical sections of the **Kick-off Report, interim and annual technical progress reports, Project Implementation Reports (PIRs), final report and other reports required by UNIDO and GEF**.
    - Work closely with MEAL colleagues to ensure that reported results are supported by up-to-date indicator data, monitoring evidence and appropriate means of verification.
    - Work closely with Finance to ensure consistency between narrative reporting, implementation progress, expenditure and financial reporting.
    - Verify that reports clearly describe progress against outputs, activities, indicators and targets and adequately explain delays, challenges, risks and corrective measures.
    - Coordinate internal review and quality assurance of reports before submission to UNIDO.
    - Maintain a structured repository of project achievements, lessons learned, case studies and other evidence that can feed into reporting and knowledge products.
- **Monitoring, Quality and Adaptive Management**
    - Support regular monitoring of implementation against the Project Results Framework, Annual Work Plan, milestones and contractual commitments.
    - Work with the MEAL team and technical staff to ensure that project monitoring data and supporting evidence are collected and available for management and reporting purposes.
    - Support the PMU in monitoring project risks and maintaining an up-to-date Project Risk Register.
    - Track agreed risk mitigation and corrective measures, follow up with responsible colleagues on their implementation, and escalate overdue or insufficiently addressed actions where they may affect project results, compliance, budget execution or contractual commitments.
    - Maintain a clear escalation pathway for significant or recurring implementation issues, including delays, compliance gaps, unresolved risks and deviations from approved workplans or project requirements. Ensure that such issues are documented, brought to the attention of the appropriate decision-maker in a timely manner, and followed up until a decision or corrective action is agreed.
- **Operational and Implementation Support**
    - Provide practical support to the PMU and technical teams in translating approved workplans into concrete implementation steps and timelines.
    - Coordinate with Procurement/Logistics and programme teams to follow the status of procurement processes required for planned activities and flag potential delays.
    - Support preparation and updating of procurement planning information required for Annual Work Plans and implementation reviews, while respecting the responsibilities of dedicated Finance and Procurement staff.
    - Support preparation of ToRs, scopes of work and other documentation for consultants, service providers and technical assignments.
- **Procurement Planning and Technical Procurement Support**
    - Support the preparation of procurement documentation required for project implementation, particularly for consultant recruitments, technical service contracts, studies, assessments and other specialized assignments.
    - Coordinate the provision of technical inputs required for procurement processes and ensure that Terms of Reference (ToRs), scopes of work, technical specifications and expected deliverables are prepared in a timely and high-quality manner.
    - Support programme and technical teams in the development and review of tender documentation and procurement packages in line with project requirements and PIN procedures.
    - Follow up with responsible colleagues to ensure that procurement processes are initiated sufficiently in advance and remain aligned with implementation timelines and workplans.
    - Participate in the technical evaluation of bids, proposals and consultant applications where relevant and support the documentation of evaluation processes.
    - Coordinate with Procurement/Logistics colleagues to monitor the status of key procurements and help address bottlenecks that may affect project implementation.
    - Ensure that procurement-related documentation and decisions are properly documented and accessible for project management, reporting and audit purposes.
- **Knowledge Management, Communication and Learning**
    - Support systematic documentation of project results, lessons learned, good practices and implementation experiences.
    - Contribute to preparation of project presentations, briefs, case studies and other knowledge products.
    - Support exchange of relevant information and learning with the PARS Global Coordination Project and other PARS country projects.

## **Main requirements:**

- At least **5 years of relevant professional experience** in project/programme management, reporting, programme quality, MEAL or a related area; experience with large institutional donor-funded projects is strongly preferred.
- Strong command of **English and Portuguese**, both written and spoken
- Demonstrated experience in donor reporting and preparation of high-quality narrative reports.
- Good understanding of project cycle management, work planning, monitoring and risk management.
- Experience coordinating inputs from programme, MEAL, finance, procurement and other functions is an advantage.
- Experience with UN agencies, GEF-funded programmes or other complex institutional donors would be a strong advantage.
- Experience in climate adaptation, private-sector/MSME development, green entrepreneurship or related programming is desirable but not essential.
- Strong organizational skills and ability to manage multiple deadlines and streams of information simultaneously.
- Excellent analytical, drafting and editing skills.
- Advanced user of MS Office, particularly Word, Excel and PowerPoint.
- Willingness to travel within Angola as required.

## **We offer:**

- Working environment in a well-established humanitarian organization;
- *Salary & Benefits*: Salary based on PIN’s salary scale and HR policies; expected salary range between 2900 - 3300 EUR super gross (based on experience).
- Additional allowances include:
    - Monthly Subsistence Allowance of 1440 EUR;
    - Accommodation provided by PIN/Monthly Housing Allowance;
    - *Time off and Rest:*
    - 25 days of holiday annually;
    - 10 sick days
- *Travel benefits:*
    - Reimbursement of travel expenses with travel to the country of residence once every 6 months of work;
    - Reimbursement of costs of visas and vaccinations; assistance with the visa application procedure;
    - Reimbursement for the medical check-up before and after the deployment;
    - Travel health insurance covering medical care, incl. the repatriation;
    - *Health and Well-being:*
    - 24/7 Medical Support available online;
    - Free psychological consultations available online;
    - *Professional Development:* Free access to e-learning platforms and PIN Learning Hub; PIN’s global Induction Training, and tailored capacity-building opportunities

title: Head of Corporate & Major Donors
body:
## **Jouw profiel**

- HBO of WO opleiding in marketing, business, management, economics, international development/relations of vergelijkbare richting.
- Vloeiend Nederlands en Engels; goede beheersing van extra talen is een pré.
- Ondernemend, resultaatgericht en besluitvaardig.
- Kan omgaan met prestatiedruk en presteren onder deadlines
- Uitstekende communicatie-, presentatie- en representatievaardigheden; kan vertrouwen wekken op senior niveau.
- Kan mensen effectief leiden, betrekken en helpen ontwikkelen.
- Analytisch en data‑gedreven: vertaalt trends naar fundraisingkansen.
- Kennis van fondsenwervingsethiek, regelgeving en safeguarding.

**Ervaring**

- Minimaal 5 jaar managementervaring in een relevante functie.
- Ruime ervaring in fondsenwerving, sales of marketing.
- Aantoonbare (commerciële) ervaring met corporate partners en/of filantropische organisaties.
- Ervaring met het opstellen en realiseren van fundraisingstrategieën, targets en budgetten.
- Ervaring met people management, capaciteitsopbouw en teamontwikkeling.
- Ervaring met CRM en automatisering; werkt met managementinformatie (KPI‑rapportages/dashboards) ter sturing.
- Ervaring met governance, compliance en het beheersen van financiële, operationele en reputatierisico’s.

## **Wie zijn wij?**

Kinderen sterker dan oorlog? Absoluut. Maar ze kunnen het niet alleen. Daarom geeft War Child mentale (nood)hulp aan kinderen in conflictgebieden. Onze werkwijze is gebaseerd op wetenschap. Maar sluit naadloos aan op de belevingswereld van kinderen. Het resultaat? Unieke en bewezen effectieve methodes, verpakt als sport, spel en creatieve activiteiten. We stimuleren zo hun natuurlijke veerkracht. Zodat ze langzaam weer durven geloven in de toekomst.

War Child Nederland zoekt een:

**Head of Corporate & Major Donors**

***"Strategisch leider voor corporate partnerships en grote donateurs"***

## **Over de functie**

Een verbindende en commercieel gedreven Head of Corporate & Major Donors. Je leidt het Corporates & Major Donors (C&MD) team, één van de drie fundraising teams binnen War Child Nederland (WCNL), dat verantwoordelijk is voor fundraising bij bedrijven en grote donateurs. Je bent lid van het Management Team (MT). Je geeft richting aan de strategie, gaat actief naar buiten om nieuwe kansen te creëren en zorgt dat deze samen met het team worden vertaald naar concrete resultaten en groei.

## **Jouw verantwoordelijkheden**

**Strategie en leiderschap**

- Vertaal War Child Nederland‑ en Alliance strategie naar strategische prioriteiten voor het team en werk hiervoor actief samen met het MT en de War Child Alliance.
- Bepaal de strategische prioriteiten voor het team en stuur op realisatie en impact.
- Neem besluiten op MT-niveau en pak complexe vraagstukken binnen WCNL op.

**Commerciële ontwikkeling & partnerships**

- Ontwikkel en realiseer duurzame partnerships met bedrijven, foundations en grote donateurs, gericht op groei van inkomsten en impact.
- Ga actief naar buiten, bouw aan een relevant netwerk en creëer nieuwe commerciële kansen voor WCNL.
- Ontwikkel samen met het team sterke proposities en vertaal kansen naar concrete partnerships en inkomsten.
- Stuur op groei van bestaande en nieuwe inkomstenbronnen en op een gezonde commerciële pipeline.
- Vertegenwoordig WCNL extern en vergroot de zichtbaarheid, het netwerk en het draagvlak voor War Child.

**Target- & resultaatmanagement**

- Stel ambitieuze, realistische targets en stuur op realisatie.
- Monitor prestaties, analyseer resultaten en zet leerpunten om in concrete verbeteracties.
- Rapporteer periodiek voortgang en risico’s aan de directie.

**Team & organisatieontwikkeling**

- Leid, ontwikkel en verbind het C&MD fundraisingteam.
- Zorg voor de juiste bezetting en capaciteit, inclusief recruitment, performance management en loopbaanontwikkeling.
- Bewaak welzijn en werkbelasting en stuur bij waar nodig.
- Draag de War Child-waarden uit en bouw aan een inclusieve en resultaatgerichte cultuur.
- Stimuleer kennisdeling, leren en continu verbeteren binnen en tussen teams.

**Risico, governance & compliance**

- Waarborg naleving van donor voorwaarden, wetgeving, ethiek en safeguarding‑standaarden.
- Identificeer en mitigeer financiële, operationele en reputatierisico’s; escaleer materiële issues tijdig.
- Zorg voor transparante verantwoording richting directie en bestuur.

**Resources & operationele sturing**

- Overzie jaarbudgettering en prioriteer op basis van return of investment (ROI), zorg dat de resource‑planning bijdraagt aan organisatiedoelen.
- Werk datagedreven: gebruik managementinformatie en KPI’s voor sturing.
- Stimuleer continue verbetering en ROI-monitoring in alle fundraisingactiviteiten.

## **Wat wij bieden**

- Salaris varieert van € 5.285 tot € 6.571 bruto per maand, op basis van 40 uur per week (het exacte bedrag wordt bepaald door de jaren van je relevante werkervaring);
- 8% vakantietoeslag op basis van het jaarsalaris;
- Een arbeidsovereenkomst voor 32-40 uur;
- 29 vakantiedagen per jaar op fulltime basis (waarvan 3 vooraf vastgestelde vrije dagen);
- Een geluksdag, die je spontaan kan inzetten om iets te doen waar je energie van krijgt.
- Een volledig door War Child Nederland betaalde pensioenregeling;
- Netto tegemoetkoming in de thuiswerk -en reiskosten volgens ons hybride werkbeleid;
- Maandelijkse mobiele telefoonvergoeding van €25 netto per maand;
- Verschillende secundaire voorwaarden gefocust op persoonlijke ontwikkeling en welzijn;
- Goede sfeer, toffe collega's en natuurlijk het betekenisvolle doel van ons werk!

title: Project Manager
body:
**Miyamoto International** is a global engineering and disaster management firm, delivering expert solutions to sustain industries and safeguard humanity. We are a purpose-driven company with a mission to make the world a better, safer place.

We are seeking a dedicated, highly organized, and results-oriented **Project Manager** to join our global Disaster Risk Management group, which specializes in disaster risk reduction, response, reconstruction, and urban resilience. With experience responding to over 100 global and U.S. disasters, our data-driven, multidisciplinary approach addresses economic, political, socio-cultural, sustainability, and technical challenges in some of the world's most demanding environments. We excel at developing strategies for post-conflict and disaster recovery, including creating resilient, affordable housing systems that empower communities to rebuild and thrive.

This position is to be based in our **Los Angeles** office. No relocation or sponsorship is provided.

**Position Summary**

The Project Manager will oversee the implementation of complex global disaster preparedness, response, recovery, and resilience programs, with a strong focus on effective **contract/award management**. Working under the direction of Miyamoto’s Senior Principals overseeing global disaster response and preparedness work, the Project Manager will work closely with technical specialists, country teams, finance, operations, and project coordination staff to ensure programs are delivered effectively, on time, within budget, and in accordance with donor requirements.

The role will provide day-to-day oversight of program implementation, including work planning, budget and expenditure management, reporting, compliance, procurement and contracting coordination, risk management, and contract/award administration. The Project Manager will support multiple country programs and help teams translate program objectives and award requirements into practical implementation.

The position will require flexibility to deploy to disaster-affected countries as needed. During emergency responses, the Project Manager may support the rapid establishment and management of project systems, budgets, reporting, coordination, and other operational requirements.

**Key Responsibilities**

- Manage the day-to-day implementation of global disaster preparedness, response, recovery, and reconstruction programs, ensuring activities are delivered on time, within budget, and in accordance with program and donor requirements.
- Lead project planning and management, including development and oversight of workplans, budgets, implementation schedules, deliverables, reporting calendars, and project management systems.
- Oversee contract and grant/award requirements, including reporting, compliance, documentation, procurement and contracting processes, and coordination of required approvals and modifications.
- Manage project budgets in close coordination with operations, finance, and program teams, including expenditure monitoring, forecasting, budget-to-actual review, and identification of potential financial or implementation issues.
- Coordinate multidisciplinary, international, and in-country teams to support effective program delivery, problem-solving, and timely decision-making.
- Work closely with Sr. Principals and technical leadership to ensure project activities and deliverables are effectively planned, resourced, coordinated, and completed to the required quality and timelines.
- Lead the preparation and coordination of donor reports, workplans, program updates, and other required project and contract/award deliverables.
- Monitor project risks, implementation challenges, and compliance requirements and proactively work with project leadership and teams to identify and implement solutions.
- Coordinate procurement, consultant contracting, and other operational requirements in collaboration with finance, operations, technical teams, and external advisors as appropriate.
- Maintain strong project and grant management systems and ensure project documentation and records are complete, organized, and maintained in accordance with donor and organizational requirements.
- Support communication and coordination with donors, government counterparts, humanitarian organizations, partners, and other stakeholders, as appropriate.
- Provide oversight and guidance to Project Coordinators and other project support staff and help establish effective project management practices across country teams.
- Support the rapid mobilization and management of disaster-response operations, including deployment planning, budgeting, contracting, coordination, information management, and establishment of project management systems.
- Contribute to program design, proposal development, budgeting, lessons learned, and continuous improvement of Miyamoto’s global disaster response and preparedness programming.

As needed, this role may involve international travel and participation in country-level disaster-response deployments.

**Qualifications and Experience**

**Education:**

Bachelor’s degree in business administration, international relations, emergency management, engineering, project management, or another relevant field. Master’s degree preferred.

**Experience:**

- Approximately 7–10 years of progressively responsible experience in project, program, or contract/award management, including demonstrated responsibility for budgets, reporting, project administration, and coordination of complex projects.
- Experience managing multiple projects or workstreams across teams, locations, or stakeholders is highly desirable.
- Experience in humanitarian assistance, disaster risk management, or other rapidly changing operational environments is an advantage but not required.

**Knowledge:**

- Strong understanding of project and grant management processes, including work planning, budgeting and financial monitoring, reporting, procurement and contracting, compliance, and project administration.
- Experience with donor-funded programs is highly desirable, as is familiarity with U.S. Government-funded programs and 2 CFR / U.S. federal award requirements.

**Skills:**

- Strong project management, organizational, analytical, and problem-solving skills, with demonstrated ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines.
- Strong budget management and financial tracking skills.
- Excellent written and verbal communication and reporting skills.
- Ability to establish practical project management systems and work effectively with technical, financial, and operational teams.
- Strong proficiency in Microsoft Excel, PowerPoint, Word, project management platforms, and related digital and AI tools.

**Languages:** Professional fluency in English required. Spanish highly preferred. Additional languages are an advantage.

**Remote Work and Travel Requirements:**

Demonstrated ability to work effectively across remote, multidisciplinary, and multicultural teams and across different time zones. Ability to exercise sound judgment, take initiative, and adapt quickly in fast-moving environments. Willingness to travel internationally and deploy to disaster-affected locations as needed.

Miyamoto is a flat, dynamic organization that values initiative, sound judgment, and practical problem-solving. We work in complex and rapidly changing environments where there is rarely a single blueprint for how work should be done. We minimize bureaucracy while maintaining strong, adaptive systems that support accountability, quality, and compliance. We look for smart, resourceful individuals who are comfortable taking ownership, navigating ambiguity, working collaboratively, and finding practical solutions in a fast-moving environment. Successful candidates share our passion for helping others and strive to improve the quality of their work with each new challenge. This is an opportunity to expand your creativity and build your expertise in the field.

body:

The role will support a broad range of operational needs, including procurement, contracting, consultant recruitment and management, logistics, travel and deployments, IT and equipment, finance coordination, and project start-up and closeout. The Operations Coordinator will also support the development of scopes of work, identification and mobilization of specialized consultants and service providers, and management of consultant rosters and other operational resources that can be leveraged across projects and disaster responses.

This is a hands-on role requiring strong judgment, initiative, and follow-through. The successful candidate will be comfortable taking ownership of operational needs from identification through completion, while recognizing when specialized expertise or management guidance is required. The position requires the ability to work across multiple projects and countries, respond quickly to changing priorities, and develop practical solutions and systems without creating unnecessary bureaucracy.

**Key Responsibilities**

- Provide day-to-day operational support across global disaster preparedness, response, recovery, and resilience programs.
- Coordinate procurement of goods and services, including supporting development of specifications and scopes of work, identifying vendors and service providers, obtaining and documenting quotations, coordinating required reviews and approvals, and tracking procurement through delivery.
- Support consultant and contractor engagement, including development of scopes of work, identification and recruitment of qualified experts, contracting, onboarding, assignment tracking, and coordination of invoicing and other administrative requirements.
- Develop and maintain rosters of specialized technical and operational consultants and service providers and support their efficient mobilization across projects and disaster responses.
- Work with Project Managers, technical teams, and country teams to identify operational and specialized expertise required for program implementation and help determine practical approaches to meeting those needs.
- Coordinate operational aspects of project and country start-up and closeout, including consultant and staff mobilization, procurement, contracting, equipment, IT, travel, documentation, and other implementation requirements.
- Coordinate international and in-country travel and deployment logistics, including flights, accommodation, ground transportation, visas, insurance, communications, equipment, and other mobilization requirements.
- Coordinate IT, communications, software, equipment, and other operational requirements for project teams and deployed personnel, working with internal or external specialists as needed.
- Work closely with finance and project teams to support purchasing, consultant and vendor invoices, expense documentation, operational budget tracking, and other financial and administrative processes.
- Maintain procurement, contracting, consultant, vendor, equipment, travel, and other operational records and trackers, ensuring documentation is complete, organized, and readily accessible.
- Coordinate with specialized consultants and advisors in areas such as procurement, safety and security, legal and compliance, logistics, IT, and other operational functions, helping translate specialist guidance into practical actions for project and country teams.
- Support development and continuous improvement of practical operational procedures, templates, tools, and workflows that enable teams to work efficiently while meeting organizational and donor requirements.
- Proactively identify operational needs, bottlenecks, and risks and work with Project Managers, country teams, leadership, and specialist advisors to develop and implement practical solutions.
- Support emergency operations and rapid-response activations, including mobilization, logistics, procurement, contracting, information management, equipment, and other immediate operational priorities.
- Provide operational support across other global initiatives and responses as organizational priorities and needs evolve.

As needed, this role may require international travel and deployment to disaster-affected locations to provide direct operational and logistical support.

**Qualifications and Experience**

**Education**:

Bachelor’s degree in business, operations, international relations, emergency management, supply chain, logistics, or another relevant field. Equivalent relevant professional experience will also be considered.

**Experience**:

- Approximately 4–7 years of relevant professional experience in operations, project coordination, procurement, logistics, contracting, business administration, or related functions.
- Demonstrated experience independently managing operational processes and taking responsibility for complex tasks from planning through completion is important.
- Experience supporting complex, international, or fast-moving operations is highly desirable.
- Experience in humanitarian assistance, disaster response, international development, or other rapidly changing operational environments is an advantage but not required.

**Knowledge**:

- Strong understanding of operational and project administration processes, with familiarity across areas such as procurement, contracting, logistics, budgeting, financial administration, IT, and operational support.
- Experience with donor-funded programs is desirable, as is familiarity with U.S. Government-funded programs and 2 CFR / U.S. federal award requirements.

**Skills**:

- Excellent organizational and problem-solving skills, strong attention to detail, and demonstrated ability to exercise sound judgment and independently manage multiple operational priorities.
- Ability to identify what needs to be done, determine a practical path forward, seek specialized guidance when appropriate, and follow through to completion.
- Strong communication and interpersonal skills and confidence working with vendors, consultants, technical specialists, and teams across different countries and functions.
- Strong proficiency in Excel, PowerPoint, Word, and digital and AI-enabled tools for organization and administration.
- Ability to appropriately handle sensitive and confidential information.

**Languages**: Professional fluency in English required. Spanish highly preferred. Additional languages are an advantage.

**Remote Work and Travel Requirements**:

Willingness to travel internationally and deploy to disaster-affected locations as needed.

Miyamoto is a flat, dynamic organization that values initiative, sound judgment, and practical problem-solving. We work in complex and rapidly changing environments where there is rarely a single blueprint for how work should be done. We minimize bureaucracy while maintaining strong, adaptive systems that support accountability, quality, and compliance. We look for smart, resourceful individuals who are comfortable taking ownership, navigating ambiguity, working collaboratively, and finding practical solutions in a fast-moving environment. Successful candidates share our passion for helping others and strive to improve the quality of their work with each new challenge. This is an opportunity to expand your creativity and build your expertise in the field.

**Languages**: Professional fluency in English required. Spanish highly preferred. Additional languages are an advantage.

Miyamoto International is a flat, dynamic organization that values initiative, sound judgment, and practical problem-solving. title: Tupande Export Logistics Senior Specialist
body:
## **About One Acre Fund**

Founded in 2006, One Acre Fund equips 5.5 million smallholder farmers to make their farms more productive. Across nine countries that together are home to two-thirds of Africa's farmers, we provide high-quality farm supplies, tree seedlings, accessible credit, modern agronomic training, and a wide range of other agricultural services. On average, this model enables any farmer to increase their income and assets on supported land by more than 35 percent, while permanently improving their resilience. This is all made possible by our team of 9,000+ full-time staff, drawn from diverse backgrounds and professions. In Nairobi, around 50 staff support global functions like procurement, recruitment, government relations, and communications.

## **About the Role**

The Export Logistics Specialist oversees and manages end-to-end export operations to ensure that goods leave the organization’s facilities and reach international vendors on time, within budget and in full compliance of all agreed regulations; including safety standards.

The role is focused on planning, coordination, documentation & stakeholder management for all exports handled by Soko.

## **Responsibilities**

Export Operations & Coordination

- Plan, organize, and oversee the entire export process from order placement to delivery at the destination.
- Coordinate with production, warehousing, and procurement teams to ensure accurate and timely order fulfillment.
- Liaise with freight forwarders, carriers, and third-party logistics providers to schedule shipments.
- Track shipments, resolve delays, and ensure smooth cargo movement.

Documentation & Compliance

- Prepare and review all required export documentation (invoices, packing lists, bills of lading, certificates of origin, export licenses, etc.).
- Ensure compliance with international trade laws, customs regulations, and organizational policies.
- Maintain accurate records of shipments for audit and reporting purposes.
- Stay updated on changes in export/import regulations, customs procedures, and trade agreements.

Customer & Stakeholder Management

- Act as the primary point of contact for clients regarding export logistics inquiries.
- Provide timely updates to customers on order and shipment status.
- Resolve customer complaints, shipment issues, or documentation errors promptly.
- Build and maintain strong relationships with shipping agents, port authorities, and regulatory agencies.

Performance Management

- Negotiate shipping rates and terms with carriers and freight forwarders to optimize costs.
- Analyze export logistics performance and recommend process improvements for efficiency and cost savings.

Reconditioning

- Support and coordinate container reconditioning logistics when overseas regulators identify non-compliance issues.
- Ensure all reconditioning processes follow approved SOPs and documentation standards before goods are released to buyers.
- Maintain close communication with third-party service providers managing sterilization or product rework.

Supply Chain Traceability

- Ensure all exported goods have a clear, verifiable origin and traceable supply chain documentation.
- Work with sourcing and quality teams to build systems that enable end-to-end traceability of export products.
- Maintain audit-ready export documentation, certifications, and inspection records in compliance with global regulatory standards.

Cost efficiency

- Monitor freight costs, customs duties, and tariffs to control budgets.
- Identify opportunities for cost reduction across shipping, warehousing, and handling processes.
- Implement strategies that improve container utilization, reduce demurrage/detention, and optimize route planning.
- Regularly review freight spend and propose cost-saving initiatives without compromising quality or timelines.

We have a strong culture of constant learning and we invest in developing our people. You’ll have weekly check-ins with your manager, access to mentorship and training programs, and regular feedback on your performance. We hold career reviews every six months, and set aside time to discuss your aspirations and career goals. You’ll have the opportunity to shape a growing organization and build a rewarding long-term career.

Across all roles, these are the [general qualifications we look for](https://oneacrefund.org/work-with-us/application-process/qualifications/). For this role specifically, you will have:

- 5+ years of experience in Supply chain, with at least 3 years focusing on Exports.
- Proficiency in export management systems and tracking tools.
- Proficiency in building complex formulas and functions in Google Sheets to support data analysis and reporting.
- Language requirement: English is required. Working knowledge of Swahili is also useful
- Strong planning and organizational skills.
- Excellent communication and coordination abilities.
- Proficient in export management systems and tracking tools.
- Analytical mindset for cost projections and performance tracking.
- Ability to manage multiple priorities and work under pressure.

As soon as possible

Nairobi, Kenya

Health insurance, paid time off

This role is only open to citizens or permanent residents of Kenya.

title: Clinical Services Supervisor
body:
**IRC Background:** The mission of the International Rescue Committee (IRC) is to help people whose lives and livelihoods are shattered by conflict and disaster to survive, recover and gain control of their future. Founded in 1933, the IRC has a presence in over 40 countries and 27 offices in the United States; the IRC leads the way from harm to home. IRC opened an office in Seattle in 1976 and provides a continuum of services including intensive case management, employment and economic empowerment services, immigration assistance, health and wellness programming, and education support to refugee and immigrant families in Washington State. IRC Seattle is committed to providing trauma-informed, inclusive and supportive workplace.

**Job Overview:**

The Clinical Services Supervisor oversees and provides culturally, and linguistically appropriate mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS) designed to improve the holistic well-being of human trafficking survivors. The position has four main functions: 1) Clinical services - conducting mental health intakes and assessments, developing individual service plans, and delivering evidence-based and evidence-informed interventions, 2) Clinical supervision - supervising non-licensed psychosocial support staff to ensure services are of quality, trauma informed, and culturally relevant, and 3) Care coordination - with internal and external providers to ensure holistic client support, and 4) Outreach and engagement - to build provider and community capacity to identify, respond to, and serve survivors of human trafficking. The Clinical Services Supervisor must be an independently licensed counselor/therapist in WA State. Strong candidates must have experience helping help high barriers clients navigate and access systems, and delivering culturally responsive, linguistically accessible services. This position reports to the MHPSS Program Manager with clinical supervision provided by IRC’s MHPSS Technical Advisor.

**Clinical Responsibilities:**

- Supervision
- Ensure clinical quality of programming
- Conduct intake and assessment and develop individual service plans
- Provide interventions and activities in-office, remotely, and in community settings
- Maintain a clinical case load (approx. 15-20 clients)
- Manage crisis (i.e., suicide assessments, safety planning, mandatory reporting, etc.)
- Care coordination including warm hand-offs as needed
- Support development and delivery of psychoeducation training to IRC staff and community partners to strengthen response and services for survivors of human trafficking.
- Supervise master’s level Practicum Interns

**Project Management Responsibilities:**

- Arrange for interpreters as needed to appropriately engage clients in services
- Ensure timely and accurate documentation, data entry, and reporting
- Monitor program activity and quality through oversight and support related to case and project documentation
- Evaluate effectiveness of program related to client progress and individual service plan objectives
- Communicate and coordinate regularly with all levels of program staff to ensure that services are being delivered effectively and in a timely manner
- Strengthen and maintain partnerships with community mental health agencies to expand client resources
- Deliver capacity-building initiatives to strengthen community response and services for human trafficking victims
- Other duties as assigned

**Key Working Relationships:**

**Position Reports to:** MHPSS Program Manager

**Position Supervises:** WARN Mental Health MSW interns

**Other Internal and/or external contacts:**

***Internal*****:** *WARN Team, Family Wellness Team, Resettlement Team, Employment Team, Immigration Team, Youth Program Team, New Roots Team, Health Empowerment Team, Volunteer Coordinator, Finance Team, Operations Team, Development Team.*

***External*****:** *API Chaya, REST, KIND, Northwest Justice Project, Northwest Immigrant Rights Project, Seattle Police Department, US Attorney’s Office, Homeland Security Investigations, Washington Advisory Committee on Trafficking, City of Seattle Human Services Division, Washington State Office for Crime Victim Advocacy, Washington State Task Force Against Trafficking in Persons, and additional partners.*

**Job Requirements:**

**Certificates or Licenses:**

- Holds a valid Licensed Independent Clinical Social Worker (LICSW) in the state of Washington
- In accordance with state Law, must possess or be eligible to receive a fingerprint clearance card
- Must have a valid driver’s license, active insurance policy

**Work Experience:**

- Proficiency in English, and Spanish language(s) required
- At least three years’ experience with therapeutic intake, assessment, service planning, treatment reviews and case closures
- At least two years’ experience providing evidence-based, evidence-informed, or best-practice interventions
- At least one year of supervisor experience
- Strong written and verbal communication skills
- Strong intercultural communication skills: demonstrated ability to work effectively with people from diverse cultural backgrounds
- Strong computer, keyboard, email, and general office skills

**Working Environment*****:***

- Standard, professional office environment (hybrid remote and in-office)
- Access to reliable transportation to travel regularly throughout the service delivery area
- Position may involve evening and weekend work and travel

**Compensation:** (Pay Rate: $81,000 - $89,100/yr). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**US Benefits:** We offer a comprehensive and highly competitive set of benefits. In the US, these include: 10 sick days, 10 US holidays, 20-25 paid time off days depending on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163 per month, dental starting at $6.50 per month, and vision starting at $5 per month, FSA for healthcare and commuter costs, a 403b retirement savings plans with immediately vested matching, disability & life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program which is available to our staff and their families to support counseling and care in times of crisis and mental health struggles.

title: PIR Case Management Specialist
body:
**IRC Background:** The mission of the International Rescue Committee (IRC) is to help people whose lives and livelihoods are shattered by conflict and disaster to survive, recover, and gain control of their future. Founded in 1933, the IRC has a presence in over 40 countries and 27 offices in the United States; the IRC leads the way from harm to home. IRC opened an office in Spokane in 2022 and provides a continuum of services including intensive case management, employment services, immigration assistance, health and wellness programming, and education support to refugee and immigrant families in Washington State. IRC Spokane is committed to providing trauma-informed, equitable, and accessible services and maintaining and evolving a diverse, inclusive, and supportive workplace.

**Job Overview:**

The Case Management Specialist provides trauma-informed services to refugees and other qualified immigrants to support a positive resettlement experience and the achievement of client self-sufficiency. This position splits time between two programs: approximately 70% in ORR's Program for Initial Resettlement (PIR) and approximately 30% in the Home ARP program. The Case Management Specialist works closely with clients, colleagues, and external parties to develop service and/or self-sufficiency plans to meet individual client needs and preferences utilizing a broad range of financial, medical, social, vocational, and other services and resources in accordance with client eligibility and program requirements.

**Major Responsibilities:**

Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

- Provide case management services across two funding streams, dedicating approximately 70% of time to PIR clients and 30% to Home ARP clients, ensuring program requirements and documentation standards are met for each.
- Coordinate timely pre- and post-arrival services to ensure each client has essentials such as airport pick up upon arrival, initial and permanent housing, food, medical care, and access to transportation, and is oriented to their new environment.
- Help clients find and apply for permanent housing and support them through the move-in process.
- Conduct intake services with clients to assess needs. Develop individualized self-sufficiency plans and SMART goals in partnership with each client.
- Provide services that are relevant to the client’s goals, including the distribution of direct financial assistance, applications for public benefits, referrals to medical and mental health services, and housing. Ensure active clients receive at least one meaningful interaction every 30 days, up to 90 days of service.
- Assess and monitor client progress to support their attainment of established goals, address challenges, and ensure that available resources are utilized.
- Detail each client interaction in accordance with program requirements. Input client information into IRC’s case documentation database, ETO, and assist with tracking and reporting as needed.
- Collaborate effectively with coworkers and partner organizations. Build and maintain relationships with area service providers for the benefit of clients.

- Experience working with refugee and/or immigrant populations strongly preferred.

- Ability to work independently and as a team member in a fast-paced, cross-cultural environment.
