And **90** employees at HQ

PUI works in 10 areas of intervention and distinguishes itself by the implementation of an integrated approach in its response. This method aims to identify and understand the needs of all those affected by a crisis. Our teams come together to bring a rapid global response to the basic needs of populations affected by humanitarian crises to help them regain independence and dignity.

Learn more on [our history](https://www.premiere-urgence.org/qui-sommes-nous/notre-histoire/), [our values](https://www.premiere-urgence.org/qui-sommes-nous/notre-valeurs/), [our areas of intervention.](https://www.premiere-urgence.org/qui-sommes-nous/nos-domaines-d-intervention/)

**Focus on our activities in COLOMBIE**

Our mission in Colombia has been open since 2019. 8 expatriates and 57 local employees are currently working on the mission. PUI is present in 7 municipalities in the departments of Arauca and Norte de Santander, in eastern Colombia. PUI provides direct assistance in primary health care, mental health, nutrition and protection to Venezuelan migrants (in transit or settled), vulnerable host communities and Colombians affected by the conflict.

**What about the Health Coordinator ?**

**As Health Coordinator, you will be responsible for the development and implementation of the mission's operational Health strategy as well as for the quality of current and future Health programmes throughout the design, implementation, monitoring and evaluation phases. You will build the capacity of the mission’s Health department and provides technical support to the project teams and in particular to the Health Project Managers via a functional relationship. You will represent PUI to the authorities, humanitarian actors and donors within the Health sector.**

For this purpose, you will be responsible for :

- Context analysis / Strategy / Development: You will participate in the development of the operational strategy in Health and contributes to the design of new relevant Health interventions on the mission based on the identified Health needs in the country, and in line with PUI’s Health policy and intervention framework. In coordination with the Health team, you will carry out epidemiological monitoring for the country and analyse strengths and weaknesses from a public health perspective.
- Programmes quality: You will provide technical support in your field of expertise to the programme teams, in particular to the Health Programme Managers, and ensure the quality and effectiveness of the mission's Health programmes.
- Representation / Coordination: You will ensure PUI's external representation for the Health sector to partners, donors, national authorities and local actors. You will represent PUI in the Health Cluster / Health sector coordination group meetings. You will contribute to the good information sharing within the Health sector.
- Human Resources / Training: You will provide technical support to the project teams and in particular to the Health teams. You will provide support to the project managers for the recruitment of technical staff in Health. Working alongside the Head of Mission (HoM) and/or the Deputy HoM for Programs and the HQ Health Advisor, you will identify key strengths, weaknesses, opportunities and gaps within Health department. You will supervise the content of Health training and the quality of Health activities on the basis of identified needs.
- Logistics and Administration: You will ensure the teams under your responsibility follow logistic and administrative procedures and keep the logistic and administrative departments informed of any relevant developments.
- Security: You will contribute to the compliance with security rules on the mission and share all information related to security with your line manager and/or to the mission's security manager. You will contribute when necessary to the choice of referral options for the health care of the mission's expatriates.

**The challenges that await you :**

**What you will need to succeed**

- **Training** You hold a Medical diploma or a Paramedic training, and completed a Medical Internship. If you got a Master’s degree in Pharmacy, Public Health or Project management, it would be an asset.
- **Experience** You are strengthened by minimum 3 years of experience in the field with international NGOs in medical project coordination. A previous experience as Medical Coordinator or in an equivalent position would be appreciated. You already worked with Première Urgence Internationale? It would be a definite asset!
- **Skills** You master humanitarian project management and team management, you have a detailed knowledge of donors prerequisites. You also have excellent writing skills.
- **Qualities** You are a good communicator, both in writing and orally. You demonstrate good team spirit, the ability to make decisions, trustworthiness and a sense of responsibility, organisational skills, reactivity, ability to be thorough and to adapt. You have a strong ability to resist stress and particularly in unstable circumstances.
- **Languages** English has no secrets for you! All the better, it is mandatory for this position. If you speak Arabic, Spanish, and/or French, it would be a definite asset.

**PUI will offer you**

- **Status :** Cadre with a Fixed-Term Contract
- **Monthly Gross Income :** 2 650,00 - 3 130,00 EUR depending on your experience in International Solidarity + 50€ per semester of seniority with PUI
- **Insurance** including medical coverage and complementary healthcare, 24/24 assistance and repatriation
- **Housing** in collective accomodation
- **Daily Living Expenses** ("Per Diem")
- **Break Policy :** 5 working days at 3 and 9 months + break allowance
- **Paid Leaves Policy :** 5 weeks of paid leaves per year + return ticket every 6 months

**Our commitments**

Première Urgence Internationale sees diversity of nationalities, genders, beliefs, profiles and statuses among its Human Resources as a major asset for its humanitarian action, and therefore compels itself to the strict observance of the principle of **non-discrimination** throughout its recruitment process.

PUI is committed to preventing all forms of inappropriate behavior in the workplace, including harassment, sexual exploitation and abuse, lack of integrity, and financial misconduct, while promoting the well-being of children and adults with whom PUI interacts. PUI expects all employees to perform their tasks and professional responsibilities in accordance with the PUI Ethical Framework.  
PUI expects all employees to fulfill their professional duties and responsibilities in accordance with PUI’s Ethical Framework. All employees will receive appropriate training and commit to promoting, disseminating, and upholding the principles set forth in its Ethical Charter.  
The holder of this position may potentially have access to personal data concerning children and vulnerable adults as part of their work (Category 2 in the safe recruitment risk classification). Consequently, all recruitments will be subject to satisfactory references and appropriate background checks, which include criminal record and counter-terrorism financing checks.  
Première Urgence Internationale considers the diversity of nationalities, genders, beliefs, backgrounds, and statuses within its Human Resources as a major asset for its humanitarian work. The organization is therefore committed to strictly upholding the principle of non-discrimination throughout its recruitment process.  
We are dedicated to ensuring diversity and gender equality within our organization and strongly encourage candidates from diverse backgrounds to apply.  
Please note that Première Urgence Internationale will under no circumstances request any financial contribution for administrative fees related to recruitment. Any information suggesting otherwise is fraudulent and should be disregarded.  
Early applications are encouraged, as we may close the process earlier than the deadline mentioned above if a suitable candidate is identified.

You recognize yourself in this profile and you adhere to our commitments ? You feel ready to take up the **challenge** and to join **PUI great family ?**

title: EOD Diver Technical Advisor & Senior Mentor (Reserve Pool)
body:
- **Organization:** HAMAP-Humanitaire (HH)
- **Duty Station:** Primarily based in Kyiv, Ukraine (with frequent travel within Kharkiv Oblast and potentially Sumy/Mykolaiv Oblasts)
- **National Partner:** Ukrainian Deminers Association (UDA)
- **Reporting Line:** Country Coordinator (Ukraine) / Head of Mine Action (HQ)
- **Contract Type:** 9-to 12-month international contract (renewable) – Reserve Pool
- **Security Level:** Volatile, high-risk environment (National Level D) – Strict safety protocols in place

## **Program Context**

In Ukraine, HAMAP-Humanitaire operates under a strict, partner-driven capacity-strengthening framework, respecting a "red line" of non-substitution. Rather than deploying as a direct operator, HAMAP-Humanitaire acts exclusively as a technical mentor, advisor, and quality controller to the **Ukrainian Deminers Association (UDA)**, the country’s premier national civilian mine action operator recently accredited for underwater clearance.

The primary objective of this program is to deploy, consolidate, and scale Ukraine’s first civilian **Land & Water Release** capability. Operations focus on surveying, mapping, and clearing explosive remnants of war (ERW) and submerged munitions from rivers, lakes, agricultural irrigation canals, and water reservoirs heavily affected by active hostilities and hydraulic infrastructure failures.

## **Core Duties & Responsibilities**

### **1. Technical Mentoring, QA/QC & Localization**

- **On-the-Job Mentoring:** Provide daily technical mentoring, coaching, and operational support to UDA EOD team leaders and diving personnel during field deployments.
- **Quality Assurance & Control (QA/QC):** Implement and supervise rigorous QA/QC protocols on UDA subaquatic worksites, ensuring total compliance with International Mine Action Standards (specifically **IMAS 09.60**) and Ukrainian National Mine Action Standards (NMAS).
- **Accreditation Support:** If requested, assist UDA’s leadership in refining and submitting their technical dossiers to secure and maintain national subaquatic demining accreditation with the National Mine Action Centre (NMAC).
- **SOP Development:** Co-evaluate, test on-site, and continuously improve the IMAS-compliant underwater Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) developed jointly by HH and UDA.
- **Technical Representation:** Participate in IMAS review boards and international technical side-event forums to contribute specialized expertise, promote the project’s technical achievements, and actively advance humanitarian and localized approaches to underwater explosive ordnance clearance.

### **2. Subaquatic Operations Supervision & Training**

- **Technical Instruction:** Co-facilitate and supervise advanced theoretical and practical training modules (inland diving operations up to 20 meters depth) for UDA's EOD divers in accordance with HAMAP-Humanitaire's training curriculum.
- **Advanced Technology Deployment:** Oversee the operational use and data analysis of advanced subaquatic detection hardware, including side-scan sonars, marine magnetometers, handheld subaquatic metal detectors, and underwater Remote Operated Vehicles (ROVs).
- **Decompression Safety Innovation:** Implement human-centric safety controls, specifically monitoring post-dive nitrogen desaturation using ultrasonic venous microbubble detection.

### **3. Security, Emergency Management & Ethical Compliance**

- **Hyperbaric Emergency Management:** Validate, update, and run weekly simulated emergency evacuation drills (*Medevac*) and decompression accident management protocols in coordination with designated national hyperbaric medical facilities.
- **HEAT & BTLS Integration:** Actively support the ongoing training and field application of Hostile Environment Awareness Training (HEAT) and Basic Trauma Life Support (BTLS) first aid protocols for all deployed team members.
- **Compliance & Safeguarding:** Ensure absolute adherence to HAMAP-Humanitaire's Code of Conduct, dual-use equipment export regulations, and **PSEAH (Protection from Sexual Exploitation, Abuse, and Harassment)** standards, including the monitoring of internal alert systems for both HH and UDA staff.

## **Job Requirements & Qualifications**

### **Mandatory Certifications**

- **IMAS EOD Level 3**
- **Professional Diving Qualification:** Recognized commercial or military diving certification (equivalent to Ukrainian Class 3 Group 3, *or French **Classe II/III Mention A, B or D** (industrial, technical, or military/rescue diving or or UK **HSE Surface Supplied** (or Royal Navy Clearance Diver equivalent)*.

### **Required Experience & Competencies**

- **HMA Experience:** A minimum of 4 years of operational experience in Humanitarian Mine Action (HMA), with active involvement in Non-Technical Survey (NTS), Technical Survey (TS), and Land Release processes.
- **EOD Diving Expertise:** Proven experience in underwater search, mapping, and EOD recovery in low-visibility, high-current, and high-turbidity inland waterways (rivers, canals, lakes).
- **Pedagogical Skills & Posture:** Proven track record in technical mentoring, training delivery, or capacity building with national personnel (civilian, civil protection, or state deminers). Ability to maintain a highly professional, objective, and standard-compliant posture under pressure.
- **Languages:** Fluent English (essential for project management, donor reporting, and technical documentation). Working knowledge of French, Ukrainian or Russian is considered a significant asset.

### **Working Conditions & Benefits**

- **Contract:** Standard international humanitarian contract
- **Financial Package:** Competitive salary/allowances, monthly per diems, and a dedicated hardship allowance calibrated for active conflict zones in Ukraine.
- **Insurance:** 100% comprehensive medical, life, and repatriation insurance (with specific war-risk coverage).
- **R&R:** Regular Rest and Recuperation cycles provided in line with HAMAP-Humanitaire’s country security guidelines.

title: Analyst, Office of the CFO (Fixed-Term)
body:
## **About One Acre Fund**

Founded in 2006, One Acre Fund equips 5.5 million smallholder farmers to make their farms more productive. Across nine countries that together are home to two-thirds of Africa's farmers, we provide high-quality farm supplies, tree seedlings, accessible credit, modern agronomic training, and a wide range of other agricultural services. On average, this model enables any farmer to increase their income and assets on supported land by more than 35 percent, while permanently improving their resilience. This is all made possible by our team of 9,000+ full-time staff, drawn from diverse backgrounds and professions. To learn more, please see our [Why Work Here](https://oneacrefund.org/careers/why-work-here) blog post.

## **About the Role**

Seeking an exceptional finance professional with experience to strengthen the CFO's office, driving strategic initiatives and turning complex data into decisions that shape Finance operations organisation-wide.

## **Responsibilities**

Division Communications & Executive Support

- Lead the drafting and delivery of Finance Division communications, including decision announcements, priority rollouts, and key organisational cycles.
- Maintain the Division's communications calendar and coordinate inputs, timelines, follow-ups, and actions with department leads.
- Prepare high-quality presentation decks, briefing notes, data summaries, and other materials for senior leadership.
- Translate complex data, analytical findings, and team inputs into clear insights, recommendations, and actionable messages.

Division Operations & Governance

- Coordinate the Finance Division's governance calendar, including leadership meetings, quarterly forums, annual events, and other key planning cycles.
- Support agenda development, meeting logistics, preparation of materials, and follow-up on key decisions and actions.
- Monitor progress against divisional priorities and OKRs, identifying risks, dependencies, and areas requiring leadership attention.
- Maintain clear trackers and work plans to support effective coordination and execution across the Division.

Strategic Projects & Problem Solving

- Own clearly defined projects and workstreams from planning through execution and delivery.
- Coordinate selected CFO- and Senior Manager-sponsored initiatives by aligning stakeholders, tracking milestones, and proactively addressing blockers.
- Lead or contribute to high-priority cross-functional and ad hoc projects across the Finance Division.
- Apply structured problem-solving to ambiguous challenges and develop practical options and recommendations for leadership.

Analysis, Strategic Insight & Flexible Resourcing

- Conduct research, benchmarking, data synthesis, and financial analysis to support strategic decision-making.
- Develop structured outputs, including summaries, frameworks, financial models, and scenario analyses.
- Provide flexible support across the Finance Division during periods of peak demand, staff transitions, or extended leave.
- Take ownership of assigned responsibilities during temporary assignments, ensuring clear communication, continuity, and effective handover.
- Support divisional recruitment and other priority initiatives as needed.

## **Career Growth and Development**

We have a strong culture of constant learning and we invest in developing our people. You’ll have weekly check-ins with your manager, access to mentorship and training programs, and regular feedback on your performance. You’ll have the opportunity to shape a growing organization and build a rewarding long-term career.

Across all roles, these are the [general qualifications we look for](https://oneacrefund.org/work-with-us/application-process/qualifications/). For this role specifically, you will have:

- Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Business, Economics, or a related field.
- CPA or ACCA finalist.
- About 5 years of working experience in finance, strategy, consulting, project management, or operations, within fast-paced medium- to large organisations.
- Strong stakeholder management and cross-functional collaboration skills.
- Proactive, detail-oriented, and solutions-focused approach.
- Familiarity with financial analysis, management reporting, and business decision-making is preferred.
- Comfortable navigating ambiguity and adapting to changing priorities.
- Full professional proficiency in English, with strong written communication skills.

## **Preferred Start Date**

As soon as possible

## **Job Location**

Kigali, Rwanda

## **Benefits**

Health insurance, housing, and comprehensive benefits.

## **Contract Duration**

2 years, renewable with a high chance based on good performance.

## **Eligibility**

This role is only open to citizens or permanent residents of Rwanda.

##

28 November 2026. Please note that we hire on a rolling basis which means that applications are reviewed and processed on a continuous basis until a hire is made.

*One Acre Fund never asks candidates to pay any money or pay for tests at any stage of the interview process. Official One Acre Fund emails will always arrive from an @*[*oneacrefund.org*](http://oneacrefund.org/) *address. Please report any suspicious communication here (globalhotline@oneacrefund.org), **but do not send applications or application materials to this email address.***

title: Zambia MEL Lead (Fixed-Term)
body:
## **About One Acre Fund**

Founded in 2006, One Acre Fund equips 5.5 million smallholder farmers to make their farms more productive. Across nine countries that together are home to two-thirds of Africa's farmers, we provide high-quality farm supplies, tree seedlings, accessible credit, modern agronomic training, and a wide range of other agricultural services. On average, this model enables any farmer to increase their income and assets on supported land by more than 35 percent, while permanently improving their resilience. This is all made possible by our team of 9,000+ full-time staff, drawn from diverse backgrounds and professions. To learn more, please see our [Why Work Here](https://oneacrefund.org/careers/why-work-here) blog post.

In Zambia, from our hub in Kabwe, we run a specialised climate-smart input and agroforestry program to address challenges such as irregular rainfall and soil degradation. By partnering with local Tree Nursery Operators, we raise and distribute agroforestry trees that enrich soils and build long-term financial resilience. Supported by a structured frontline field team across Central and Southern Provinces, we use rigorous, data-driven frameworks to measure our impact and ensure we drive meaningful improvements in farmer yields, asset accumulation, and food security.

## **About the Role**

We are seeking an exceptional MEL professional with 4+ years of experience to run our day-to-day field data collection operations, and statistical analysis, strengthen data quality, and manage our 13-person field implementation teams. You will coordinate the entire survey lifecycle from questionnaire scripting and data cleaning to field deployment across our operational districts, ensuring our climate-smart agriculture and agroforestry programs are backed by bulletproof evidence to drive impact for smallholder farmers in Zambia. As the team’s direct link to our Global MEL team, you'll be based in Kabwe and report to our Research and Data Lead.

## **Responsibilities**

**Survey Design & Data Management**

- Design statistically sound data collection instruments and survey methodologies tailored to rural agricultural interventions.
- Establish rigorous data management workflows, cleaning protocols, and automated quality assurance checks to minimise data errors.
- Continuously audit and improve data collection processes to streamline reporting pipelines.

**Survey Analysis**

- Analyse survey data using statistical software (R, Python, etc.) to produce summary statistics and rigorous impact analysis and other statistical analysis as needed (e.g. regression, multi-level modeling, and difference-in-difference methods).
- Apply appropriate statistical approaches, including parametric and non-parametric methods, based on the nature of the data.
- Translate findings into clear, actionable recommendations for program and leadership teams, including contributing to the yearly impact report.

**Field Implementation & Team Management**

- Coordinate and execute large-scale field survey implementations from inception to final dataset delivery across Central and Southern Provinces.
- Directly manage, mentor, and build the capacity of the field implementation team and supervisor networks.
- Plan complex field logistics, timelines, and deployment strategies for remote, rural data collection exercises.
- Guarantee field data integrity by enforcing strict validation protocols and back-checking procedures.

**Cross-Functional Collaboration & Execution**

- Work closely with operational managers and global technical advisors, actively integrating feedback to iterate on survey designs
- Proactively identify and resolve operational and logistical bottlenecks in the field
- Take absolute ownership of final dataset accuracy, operational metrics, and team deliverables.
- Serve as a key point of contact with the Global MEL team, sharing performance data and program learnings.

## **Career Growth and Development**

We have a strong culture of constant learning and we invest in developing our people. You’ll have weekly check-ins with your manager, access to mentorship and training programs, and regular feedback on your performance. We hold career reviews every six months, and set aside time to discuss your aspirations and career goals. You’ll have the opportunity to shape a growing organization and build a rewarding long-term career.

## **Qualifications**

Across all roles, these are the [general qualifications we look for](https://oneacrefund.org/work-with-us/application-process/qualifications/). For this role specifically, you will have:

- Knowledge of R, Python, or suitable languages, combined with survey tools (e.g., CommCare, ODK, KoboToolbox), and Google Sheets.
- Proficiency in quantitative/qualitative survey design, handling complex datasets, with a solid grounding in statistics
- Prior experience directly supervising field teams, enumerator networks, or data collectors in rural environments.
- Demonstrated capability in training, coaching, and elevating the technical execution and data capacity of junior field staff.
- Ability to look ahead, manage team timelines, and resolve personnel or logistical field issues before they impact data quality.
- Bachelor's degree in Economics, Statistics, Agricultural Economics, Development Studies, or a related field. Masters degree (or higher) preferred.

## **Preferred Start Date**

As soon as possible

## **Job Location**

Kabwe, Zambia

## **Benefits**

Health insurance, paid time off

## **Contract Duration**

1 year

## **Eligibility**

This role is only open to citizens or permanent residents of Zambia.

28 November 2026. Please note that we hire on a rolling basis which means that applications are reviewed and processed on a continuous basis until a hire is made.

One Acre Fund aspires to build a culture where all staff feel consistently valued, represented, and connected – so that our team can thrive as professionals, and achieve exceptional impact for the farmers we serve.*

*We are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, marital status, disability, gender, gender identity or expression. We are proud to be an equal opportunity workplace.*

## **Why Work Here**

We’re one of the largest agricultural organizations in Africa, operating in ten countries that together are home to two-thirds of Africa's farmers.  
Guided by our mission, we use the discipline of a business to deliver cost-effective services to millions of people. We believe that heart plus rigor can change the world. [Read more.](https://oneacrefund.org/careers/why-work-here)

title: Senior Manager Global Procurement-Corporate and Professional Services
country: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
body:
**Organizational Background**

Founded in 1933 at the request of Albert Einstein, the International Rescue Committee (IRC) helps people whose lives and livelihoods are shattered by conflict and disaster, including the climate crisis, to survive, recover, and rebuild their futures. Headquartered in New York and London, the IRC operates in more than 40 countries and supports refugee resettlement through 25 offices across the United States. Our work is grounded in bold leadership, innovation, partnership, and accountability to the people we serve.

**Role Purpose**

The Senior Manager, Global Procurement (GP) - Corporate and Professional Services provides strategic leadership across Travel, Translation, Insurance, Cash, Financial and HR Services, including payroll and benefits administration, learning and development platforms, recruitment and RPO, and global mobility and relocation.

The role establishes disciplined, forward-looking category management across this portfolio: translating business demand into sourcing strategies, shaping competitive markets, negotiating high-value agreements, and building supplier ecosystems that improve value, service quality, risk management, and staff experience. As the Senior Manager within GP for these categories, the postholder influences decisions across People & Culture, Safety & Security, Finance, Legal, Risk & Compliance, and country programs.

**Key Accountabilities**

**1. Category Strategy and Portfolio Leadership**

- Own and execute multi-year category strategies for Travel, Translation, Insurance, Cash, HR Services, and additional corporate and professional services categories as assigned.
- Convert spend, demand, market, supplier, and risk insights into clear category plans, sourcing priorities, value targets, and implementation roadmaps.
- Create fit-for-purpose sourcing guide for each category, including market intelligence, pricing and commercial models, contracting approaches, evaluation criteria, and negotiation levers.
- Build an integrated pipeline with business owners, aligning sourcing activity to contract expiries, renewal windows, benefits cycles, and operational priorities.
- Identify and deliver measurable value through cost optimization, demand management, service improvement, risk reduction, and a stronger employee experience.

**2. Strategic Sourcing and Commercial Delivery**

- Lead complex, high-value sourcing initiatives from strategy and market engagement through RFx, evaluation, negotiation, award, and implementation.
- Design sourcing and negotiation strategies that strengthen competition, improve commercial terms, and reflect the operational and regulatory realities of IRC's global footprint.
- Establish robust evaluation governance, ensuring transparent decision-making, clear stakeholder accountability, and complete audit trails.
- Advise business owners on specifications, statements of work, service levels, pricing structures, and contract models that drive performance and protect IRC's interests.
- Lead commercial escalations and resolve material supplier, service, and contractual issues in partnership with Legal, Finance, Risk & Compliance, People and Culture, and operational stakeholders.

**3. Supplier Strategy and Performance**

- Develop resilient supplier pool through framework agreements, pre-qualified panels, strategic partnerships, and appropriate regional or global coverage models.
- Segment suppliers by value, criticality, and risk; apply differentiated governance and relationship-management approaches across the portfolio.
- Set performance expectations and lead structured business reviews using service, cost, risk, innovation, and stakeholder-experience measures.
- Drive supplier accountability, corrective action, and continuous improvement, while identifying opportunities for innovation and stronger market capability.
- Evaluate and document single-source or waiver recommendations when competition is not viable, ensuring a defensible rationale and full policy compliance.

**4. Stakeholder Leadership and Business Partnership**

- Act as the principal Global Procurement partner to People & Culture, Safety & Security, and other corporate functions that depend on the assigned categories.
- Influence senior stakeholders with evidence-based recommendations on market options, supplier strategy, commercial trade-offs, risk, and total value.
- Translate functional priorities into executable procurement plans, creating clarity on scope, roles, timelines, decisions, and dependencies.
- Partner with Safety & Security on travel duty of care and traveler risk-management requirements, ensuring supplier and contracting strategies support organizational obligations.
- Build procurement capability among stakeholders by promoting early engagement, disciplined planning, and consistent use of category and sourcing standards.

**5. Governance, Risk, and Performance**

- Ensure all sourcing and supplier-management activity complies with IRC policies, donor requirements, delegated authorities, and audit standards.
- Embed privacy, information-security, ethical, and regulatory requirements into sourcing and contracting, with particular focus on HR and Insurance providers handling sensitive personal data.
- Maintain accurate spend, contract, pipeline, savings, risk, and supplier-performance data; use insights to guide priorities and demonstrate portfolio impact.
- Keep sourcing decisions and contract records complete, current, and audit-ready.
- Contribute category expertise and market insight to enterprise-wide procurement transformation and continuous-improvement initiatives.

**Person Specification**

**Essential**

- Bachelor's degree in supply chain, business administration, or a related discipline, or equivalent professional experience.
- CIPS Level 4 or higher, or an equivalent procurement qualification.
- At least seven years of progressively responsible procurement experience, including substantial ownership of category management and strategic sourcing.
- Demonstrated success leading complex competitive sourcing, multi-supplier evaluations, commercial negotiations, and contract awards.
- Strong commercial judgment and a track record of improving value, supplier performance, and risk outcomes.
- Ability to influence senior stakeholders, navigate competing priorities, and convert business requirements into practical sourcing strategies.
- Strong analytical capability across spend analysis, market assessment, business-case development, and performance reporting.
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to present complex issues and recommendations clearly.

**Desirable**

- Master's degree in a relevant field.
- Direct category experience in travel, insurance, HR/BPO, language services, or other corporate and professional services.
- Procurement experience in an NGO or nonprofit environment, including familiarity with donor compliance frameworks.
- Working knowledge of Spanish, or Arabic.

**Professional Competencies**

- Strategic and commercial thinking
- Influence and stakeholder leadership
- Market and supplier insight
- Negotiation and decision quality
- Risk awareness and integrity
- Execution discipline and accountability
- Collaboration across cultures and geographies

**Compensation:** (US Pay Rate: $72,930 - 119,000/yr; UK Pay Rate: £52,000 - £62,000/yr). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**US Benefits:** We offer a comprehensive and highly competitive set of benefits. In the US, these include: 10 sick days, 10 US holidays, 20-25 paid time off days depending on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163 per month, dental starting at $6.50 per month, and vision starting at $5 per month, FSA for healthcare and commuter costs, a 403b retirement savings plans with immediately vested matching, disability & life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program which is available to our staff and their families to support counseling and care in times of crisis and mental health struggles.

title: Senior Research and Evaluation Lead in Palestine
body:
**Reference Code: Lead-C235**  
**Number of Positions: 1**

**About ARFADA:**

ARFADA Company for Development and Consultancy is a research company based in Palestine. Founded by a group of professional consultants from various and integrated disciplines, ARFADA is dedicated to providing high-quality evaluations, assessments, and third-party monitoring services. Our mission is to deliver insightful, data-driven solutions that drive development and inform policy decisions.

For more information, please visit our website at [www.arfada.org](http://www.arfada.org/).

**Position Overview:**

We are seeking **highly skilled and experienced Senior Research and Evaluation Leads based in west bank** to spearhead projects related to evaluations, assessments, and third-party monitoring services.

The ideal candidates will possess a strong background in research and evaluation methodologies, excellent analytical and report-writing skills, and demonstrated experience in leading complex projects from inception through completion. They will also serve as the company’s primary points of contact with clients, ensuring effective communication, coordination, and high-quality project delivery.

**Key Responsibilities:**

- Lead the design, implementation, and management of evaluation and assessment projects in **west bank and Gaza** .
- Develop and apply robust research methodologies to ensure high-quality data collection and analysis.
- Oversee third-party monitoring services, ensuring compliance with project objectives and client requirements.
- Be the focal point and collaborate with clients and stakeholders to understand their needs and tailor project frameworks accordingly.
- Produce comprehensive reports and presentations to communicate findings and recommendations effectively.
- Lead and guide staff, project managers, operations manager, and researchers, fostering a culture of continuous learning and improvement.
- Ensure all projects are completed on time, within scope, and budget.
- Stay abreast of the latest trends and developments in research and evaluation methodologies.

**Qualifications:**

- Advanced degree in a relevant field (e.g., social sciences, economics, public policy, statistics).
- A minimum of 10 years of experience in research, evaluation, or a related field.
- Proven track record of leading complex evaluation and assessment projects.
- Strong analytical and critical thinking skills.
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
- Strong organizational and project management skills.

**Note:**

These positions are open only to candidates currently based in **west bank**.

title: Shelter Project Manager, Generic
body:
*Please note that this is a generic recruitment posting. We continuously welcome applications from professionals who are interested in joining Medair in future field opportunities.*

*By applying, you will be considered for both current and upcoming positions across our country programmes. As opportunities arise and your profile matches our anticipated recruitment needs, a member of our team will contact you regarding the next steps.*

*Please note that the standard application response timeline does not apply to generic recruitment postings.*

‍

## **Initial Contract Details**

Full time, 12 to 24 months

## Role Overview

Plan, develop, monitor and evaluate the assigned shelter project(s), assessing shelter needs, designing projects, writing proposals, initiating and effectively managing and reporting on the projects in line with the objectives, timeframe and budget. Provide technical support, leadership and strategic direction; meet quality standards in shelter delivery, encourage beneficiary participation, liaise with other stakeholders and manage and train shelter staff.

## Key Activity Areas

### *Shelter Project Management*

- Manage the assigned shelter project(s) in order to meet the project objectives within budget and within the allotted time frame.
- Provide strong leadership of the assigned shelter project(s), working to ensure both short and long-term positive impacts and outcomes for the beneficiaries, local authorities (where applicable) and local shelter staff.
- Develop and implement an appropriate and effective shelter strategy in consultation with other shelter staff and field managers.
- Set clear objectives and indicators for shelter activities in collaboration with the shelter staff, field managers and, where appropriate, with the local communities.
- Continuously monitor and supervise shelter activities, overseeing the technical design and execution and evaluating progress through outputs and impacts using both quantitative and qualitative data.
- Input into the integration of beneficiary participation and accountability in all aspects of the project.

### *Staff Management*

- Line-manage the Shelter Manager(s) of the assigned project(s), including day-to-day management, development and training, appraisals, etc.
- Facilitate regular meetings to assist information sharing between project staff, to ensure staff members are aware of project objectives and current work plans and to provide the opportunity for feedback.
- Provide coaching and technical supervision to staff in order to develop ownership and full responsibility for shelter activities.

### *Financial Management*

- Manage the shelter budget for the assigned project(s) and ensure all expenses are according to budget and meet the Medair standards with regard to financial management, including accountability and good governance.

### *Communication and Coordination*

- Develop and maintain appropriate, regular, transparent and supportive communication structures with the assigned shelter team, Medair in-country and HQ shelter managers and advisers and other relevant stakeholders (e.g. beneficiaries, community leaders, local and national government officials, UN agencies and other NGOs), with the objective of ensuring good cooperation and partnerships.
- Participate in shelter coordination meetings and other working groups or meetings as required, representing Medair and feeding back to the shelter staff and field managers on relevant issues.

## Qualifications

- Higher level qualification in a technical field, preferably in civil engineering or in another relevant field such as architecture / engineering / construction management; BSc / BEng in a relevant field desirable.
- Strong working knowledge of English, spoken and written.

## Experience

- 2 years post-qualification professional experience in a relevant field.
- Management exper. in a construction context; technical construction skills within humanitarian setting.
- Experience working in a construction / shelter programme in a developing country, preferably in a humanitarian context desirable.
- Good numerical, report writing and administration skills.
- Experience in training / mentoring / coaching staff.
- Advanced planning, assessment and analytical skills desirable.
- Knowledge and understanding of humanitarian standards such as Sphere and HAP.
- Able to cope with basic living conditions in the field and during field trips.

## Team Spiritual Life

Reflect the values of Medair with team members, local staff, people we serve, and external contacts. Work, live, and pray together in our Christian faith-based teams. Fully contribute to a rich spiritual team life, including team devotion, prayer, and words of encouragement.

## **Before you apply**

Please ensure you are fully aware of the:

1. [Medair organisational values](https://www.medair.org/jobs/our-culture/).
2. Medair is committed to safeguarding the protection of beneficiaries, volunteers, staff and partners, and particularly children. Therefore, we do not employ staff whose background we understand to be unsuitable for working with children. Medair staff are required to give the utmost respect to, and comply with,[Medair’s accountability policies and best practices.](https://www.medair.org/accountability/)
3. Medair Relief & Recovery Orientation Course (ROC) (which forms part of the recruitment selection process for field positions).

title: Early Education Specialist
body:
This position is represented by the OPEIU union and subject to the terms and conditions of a collective bargaining agreement.

**Job Overview:** The Early Education Specialist supports refugee children to access preschool services and to succeed academically and socially in elementary school. They also assist parents to participate in their children’s school activities and support schools to identify resources needed to meet the language and cultural needs of refugee students and families. The Early Education Specialist develops strong relationships with local school systems, students, their parents, and other relevant stakeholders through workshops, parent education and case management.

**Major Responsibilities:**

Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

- Lead the planning and implementation of IRC’s efforts to maximize accessibility for its clients to early childhood educational opportunities including Head Start, pre-kindergarten, early learning scholarships to enrich childcare opportunities, daycare, afterschool care, VPI and other school and educational opportunities, including application support as needed.
- Connect families with community resources, including early childhood education programs, childcare programs, in-home providers, parenting support, and programs to support children, ages 0-5.
- Provide individualized case management support to students and families, including referrals to internal services and community resources as appropriate.
- In consultation with management, support parents and caregivers in advocating for students with special needs, including identification, assessment, and access to special education services.
- Maintain accurate and timely case documentation, including case notes, service plans, participant files, and other required records.
- Ensure program data is consistently collected, entered, and maintained in ETO and other required systems in accordance with IRC standards, donor requirements, and contractual obligations.
- Monitor and track service delivery to ensure compliance with program requirements and quality standards.
- Contribute to program monitoring, evaluation, and internal and external reporting efforts.
- Maintain program information and data collection systems in compliance with IRC policies, procedures, and contractual requirements.
- Perform other duties as assigned.
- Other duties as assigned.

**Job Requirements:**

**Education:** Bachelor’s degree in education, social services, or related field required, or equivalent work experience.

**Work Experience:**

- Relevant work experience in positive childhood development, social-emotional development, youth academic support, or a school-based setting required; minimum of 2 years’ experience preferred.
- Prior experience providing support to recently arrived immigrant children and/or parents and families strongly preferred.

**Demonstrated Skills & Competencies:**

- Demonstrated competency in program planning and implementation skills, including the ability to manage groups of students and to think creatively and strategically.
- Strong relationship building, diplomacy, and networking skills; ability to effectively build internal and external relationships.
- Demonstrated success working and communicating effectively in a multi-cultural environment.
- Self-starter with excellent problem-solving skills combined with the proven ability to prioritize and manage time effectively.
- Attention to detail and accuracy in work product.
- Fluent in English, both spoken and written; proficiency in language(s) spoken by client group is desired.
- Proficient in Microsoft Office applications (Word, Excel, Outlook); ability to use the internet and other digital tools for accurate data entry, research, and problem-solving purposes.
- Valid driver’s license and access to a personal, insured vehicle.

**Working Environment:**

- A combination of standard office environment, remote work, and ‘field’ time within the service delivery area to perform the above outlined responsibilities.
- May require occasional weekend and/or evening work.

***This position is expected to end on September 30, 2027.***

**Compensation:** (Pay Rate: $22.75-$24.20). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**US Benefits:** We offer a comprehensive and highly competitive set of benefits. In the US, these include: 10 sick days, 10 US holidays, 20-25 paid time off days depending on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163 per month, dental starting at $6.50 per month, and vision starting at $5 per month, FSA for healthcare and commuter costs, a 403b retirement savings plans with immediately vested matching, disability & life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program which is available to our staff and their families to support counseling and care in times of crisis and mental health struggles.

title: Middle School Alliance Site Coordinator
body:
This position is represented by the OPEIU union and subject to the terms and conditions of a collective bargaining agreement.

**Job Overview:**

The Middle School Alliance (MSA) Site Coordinator provides day-to-day operational and administrative coordination for Out-of-School Time (OST) programming at assigned middle school sites, working within clearly defined procedures and under the general direction of MSA leadership. The coordinator carries out established site operations, logistics coordination, family engagement, and data-accountability tasks -- coordinating schedules and communication with program providers, volunteers, and site-based staff on clearly defined tasks, without formal responsibility for supervising their work -- and escalates unusual or non-routine issues to MSA leadership for resolution.

**Major Responsibilities:**

Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

***Site Operations & Program Coordination***

- Serve as the primary on-site coordinator responsible for overseeing daily MSA operations and implementation, including coordination of related logistics, schedules, and communication with program providers and site-based staff on clearly defined tasks.
- Coordinate daily program logistics including scheduling, room allocation, meal distribution, transportation coordination, dismissal procedures, and site transitions.
- Support scheduling and coordination of program providers to ensure alignment with site needs, school schedules, and MSA priorities.
- Monitor daily site operations to ensure programming is implemented with consistency, efficiency, and fidelity.
- Serve as the primary point of contact for site-based operational communication between school staff, providers, transportation, security, and MSA leadership.
- Troubleshoot routine operational challenges within established procedures and proactively communicate concerns and solutions, escalating unusual or non-routine issues to MSA leadership.
- Assist with coordination of site calendars, events, special activities, and school-based initiatives.
- Ensure site implementation aligns with MSA operational expectations, procedures, and standards.

***Student Recruitment & Family Engagement***

- Collaborate with the Manager of Partnerships & Community Engagement to support student recruitment and enrollment efforts.
- Support outreach and engagement efforts for students, families, teachers, and school personnel.
- Assist with family communication regarding programming schedules, attendance expectations, transportation updates, and special events.
- Promote inclusive access to OST opportunities and support student participation across diverse student populations.
- Build and maintain positive relationships with youth and families to encourage consistent engagement and participation.
- Support implementation of student and family engagement activities throughout the school year.

***Data Management & Reporting***

- Work closely with the Data & Evaluation Manager to support accurate and timely attendance tracking, data collection, and reporting.
- Monitor registration, attendance, participation trends, and Average Daily Attendance (ADA) data.
- Support implementation of evaluation tools, surveys, assessments, and data collection processes, including SAYO-Y and other program quality measures.
- Ensure site-based data systems and reporting procedures are completed accurately and consistently, following established formats and deadlines.
- Use data insights to identify operational challenges and support continuous improvement, in consultation with the Data & Evaluation Manager.
- Maintain organized and accurate records related to attendance, participation, case management, schedules, and operational documentation.

***Program Quality & Continuous Improvement***

- Collaborate with the Network Quality Manager to support implementation of NextUp quality standards and Youth Program Quality Initiative (YPQI) practices.
- Participate in professional development, coaching, training, and quality improvement activities.
- Support program providers in creating safe, engaging, and youth-centered learning environments.
- Monitor program implementation and communicate concerns related to quality, consistency, youth engagement, or operational effectiveness to MSA leadership.
- Gather and communicate feedback from youth, families, providers, and school staff to support continuous improvement.

***Relationship Management & Communication***

- Build and maintain collaborative relationships with school administrators, teachers, providers, families, community partners, and youth.
- Facilitate clear, timely, and professional communication between all stakeholders.
- Attend and support school-based meetings, provider meetings, site leadership meetings, trainings, and MSA planning meetings.
- Represent NextUp and the MSA professionally within school communities and partner spaces.

***Safety, Supervision & Risk Management***

- Support implementation and monitoring of established safety and supervision procedures during OST programming.
- Ensure students are properly supervised during transitions, programming, transportation, and dismissal.
- Maintain awareness of site safety concerns and communicate incidents promptly to MSA leadership.
- Assist with incident reporting, documentation, and follow-up procedures, per established protocols.
- Assist with emergency response coordination and communication when necessary, following established emergency procedures.

***Administrative & Organizational Support***

- Maintain organized operational records and documentation.
- Assist with inventory management, supply coordination, and site preparation.
- Support preparation of operational updates, reports, and presentations.
- Monitor implementation timelines, deadlines, and deliverables related to site operations.
- Follow site-based operational procedures and systems established by MSA leadership.

**Job Requirements:**

- Bachelor's degree is preferred in education, youth development, nonprofit management, public administration, social work, or a related field.
- Minimum of 2–3 years of related experience in youth development, education, afterschool programming, or community-based programming.
- Proficient in English and Spanish, both spoken and written.
- Experience working with middle school youth, school communities, or after-school programming strongly preferred.
- Experience with attendance tracking, data systems, and reporting processes preferred.

**Demonstrated Skills & Competencies:**

- Strong organizational, time management, and project coordination skills.
- Ability to manage day-to-day operational responsibilities and site-based priorities within clearly defined procedures, escalating exceptions to MSA leadership.
- Demonstrated ability to build collaborative relationships and function effectively within a team environment.
- Strong communication skills, both written and verbal in Spanish and English.
- Ability to solve problems, adapt, and manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment.
- Knowledge of positive youth development and youth engagement practices preferred.
- Strong attention to detail and commitment to high-quality implementation.
- Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite and database/data management systems preferred.
- Ability to exercise sound judgment and maintain professionalism in school and community settings.

**Working Environment:**

- Primarily an in-person, school-based environment across assigned middle school sites, with standard office/administrative time for planning and reporting.
- Hours during programming are 11am-7pm. Biweekly staff meetings are held at IRC office.

**Compensation:** (Pay Rate: $28.94-$29.90/hr). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

title: Business Development and Grants Manager
body:
**Country Programme:** Moldova

**Contract Length:** 1 year

**Base:** Chisinau

**Starting date**: September 2026

**Line Manager**: Deputy Head of Programmes

**People in Need (PIN)** is a Czech-based international non-governmental organization (NGO) that has been providing humanitarian and development assistance worldwide since 1992. Today, PIN operates in more than 40 countries, responding to humanitarian crises and supporting long-term development through programmes in education, human rights, climate resilience, and social inclusion. As one of the largest organizations of its kind in Central and Eastern Europe, PIN works across Asia, Africa, the Middle East, and Eastern Europe to support vulnerable communities, strengthen civil society, and promote democratic values and human dignity.

## **About the Moldovan Programme of People in Need:**

People in Need (PIN) has been operating in Moldova since 2003, delivering development and humanitarian assistance across social protection and inclusion, civil society empowerment, agriculture and economic development. Following the escalation of the war in Ukraine in February 2022, PIN significantly scaled up emergency programming, including protection, cash assistance, education, winterization, and livelihoods support for refugees and host communities.

PIN Moldova currently manages a large and diverse portfolio of emergency and development projects implemented nationwide and funded by a range of institutional donors, while increasingly shifting toward long-term development assistance, particularly in the context of Moldova’s EU integration and the need to support local CSOs and line ministries in meeting EU accession commitments.

## **About the role:**

The Business Development and Grants Manager works closely with Programme, Grants, and Partnership teams to secure funding and build sustainable donor relations. The role drives strategic resource mobilization for the Country Programme – identifying, mapping, and pursuing donor opportunities aligned with the Country Programme’s strategic direction.

The position collaborates with Programme Leads in Moldova and HQ Technical Advisors and partners to co-create high-quality concept notes, pitches, and funding proposals, including leading complex multi-stakeholder proposals, and ensures that all concept notes and pitches reflect dignified, non-paternalistic narratives that respect local knowledge and partner expertise.

The role also ensures communication, with donors and maintains strong donor relationships through high-quality reporting and proactive relationship management, including with the Czech Embassy and the Czech Development Agency (CzDA), the European Union Delegation, and other current and prospective donors (e.g. GCF, U.S. Government donors, FCDO, and Swiss Cooperation, etc.). Additional responsibilities include supporting visits of international experts and study visits to countries outside Moldova, conducting institutional funding and proposal design, development and writing mentorship sessions for local team and local partners, and providing broader support to the Programme and Grants functions.

The Business Development and Grants Manager reports to the Deputy Head of Programmes and works in close cooperation with senior CP management (HoP/CD/HoSo/Head of MEAL) and relevant HQ departments.

The Business Development and Grants Manager supports the Grants and Reporting Team on grants health review and oversight, particularly on compliance and donor communications, and may also act as a secondary focal point for external liaison, including representing PIN vis-à-vis donors and in other coordination forums (clusters, working groups, etc.).

## **Main Duties and Responsibilities:**

**1. Strategic Pipeline Management and Donor Intelligence**

- Maintains and regularly updates the donor mapping and funding strategy, tracking funding trends and donor priorities, with particular attention to diversifying the portfolio into development sector in line with PIN’s Country Programme Strategy; keeps management informed of opportunities and strategic trends.
- Continuously monitors emerging and anticipated funding opportunities through donor websites, humanitarian assistance portals, clusters, and bilateral scoping with existing and potential donors; leads funding opportunity review (Go/No-Go) meetings.
- In coordination with the line manager and/or HoP, engages with donors during field visits to build and nurture relationships and promote PIN’s work in its strategic domains; documents donor intelligence and engagement efforts.
- Liaises with HQ funding advisors to strengthen donor knowledge and support proactive fundraising for the Country Programme.
- Maintains up-to-date grant files, donor guidelines, and resource materials, coordinating with relevant HQ desk colleagues.

**2. Proposal Development and Co-Creation**

- Collaborates with Programme Leads in Moldova and HQ Technical Advisors and partners to design high-quality concept notes, pitches, and funding proposals, facilitating a collaborative proposal-design process.
- Leads complex, multi-stakeholder proposals, coordinating the development process across all relevant departments — including supporting the design of logical frameworks, setting realistic and measurable targets, and supporting the development of narrative proposals and budgets.
- Ensures concept notes and proposals reflect dignified, non-paternalistic narratives that respect local knowledge and partner expertise.
- Supports proofreading and translation of proposals and budgets ahead of submission.

**3. Grants Compliance and Reporting Oversight**

- Supports the Grants and Reporting Team on grants health review and oversight, with particular focus on compliance and donor communications.
- Ensures reports meet donor requirements in structure and content, including mainstreaming issues (protection, gender, do-no-harm, conflict sensitivity), and that programme staff receive timely guidelines, templates, and examples to develop quality reporting contributions.
- Oversees compliance with donor guidelines on programme implementation, information collection and storage, and project deliverables.
- Maintains standardized reporting formats and an internal tracking database of reporting timelines by donor/grant, coordinating with the Deputy Head of Programmes, Programme/Project Managers, and MEAL to ensure timely, quality data collection and compilation.
- Drafts, proofreads and compiles interim and final donor reports.
- Prepares documentation and collects inputs from finance and programme teams to facilitate regular project review meetings, using standardized tools provided by PIN.
- Supports administration of project documentation in ELO and Navision (IRPs and other project documentation).

**4. Donor and Stakeholder Relations**

- Ensures communication, with donors and maintains strong donor relationships through high-quality reporting and proactive relationship management, including with the Czech Embassy and the Czech Development Agency (CzDA), the European Union Delegation, and other current and prospective donors (e.g. GCF, U.S. Government donors, FCDO, and Swiss Cooperation, etc.)
- Acts as a focal point for selected donors and grant contracts, both in external representation and in internal coordination with programme and operations teams on programme development and reporting matters.
- May act as secondary focal point for external liaison, representing PIN with donors and in other coordination forums (clusters, working groups, etc.).
- Supports visits of international experts to Moldova and study visits to countries outside Moldova, and coordinates and finalizes related documentation with the regional desk and CP senior management.

**5. FSTP Schemes, Subgranting and Partners Management**

- Oversees the design and set-up of Financial Support to Third Parties (FSTP) schemes, ensuring the scheme’s objectives, eligibility criteria, and financial ceilings comply with EU and other donors’ grant agreement requirements.
- Leads or supports the launch of calls for proposals to sub-grantees (e.g., local CSOs, community structures), including drafting guidelines for applicants, organizing information sessions, and managing the selection and evaluation process.
- Coordinates capacity and due diligence assessments of prospective sub-grantees, ensuring findings inform award decisions, tailored support plans, and risk mitigation measures.
- Ensures sub-grant agreements are properly contracted, with clear deliverables, budgets, and reporting obligations, in line with PIN’s internal grant management policy and donor rules.
- Maintains a subgrant tracking system/database recording contract values, disbursement schedules, reporting deadlines, and compliance; flags, and provides regular updates to the line manager and relevant donors.
- Identifies and flags subgranting risks (financial, reputational, safeguarding) in a timely manner and proposes mitigation measures, including site visits and spot-checks as needed.
- Ensures proper close-out of sub-grants, including final financial and narrative reporting, asset verification/transfer where applicable, and archiving of documentation for audit purposes.

**6. Capacity Strengthening and Partner/Programme Support**

- Conducts institutional funding and proposal design, development and writing mentorship sessions for local team members and local partners.
- Provides general support, direction, and advice to staff as workload and time permit.
- Supports internal coordination of meetings and events.
- Updates the grants management tools provided by PIN and liaises with other departments (Finance, MEAL, etc.).
- Supports proofreading and translation of project documents during implementation.
- Compiles documentation and supports related administrative tasks as needed.

## **Main requirements:**

- Minimum 5 years of professional experience in development and/or humanitarian programming, with demonstrated involvement in program and project implementation in Eastern Partnership or comparable contexts.
- At least 2 years of experience in senior or middle management roles, such as Program Manager, Portfolio Manager, or similar positions with responsibility for overseeing and supporting project teams.
- Proven experience in program and project design, program development, and preparation of project proposals for institutional donors.
- Solid experience in humanitarian and development sectors relevant to PIN Moldova's portfolio, such as civil society support, including governance, protection, social inclusion, livelihoods, education, agriculture, or climate resilience programming.
- Proven experience managing and coordinating multi-partner or consortium-based initiatives.
- Experience engaging and collaborating with governmental stakeholders, including representatives of central and local government institutions, and representing programs in institutional and policy dialogue.
- Experience supporting Project Managers across the full Project Cycle Management, including planning, implementation, monitoring, reporting, and project closure.
- Strong leadership, communication, and interpersonal skills, with the ability to guide, support, and coordinate Program Managers and Project Managers and engage effectively with donors, partners, and internal teams.
- Good contextual understanding of the Moldovan operating environment, including humanitarian needs, development challenges, and coordination mechanisms.
- Strong program planning and coordination skills, ensuring coherence between project objectives, donor requirements, work plans, and budgets.
- Proven ability to operate effectively in complex, high-pressure, and evolving environments, including emergency and politically sensitive contexts.
- Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities, enabling timely identification of implementation risks and support to practical, solutions-oriented responses.
- High commitment to quality programming, accountability, and continuous improvement, including the use of monitoring data to inform decision-making.
- Demonstrated commitment to safeguarding, protection mainstreaming, and accountability to affected populations, in line with PIN policies and humanitarian
- Languages – English - Fluent in all aspects

## **We Offer:**

- Working environment in a well-established humanitarian organization in a challenging context;
- **Salary & Benefits**: Salary based on PIN’s salary scale and HR policies; expected salary range between 2900 - 3350 EURsuper gross (based on the assessment of the candidate’s knowledge, skills, abilities and previous experience)
- **Additional allowances include**:
- - Monthly Subsistence Allowance of 1440 EUR; - Accommodation provided by PIN/Monthly Housing Allowance of up to 750 EUR;
- **Time off and Rest:**
- - 25 days of holiday annually; - 10 sick days
- **Travel benefits:**
- - Reimbursement of travel expenses with travel to the country of residence once every 6 months of work; - Reimbursement of costs of visas and vaccinations; assistance with the visa application procedure; - Reimbursement for the medical check-up before and after the deployment; - Travel health insurance covering medical care, incl. the repatriation;
- **Health and Well-being:**
- - 24/7 Medical Support available online; - Free psychological consultations available online;
- **Professional Development:** Free access to e-learning platforms and PIN Learning Hub; PIN’s global Induction Training, and tailored capacity-building opportunities;
- This positions is unaccompanied.

**Application Deadline –** **Sunday, October 11, end of day**, by COB.

**Applications will be reviewed on an ongoing basis. Candidates will be assessed as applications are received, and the recruitment process may be closed before the stated deadline if a suitable candidate is identified.**

title: Senior Program Manager, Safety, Health & Wellness
body:
**Background:**

IRC Arizona operates Health, Safety, and Wellness programming across both the Phoenix and Tucson offices, addressing the health, safety, and stabilization needs of refugees, asylees, survivors of trafficking and torture, and other vulnerable populations. The Health Program addresses vulnerable populations' health needs through medical case management, health education, and public health interventions, working in collaboration with the healthcare sector, public health authorities, medical providers, facilities, universities, and community agencies. The Safety & Wellness Department provides therapeutic services, asylum casework, survivor support, anti-trafficking and victim services, and case management for individuals with acute safety and stabilization needs.

As IRC Arizona continues to rebuild and adapt to changing refugee arrivals, an uncertain federal funding environment, and evolving community needs, there is a growing need for statewide coordination across these programs. Rather than operating independently across Phoenix and Tucson, IRC Arizona can strengthen its statewide impact through a unified Safety, Health, and Wellness strategy that aligns resources, expands partnerships, builds staff capacity, and improves outcomes for clients and communities in both offices.

**Job Overview:**

The Senior Program Manager for Safety, Health & Wellness provides unified, statewide program oversight, staff supervision, partnership development, and grant maintenance for IRC Arizona's Health and Safety & Wellness programs across both Phoenix and Tucson. This position maintains service provision and contract compliance for Therapeutic Services, Asylum Casework, Survivors of Torture, Anti-Trafficking and Victim Services, the Arizona Asylum Network, Preferred Communities, medical case management (Program Initial Resettlement, Matching Grant, and Refugee Support Services), and public health and health literacy programming. This position builds a shared statewide strategy that strengthens program quality, expands partnerships and diversified funding, and coordinates growth and shared learning across both offices, while preserving the ability of each office to respond to its community's distinct needs.

**Major Responsibilities:**

**Statewide Strategy & Coordination**

- Serve as IRC Arizona's statewide point of coordination for Health and Safety & Wellness programming, aligning strategy, tools, and resources across Phoenix and Tucson without centralizing day-to-day office operations.
- Identify statewide and office-specific program priorities and support leadership in decisions about program investment, expansion, consolidation, or redesign.
- Create a shared framework for collaboration and shared program standards that promote consistency and quality while preserving local flexibility.
- Build and disseminate knowledge and analysis of local and national public health, safety, and wellness trends that affect IRC clients; act as IRC Arizona's subject matter expert on these issues.

**Program Oversight & Quality**

- Oversee Health and Safety & Wellness program staff in a manner that supports the exchange of ideas, encourages camaraderie and collaboration, and fosters professional development.
- Design strategies and frameworks to effectively operate programs and coordinate logistics for grant implementation, program subcontracts, and monitoring of grant activities across both offices.
- Implement, monitor, and provide ongoing training on a trauma-informed service model for Health and Safety & Wellness staff.
- Provide appropriate supervision and case coordination to ensure acute client needs are met in a timely and culturally appropriate manner across all programs.
- Monitor provision of services through regular and systematic file reviews, client interviews, and field visits to ensure compliance with donor requirements and delivery of quality services.
- Track budgets, program expenditures, and activities across programs; ensure donor deliverables are met; compile data and draft reports as required by donor and agency specifications.

**Program Development & Community Expansion**

- Support the development of new and expanded programming, including intensive case management, anti-human trafficking and survivor support services, behavioral health and psychosocial support, chronic disease prevention, maternal and child health, healthcare navigation, community health worker initiatives, and health education.
- Identify key stakeholders, partners, resources, donors, and volunteers to support program growth.
- Assess opportunities to responsibly adapt or expand select services to broader underserved populations whose needs overlap with those of IRC's existing clients, consistent with IRC's mission, policies, and operational capacity.
- Coordinate with other IRC teams to create multi-disciplinary approaches to services that facilitate the best possible client outcomes.

**Partnership & Funding Development**

- Build and maintain statewide relationships with state and local health agencies, FQHCs, hospital systems, universities, Medicaid health plans, behavioral health providers, law enforcement, community organizations, and philanthropic partners.
- Develop strategies to enhance community outreach and engage new stakeholders.
- Review, recommend, and write new grant opportunities in alignment with the office strategic action plan and in partnership with the Grants Manager, identifying federal, state, county, municipal, foundation, healthcare, and victim-services funding opportunities.
- Support diversification of funding to reduce dependence on refugee arrival levels or any single government funding stream.

**Staff Supervision & Development**

- Provide direct supervision to program supervisors and staff across the Health and Safety & Wellness departments (see Key Working Relationships).
- Provide coaching, leadership development, technical assistance, and opportunities for cross-office collaboration to strengthen local leadership and staff capacity.
- Provide supervision to AmeriCorps members, MSW interns, and volunteers associated with each program.

**Compliance & Organizational Commitment**

- Ensure coordination with the development and implementation of outreach and training activities to meet program outcomes.
- Participate in senior management meetings and staff development activities as requested.
- Role model IRC values and commitment to mission and clients.
